title: B-final F3a: fn-body statement source positions lost (null-deref/coverage line=0) — diff-test IR divergence
description:
F3a (d8d3ca8c) is NOT byte-identical to base: make diff-test fails with a selfhost divergence + 5 corpus divergences. Root symptom (corpus collections.av): the avra_null_deref_trap call's source_line arg is i64 0 under F3a vs i64 17 under base — the guard for p2.y on line 17. Repro (minimal): fn main() { let p = Point{x:1,y:2}; println(string(p.y)) } — the p.y null_check emits source_line=0 (base: the real line). ALL of main's body statements end with pos=0 at codegen (systematic, not field-access-specific).

DIAGNOSIS (partial): the codegen null_check (codegen/types.av:1027) passes ctx.source_line, set per-statement in emit_function_body -> emit_block_loop_ctx from ss.line (= sstmt_of's pos-column read). Parse records pos correctly (parse_statement_list_ids record_pos, verified: println gets line 4). But by codegen the fn-body statement ids carry pos=0. Traced the alloc chain via avra_trace_ptr in StmtArena.add/add_leaf/record_pos: the FINAL body ids are created by restmt copying pos from prior ids that were created via a DIRECT add_leaf WITHOUT a following record_pos (so pos=0), and restmt's record_pos(id, pos_of(from)) only sets when line>0, so the 0 propagates. The known direct-add_leaf sites (resolver.av:1200 @external_unit — gated on take_meta; component_decl/expand.av:538 — components only; generics/mono.av:1611/1760 — generic specialization only) do NOT fire for a plain non-generic single-file compile, so there is at least one more add_leaf-drops-pos path (possibly a store/program copy) not yet pinned.

IMPACT: diagnostic-only (the null-deref/coverage line number in a RUNTIME error message; program behaviour is identical — corpus null_checks don't fire, so --run-equiv would pass). But it breaks the HRN byte-identity invariant, so F3a cannot land on the normal diff-test path. Blocks pushing F3a.

FIX DIRECTION: find the add_leaf (or store-copy) that rebuilds fn-body statements without preserving the pos column, and make it pos-preserving (restmt / record_pos). Add a diff-test corpus entry that triggers a null_deref position (or a spec asserting stmt pos survives the full pipeline) so this can't regress silently. Consider whether the codegen should fall back to the enclosing statement's source_line when a statement's pos is 0 (defensive), but the real fix is upstream pos preservation.
close_reason: Closed

comments.author: Claude
comments.text: ROOT CAUSE FOUND + FIXED. Bisected the compile pipeline with a per-pass main-body pos tracer: pos correct (line 3) through P7 (run_comptime), dropped to 0 at P8 (typecheck_program). Culprit: core/ast.av stamp_ids_stmt_ids rebuilt each fn-body statement via `store.stmts.add_leaf(...)` — which does NOT record the pos column — while its sibling annotate_stmt_ids correctly uses `restmt`. Fix: stamp_ids_stmt_ids now uses `store.restmt(stamp_ids_stmt(...), id)` so each rewritten row inherits the source row's pos + span + provenance. Verified: nd_a null_deref source_line 0 -> 4 (correct). diff-test running to confirm byte-identity.

title: [type-system] B6: Content-addressed TypeId — deterministic, cross-process, cache-stable
description:
# Goal

Replace TypeRegistry's incrementing-counter TypeId with content-addressed identity: `TypeId = blake3(canonical_serialization(TypeDefinition))`. Recursive types resolved via Merkle-style fixed-point hashing.

## Why

Today's TypeId is a per-process counter. Same type gets different IDs in different registries. bs2 might assign Stmt=47; bs3 might assign Stmt=51. IDs are meaningless across processes, compilations, or machines.

Content-addressed identity makes TypeIds cryptographically deterministic. Same type → same ID on every machine, every build, every day. Bazel/Nix/Unison built whole systems on this primitive; we'd be the first compiler to use it for type identity.

## Beats

- rustc's `DefId` (crate-local, opaque, unstable across builds)
- Swift's `NominalTypeDecl*` (pointer-local, dies with process)
- OCaml's `Ident.stamp` (process-local counter)
- Go's `*Named` (pointer identity, breaks on generic instantiation)

## What you get

- Distributed compilation: machine A's decoded results consumable on machine B without coordination. The hash IS the validation.
- Fixture cache survives bs2 rebuilds where Stmt's structure is unchanged. Today's invalidation is bs2-hash-based and re-runs walker tests for 80s; content-addressed would invalidate only when Stmt's structure changes.
- The so07.8 brief's P2 concern (Values must never serialize raw TypeIds) disappears — TypeIds are universal.
- Migration tooling: "find all decoders that match this historical Stmt shape" becomes a cache query.

## Implementation

1. Add `canonical_serialization(TypeDefinition) -> bytes` — byte-stable serialization that normalises field order, strips comments, etc.
2. Add `blake3` extern binding (or import from std-crypto).
3. Replace `next_id = counter + 1` in `type_registry_register` with `next_id = compute_content_hash(type_def)`.
4. Handle recursive types via Merkle fixed-point: a `Stmt` referencing `Expr` referencing `Stmt` becomes a graph hash. Use the same algorithm git uses for trees.
5. Verify TypeIds are deterministic across `make clean && make build` cycles.

## Acceptance

- Two consecutive `make clean && make build` cycles produce identical TypeIds for `@std::avrac::core::Stmt`, `Expr`, `ValueType`.
- A serialize/deserialize round-trip test via `@marshal-binary` proves a Value's `type_id` is meaningful across processes.
- The fixture cache survives an unrelated bs2 commit (e.g., perf tweak in `runtime.c`) without invalidating walker fixtures keyed on TypeId.

## Cost

- Hash computation per type at registry-population (~µs per type, negligible).
- Canonical serialization is pedantic — comment stripping, field-order normalisation, type-param-order normalisation. ~150-300 lines.
- Cyclic types need the Merkle fixed-point algorithm (~200 lines of math).

## Design memo

See `docs/2026_06_02_SO07_8_TYPEID_MIGRATION_BRIEFING.md` § "Stretch B6 — Content-addressed TypeId".

## Depends on

- forge-crafting-intepreters-so07.8 (Value/EnumCtor → TypeId migration must land first; B6 changes the ID SOURCE but not the threading or dispatch).
design:
DECISION (this session): implement wc5w as the ROOT fix for 24yd, instead of
extending op3w's FQN-string nominal-compare stopgap in vtype_eq.

WHY (root cause of 24yd): type_registry.av:84 assigns TypeId = infos.length + 1
— a per-registry registration-ORDER counter. @std's registry and a user
program's registry assign DIFFERENT ids to the same FQN, so id1==id2 gives
false-negatives across package boundaries. op3w worked around it by comparing
fully-qualified NAME STRINGS (ast.av vtype_eq line ~939 short-circuit +
n1==n2 fallbacks) — its own notes say "SUPERSEDED — fold into wc5w".

LAYER FIT (from docs/2026_06_14_AST_SOURCE_OF_TRUTH_EPIC.md): wc5w is L3
(ps3t.4, folds wc5w+e5qo). Doc sequencing (lines 475-483) puts L3 PARALLEL TO
L1, AHEAD of L2. wc5w does NOT depend on so07.8 (L2). The arrow runs the other
way: so07.8 depends on stable TypeId identity; so07.7 (T6 interned TypeId) is
CLOSED and is the shared foundation both build on; wc5w upgrades so07.7's
counter to a content hash. Content-addressed ids are RE-DERIVABLE on decode, so
so07.8's open tail ("enum_value_to_value_type sets id=0", y9y4.17) evaporates.
bd marks wc5w READY (no open blocker).

PLAN: TypeId = blake3-or-sha256(canonical_serialization(TypeDefinition)).
1. Add canonical_serialization(name, kind, fields, variants, inner_vt) -> bytes
   (normalize field/variant order, strip transient state).
2. Reuse the existing sha256 primitive (runtime.c avra_sha256_hex / @std.crypto)
   unless blake3 is warranted; recursive types via Merkle fixed-point.
3. KEYSTONE PREREQUISITE — the "opaque-handle rule": TypeId is currently a
   1-based INDEX into TypeRegistry.infos (type_registry_lookup: infos[id-1]) and
   the key of the id_to_name intmap. Content-hash ids break positional indexing
   => convert TypeRegistry storage from list-indexed-by-counter to MAP-keyed-by-
   hash, and AUDIT every TypeId consumer for positional/sequential assumptions.
4. IR-NEUTRALITY GATE: content-hash ids must NOT leak into emitted IR or mangled
   symbols, else selfhost fixed point + diff-test semantics change. Audit whether
   any TypeId reaches codegen output / mangling / metadata-on-disk. Ideal: ids
   stay purely compile-time identity => diff-test stays byte-identical.
5. Once ids are stable cross-registry: vtype_eq compares ids; DELETE op3w's
   FQN-string short-circuit + the n1==n2 fallbacks; 24yd's Newtype#id vs
   Struct#id (same name, diverged-counter) resolves at the root.

SCOPE-SIZING = the TypeId-consumer audit (step 3/4). Run it FIRST; it decides
whether wc5w is a tight PR or a sprawl.

SEED/SEQUENCING: wc5w is semantics-only (no new syntax/keywords) so not
parser-seed-affecting, BUT it root-fixes 24yd which IS seed-gating for B1b.
Order: land wc5w -> seed-train cycle -> rework B1b/c bridgeless on stable ids.

WIP STATE: B1a merged-locally+pushed (7d1ab0d8). B1b/c + 24yd investigation
artifacts preserved at fb2a4f6b on origin/claude/ps3t-b1-inverse-walker.
acceptance_criteria: All child tickets closed and the epic goal delivered: B6: Content-addressed TypeId — deterministic, cross-process, cache-stable.
notes: CORE IMPLEMENTED + VERIFIED on v40. Branch claude/wc5w-content-addressed-typeid (b0f7c1e9 core + 3c638240 cleanup, force-pushed, rebased onto v40+#587). content_id_for(FQN) FNV-1a-64 lives in core/type_registry.av; register assigns it; id_to_index intmap replaces infos[id-1]; vtype_eq compares nominal identity by content id KIND-AGNOSTICALLY (fixes 24yd) with Newtype-inner + NarrowedEnum-variant discriminators and an FQN-string fallback ONLY pre-resolve (id==0); sym_id_for delegates to content_id_for (the two identity schemes unified). Verified: full suite 3488/3488, selfhost byte-identical (590769-line IR); 15/15 existing vtype_eq T6 specs; 8/8 new wc5w specs (determinism, cross-registry stability, sparse-id round-trip, 24yd). diff-test (IR-neutrality vs v40 integration) running. SCOPE: this is the NAME-content-addressed core = the correct NOMINAL identity, meets wc5w acceptance, kills op3w's string stopgap. STRUCTURE-hash/Merkle (finer cache invalidation, Layer-6) deferred to sh48. STAYS OPEN pending merge + the user's call on whether structure-hash is in wc5w or stays sh48.
close_reason: Core deliverable merged in PR #590 (squash 8875ffd7): content-addressed TypeId = content_id_for(FQN), deterministic + cross-registry/process/build stable — meets the acceptance (identical TypeIds across clean builds) and is the correct NOMINAL identity. sym_id_for unified onto the same hash. The structure-hash/Merkle refinement (finer cache invalidation, Layer-6) is split into sh48 (sibling under ps3t.4), per the agreed scoping. 3518/3518, selfhost+diff-test byte-identical, 0 warnings.

title: [epic] COMPILER-FAST: Compiler is fast (incremental + parallel + distributable)
description:
# Goal

The Avra compiler is fast, incremental, distributable. Pre-commit cycles drop to sub-30-seconds. CI runs in seconds via shared content-addressed cache. IDE feedback is sub-100ms. When this epic closes, you can honestly say "compiler is world-class fast."

## Scope

Owns every epic that exists to make the COMPILER ITSELF fast. The language-correctness side and the world-class type-system stretches both live in sibling epics (BOOTSTRAP-V1, BEYOND-V1). This epic is purely about cycle time, parallelism, incrementalism, and the daemon architecture.

Closes when ALL the following land:
- `uzs9` closes (test cycle speed epic; jdgo + cbg3 + 6w6v + i7gw + 20l2 + zp5b all done).
- `ylye` closes (Test Runner V2 — structured JSON results, `shard → test unit` rename).
- `y4n1.4`, `.5`, `.8` close (CLI extraction completes — packages/cli/ + Makefile cutover + module graph pass-2).
- `y4n1` closes.
- `i7gw` closes (bundled compile parallelization — unblocks 20l2's per-binary parallel target).
- `qvfb` closes (all 6 layers: PCH → daemon → Salsa → content-addressed cache → LSP → per-fn codegen).

## Why

The user feedback loop is the second-most-leveraged compiler property after correctness. If a developer waits 9 minutes for cold pre-commit, the feedback latency dominates the experience even when the LANGUAGE is sound.

jdgo (closed 2026-06-01) proved continuous shard dispatch alone gives 2× cold speedup. The qvfb-layer roadmap promises another 30-60× via daemon-resident, demand-driven, content-addressed memoization. The remaining test-speed and CLI-extraction work is the engineering pavement that lets the qvfb daemon ship cleanly.

## How `bd ready` reads under this epic

`bd ready` walks children in dependency order. The recommended sequence is:

1. **Now**: remaining uzs9 children (cbg3 follow-ups, 20l2 once i7gw lands).
2. **In parallel**: y4n1.4, y4n1.5 (CLI extraction verification closes).
3. **After uzs9 + y4n1 close**: ylye (Test Runner V2) — depends on stable test infrastructure.
4. **Concurrent with ylye**: qvfb layer 1 (PCH blob) — depends on nothing structural.
5. **After qvfb L1**: qvfb L2 (daemon) — depends on PCH.
6. **After qvfb L2**: qvfb L3-L6.

## Acceptance

- All listed children show `[CLOSED]` in bd.
- `bd ready --epic COMPILER-FAST` returns empty.
- `make test` cold wall < 30 seconds.
- Edit-to-test-result latency in `bs2 test --watch` < 1 second.
- Cross-developer cache via shared volume produces measurable speedup on second build.

## Lineage

Restructured 2026-06-02 from the prior flat epic list. Combines:
- uzs9 (Test cycle speed)
- ylye (Test Runner V2)
- y4n1 (Extract CLI)
- y4n1.4, .5, .8 (y4n1 children)
- qvfb (Demand-driven incremental compiler)
- i7gw (bundled compile parallelization)

These were filed as peer epics during 2026-04 through 2026-06; consolidating under one umbrella gives `bd ready` a single answer for "what's next to make the compiler fast."

title: [epic] BOOTSTRAP-V1: Bootstrap is correct (language + types + macros sound)
description:
# Goal

The bootstrap language + type system + macros are sound. Avra compiles itself with full correctness guarantees and no foundational debt. When this epic closes, you can honestly say "bootstrap is solid."

## Scope

Owns every epic that exists to make the LANGUAGE ITSELF correct. The compiler-performance side and the world-class type-system stretches both live in sibling epics (COMPILER-FAST, BEYOND-V1). This epic is purely about correctness, exhaustiveness, and structural soundness.

Closes when ALL the following land:
- `so07.8` completes (Stmt/Expr as first-class Values; closes so07's last open child).
- `so07` closes (all 8 structural foundations done).
- `y9y4` closes (derive_walker autogenerates AST walkers).
- `vndt.1` and `vndt.2` close (F9001 promoted to error; `bs2 fix` migrates existing wildcards).
- `vndt` closes (zero wildcard arms in matches over declared enums).
- Remaining `vez6` children land (Components V2 reaches 14/14).
- `vez6` closes.
- `0q0m` closes (auto-register pure @std.avrac.core fns for @comptime macros).
- `rlb4` closes (List<T>.sort() and .insert() codegen bug fixed).

## Why

Without bootstrap-level correctness, every higher tier (compiler perf, world-class type system) builds on unsound foundations:

- COMPILER-FAST's incremental cache cannot trust types it can't prove are exhaustive.
- BEYOND-V1's content-addressed TypeId requires structural canonical form — wildcards make canonicalization ambiguous.
- BEYOND-V1's `@codec` derive requires exhaustive variant dispatch — wildcards undermine the generated code's correctness.
- BEYOND-V1's dependently-typed `Value<T>` requires the type system to enforce exhaustive matches — wildcards are escape hatches that defeat the guarantee.

This epic is the prerequisite for everything else honest.

3. **After y9y4 closes**: `vndt.1` (spec promotion) and `vndt.2` (auto-expand tool). These close vndt.
4. **After so07 and y9y4 close**: remaining vez6 children. These close vez6.

title: [epic] Demand-driven incremental compiler: PCH → daemon → Salsa → content-addressed → LSP → per-fn codegen cache
description:
# Goal

Eliminate per-fixture re-parse + re-typecheck of the @std/avrac universe (~430k LOC, currently 13.7s of every cold fixture compile). Convert bs2 from a single-shot batch compiler into a daemon-resident, demand-driven, content-addressed incremental compiler. Target: cold pre-commit ~5s, warm ~1s, edit-to-test-result feedback in the same blink.

This is the "what" only — no time estimates. Ordered as a ladder so any layer can ship and deliver value standalone; later layers compound.

---

## Ladder layer 1: Precompiled @std/avrac AST blob (C++ PCH analog)

The smallest fix that targets the actual bottleneck. Each fixture pays 13.7s in `resolve_mods` walking + parsing 389 std-avrac source files. Eliminate by shipping a pre-parsed binary alongside bs2.

### Required components

- **@marshal-binary derive on every AST type**: Stmt, Expr, ValueType, Pattern, SStmt, SExpr, ParamEntry, TypeParamEntry, all variant payloads, all enclosed List<T> shapes. The infrastructure exists (TestResults already uses it at the shard boundary) but coverage today is partial.
- **AST serializer/deserializer with stable encoding**: 1-byte tags + length-prefixed payloads. No format drift between bs2 versions without an explicit version bump in the blob header.
- **Build-time emit step**: a `make` target that runs bs2 over @std/avrac, captures the resolved-but-unstamped AST, writes `bootstrap/build/std-avrac.parsed.bin`.
- **Resolver fast-path**: before walking @std/avrac sources, check whether `std-avrac.parsed.bin` exists AND every source file's mtime is older than the blob. On hit, deserialize the blob in one read (target: ~100-200ms). On miss, fall back to the existing path AND emit a stale-cache warning.
- **Span preservation**: serialized AST nodes must carry their original `Span { file, line, col }` so post-resolve diagnostics still point at the right source lines.
- **CI invalidation**: the blob is a build artifact, not checked in. Pre-commit and CI ensure the blob is rebuilt when any @std/avrac source changes.

### What this DOESN'T solve

- Same-binary repeat runs of a fixture (warm hits at the per-fixture level still need j568).
- Non-@std/avrac modules (other packages still re-parse, but they're small).
- Salsa-style fine-grained invalidation: edit one fn in @std/avrac/core.av and the WHOLE blob has to be rebuilt, not just the affected query subtree.

---

## Ladder layer 2: Long-running compiler daemon

The fundamental wasted work isn't just parsing — it's process startup + heap warm-up + every-pass-from-scratch. bs2 starts ~562 times per cold suite. Replace with a single long-running compiler service.

### Required components

- **Daemon entry point**: `bs2 daemon` starts a long-running process that binds a Unix socket at `$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/avra-bs2.sock` (or `/tmp/avra-bs2.$UID.sock` fallback).
- **Compile-RPC protocol**: framed JSON or `@marshal-binary` messages over the socket. Requests: compile(source, env), check(source), expand(source). Responses: ok(ll_bytes, diagnostics) or err(diagnostics). Cancellation tokens for interactive use.
- **Per-request isolation**: each RPC gets its own compile arena (`avra_arena_new`) so memory doesn't leak across requests. The shared parsed @std/avrac AST is reference-counted, not copied.
- **In-memory parsed-AST cache**: parsed std-avrac lives in the daemon's heap. Subsequent requests skip parse + resolve_mods entirely for that prefix. Eviction policy: bounded LRU by parsed-tree size; full eviction on AVRA_LIB env change.
- **Source-file mtime watcher**: when any @std/avrac/* source file's mtime changes, invalidate the parsed cache for that file + everything that imported it. Linux: inotify. macOS: kqueue. Fallback: poll mtime per request.
- **Daemon lifecycle management**: a wrapper `bs2 compile` client transparently starts the daemon if not running, sends the RPC, exits. The daemon self-shuts-down after N minutes of inactivity. `bs2 daemon --stop`, `bs2 daemon --status`.
- **Concurrent request handling**: requests dispatch into a worker pool (one OS thread per request, capped at jobs=N). The shared parsed-AST cache is locked for reads (RwLock-style) so reads are concurrent.
- **Thread-safety audit of the entire compile pipeline**: every static in bs2 (and the std-avrac library it links against) must be either (a) per-request (passed via Ctx), (b) immutable after init, or (c) mutex-protected. The CLAUDE.md "process-level parallelism" rule has to be retired with care — every mutable global is a potential race.
- **Crash isolation**: if a single RPC's compile panics, the daemon catches the panic (sigsetjmp-style) and returns an error to that client without killing the daemon. Other in-flight requests continue.
- **Migration path**: per-file test runner (`run_per_file_test_command`) gets a `--daemon` flag. When set, dispatch shards send compile RPCs instead of forking new bs2 processes. Pre-commit migrates once verified.

### What this DOESN'T solve

- Cross-machine cache sharing (still local to one process).
- Fine-grained invalidation within a file (edit one fn, the whole file's resolve+typeck re-runs).
- IDE/LSP integration (still requires the daemon to also speak LSP).

---

## Ladder layer 3: Demand-driven query architecture (Salsa-style)

The full Wow. Replace the pipeline-of-passes design with a database of memoized queries. Every compiler function becomes a pure query keyed on its inputs.

### Required components

#### Query infrastructure

- **Query trait + macro**: every memoizable function becomes `#[query] fn parse(file_id: FileId) -> ParsedFile`, `#[query] fn typeck(fn_id: FnId) -> TypedFn`, etc. The macro derives input-tracking and cache-storage.
- **Query database type**: a single `Database` struct that owns every query's cache. Queries borrow `&db` and call other queries through it; the database tracks the call edges as a dependency DAG.
- **Stable IDs**: every AST entity (file, fn, struct, expr) gets a stable ID that survives invalidation. Today bs2 uses positional pointers; those need to become interned IDs.
- **Input invalidation**: changing `file_contents(id)` invalidates every query whose dependency graph transitively touched that file. Triggered by file-watcher events or explicit `db.set_file_contents(id, new)`.
- **Versioned caches**: each query result has a revision number. When an input changes, dependents see "your input revision is stale" and re-run; their output revision stays the same if the result is unchanged, so THEIR dependents don't re-run (early cutoff).

#### Pass-by-pass rewrite

Every existing pass becomes one or more queries:

- `parse(file_id) -> ParsedFile` (cached on file_id; invalidated on file_contents change)
- `module_tree(root_file_id) -> ModuleTree` (cached on root + transitively-loaded file_ids)
- `decls(module_id) -> List<DeclId>` (cached on module)
- `resolve_use(use_id) -> ResolvedTarget` (cached on use + visible decls)
- `fn_signature(fn_id) -> FnSig` (cached on fn body + resolved use)
- `fn_body_typed(fn_id) -> TypedFnBody` (cached on fn + every called-fn's signature)
- `monomorphize(fn_id, type_args) -> MonoFnBody` (cached on fn + type args)
- `codegen_fn(mono_id) -> LLVMValueRef-equivalent` (cached on mono fn body)

Reading a query MAY trigger re-execution of stale upstream queries; the database memoizes everything.

#### Cycle handling

Macro/comptime evaluation can create query cycles: `expand(macro_id)` calls `typeck(target_fn)` which calls `expand(macro_id)` again on the synthesized fn. The query database needs cycle detection with explicit fixed-point semantics or fatal-error reporting.

#### Diagnostic ordering

Queries can run in any order. Diagnostics need to be sorted into a stable order at the boundary (today's render_bag step) so user-facing output is deterministic across runs.

#### Mutation boundary

The whole query graph is pure-functional internally. Mutation happens only at the database boundary via `db.set_*` calls. The CLAUDE.md "no mutable globals" rule extends to "no mutable state inside queries" — Ctx threading becomes the universal pattern.

### What this DOESN'T solve

- Initial cache warm-up (first compile after restart is still slow).
- Inter-machine sharing (still single-process).
- Persistence across daemon restarts (in-memory only).

---

## Ladder layer 4: Content-addressed persistent cache

The query database is in-memory and per-daemon. To survive restarts and enable cross-machine sharing, every query's result gets keyed not on its input IDs but on its inputs' content hashes. Same syntax anywhere → same hash → shared cache slot.

### Required components

- **Content-addressed query keys**: instead of `parse(file_id)`, the key is `parse(sha256(file_contents))`. Same file content in two different projects (or two branches of one project) shares the cache slot.
- **Disk-backed query store**: each query result serialized to `~/.cache/avra/queries/<hash>.bin` (or a configurable path). LRU eviction by access time. Hash collisions handled by storing the full input alongside the output.
- **Garbage collection**: a periodic compactor walks the cache, deletes entries older than N days, defragments the on-disk slabs.
- **Remote cache protocol**: optional HTTP/2 or gRPC endpoint where multiple developers / CI runners push and pull query results. Authentication via shared token or OIDC. Bandwidth-aware: small queries always hit local; large IR blobs only fetch when the local cache misses.
- **Cache fingerprint**: every cached entry carries (bs2_version, query_name, input_hash). Loading a stale-version entry triggers re-execution + overwrite.
- **Reproducibility tier**: the entire cache becomes a build oracle. `bs2 build --sealed` refuses to compute anything not already in the cache (CI hermeticity). `bs2 build --explain <fn>` walks the cache to show which queries fed which result, for diagnostic.

### What this DOESN'T solve

- IDE/LSP integration is a separate workstream (layer 5).
- Differential compilation at fn-level granularity for codegen (Salsa gets you to "this fn changed, recompile its mono instances"; per-fn .o-level cache adds another tier).

---

## Ladder layer 5: LSP integration on the same query database

Once the daemon owns a query DB, the IDE can query it too — type info, go-to-def, find-usages, completions, errors-as-you-type all hit the same in-memory cache the batch compiler uses. No second compiler implementation.

### Required components

- **LSP server entry point**: `bs2 lsp` starts a daemon variant that speaks Language Server Protocol over stdio. Same query DB underneath as `bs2 daemon`.
- **Position-to-query mapping**: an LSP request like "what's at line 42 col 10 of file X" translates to query-database lookups (parse_at_position, resolve_at_position, typeck_at_position).
- **Incremental syncing**: LSP `didChange` notifications call `db.set_file_contents`; the next query reflects the new input. The Salsa early-cutoff property means most queries don't re-run.
- **Diagnostics push**: on `didChange`, eagerly re-run the typecheck queries for the changed file's fns and push diagnostics back via `publishDiagnostics`.
- **Cancellation**: in-flight queries get cancelled when their inputs change before completion. The daemon's RPC layer needs to surface cancellation through `Result<T, Cancelled>`-style returns at every query boundary.
- **Workspace symbols**: `workspaceSymbol` walks the decls query across every file in the project. Cached, so it's instant after warm-up.

### What this DOESN'T solve

- Debugger integration (separate).
- Format/lint queries (separate, but reusable query infrastructure).

---

## Ladder layer 6: Differential codegen + per-fn object cache

The codegen pass walks every fn in the module and emits LLVM IR. Salsa cuts re-codegen of unchanged fns at the IR level; this layer pushes the cut further to the object-file level.

### Required components

- **Per-fn object emit**: change codegen from "emit one .ll for the whole module" to "emit one .ll per fn". Each fn's .ll goes through llc independently, producing one .o per fn.
- **Per-fn cache key**: hash of (fn_id, mono_args, llvm_ir_bytes, llvm_version, optimization_flags). Cache hit means skip llc.
- **Static archive linking**: the final binary links from a hash-named archive of per-fn .o files. Adding/removing one fn touches one .o; the rest of the archive is shared.
- **Inline budget control**: aggressive inlining would defeat the cache. Per-fn objects need stable inline boundaries; cross-fn inlining moves to a final LTO pass that's also query-driven.

### What this DOESN'T solve

- Whole-program optimizations (LTO becomes its own query).
- Profile-guided optimization caching (PGO is a separate cache shape).

---

## Cross-cutting concerns

### Determinism

Every query MUST be deterministic for the same input. Iteration over maps with non-deterministic ordering, time-based randomness, address-based hashing — all forbidden inside queries. Tests run with deterministic seeds.

### Diagnostics

Today bs2 emits diagnostics as a side-effect during compilation. The query model requires diagnostics to be query OUTPUTS, not side-effects. Each query returns its result PLUS a list of diagnostics. A boundary layer collects them all and sorts them for display.

### Memory model

The shared query database holds parsed ASTs, typed bodies, and IR. Estimated working set for the full @std/avrac universe: 200-500MB resident. Acceptable for a developer machine; CI ergonomics depend on the daemon's eviction behavior.

### Bootstrap loop

bs2 itself is built from bs2. Changing the query architecture means the bootstrap seed needs to encode it. Either: (a) keep the seed using the old pipeline architecture and have bs2-built-from-seed bootstrap the query-based bs2 (two-stage), (b) extend the seed to also be query-based from day one (more seed delta but conceptually cleaner). Decision deferred to the architectural design phase.

### Testing

Every query gets unit tests against synthetic inputs. The whole test suite migrates from "fork bs2 per fixture" to "send compile RPC to daemon". The fixture-stdout cache layer (cbg3.1/zp5b) becomes redundant — daemon's query cache subsumes it.

### Migration

Layers ship independently. Layer 1 (PCH blob) is a self-contained delta. Layer 2 (daemon) can adopt the PCH blob OR re-parse on first request — either works. Layer 3 (Salsa) requires the daemon as substrate. Layer 4 (persistent cache) bolts onto Salsa. Layer 5 (LSP) bolts onto Salsa. Layer 6 (per-fn cache) bolts onto Salsa.

If only layer 1 ships, walker tests drop from 18s/fixture to ~2s/fixture (the resolve_mods cost evaporates; typeck + codegen remain).

If layers 1+2 ship, cold suite goes to ~5s and warm to ~1s.

If layers 1+2+3 ship, edit-to-feedback latency in `bs2 test --watch` becomes the daemon's RPC round-trip plus the changed-fn-subtree's typeck. Sub-100ms feasible.

Layers 4+5+6 add reach (cross-machine, IDE, finer codegen granularity) but don't move the per-edit feedback floor.

---

## What this epic explicitly does NOT include

- A new language feature.
- A REPL (would build on the daemon trivially, but separate).
- A package manager redesign (current packages/std-* layout is fine).
- A different LLVM backend.
- Anything that changes the user-facing source syntax.

It's pure compiler infrastructure: the same input source → the same output binary, just produced via a fundamentally different control flow.
acceptance_criteria: All child tickets closed and the epic goal delivered: Demand-driven incremental compiler: PCH → daemon → Salsa → content-addressed → LSP → per-fn codegen cache.
notes: PLAN RECONCILE (2026-06-15): the PCH-blob/@marshal-binary strategy is largely SUPERSEDED by the L6 query engine on the new immutable+hash-consed foundation (ps3t.8.*); the 13.7s @std re-parse bottleneck analysis remains valid input. Dedupe this ladder against ps3t.8.2-.7. See doc Layer 6.

title: per-file 'bs2 test <path>' cache MISSES on identical reruns — never prints '[test-cache] hit'
description:
## Repro

```
shasum build/bs2  # stable across the two runs
time ./build/bs2 test packages/std-avrac/src/features/match_expr/tests/enum_match_test.av
# 14.91s user, 0.70s system, 15.22s real
time ./build/bs2 test packages/std-avrac/src/features/match_expr/tests/enum_match_test.av
# 14.96s user, 0.71s system, 15.33s real
shasum build/bs2  # still stable
```

Neither invocation prints `[test-cache] hit`. Cache directory `build/cache/` has 2753 entries with unit.bin files — they're being written elsewhere but the per-file test lookup isn't matching.

## Expected

Second run should print `[test-cache] hit` and exec the cached binary in <2s. The cache infrastructure landed under hkms; per-file test mode is what should benefit most from it.

## What the code does

```
fn run_test_command() (packages/cli/src/main.av:2953)
    args.per_file defaults false → bundled-cache path
    args.coverage defaults false → run_test_cached_path
    → check_test_cache_or_miss (line 3031)
        decide_build(inputs) — fingerprint over:
          - unit_name ('test:all' for unfiltered)
          - compiler_hash (sha256 of build/bs2)
          - profile_key (opt level / debug / coverage flags)
          - target_triple
          - sources: [test_file, runtime.o, llvm_wrap.o, 377 @std/avrac/src/*.av]
          - dep_fps: [] (pdme.1 already tracks this, but empty here only means
            no transitive deps go into fp — would cause false HITS, not MISSES)
        if cache_has_test (entry_bin_path file exists) → Hit
        else → Miss
```

cache_has_test is a simple `avra_selfhost_file_exists` check on entry_bin_path. Either:
1. The fp computed for run 1 differs from run 2 (something path/time-dependent in inputs.sources or compiler_hash).
2. The publish path on run 1 fails silently — bin never lands at entry_bin_path.
3. The hit detection finds the file but check_test_cache_or_miss returns Miss anyway.

## Diagnosis hints

- runtime.o + llvm_wrapper.o land in inputs.sources. Their .o content is *should* be stable on identical input but C compilers sometimes embed build paths or timestamps. `shasum build/runtime.o` should be invariant across two consecutive test runs without rebuild — verify.
- compiler_hash_for(inputs.compiler_path) — should be the bs2 sha. Probe: does compiler_hash itself change between runs?
- Path normalisation: `enum_match_test.av` is relative; if cwd shifts or the cli canonicalises differently, the source list could differ.

## Why this matters

Closing this unblocks fast iteration on every other epic — particularly y9y4.9 (12 walker refactors, each needing test re-runs).

## Related (already in this umbrella)

- i7gw — even with cache fixed, cold-cache bundle compile is 360s.
- pdme.1 — false HITS not misses; doesn't explain this bug but lives in the same cache key code.
- j568 — /tmp path exclusion. Doesn't apply here (path is under packages/).
notes: INVESTIGATION HANDOFF (this session). Confirmed: bs2 test <path> takes ~15s × 2 runs, cache miss reproduces. KEY DATA: (1) 3 distinct cache manifests exist for unit 'test_shard:enum_match_test' (fps 46afff85, 0f80d200, 3c61cdf2) — proving fp differs across runs. (2) After 2 latest clean runs NO new manifests written → likely cache HIT but 15s wall time still spent in orchestrator. (3) AVRA_SKIP_PREBUILD=1 doesn't speed it up → prebuild is NOT the 15s bottleneck. (4) Test execution itself reports 0.0-0.3s. (5) All std-avrac .avra-sha256 sidecars are valid. PROBE BLOCKERS: edits to packages/std-avrac/src/build/driver.av don't show in compiled bs2 — the seed compiler appears to use a cache path that ignores edits even with sidecar deletion. NEXT STEPS: (a) ROUTE: maybe the 15s is split between universe_fp computation (280 sha256_file calls) and shard subprocess startup; instrument compute_test_universe_fp with rdtsc or system_time markers in runtime.c instead of Avra-side probes. (b) ROUTE: log the universe_fp env var directly from shard subprocess. (c) ROUTE: check whether the orchestrator's compute_test_universe_fp is fired even when bs2 is invoked with a path filter — maybe a 'single shard' fastpath would skip 90% of overhead. The repro and timing both reproduce; just need a probe mechanism that actually compiles in.
close_reason: Both acceptance criteria now met. PERF (rerun <2s): already fixed by the 05yc per-file rewrite — the sharded path is the default and caches correctly, so 'bs2 test <file>' reruns are ~0.5-0.6s, NOT the 15s in the repro. OBSERVABILITY (prints '[test-cache] hit'): fixed in #550 (squash 8ff4390a) — run_test_shard_command exec'd the cached binary SILENTLY ('.Hit(_, cached_bin) -> cached_bin'); only the legacy --bundled path logged hit/miss. Gave the shard path the same symmetric logging (surfaces via aggregate_shard_logs' println). Verified: run1 '[test-cache] miss <fp> — compiler binary changed', run2 '[test-cache] hit <fp>'; fp IDENTICAL across reruns (disproves the ticket's fingerprint-instability hypothesis #1). Spec: test_runner/tests/uzs9_cache_hit_logged_test.av drives 'bs2 _test_shard' twice. Suite 3287/3287, selfhost byte-identical. Non-neutral (edits main.av) -> seed-train cycles v14.

title: [lang/test-runner] Test cycle speed — bundled compile + per-file cache + parallelism
description:
Umbrella for the test-suite speed work. Bumped to P0 — dev-cycle pain is now blocking iteration on every other epic.

## Today's measured state

- `make test` (bundled): ~360s. Dominant cost is the single-binary compile of all 2577 spec tests, not the test execution itself.
- `./build/bs2 test <single_file>`: ~15s per invocation. Cache infrastructure exists (2753 entries on disk) but doesn't hit on rerun. Identical second run with unchanged bs2 binary still takes 15s; no `[test-cache] hit` message ever prints. This was discovered while answering 'why isn't hkms fast?' — hkms shipped the cache scaffolding but the lookup path doesn't fire.
- Filter-and-isolate is the only workflow that runs in <15s right now.

## In-scope tickets (reparenting as children)

- i7gw: parallelize the bundled _test.bin compile — directly attacks the 360s. Highest leverage.
- d4jv (epic): in-process spawn/channels test runner — replaces bash worker pool, fixes per-test execution overhead. Doesn't shrink the bundled compile but improves shard-mode + future per-file mode.
- 05yc: shared @std metadata across shards (hkms.2 revisit).
- pdme.1: transitive package fingerprint propagation in cache key — currently causes false HITS not false MISSES; relevant to correctness, peripheral to speed.
- j568: /tmp paths excluded from grgg compile cache — fixture-based tests miss cache. Has known fix shape (~30 lines).
- 5mq4: build cache wastes ~24MB/slot via duplicate unit.o + unit.realobj.o — disk space, marginal speed impact.
- pdme.2: cache fp validation on every read — correctness, gates ripping out workarounds.

## New discovery filed under this umbrella

- Per-file `bs2 test` cache miss on rerun. Repro + traced state below.

## Goal (acceptance)

- `make test` bundled compile < 60s.
- `./build/bs2 test <single_file>` repro: second run <2s (cache hit).
- Per-test isolation preserved (hkms.3 invariant).
- No regression in selfhost fixed-point check.

## Coordination

i7gw + d4jv together are likely sufficient for the 60s target. The per-file cache miss bug is independent — it's a hkms.cache-lookup regression and should be a fast fix once isolated.

Filed while the bootstrap iteration loop was hitting 'run full suite → fail → grep → rerun' patterns burning minutes per round. CLAUDE.md updated alongside this epic with an anti-pattern rule.

title: [lang/test-runner] In-process parallel test runner — spawn + channels, replace bash worker pool
description:
## Problem

The test runner currently uses a shell-fork worker pool (epic e20h) to parallelise spec execution. Each shard is a separately-compiled program that bash launches as a subprocess; results are aggregated by reading subprocess stdout / exit codes.

The bootstrap has `spawn` (green threads), `Task<T, E>`, channels (`<-`), `select`, `parallel`, and structured concurrency. Zero of these features are used in the test runner — or anywhere else in the bootstrap. The most powerful concurrency surface in the spec runs zero call sites in the language's own implementation.

The result: the worker pool is bash, not Avra. Per-shard cost includes fork(), exec(), shared-library load, runtime init, RC-arena setup. The bash dance also forces the test runner to operate on compiled binaries, which means the entire "compile → link → spawn → wait → read" cycle happens N times — once per shard.

## Proposal

Replace the shell-fork worker pool with an **in-process `spawn` + channel-based test runner**. Each spec block runs as a green thread; results flow back through a channel; the driver fans in completions via `select` (so the runner can also handle SIGINT / timeout / progress events on sibling channels).

### Architecture

    fn run_test_suite(tests: List<TestProgram>, jobs: int) -> SuiteResult {
        let results_chan = Channel<TestResult>.bounded(jobs)
        let progress_chan = Channel<ProgressEvent>.unbounded()
        
        // Producer: spawn one fiber per test, capped by 
        spawn {
            parallel(jobs) {
                for test in tests {
                    let result = run_one_test(test)
                    results_chan <- result
                    progress_chan <- ProgressEvent.Done(test.name)
                }
            }
            results_chan.close()
            progress_chan.close()
        }
        
        // Consumer: fan in results + render progress
        mut tally = SuiteResult.empty()
        select {
            r <- results_chan -> tally = tally.add(r)
            p <- progress_chan -> render_progress(p)
            results_chan.closed -> break
        }
        tally
    }

### Why this is a real win, not just "use the feature for fun"

1. **Eliminates per-shard fork + exec + dynamic-link overhead.** Each shard becomes a green-thread spawn — microseconds vs milliseconds. The e20h ticket notes that test-suite wall time is dominated by startup; spawn-based execution collapses that to near-zero.

2. **Crash isolation moves from process-level to fiber-level.** Currently a SIGABRT in one shard kills only its subprocess (good); the bash driver continues. Fibers don't have that for free — a panicking fiber would tear down the whole runtime. But the existing `avra_test_run_spec_guarded` extern (test_runner/mod.av) already wraps spec bodies in a sigsetjmp checkpoint to catch fatal signals. Keep that wrapper at the per-spec level; the green-thread layer above it doesn't need to re-implement isolation.

3. **Progress UI is real-time** without file polling. Currently `emit_progress_start` / `emit_progress_done` append to a file that the parent polls every 100 ms. With a progress channel, the renderer reacts to events directly.

4. **Dogfoods the concurrency surface.** Channels / spawn / select get exercised by the language's own test runner — same way Rust's `std::sync` is exercised by rustc's test runner. Bugs in the concurrency runtime surface immediately instead of waiting for user code to hit them.

5. **Removes the bash dependency for parallel execution.** `scripts/diagnose.sh` and friends still exist for diagnostic-collection workflows, but the hot test-runner path stops shelling out.

### What stays the same

- Per-shard compilation (each test → its own .ll → .o → linked binary) still happens — the change is at the *execution* layer, not the build layer.
- Existing `avra_test_summary` / `avra_test_capture_start` / `avra_test_flush` runtime externs keep working — they're called from inside the spec body and don't care if the body is a process or a fiber.
- `avra_test_run_spec_guarded` per-spec sigsetjmp guard stays — handles SIGABRT / SIGFPE within a fiber.

## Implementation

### Phase A — minimum viable

1. Build a single per-test-suite linked binary (instead of one per shard). All specs live in one program; the runner picks which ones to run.
2. `run_test_suite(specs, jobs)` spawns `jobs` worker fibers, each pulling from a work-stealing queue of pending specs.
3. Workers push (spec_id, result) onto a results channel.
4. Main fiber reads from the channel until all workers finish, aggregating pass/fail counts.
5. Existing `avra_test_capture_*` for stdout isolation stays — already fiber-safe because it uses thread-local capture buffers (verify; may need an audit).
6. Replace the bash worker-pool script with a single `bs2 test` invocation that runs the in-process suite.

### Phase B — progress + cancellation

1. Add a progress channel emitting `Started`, `Done(pass/fail)`, `Crashed(reason)` events.
2. Use `select` in the main loop to multiplex results + progress + a SIGINT channel (clean shutdown on Ctrl-C).
3. Add per-spec timeout via `Task.race(spec_fiber, sleep(deadline))`.

### Phase C — distributed (optional, much later)

The per-shard binary indirection becomes useful again for *distributed* execution (sharding across machines). Keep the bash-spawn path as a separate driver, not the default.

## Out of scope

- **Per-spec capture isolation under fibers** — needs a careful audit. `avra_test_capture_start/stop` currently uses thread-local state; under green threads on a single OS thread, that might collapse. If so, the per-fiber capture needs an arena-per-fiber model. This is a real risk; flag it as the first thing to validate.
- **Replacing the compile-side process parallelism** — multi-module compile parallelism is a separate ticket (the "parallel per-fn codegen" one filed alongside this).

## Acceptance

- `bs2 test` runs the spec suite in one process with N fibers in parallel.
- All 2424 specs pass under the new runner.
- Wall time on the bootstrap suite drops at least 30% from current bash-worker-pool baseline (current runs take ~90s; target <60s).
- Per-spec stdout capture works correctly under fiber concurrency (no cross-contamination between simultaneous specs).
- SIGABRT / SIGFPE in one spec fiber doesn't kill sibling fibers (the existing sigsetjmp guard handles this).

## Why P2

Highest single-system win available from the concurrency surface. It dogfoods the entire spawn / channel / select / parallel / Task feature set that's currently sitting unused. Independent of all other open epics.
close_reason:
All acceptance criteria met, tested, and pushed (PR #20, 18 commits, every one gated on the full suite + selfhost fixed point).

- bs2 test runs spec units in-process across AVRA_TEST_JOBS worker threads (default: cores) — spawn + typed channels + select dogfooded in the runner itself (spec_test/runner.av)
- All 2796 specs pass under the runner; selfhost fixed point byte-identical
- Wall time: warm 39s -> 19s (-51%), cold 471s -> 334s (-29%) via batched shards (8 files/binary, striped) × in-process parallel units — exceeds the >=30% acceptance
- Per-spec stdout capture correct under concurrency BY CONSTRUCTION: println lowers through per-thread sink stacks (dup2 capture machinery deleted)
- SIGABRT/SIGFPE isolation: per-spec guards nest inside per-unit guards; sinks and file locks unwind on crash

Re-scoped during execution with owner approval: 'replace bash worker pool' was stale (e20h already did); 'one bundled binary' is OOM-dead at this scale (measured 15.2GB) — batched shards are the delivered architecture. Typed channels (channel<T>, send/recv/try_recv/close, recv -> T? null==closed+drained) and @deferred_init shipped as the supporting language features.

Eight latent compiler/runtime bugs found by the dogfooding, all root-fixed with regression specs: 256-slot intmap silent drop, two mono type-canonicalization gaps, two annotation-stripping walkers (rewrap_annotations now in core), ~60 divergent extern decls hidden by LLVM symbol renaming, conflicting-extern ICE -> F3105, single-root library-mode ownership, span-less metadata stubs.

title: test runner: parallelize the bundled _test.bin compile
description: The 'bs2 test' bundle compile (parse + lower + desugar + resolve + typeck + codegen of all *_test.av concatenated into one program) is serial. With 2254 spec tests across hundreds of files this is the dominant cold-cache cost. Two wins are possible: (1) parallel parse/lower per file before bundling — each file is independent; (2) parallel codegen-per-fn within the bundle — the codegen pass walks fns in a flat list; mono-style work could shard across goroutines via the existing e20h worker pool. Targets the user's complaint that test cycles take 3-10 min and even after grgg/rqwh caches the bundle compile dominates. Filed as a companion to il75 (bs2 test --changed), qfk7 (pre-commit gating), of94 (hardlink link cache).

title: Coverage: full LCOV output with BRDA/FN/FNDA
description:

- FN:line,name for each function
- FNDA:count,name for each function's entry counter
- DA:line,count for each line (sum of all counters on that line)
- BRDA:line,block_id,branch_id,count for each branch
- BRF/BRH totals
- LF/LH totals

This produces standard LCOV that genhtml and CI tools fully understand.

title: Coverage: branch counters for if/match/when

title: test-runner: toolchain fingerprint hashes the WHOLE bs2 binary → any main.av edit over-invalidates every shard cache (cold ~20-24min suite)
description:
## Symptom
`make test` is ~19-24 min COLD after ANY compiler-source change — even a one-line help string (observed live: PR #699's print_usage edit forced a full-suite cold recompile; the 2pps run was 19m21s dominated by all-shards recompiling). Warm it is ~19s.

## Root cause (distinct from pdme.*)
The per-shard test-binary cache key (test_runner/mod.av) is
`sha256("${toolchain_fp}:${fixture_h}:${fixture_path}:${verb}")`, and
`read_or_compute_toolchain_fp` computes
`toolchain_fp = sha256(bs2_binary : runtime.o : wrapper.o : @std.avrac-src)`.
The `bs2_binary` term is the WHOLE compiled compiler image. So any source change
that alters main.av's codegen — including a print string — changes the binary →
new toolchain_fp → EVERY shard's key changes → all shards recompile cold
(~15s/file, uzs9.1). This is OVER-invalidation.

NOTE: this is NOT pdme.1/pdme.2. Those are the per-PACKAGE build cache
(build/cache/<fp>/metadata.bin) and UNDER-invalidation (stale cache served when a
dependency changes). This is the TEST-RUNNER shard cache and the OPPOSITE
problem. Different cache, different direction — do not merge.

## Design tension (owner to decide — do NOT hack)
Conservatively, a compiler change CAN change output for any input, so invalidating
all shards is 'correct'. Two honest directions:
(A) Make the invalidation acceptable by making the recompile FAST + PARALLEL:
    i7gw (parallelize the bundled _test.bin compile) + 2pps (per-compile strlen,
    DONE) already attack this. If a cold recompile were parallel + fast, the
    over-invalidation would sting far less — possibly the pragmatic fix.
(B) Scope the fingerprint finer than 'whole binary' so codegen-irrelevant changes
    (help strings, comments, dead paths) don't invalidate shards. Hard in general
    (the compiler is a monolith; 'does this change affect THIS test file's IR' is
    undecidable), and risks UNDER-invalidation (staleness) if done wrong — the
    dangerous cache-correctness class (zp5b/fxfz/kaux/rrio). A safe partial: a
    'codegen-relevant source' fingerprint that excludes provably-non-codegen files.

## Recommendation
Pursue (A) first (i7gw + 2pps already land most of it; measure the cold suite after
i7gw). Only attempt (B) with a correctness gate (compile X with OLD toolchain,
change toolchain, confirm the shard cache correctly MISSES). Diagnosed while
landing 2pps (2026-07-10).

title: parser-built FnTyped fails a sparse .FnTyped match (blocks return-position lambda param inference; arena/enum-tag anomaly)
description:
REPRO: under the ps3t.4.5 lambda gate, compile `fn mk(n: int) -> fn(int) -> int { (x) -> x + n }`. In resolve_fn_ret (codegen/setup.av), `base = resolve_setup_vt(regs, rvt)` where rvt is the parsed return annotation. vtype_display(base) renders 'fn(int) -> int' (which ONLY the .FnTyped(params,ret) arm produces, so base IS FnTyped), yet `match base { .FnTyped(p, r) -> ..., _ -> ... }` takes the '_' arm. Same for `match rvt { .FnTyped(pp,rr) }`. vtype_fn_params(base) (ast.av, .FnTyped(p,_)) also returns []. 

CONTRAST: emit_expr_ctx_typed (codegen/mod.av) matches .FnTyped(p,_) FINE on a resolve_codegen_vtype'd FnTyped (annotated-let/struct-field threading works). And vtype_display (exhaustive match, ast.av) matches base FINE. So: a PARSER/arena-sourced FnTyped matches EXHAUSTIVE dispatch (vtype_display) and matches after resolve_codegen_vtype reconstruction, but FAILS a SPARSE '.FnTyped + _' match in resolve_fn_ret / vtype_fn_params / resolve_setup_vt. Wildcard-vs-both-named made no difference (tested .FnTyped(p,r) too). Likely an enum-tag / arena-representation inconsistency where the value's tag reads correctly under jump-table (exhaustive) dispatch but not under sparse tag-comparison dispatch — or the parser/type_expr_to_vtype-built FnTyped (ast.av:692) carries a representation that only survives a fresh reconstruction.

IMPACT: resolve_fn_ret can't recover a returned lambda's param types (drops them to Closure(-1, ret)), so ps3t.4.5 return-position lambda inference is blocked — a fn returning an un-annotated lambda (`fn f() -> fn(int)->int { (x) -> x }`) can't thread its params and currently requires an explicit annotation. This is a COMMON pattern (~15 test files). Likely also mis-fires other sparse .FnTyped matches on parser/arena values elsewhere (latent). 

FIX DIRECTION: root-cause why a parser-built FnTyped fails sparse .FnTyped dispatch (compare the emitted match IR for vtype_display vs vtype_fn_params; check arena store/load of ValueType with a List payload; check djb2 tag collision for 'FnTyped'). Once fixed, restore resolve_fn_ret to preserve FnTyped params + re-enable the return/block-tail threading (emit_expr_ctx_typed at codegen/mod.av Return + blocks.av tail).
close_reason: Root-caused and fixed: monomorphization's rewrite_fn_ret round-tripped return types through strings (vtype_render_full → vtype_from_type_string), and vtype_from_type_string had no fn(...) case, so a returned function type degraded to Struct(its-own-text) — which is why every sparse .FnTyped match misfired (the value literally carried Struct's tag, not FnTyped's; the enum-tag/arena hypothesis was a red herring). Fixed by teaching vtype_from_type_string to peel fn(params)->ret back into FnTyped (+ matching_paren helper, top_level_split_idx -> arrow hardening). Returned function types now work end-to-end (single/multi/zero-param, nested, generic, higher-order) — mutation-verified regression test fn_type_return_mono_roundtrip_test.av. The speculative 'restore resolve_fn_ret / re-enable threading' sub-instructions were premised on the wrong hypothesis and are moot: resolve_fn_ret's Closure(-1,ret) predates the bug and returned fn-types work without changing it (verified). Full suite 3941/3941, selfhost + diff-test byte-identical. Merged #726 (squash 8f0db5d0). Follow-up 424f filed for the structural fix (stop string-round-tripping compound ValueTypes in mono).

title: omitted nullable struct field reads stale arena memory (f1005_nullable_omit flakes in bundled seed-train shard)
description:
ROOT CAUSE (confirmed): emit_struct_lit (features/struct_decl/codegen.av:24) allocates the struct buffer via malloc_struct_bytes -> ctx.arena_alloc (line 45), which does NOT zero the bytes. fill_struct_fields only writes the PROVIDED field inits; an OMITTED field's slot is never written. So an omitted nullable field (`Rec { id: 7, count: 3 }` omitting nullable `note`) reads whatever was in the arena. A fresh mmap page is zero -> note==null -> pass (isolation, most runs). A REUSED arena region (bundled --per_file shard under memory pressure, e.g. seed-train-verify) holds stale non-zero bytes -> note != null -> FAIL.

SYMPTOM: packages/std-avrac/src/features/struct_decl/tests/f1005_nullable_omit_test.av:13 'the omitted nullable field defaults to null' fails deterministically in its 41-test seed-train-verify shard (2 consecutive runs on PR #695 head), while rc-strict (same suite, branch compiler) and isolation both PASS. PR #695 is byte-identical (diff-test) and does not touch f1005 -> pre-existing, exposed by shard memory reuse.

FIX OPTIONS: (a) zero the struct buffer after arena_alloc before fill_struct_fields (memset 0, fields.length*8); (b) surgically write i64 0 to each OMITTED nullable field slot in fill_struct_fields. Both are INTENDED IR CHANGES (add stores) -> land via the intended-ir-change / run-equiv path. (a) is simplest+safest (guarantees every omitted field defaults to its natural zero, matching spec 9 'omitted nullable -> null'); (b) is leaner (no cost for full literals). Prefer (a) unless perf-profiled.

BLAST: any struct literal that omits a nullable field relies on this; the flake surfaces under memory pressure so it also intermittently reds the seed train (blocks seed advancement).

title: metadata fast-path: @comptime macros can't call non-@comptime helpers (F4006) — ship comptime-reachable bodies
description: ROOT CAUSE (confirmed 2026-07-10): a cross-package @comptime macro that transitively calls a REGULAR (non-@comptime, non-generic) helper fails under the metadata fast-path (AVRA_USE_METADATA=1) with F4006 'macro returned a value the expander could not decode (kind=null)'. Witness: @std.cli.cmdgen expand_cli (@comptime, ships its body via GenericBodyEntry) calls @std.avrac synth_deref_stmt (comptime/synth.av:89 — a plain 'export fn', NOT @comptime). metadata_extract.av:407 ships bodies only when 'ships_generic || is_comptime', so synth_deref_stmt's AST is NOT carried; at comptime eval the interpreter can't run it -> null -> expand_cli degrades to null -> F4006. Works in SOURCE mode (all bodies present). This blocks main.av from consuming a cross-package @expand (vez6 Components V2 CLI); every cmdgen test uses write_fixture_and_run_no_metadata to dodge it. NOT ps3t.5/JIT's zone (the handoff diagnosis was over-conservative) — the interpreter already works; the gap is metadata not shipping the transitive comptime-reachable body closure. FIX TIERS: (a) targeted — mark the regular comptime-only helpers (synth_deref_stmt/_ids, …) @comptime so their bodies ride (small, whack-a-mole if the chain is long); (b) systemic — extend metadata_extract to ship the transitive closure of fns reachable from @comptime fns, not just @comptime fns themselves (robust, one-time; costs some metadata size). L2 JIT (link @comptime against the producer .o) is the eventual clean fix but NOT required now. VALIDATE against the 9ixv cli_metadata_compile_test regression + a minimal @expand-under-metadata repro.
close_reason: Fix merged: #729 (7deda0d1) — the close condition its original close note named ('will close on merge of #729') is now met; #728 (3a2be4b2) adds the string re-escaping + diagnostics residuals on top. Cross-package @comptime macro calls work under AVRA_USE_METADATA (cmdgen suite 54/54 through the fast-path as live regression).

comments.author: Claude
comments.text: READ-ONLY RE-INVESTIGATION (2026-07-10) — the stated root cause is LIKELY MISDIAGNOSED; verify empirically before coding. synth_deref_stmt is NOT a plain helper whose body must ship — it's a COMPTIME-ONLY IDENTITY SHIM (features/comptime/synth.av:89, body = synth_shim_unreachable, unreachable by design). features/eval/mod.av:1081 intercepts it by NAME via call_is_synth_shim (last-segment match: synth_expr_id/synth_stmt_id/synth_stmt_ids/synth_deref_expr/synth_deref_stmt/synth_deref_stmt_ids) and returns eval_shim_passthrough — the body is NEVER run, shipped or not. So 'ship synth_deref_stmt's body' fixes nothing. Traced expand_cli (cmdgen/mod.av:327): its direct callees are str_lit/config_value_or_empty/flagdef_lit/build_command_gen — ALL @comptime (bodies ship via is_comptime, line 406-407) — plus synth_deref_stmt (name-intercepted). Nothing in that chain needs an unshipped plain body. CONCLUSION: the real F4006 culprit is NOT synth_deref_stmt; it's some OTHER symbol/type not surviving the metadata roundtrip (candidate: a struct TYPE like CommandGen/CompConfigPair not decodable at comptime, or an @comptime annotation not detected by the extract walker for a private fn, or the name-intercept's last-segment match failing on the re-parsed shipped body). NEXT STEP (decisive): reproduce F4006 under AVRA_USE_METADATA=1 on a minimal cli{command...} fixture and read the ACTUAL failing symbol/kind — do NOT trust the synth_deref_stmt hypothesis. Fix tier (b) 'ship transitive closure' may be unnecessary; the true fix depends on what the repro shows. (Best done on the post-#692 merged base; the @std metadata prebuild can OOM at 16GB — snw0.)

comments.author: Claude
comments.text:
DEFINITIVE DIAGNOSIS (empirical, 2026-07-11) — the stated root cause AND the 2026-07-10 re-investigation were BOTH wrong. Reproduced F4006 under AVRA_USE_METADATA=1 on a minimal cli{command{fn run}} fixture (write_fixture_and_run keeps metadata on). Traced with instrumentation at 4 layers:
(1) NO helper is called with an empty body (eval_call probe silent) — so 'private @comptime body not shipped' is FALSE.
(2) The EXPORTED macros themselves (expand_cli, expand_command) have body_len=0 at invocation (eval_fn_with_resolved_args in expand_macro.av).
(3) synth_fn_decl DOES see them: is_comptime=true, body_src_len=2304/171 — the bodies SHIP fine in @std.cli's metadata and are stashed via avra_lazy_comptime_set.
(4) comptime_lookup_lazy: has=1, src_len=2304, idx_has=1, but parse_body_source(source) returns parsed_body_len=0. => THE FMT->PARSE ROUND-TRIP FAILS.
ROOT CAUSE: fmt_stmt_ids renders the RESOLVED body with '::'-qualified names that the parser rejects. The dumped expand_command body: 'let no_global_defs: List<@std::avrac::core::ExprId> = []  return @std::cli::cmdgen::build_command_gen(s, no_globals, no_global_defs).decls'. Isolated: (a) EXPRESSION position '@std::cli::cmdgen::build_command_gen(...)' => F0040 (parser wants '.' not '::'; '@std.cli.cmdgen.build_command_gen(...)' parses fine); (b) TYPE-ARG position 'List<@std::avrac::core::ExprId>' => F0001 'expected generic type argument' — the type-arg parser rejects a qualified name ENTIRELY, even with dots. So any cross-package @comptime body that mentions a qualified cross-package fn call or a qualified type-arg fails to re-parse -> empty body -> macro returns null -> F4006. This is the SAME root cause as znl0 ('library-authored macros eval to null when the package is stubbed'). type_short_name (9p1d) round-trips fine only because its body has no qualified refs. FIX DIRECTION: make the fmt->parse round-trip total for qualified names — the parser must accept the fully-qualified forms fmt emits in BOTH expression and type-argument positions (or fmt must emit re-parseable forms + the type-arg parser must accept qualified names). Repro: packages/std-cli/src/cmdgen/tests/pqc9_repro_test.av (temp, to be replaced by a proper regression). Memory stayed clean throughout (single-file metadata compile, no OOM).

comments.author: Claude
comments.text:
FIX IN PROGRESS — the full fix is MULTI-LAYER (render->parse->eval round-trip fidelity for cross-package @comptime bodies). Layer 1 (PARSE round-trip) DONE + committed as groundwork on claude/ps3t-bead-pr-tjzo4c (pqc9 stays OPEN, no PR yet). It advanced the failure from kind=null (body re-parsed to empty) to kind=list (body now executes fully). The 4 parser rules added (parse/mod.av, all byte-identical to selfhost since no compiler src uses the syntax; 111/111 parse tests green; new regression parse/tests/qualified_name_roundtrip_test.av):
  (1) parse_qualified_at_name() helper: reads @pkg::mod::name (:: = two Colon tokens) into the canonical ::-joined string.
  (2) parse_primary: @-qualified name -> Expr.QualifiedIdent (eval resolves it by full path, so a rehydrated body needs no re-resolve).
  (3) parse_primary: @qualified { fields } -> Expr.StructLit(qname, ...) (mirrors the bare-ident struct-lit path).
  (4) parse_type_atom: @qualified -> TypeExpr.Named(qname) (covers List<@std::...::ExprId> type-args + top-level annotations).
  (5) peek_after_at_is_qualified() + parse_declaration gate: a statement-start @pkg::mod::name (a tail-return of a resolved name) routes to expression parsing, NOT annotation parsing.
REMAINING LAYERS (next tick, same branch):
  Layer 2 (ENUM-CTOR round-trip): the returned decls are enum Values with enum_variant=TypeDecl but enum_type="" (EMPTY) -> value_to_stmt decode fails 'not a Stmt' -> F4006 kind=list. fmt renders a resolved EnumCtor (e.g. Stmt.TypeDecl(args)) in a form that loses the qualified enum TYPE on re-parse; eval_enum_ctor then builds enum_type="". Fix: fmt must render the ctor's qualified type (@std::avrac::core::Stmt.TypeDecl(args)) AND the parser/eval must reconstruct enum_type from it (a @qualified.Variant(args) postfix -> EnumCtor with the qualified type). Verify with value_to_stmt's enum_type=="@std::avrac::core::Stmt" check (eval/mod.av enum_value_to_expr:2409 is the sibling for Expr).
  Layer 3 (possible): re-run the metadata repro after Layer 2 — there may be further render/parse/eval fidelity gaps (the whack-a-mole the ticket warned about). title: fmt drops Stmt/Expr prefix on AST-ctor calls → @comptime macro bodies corrupt through the metadata fast-path (F4006)
description:
SYMPTOM
A consumer that @expand's a cross-package @comptime macro built with DIRECT AST
construction (Expr.X(...)/Stmt.X(...)) compiles fine in SOURCE mode but fails
under the metadata fast-path (AVRA_USE_METADATA=1):

  error[F4006]: @expand(@std::cli::cmdgen::expand_cli) — macro returned a value
  the expander could not decode into a Stmt/List<Stmt>/ResolvedDecls (kind=null)

First hit by vez6.12 (migrating packages/cli/src/main.av onto the declarative
Components V2 App via @expand(expand_cli)). main.av must compile via the
metadata fast-path (tests/cli_metadata_compile_test.av, the 9ixv regression),
so this BLOCKS vez6.12.

MINIMAL REPRO
  1. cd packages/std-avrac && ../../build/bs2 build --lib --emit_metadata
  2. AVRA_USE_METADATA=1 ./build/bs2 compile <file using @expand(expand_cli)>
  Source mode (no AVRA_USE_METADATA) compiles the same file cleanly.

ROOT CAUSE (confirmed by inspecting the emitted unit.meta.bin)
The 9p1d mechanism ships @comptime fn bodies as fmt-rendered source
(metadata_extract.av: `source: fmt_stmt_ids(...)`), re-parsed lazily on @expand
(metadata_synthesize.av: avra_lazy_comptime_set). derive_walker works through
this because quote-lowered AST goes via lower.av. But cmdgen uses DIRECT AST
construction (forced by rmzs, which blocks quote/splice), and fmt renders those
enum-constructor calls in SUBJECTLESS form, dropping the AST-type prefix:

  original cmdgen source        fmt-rendered in meta.bin
  --------------------------    -------------------------
  Stmt.Let(inst, vt, lit)       .Let(inst, vt, lit)
  Expr.StructLit("...", [...])  .StructLit("...", [...])
  Expr.ListLit(sub_lits)        .ListLit(sub_lits)

On re-parse+re-eval the subjectless .StructLit/.ListLit collide with the
evaluator's fwyx special-casing (features/eval/mod.av eval_expr:
`.StructLit(type_name, inits) -> eval_struct_lit(...)`, `.ListLit -> eval_list_lit`)
— they evaluate as ACTUAL struct/list literals instead of constructing the
Expr/Stmt AST node the macro intended. The macro result is corrupted -> null
-> F4006.

FIX DIRECTION (owner: ps3t.5 / metadata+comptime infra — NOT vez6 zone)
Either:
 (a) fmt must render enum-ctor calls on the AST types WITH their Stmt/Expr
     prefix (round-trip fidelity for @comptime-body serialization), OR
 (b) the metadata @comptime-body path must preserve the qualified ctor so the
     re-eval builds the AST node, not a literal, OR
 (c) land the rmzs quote/splice fix so cmdgen can use quote (lower.av path,
     which already round-trips).

vez6 stays a pure consumer; handing off rather than patching features/* inline.
close_reason: Duplicate of znl0 (same bug: library-authored @comptime macro evaluates to null through the metadata fast-path). Refined root cause (fmt subjectless enum-ctor rendering) ported to znl0 as a comment.

title: Extend std-cli App parser (space-separated options + flag aliases) to unblock main.av single app.run()
description:
vez6.12 migrated the user-facing avra commands onto the declarative Components V2 App (app.run() dispatch reading CliResult). The compiler-internal commands (build, test, docs, lang, clean, cache, lsp, _test_shard) could NOT be collapsed into app.run() and remain behind an explicit raw-argv guard in main() because App's parse_tokens (packages/std-cli/src/cli.av) does not model the argv shapes they use:

1. Space-separated options: parse_tokens only accepts --key=value; the bespoke parsers (parse_docs_args via read_kv_value, etc.) also accept '--key value' (two tokens). e.g. 'avra docs --search foo'.
2. Word aliases: '--used-by' as an alias for '--callers' (docs); a flat FlagDef has no alias list.
3. Option-form flag aliases: '--message-format=json' as an alias for the 'json' flag (build).

Routing the complex commands through app.run() as-is rejects valid invocations — notably 'avra build --lib --emit_metadata', used by the test runner's std-avrac prebuild — so the guard is load-bearing until this lands.

SCOPE:
- parse_tokens: support '--key value' space-separated options (convert the for-loop to an indexed while-loop that can consume the next token as the option value). Add cmdgen/cli spec tests for both '--key=value' and '--key value'.
- Add an alias mechanism to FlagDef/OptionDef (or a per-command alias map) so '--used-by'->callers and '--message-format=json'->json parse without phantom schema entries.
- Then complete the 7 complex commands' schemas, remove the main() guard, and (the deeper vez6.12 target) convert their handlers to read from CliResult, deleting parse_*_args/run_*_command raw-argv scanning.

DISCIPLINE: std-cli + main.av + vez6 tests only. Pure consumer of the comptime surface; do NOT touch features/eval or features/comptime.

Blocks: vez6.12 full completion (single app.run(), delete all helpers).

title: codegen: dyn Trait struct fields must box concrete values (966j struct-field analog) — FIXED
notes: FIXED in commit 4c804843 (PR #669). A dyn Trait STRUCT FIELD initialised or assigned with a concrete value stored the raw struct ptr instead of a boxed trait object (value+vtable); a later field.method() read a garbage/OOB vtable, surfacing for List<{...,f: dyn T}> as 'index on null list' (the null = bogus vtable). Root-caused via IR: emit_struct_lit's generic field-store arm + emit_field_assign stored r.value raw for dyn fields, unlike the List<dyn> arm (966j) and the arg-passing path (fill_arg_array_boxing) which box. Fix: both paths now box a concrete value into a bare dyn Trait field (box_for_trait), passing through already-boxed dyn values (empty concrete name). Test: features/struct_decl/tests/dyn_field_boxing_test.av (5/5): bare field, list dispatch, sibling direct-access field, reassignment, dyn->dyn passthrough. Byte-identical (pattern absent from selfhost+corpus). UNBLOCKS the vez6.11 CLI redesign: Subcommand { meta: CommandSpec, body: dyn Runnable } (data+behavior split -> direct field access + 1-method Runnable trait). Found while designing world-class CLI DX with the user.

title: Struct-literal field of type List<dyn Trait> does not box its element struct-literals — runtime segfault on dispatch
description:
A struct literal whose field has type List<dyn Trait>, initialized with an inline list of concrete struct literals, does NOT box the elements to dyn — the concrete structs are stored raw, so a later trait-method call reads a garbage vtable and segfaults (null ptr deref at a tiny address, e.g. 0x13).

ISOLATED (pure language, no macros; @std.cli.Runnable):
  type CliV2 = { name: string, commands: List<dyn Runnable> }
  let c = CliV2 { name: "avra", commands: [Foo { name: "build", code: 11 }, Bar { ... }] }
  for cmd in c.commands { cmd.name() }   // SEGV: 'null pointer dereference (accessed address 0x13)'

The expected-type propagation for a struct FIELD init does not reach into the list-literal's elements to trigger dyn-boxing. The let-annotation path DOES:
  let cmds: List<dyn Runnable> = [Foo { ... }, Bar { ... }]   // boxes correctly, dispatch works
  let c = CliV2 { name: "avra", commands: cmds }              // assigning a pre-boxed list to the field also works

So the gap is specifically struct-field-init -> list-literal-element dyn coercion (codegen/typeck expected-type threading); the single-value field/let box (let x: dyn T = Foo{}) and the list-annotated let both work.

IMPACT: blocks the design's canonical Components V2 dispatch literal (docs §4.3 ). vez6.11 expand_cli sidesteps it by emitting the pre-boxed-let form ( then ) — a correct alternative, not a hack — but the inline field form must box for hand-written code (design §4.5 escape hatch) and for parity with the let form. Fix: thread the field's declared element type as the expected type into list-literal element emission (mirror the let-annotation path's dyn coercion).

Found-by: vez6.11 (Components V2 dispatch). Related: vez6.11, vez6.8 (per-instance subtype gen).
close_reason: Fixed upstream by #678 (ece0691) — struct-literal List<dyn Trait> field now boxes its inline element literals. Verified on the rebased base (inline CliV2 { commands: [Foo{}, …] } dispatches; no SEGV). vez6.11 expand_cli simplified to the inline form (dropped the pre-boxed-let workaround), commit b9ec3e0.

title: enum_value_to_expr String decode double-wraps parser-form string literals (macro-carried/constructed strings gain a quote pair)
description:
features/eval/mod.av enum_value_to_expr decoded the String variant as Expr.String("\"${head.text}\"") — wrapping head.text in a SECOND quote pair. Every sibling leaf (Number/Bool/Ident/QualifiedIdent/FloatLit) decodes via head.text DIRECTLY; String was the lone exception.

The macro-boundary encode (quote_expr/lower.av construct_expr:472 -> string_arg -> eval) preserves the parser-form Expr.String value (WITH its outer quotes) in head.text — faithful, matching how Number/Bool carry their raw value. So the decode's extra wrap double-quoted: a carried/constructed "X" round-tripped to "\"X\"", which codegen strip_quotes reduced to "X" (one pair) at RUNTIME. Any string a macro carries (user run body via synth_deref) or constructs (Expr.String) printed WITH surrounding quotes.

Exposed by vez6.11 expand_command: the first macro to read + re-emit user statements (the ytwb read path) containing string literals, and the first to construct Cli/flag-name string literals. Hard blocker for all Components V2 macro string output.

FIX (applied on claude/vez6-bead-structures-ye68a0): enum_value_to_expr String arm -> .Ok(Expr.String(head.text)) (use directly, uniform with Number/Bool/Ident). Validated: comptime 100/100, marshal/derive 47/47, quote_expr 13/14 (the one failure, quote_iteration_splice, was ASSERTING the double-quote bug — updated to assert the corrected unquoted output). New regression specs: synth_deref_string_roundtrip_test (carried literal) + the corrected quote_iteration_splice (quote-constructed literal). Selfhost + diff-test pending.

COORDINATION: this edits features/eval/mod.av (ps3t.5's L2-interpreter zone). It is a 1-line correctness fix to the LEGACY structured decoder (the path value_for_stmt is slated to replace), not an architectural change — trivially reconcilable with the L2 rewrite. Direct continuation of ytwb (macro AST read/re-emit correctness). Related: ytwb, vez6.11, ps3t.5, nlnd.
close_reason: Fixed upstream by #677 (2fc4ced) — enum_value_to_expr decodes String via head.text directly, no second quote pair. Verified: my branch's macro-carried/constructed strings round-trip unquoted on the rebased base; synth_deref_string_roundtrip_test (complementary regression) ships in #669.
