title: [ci] shard-compile bug: file-local newtype NodeRef in arm_let_no_leak_into_sibling_test unresolved when batched — 'undefined enum type' reddens seed-train-verify (deterministic, 4m1e class)
description:
CI seed-train-verify + rc-strict on PR #669 (c384127) both red on the SAME shard-compile failure: "codegen error: undefined enum type arm_let_no_leak_into_sibling_test::NodeRef". Not a test FAIL — the whole shard fails to COMPILE.

File: packages/std-avrac/src/features/match_expr/tests/arm_let_no_leak_into_sibling_test.av. It declares a file-local `type NodeRef = int` newtype and uses it as an enum-variant payload. When the test runner batches this file into a shard with 7 unrelated files (content_hash_test, desugar/assert_test, union_type_example_test, break_list_assign_test, drop_trait_test, link_objects_test, stress_maps_test), codegen cannot resolve NodeRef as a type in the batched unit → "undefined enum type ...::NodeRef", shard compile fails, job red.

PRE-EXISTING + unrelated to #669's code (ytwb/0o7e, all in std-cli, passed cleanly in fully-passing shards in both jobs). SURFACED by #669 adding test files, which shifted the runner's shard batching so arm_let_no_leak_into_sibling_test landed in this triggering batch — the 4m1e 'adding a test file flips batch composition' class. DETERMINISTIC given the batch (unlike the f1005 order-flake wi2l), so a CI re-run will NOT clear it.

ROOT CAUSE shape: a test-file-local newtype/enum type isn't resolved across the batched @deferred_init shard unit — likely the type registry / codegen not seeing the per-file type decl when multiple files are compiled into one shard binary. FIX: features/match_expr + codegen (type resolution across batched shard units), OR make shard batching not co-compile files whose file-local types collide/leak. Outside vez6's pure-consumer scope. RELATED: 4m1e (batch-composition fragility), wi2l (the f1005 order-flake), i7gw/uzs9 (test-runner sharding).
close_reason: Fixed: resolve_type_in_ctx now consults the file's own use-alias before the global item index, so an explicit import wins over a colliding sibling file-local type. Merged in #676 (squash 33bc0cb3). CI fully green (rc-strict + seed-train-verify passed cleanly — the batched-shard flake is gone). Regression test + mutation-verified + diff-test byte-identical. Residual (unimported bare cross-module ref) filed as xozi.

comments.author: Claude
comments.text:
REPRODUCED + MINIMIZED (2026-07-09, deterministic 2-file repro). Batch `arm_let_no_leak_into_sibling_test.av` + `content_hash_test.av` into one shard → 'codegen error: undefined enum type arm_let_no_leak_into_sibling_test::NodeRef', shard fails to COMPILE. content_hash_test is the ESSENTIAL second file (arm_let + union_type_example_test does NOT trigger it). Local repro: cp both into a scratch dir, run bs2 test <dir>.

TRIGGER refined: arm_let declares a FILE-LOCAL 'type NodeRef = int' newtype used as an enum-variant payload (enum RefNode { Ref(value: NodeRef) }). content_hash_test imports + USES core's NodeRef ENUM (@std.avrac.core NodeRef). NOTE: a bare 'use @std.avrac.core.{NodeRef}' in a sibling file does NOT trigger it (tested) — content_hash_test's actual USE of the core NodeRef enum is what registers it such that the collision surfaces. When both are co-compiled into one @deferred_init shard binary, the codegen resolves arm_let's 'NodeRef' enum-payload reference as an ENUM in the arm_let file namespace and fails (arm_let's NodeRef is a NEWTYPE, not an enum) — the file-local newtype is shadowed/leaked by core's same-named enum in the shared shard type registry (the TYPE analog of zo1a's fn/local leakage).

ROOT-CAUSE AREA: the batched-shard type registration doesn't scope file-local type decls per-file — a same-named type in another batched file collides. FIX (proper, rule 4/16): scope file-local types per-file within a shard unit (like modules), so arm_let's newtype NodeRef and core's enum NodeRef don't collide. Emission site: grep 'undefined enum type' in codegen. NEXT: branch off integration (NOT off an existing feature branch), diagnose the enum-type resolution using the batched shard's per-file namespace, fix the scoping.

comments.author: Claude
comments.text: FIX UP as PR #676 (branch claude/xvv5-file-local-type-scope-shard, off integration 14be83e1). ROOT CAUSE differed from this ticket's hypothesis. Actual: the IMPORTING file mis-resolves. content_hash_test imports core's NodeRef ENUM and builds NodeRef.ExprRef(..); resolve_type_in_ctx consulted the resolver's flat first-write-wins GLOBAL item index BEFORE content_hash's own use-alias, so NodeRef resolved to arm_let's file-local newtype (which won the global slot) instead of the imported enum -> 'undefined enum type arm_let::NodeRef' at codegen. FIX: reorder resolve_type_in_ctx to consult the file's use-alias before the global index. arm_let stays correct via the earlier local-declaration lookup. Byte-identical diff-test PASS; deterministic 2-file repro now 20/20; regression test committed + mutation-verified. Residual (unimported bare cross-module ref) -> filed xozi (P3). Close on merge.

title: comptime foundation gaps block library-authored macros (vez6.11 expand_command): repeating-splice + computed-splice → F4006, sequential @comptime helper calls → F4005
description:
Building vez6.11's expand_command as pure-consumer std-cli macro code hit THREE comptime-foundation gaps (features/eval, features/quote_expr, core/registry — outside vez6's pure-consumer scope; overlaps ps3t.5's L2 comptime rewrite). Each independently blocks the design's §4.2 expand_command. Verified 2026-07-09 via bs2 expand.

GAP 1 — repeating statement-splice unimplemented (F4006). `quote stmt { fn f() { ~body } }` where body: List<Stmt> → 'error[F4006]: macro returned a value the expander could not decode (kind=enum/list)'. Design §3.4 explicitly claims '~list_value | Repeating slot (statement-list) | Each element spliced in turn' — NOT implemented. The design's expand_command relies on it: `fn run(...) { ~bindings  ~user_run }`.

GAP 2 — computed-value splice into an expression slot (F4006). `quote stmt { println(~("PREFIX-" + kind)) }` (splicing a runtime-computed string into an expr position) → F4006. Only a bound bare identifier splices cleanly (e.g. `~tn` into a type-name/impl-target position works — vez6.4.4). Design §3.4 '~(expr) | Any slot | evaluated at expansion' — not honored for expression slots.

GAP 3 — comptime evaluator 'no eval_expr handler' (F4005) on sequential list-building @comptime helper calls. A macro that calls comp_children(s,\"flag\") AND comp_method_body(s,\"run\") (each returns List, each does a for-loop + push + synth_deref_stmt) → 'error[F4005]: macro evaluation failed: no eval_expr handler' (core/registry.av:88 eval-noop fallback — registry dispatch found no handler). EACH helper works ALONE (verified); the PAIR fails. Looks like evaluator state/dispatch corruption across two sequential list-returning helper calls.

WHAT WORKS (shipped/tested): synth_deref_* read shims (ytwb, #669); comp_children + comp_instance_name (@std.cli.introspect, tested cross-module on the source build); quote of a type + impl skeleton with a bound-identifier name splice (`type ~tn`, `impl Runnable for ~tn`), including a computed-then-bound name; multi-decl return via `quote stmts { type... impl... }`; direct AST construction is the proven body pattern (derive_walker builds fns via Stmt.Function(..., synth_stmt_ids(body)), NOT quote-splice).

IMPACT: vez6.11's expand_command / expand_cli CANNOT be completed as pure-consumer std-cli code on the current comptime foundation. It needs foundation work — splice completeness (repeating + computed) + evaluator robustness (multi-helper dispatch) — which is compiler work overlapping ps3t.5 (L2 comptime interpreter→JIT rewrite). Options: (a) fix these three gaps in features/eval + features/quote_expr (comptime-foundation owner / ps3t.5); or (b) rebuild expand_command entirely via DIRECT AST construction (derive_walker style — bypasses splice AND avoids the multi-helper quote path), which MIGHT sidestep gaps 1-2 but still risks gap 3's eval fragility. Recommend the foundation fixes; they unblock all library-authored macros (the whole vez6 premise), not just cli.

BLOCKS: vez6.11, vez6.12. RELATED: ps3t.5 (L2).
close_reason: Closed

comments.author: Claude
comments.text:
OUTLOOK UPGRADE (2026-07-09): the 3 gaps are AVOIDABLE in pure-consumer std-cli code, so expand_command is NOT hard-blocked — it needs a different construction strategy than the design's quote-splice:
- Gap 3 (eval F4005 on two sequential list-building helper calls) is avoided by reading everything in ONE body-walk: a single helper (or inline pass) that collects instance name + flag/arg children + the run fn body in a single  loop. VERIFIED: a macro doing one walk reading BOTH flag count AND run-body length expands cleanly (SINGLEWALK-OK), where calling comp_children + comp_method_body sequentially hit F4005.
- Gaps 1-2 (splice) are avoided by DIRECT AST construction (Stmt.TypeDecl + Stmt.Impl + Stmt.Function(..., synth_stmt_ids(body))), the derive_walker pattern — no ~body / ~(computed) splice; only the bound-identifier name splice (which works) or direct name fields.
NEXT: (1) verify direct Stmt.Impl construction in a macro (derive_walker builds a fn, not an impl — confirm the Impl ctor path). (2) build expand_command: single-walk read → direct-construct  +  with flag/arg lets prepended to the run body. Still worth fixing the gaps properly (rmzs stays open, P1) so the ergonomic design §4.2 quote-splice form works, but vez6.11 can proceed now via this construction strategy.

comments.author: Claude
comments.text:
NOW ON THE vez6.12 CRITICAL PATH (via znl0). Landing rmzs (computed/repeating splice, F4006) is the CLEAN way to unblock the declarative main.av CLI:

cmdgen (@std.cli.cmdgen expand_cli/expand_command) is forced to build the App by DIRECT AST construction (Expr.StructLit(...), Stmt.Let(...)) ONLY because rmzs blocks quote/splice. Direct construction is exactly what does not survive the @comptime-body metadata round-trip (znl0): fmt serializes the ctor subjectless, it re-parses as a struct literal, the macro returns null -> F4006. derive_walker works precisely because it uses quote -> quote-lowered AST rides lower.av, which round-trips.

So: land rmzs -> cmdgen switches expand_cli/expand_command to quote/splice -> znl0 becomes moot -> the beautiful declarative main.av flip (vez6.12) lands.

ALTERNATIVE (if rmzs is far off): fix znl0 directly -- the two-layer core patch is fully diagnosed on the znl0 ticket (fmt/mod.av:47 render the type qualifier + the parser recognizing a qualified `@...::Expr.StructLit(...)` as an EnumCtor; multi-path parse work).

Both live in features/eval/parse/fmt = ps3t.5 zone. vez6 has shipped all consumer-side value (2 PRs merged) and is a pure consumer here -- handing off. This + znl0 are the P1 lever for the vez6.12 goal.

comments.author: Claude
comments.text:
GROUND TRUTH re-verified on integration v149 (4ccfd76d), fresh bs2:
- GAP 3 (F4005 'no eval_expr handler' on sequential list-returning @comptime helper calls): **FIXED**. Minimal repro — two @comptime fns each returning List<StmtId> built via a for-loop+push, a build() that calls BOTH sequentially and concatenates, @expand(build) — COMPILES exit 0 and expands correctly (both helpers' stmts present). The evaluator dispatch corruption is gone (later ps3t.5.x eval work). GAP 3 no longer reproduces.
- GAP 1 (repeating statement-splice: quote stmt { fn f() { ~body } }, body: List<Stmt>): still FAILS — error[F4006] 'could not decode ... (kind=enum)'.
- GAP 2 (computed splice into expr slot: quote stmt { println(~("PREFIX-" + kind)) }): still FAILS — same error[F4006] kind=enum.
Both remaining gaps fail IDENTICALLY (F4006 kind=enum) → likely a SHARED quote-lowering root: the ~splice in these positions lowers to a value the expander can't decode into a Stmt. Investigating quote_expr/lower.av splice lowering. Repros: /tmp/rmzs_gap1.av, /tmp/rmzs_gap2.av.

comments.author: Claude
comments.text: GAP 1 FIXED — PR #722 opened (https://github.com/tristanMatthias/forge-lang/pull/722). construct_stmt_ids now flattens a bare ~list statement's List<Stmt> target into the enclosing block via list_concat (the statement-list analogue of the match-arm ~arms splice; new helper bare_stmt_splice_target). Test quote_stmt_list_splice_test.av: basic flatten in-order + non-splice stmts preserved on both sides (segment handling) + empty-list splice — 3/3, mutation-verified (disable detection → all 3 FAIL). Full validation: make test 3920+/selfhost byte-identical (657947 lines); diff-test BYTE-IDENTICAL (selfhost 657723 + corpus, EXIT=0) — NOT an intended-IR-change (splice bodies were F4006-failing before, so no valid program's IR changes; no-splice path is byte-identical). Status: GAP 3 already-fixed, GAP 1 this PR, GAP 2 (computed value→expr-slot splice) remains — rmzs stays OPEN until GAP 2 lands. No CodeRabbit config on repo (per #719/#721); merge on green CI.

comments.author: Claude
comments.text: GAP 2 PLAN (computed value-splice into an EXPR slot, e.g. quote stmt { println(~("PREFIX-" + kind)) }). ROOT: construct_expr's .Splice arm (lower.av:519) pastes the raw target, so in an expr-ID position the arg becomes synth_expr_id(<string value>) — a scalar where an Expr AST node is required → the Call's arg slot holds a string → @expand decode fails F4006 kind=enum. FIX (3 parts): (1) new shim synth_coerce_expr(v) in features/comptime/synth.av (unreachable body like the other synth_* shims); (2) eval intercept in features/eval/mod.av (alongside call_is_synth_shim/eval_shim_passthrough, ~line 1550) that COERCES the arg value to an Expr — passthrough if already Expr/ExprId, else wrap a scalar (string→Expr.String, int→Expr.Number, float→Expr.FloatLit, bool→Expr.Bool) into a literal Expr node (reuse value_to_expr where possible); (3) lower.av: route EXPR-position splices through synth_coerce_expr (in construct_expr_id, or a splice-aware branch) instead of pasting raw — name-position (name_or_splice) and stmt-list-position (GAP1 bare_stmt_splice_target) already handled separately, so scope this to expr-id contexts only. Design decision (mine): ~(expr) in expr slot splices the VALUE as a literal (the design §3.4 'evaluated at expansion' intent); an already-AST value passes through unchanged (byte-identical to today's ~ident). Do AFTER PR #722 (GAP1) merges — same file (lower.av), keep PRs focused.

comments.author: Claude
comments.text: GAP 2 ATTEMPT REVERTED — key finding for the next attempt. Tried the decoder-level fix: value_to_expr_node (features/eval/mod.av) coerces a scalar Value (number/string/bool/null) to the matching literal Expr before enum_value_to_expr. It WORKED for the splice cases (string/int/float/bool all folded correctly, 4/4 unit tests + mutation-verified) BUT broke the full gate: 18x 'non-exhaustive match in @std::avrac::core::ValueType__all_children_spanned' + 6x Expr__all_children_spanned, across many shards (walker_list_self_test etc.). ROOT CAUSE (confirmed by revert→pass in isolation): the @derive(Walker) macros DEPEND on value_to_expr_node ERRORING on a scalar Value as a 'this field is a leaf scalar, NOT a walkable AST child' signal — my coercion makes those scalars SUCCEED as spurious literal Exprs, corrupting the generated walker's match arms. So the coercion must NOT live in the general decoder. CORRECT SCOPE: splice-site only. Candidate approaches, in preference order: (a) coerce in synth_expr_id's EVAL INTERCEPT (features/eval call_is_synth_shim/eval_shim_passthrough) — synth_expr_id wraps every expr-child in construct_expr_id; normal children are kind=expr (passthrough), only a splice hands it a scalar, so coercing scalars there is splice-scoped and does NOT touch value_to_expr_node → derive unaffected. VERIFY FIRST that no synth_expr_id caller legitimately passes a scalar expecting the identity (grep uses; the derive uses value_to_expr_node not synth_expr_id, so likely safe). (b) a dedicated synth_coerce_expr shim wrapping ONLY expr-position splices in lower.av — needs the heterogeneous-arg typing solved (union param string|int|bool|Expr, or verify the by-name eval intercept survives a generic call). GAP 2 stays OPEN; unit test preserved at scratchpad/gap2_test_preserved.av. GAP 1 (#722) + GAP 3 remain done.

comments.author: Claude
comments.text: GAP 2 FIXED (correct approach) — PR #723 (https://github.com/tristanMatthias/forge-lang/pull/723). After the decoder approach broke @derive(Walker), moved the coercion to synth_expr_id's EVAL INTERCEPT (the CONSTRUCTION path): only an expr-position splice hands that shim a scalar (normal construction yields Expr-enum values), so scalars coerce to boxed Expr literals there while the decoder (value_to_expr_node) stays untouched → derive's scalar-error signal preserved. Validated: GAP2 test 4/4 (string/int/float/bool, float assertion strengthened to a distinctive marker after the mutation check caught a loose 'contains(4)'), mutation-verified; WALKER SUITE GREEN (18/18+14/14+32/32, the decoder-approach regression absent); diff-test BYTE-IDENTICAL (selfhost 657947 + corpus, EXIT=0) → not an intended-IR-change. The full 'make test' had ONE unrelated failure — comptime_loop_budget_test (pre-existing comptime-ceiling global-state ordering flake, filed o092): passes in isolation AND bundled with the GAP2 test, so orthogonal to this change. rmzs is now COMPLETE pending #723 merge (GAP 3 already fixed, GAP 1 #722 merged, GAP 2 #723).

comments.text: DONE + MERGED. All three comptime-foundation gaps resolved: GAP 3 (sequential @comptime helper calls → F4005) already fixed by later ps3t.5.x eval work; GAP 1 (repeating statement-splice ~list) #722 merged; GAP 2 (computed value-splice into an expr slot) #723 merged (6a7b9776). GAP 3 ROOT CAUSE (v151, empirical 11-probe matrix): F4005 fires iff a match-arm wildcard body `_ -> {}` EXECUTES inside a @comptime fn — bare {} parses as an EMPTY MAP LITERAL and map_lit_feature had NO eval_expr (noop). title: build/metadata: cross-package @comptime bodies unavailable in the metadata-stub path — library-authored macros (std-cli) eval to null when the package is stubbed
description:
Cross-package @comptime bodies are unavailable in the metadata-stubbed build path — a library-authored @comptime macro/helper in @std/cli (or any non-compiler package) evaluates to null when that package is stubbed to symbols-only.

DISCOVERED 2026-07-09 building 0o7e (comp_children in @std.cli.introspect). Symptom: a fixture whose @comptime macro calls @std.cli.introspect.comp_children fails under the test runner with F4005 'eval error: field access on non-struct value (kind=null)' — comp_children returned null. Root cause: the test shard runs with AVRA_USE_METADATA=1 + AVRA_LIB_OBJS pointing at pre-built std producers; std-cli is stubbed to symbols-only, so the comptime interpreter has no @comptime fn BODY to run for a cross-package call. The SAME fixture compiled from source (clean env, `bs2 expand`) expands correctly. The 0o7e helpers test works around it by clearing the metadata env vars so the fixture compiles from source (~20s each).

This is the design's §6 open question 'cross-package macros' made concrete (docs/2026_05_08_COMPONENTS_V2_DESIGN.md). It matters because it gates whether vez6.11's library-authored expand_command/expand_cli (living in @std/cli) work when a CONSUMER build (vez6.12 main.av, or any user CLI) is built via the metadata/manifest fast-path rather than whole-program source.

INVESTIGATE + DECIDE:
1. Does the canonical vez6.12 build of packages/cli/src/main.av use the metadata path? If yes, it hits this and vez6.11/.12 are blocked until fixed.
2. Fix direction: the build metadata (meta.bin) must carry @comptime fn BODIES (not just symbols) for any package exporting @comptime fns, so a stubbed dependency can still be evaluated at a consumer's comptime. LOCATION: build metadata extract/synthesize (features/build) — compiler infra, OUTSIDE vez6's pure-consumer scope. Hand to the build/metadata owner (relates to snw0/08ro/pdme metadata fast-path).

Until resolved, cross-package @comptime macro tests must source-compile (slow); library macros are only guaranteed on whole-program-source builds.
close_reason: DONE + MERGED across the PR pair: #729 (7deda0d1) landed the shared core (qualified-name parsing in expr/type positions, enum-ctor qualifier in fmt, cross-pkg metadata test) and #728 (squash 3a2be4b2) landed the residuals — fmt string re-escaping (fmt_string_lit), loud rehydration-failure diagnostic in invoke_macro, hardened parse_qualified_at_name (strict adjacent-::, validated segments, >=1 ::, bounds-guarded lookahead), qualified generic/optional type forms, retirement of all 15 std-cli test workarounds (cmdgen 54/54 through the metadata fast-path), qualified_path_ctor_test, design doc §6 resolved. Cross-package @comptime bodies now round-trip fmt->parse->eval under the metadata stub path. Residual follow-ups tracked: jikf (helper-level rehydration diagnostics), 424f (systemic: stop string round-tripping), swjz (typeck f-shadowing found en route).

comments.author: Claude
comments.text: CORRECTION / downgraded P1→P2 — NOT a vez6.11/.12 blocker. The CANONICAL main.av build compiles @std deps from SOURCE: (1) a plain 'bs2 compile/expand' sets no AVRA_USE_METADATA, so std-cli is compiled from source (verified — the comp_helpers fixture expands correctly under a clean-env bs2 expand); (2) the seed-train recompiles main.av HERMETICALLY with the metadata fast-path STRIPPED (CLAUDE.md — 'the seed MUST be self-contained'). So library-authored @comptime macro bodies ARE available on the real/canonical build. znl0 only bites the OPT-IN metadata fast-path (test-runner shards; optional lib-build speed) — cross-package @comptime tests must source-compile (~20s) until it lands. Fix still wanted (metadata should carry @comptime bodies so the fast-path works for library macros too), but it does not gate vez6.11/.12.

comments.author: Claude
comments.text:
REFINED ROOT CAUSE + this DOES gate vez6.12 via a test (re: the P1->P2 downgrade). vez6.12's flip makes packages/cli/src/main.av use @expand(expand_cli); tests/cli_metadata_compile_test.av (9ixv) compiles main.av under AVRA_USE_METADATA=1 and now FAILS (F4006). So even though the CANONICAL build is source-mode, the metadata fast-path IS exercised for main.av by that test (and by incremental avra build).

Precise mechanism (confirmed from the emitted unit.meta.bin): @comptime bodies ARE shipped (9p1d, metadata_extract.av fmt_stmt_ids), NOT absent -- but fmt renders AST enum-ctor calls SUBJECTLESS, dropping the type prefix: source Stmt.Let(...) / Expr.StructLit(...) become stored .Let(...) / .StructLit(...). On lazy re-parse+re-eval the subjectless .StructLit/.ListLit collide with the evaluator's fwyx special-casing (features/eval/mod.av eval_expr: .StructLit -> eval_struct_lit, .ListLit -> eval_list_lit) -> evaluated as struct/list literals, not AST-node ctors -> macro returns null -> F4006.

derive_walker survives because quote-lowered AST rides lower.av (round-trips); cmdgen uses DIRECT construction (forced by rmzs). Fix options: (a) fmt keeps the Stmt/Expr prefix on AST-ctor calls for @comptime-body serialization, or (b) metadata path preserves qualified ctor, or (c) land rmzs so cmdgen can use quote (lower.av path). 81u7 closed as dup of this.

comments.author: Claude
Claude
comments.text:
COMPLETE DIAGNOSIS + HAND-OFF (core parse/fmt = ps3t's active AST-rewrite zone; NOT landing as a vez6 consumer patch). The metadata fast-path corrupts direct-AST-construction @comptime macro bodies (cmdgen expand_cli/expand_command) -> F4006 "macro returned null". Two layers:

LAYER 1 (verified fix) -- fmt/mod.av:47 drops the enum-ctor type qualifier:
  BEFORE: .EnumCtor(tn, variant, args) -> ".${variant}(${fmt_expr_ids_comma(store, args)})"
  AFTER:  .EnumCtor(tn, variant, args) -> "${tn}.${variant}(${fmt_expr_ids_comma(store, args)})"
  tn is "" for a genuinely subjectless .Variant (byte-identical there); matches render_expr which already qualifies. VERIFIED: after this the regenerated std-cli unit.meta.bin serializes @comptime bodies with qualified ctors, e.g. "@std::avrac::core::Expr.StructLit(...)" and "...Stmt.Let(...)" (were ".StructLit(...)" / ".Let(...)").

LAYER 2 (the harder half) -- with Layer 1 alone it STILL F4006s, because the parser doesn't re-parse the qualified ctor as an EnumCtor. This is MULTI-PATH, non-trivial:
  * parse/mod.av:1491 (postfix field/ctor gate) only makes an EnumCtor from a BARE PascalCase Ident. Adding a .QualifiedIdent arm there did NOT fix it -- the qualified form routes through a different parse path.
  * `@std::...::Expr.StructLit(...)` does not parse in normal expression position at all (F0040 -- `@` rejected); the fully-qualified ctor exists only on the @comptime-body reparse path.
  * eval already handles EnumCtor with a qualified type_name (eval/mod.av:840 -> eval_enum_ctor), so NO eval change -- the gap is purely the parser recognizing the qualified ctor on the body-reparse path.
  => genuine multi-path core-parser work, in ps3t's AST-rewrite zone.

CLEANER ALTERNATIVE: land rmzs (computed splice) so cmdgen uses quote/splice -> quote-lowered AST rides lower.av which already round-trips (that's why derive_walker works) -> both layers moot.

Blocks vez6.12 (main.av flip can't compile via the metadata fast-path until this or rmzs lands). Diagnosed end-to-end by vez6 (the fmt fix is confirmed; the parser attempt is proven insufficient) and handed to the ps3t/comptime owner rather than hand-surgered mid-rewrite.

comments.author: Claude
comments.text: FIXED by PR #729 (same root cause as pqc9): cross-package @comptime bodies now round-trip through fmt->parse->eval under the metadata-stub path. Library-authored macros (@std.cli.cmdgen expand_cli/expand_command) no longer eval to null when the package is stubbed. Will close on merge of #729.

comments.author: Claude
comments.text: REPLAYED after beads sync repair. FULL FIX on claude/znl0-metadata-comptime-ctors (PR #728): the 2-part diagnosis was necessary but NOT sufficient — invariant: FMT OUTPUT MUST BE VALID AVRA SOURCE. Five parts: (1) fmt keeps enum-ctor type qualifiers; (2) fmt re-escapes string literals (fmt_string_lit inverts the lexer decode incl \x24 for literal ${ — str_lit's nested-quote body rendered unparseable); (3) parser accepts @pkg::mod::Type in TYPE position; (4) parser accepts qualified refs in EXPRESSION position (Expr.QualifiedIdent was resolver-only — rehydration died at the @, making the ticket's EnumCtor-gate part unreachable; qualified StructLit included; >=1 :: required so @ident stays annotation syntax); (5) parse_declaration disambiguates @ident:: (expression) from @ident (annotation) — a qualified TAIL struct-lit was eaten as an annotation. PLUS invoke_macro fails loudly on rehydration-parse failure (was silent null -> misleading F4006). Workarounds retired: all 15 std-cli sites (6 env-clears + 9 write_fixture_and_run_no_metadata); cmdgen 52/52 through the fast-path. Gates: suite 3951/3951, selfhost fixed point, diff-test byte-identical, 3 mutants distinct kills. RACE: #729 (parallel session) fixes the same class + pqc9; unique-to-#728: string re-escaping + loud diagnostic + workaround retirement; unique-to-#729: pqc9 evidence, qualified_name_roundtrip_test, cross_pkg_expand_metadata_test, 424f. Whichever lands second ports the other's unique pieces.

title: vez6: pin + test hygiene treatment of macro-EMITTED type/impl/fn names (must NOT be renamed) — load-bearing for expand_command
description: Design §6 flags as OPEN: 'do generated type names get hygiene treatment?'. This is load-bearing for vez6.11: expand_command emits 'type Command_<inst>' + 'impl Runnable for Command_<inst>' and the cli references them across decls, so those names MUST survive hygiene un-renamed, while LOCAL bindings the macro introduces inside run() bodies (let foo = ...) SHOULD stay hygienic to avoid capturing user names. vez6.5 (hygiene) is closed but the design lists this specific case as unresolved. ACTION: verify current hygiene-pass behavior on macro-emitted top-level type/impl/fn names, pin the rule (emitted declared-output names = not renamed; interior let/mut = renamed, with @unhygienic opt-out per §3.7), and add a spec test. Found during design review 2026-07-09.
close_reason: Closed

comments.author: Claude
comments.text: PINNED — PR #724 (https://github.com/tristanMatthias/forge-lang/pull/724). DESIGN DECISION (resolves the open §6 question 'do generated type names get hygiene treatment?'): NO — macro-emitted TOP-LEVEL declared names (type/enum/fn/impl-target) are NOT renamed, so sibling decls + user code reference them by the exact emitted name. Verified: @expand renames NOTHING today. Pin test expand_name_survival_test.av (2/2): the exact expand_command shape (emitted type + impl Runnable for it + maker fn, cross-referenced from main) and an emitted enum matched by its emitted variant — both would FAIL if a hygiene pass renamed a declared output name. Test-only (selfhost byte-identical). The INTERIOR half (spec §3.7 hygienic-by-default let/mut + @unhygienic — currently unimplemented) is a distinct feature, split to rvcy. This closes pqyp's title-scoped, load-bearing deliverable + resolves the design question; rvcy tracks the interior hygiene implementation.

title: vez6: build the ergonomic macro introspection helpers (children_of_type/method_body/instance_name) on the ytwb deref primitive; reconcile design §3.2/§4.2
description:
DESIGN-vs-REALITY GAP (found doing aggressive design review, 2026-07-09). docs/2026_05_08_COMPONENTS_V2_DESIGN.md §3.2/§4.2 presents the macro API as: a macro receives a ComponentDecl with decl.instance_name / decl.children_of_type(Flag) / decl.method_body('run') / decl.parent_chain_flags(), and returns List<Decl>. NONE of this exists:
- A macro receives a raw Stmt (ComponentBlock), not a ComponentDecl wrapper.
- The inspection helpers were nominally 'Phase 1' but vez6.1 only EXPOSED core/ast.av types — it never built children_of_type/method_body/parent_chain.
- Return type is Stmt / List<Stmt>; there is no Decl type (see also the doc-reconciliation note below).
The design's central worked example (§4.2 expand_command) therefore does not compile against the real language.

NOW UNBLOCKED by ytwb (synth_deref_stmt/expr/stmt_ids read shims): build these helpers as PURE LIBRARY code (std-cli or a shared macro-support module) on top of the deref primitive — walk ComponentBlock.body via synth_deref_stmt_ids, filter children by their component-name (flag/arg), find the run() Function, read config pairs. This is the natural next slice of vez6.11 and keeps the ergonomic layer OUT of the evaluator (pure consumer).

ALSO reconcile the doc with reality: Decl→Stmt naming, receiver shape (Stmt not ComponentDecl), and the non-compiling example syntax (semicolons in §4.2 'print_help(self); 1'; Axis 28 forbids them). Depends on ytwb.

comments.author: Claude
comments.text:
Two more design-review findings (2026-07-09), fold into this reconciliation:

(10) ARCHITECTURE DRIFT — doc §4.2 shows independent @expand(expand_command) + decl.parent_chain_flags() walking UP to cli for global flags. But a macro receives ONE ComponentBlock (the command) with no parent pointer, so a bottom-up parent walk is not implementable from the received node. The CHOSEN architecture (vez6.11 notes, 2026-06-03) is TOP-DOWN: a single @expand-registered expand_cli owns the whole DSL and calls expand_command as a @comptime helper per command, threading global flags DOWN. The doc's independent-macro + parent_chain model contradicts this. Reconcile the doc to the top-down ownership model; drop parent_chain_flags in favor of expand_cli passing inherited flags into expand_command.

(11) INCOMPLETE B-final MIGRATION in the component AST we consume (ps3t/L1 territory — coordinate, do NOT fix here): CompConfigPair.value is still a boxed Expr (never flipped to ExprId), while its sibling CompConfig.default_id DID flip to ExprId?. CompConfig also carries a ty_vt: ValueType + ty_id: TypeId? dual the source comment calls 'still mid-migration (F1a dual)'. Net: config values are conveniently direct-readable today (no synth_deref_expr needed), but the boxed-Expr island + half-migrated dual are drift. Flag to the ps3t/B-final owner to finish; the introspection helpers here should read config via the current (Expr) shape but not depend on it staying unflipped.

title: macro-facing AST introspection: read component-block children + method bodies from a @comptime macro (typed id->node read shim + eval intercept)
description:
BLOCKER surfaced while starting vez6.11 slice B (expand_command). The Components V2 design (docs/2026_05_08_COMPONENTS_V2_DESIGN.md §4.2) assumes a @comptime macro can introspect a received component block: read its child flag/arg decls and the run() method body, i.e. decl.children_of_type(Flag) / decl.method_body("run") / instance_name.

CURRENT STATE (verified 2026-07-09 on seed v110, post-B-final flip):
- A macro CAN destructure the top-level node: match s { .ComponentBlock(comp_name, instance, config, body) -> ... } binds body: List<StmtId>.
- But reading each child requires turning a StmtId into a Stmt (and ExprId into Expr). NO such typed id->node read shim exists. synth.av ships only the WRITE direction (synth_stmt_id/synth_expr_id/synth_stmt_ids: node->id). store.stmts.get(id)/children_of(id) need a NodeStore handle, which the tree-walk evaluator's Value space does NOT give a macro (see synth.av header comment).
- The design's inspection helpers (children_of_type/method_body/parent_chain) were NOT built — vez6.1 only exposed core/ast.av TYPES.

NEEDED: a macro-surface id->node read path — e.g. synth_deref_stmt(StmtId)->Stmt / synth_deref_expr(ExprId)->Expr as type-level shims + an eval intercept in features/eval/mod.av (mirroring the existing synth write-shim + ctx_* intercept pattern), OR higher-level component-introspection getters (children_of_type/method_body) backed by the avra_rd_*/ctx_* C-side layer.

LOCATION: features/comptime (synth.av) + features/eval/mod.av (intercept) [+ possibly runtime.c]. This is INSIDE ps3t.5's active-rewrite zone (interpreter->JIT, Value deletion) and OUTSIDE vez6's pure-consumer footprint (std-cli/main.av). Cross-agent coordination decision required — see ps3t.5.1 comment.

BLOCKS: vez6.11, vez6.12, vez6.10, vez6.9 (all remaining vez6 work needs macro introspection).

title: Bug: bare null/none literal as an enum-ctor arg for a nullable field is typed void -> false F1000
description:
REPRO: enum E { A, B(f: int?) }; E.B(null) -> error[F1000] 'E.B field f expects int?, got void'. Through a variable (let x: int? = null; E.B(x)) it's CLEAN, and the struct-literal analogue S { f: null } is CLEAN. Only the enum-ctor-arg + bare-null-literal path is broken.

ROOT: typeck/mod.av tc_check_enum_ctor_args. It computes aty = check_expr(null).ty = void (a bare null/none literal, Expr.None, has no expected-type context here so it types void), then the value-scalar-class check vtype_is_value_scalar(strip_optional(fty)) != vtype_is_value_scalar(aty) sees int (scalar) vs void (non-scalar) -> false mismatch. The strong scalar-class check intentionally catches null->non-nullable-scalar, but wrongly flags null->NULLABLE field. Struct-lit's check_one_field_ty uses narrower checks that don't false-positive on null.

FIX: skip the scalar-class check when the arg is Expr.None AND the field type is optional (null is valid for any optional; a null into a non-optional field still errors). Mirrors struct-literal null handling.

FOUND VIA qm8l: dormant until the spec/given/then arity+type gate (qm8l) was wired — the test if_expr_followed_by_enum_ctor_test.av has E3r6q.B(..., null) in a spec body, so gating the spec body surfaced this. Fixed together with qm8l.
close_reason: Fixed + merged (squash 580344d8, PR #664). Bare null/none literal as an enum-ctor arg for a nullable field was typed void -> false F1000. tc_check_enum_ctor_args now skips the scalar-class check for Expr.None into an optional field; null into non-optional still errors (precision test). Regression tests gwa0_null_enum_ctor_arg_test.av + err_null_nonoptional_ctor_test.av, both mutation-verified. Byte-identical; all CI green.

title: test-coverage: metadata FAST PATH has no hard-failing regression test (crashes/wrong-output degrade silently)
description: The metadata fast path (resolver take_meta_fast_path: read a dep's .meta.bin -> synthesize_unit_body -> stamp_stub_spans -> resolve stubs instead of parsing source) has ZERO tests that HARD-FAIL when it's broken. Two safety nets both miss it: (1) diff-test compiles the selfhost + corpus FROM SOURCE, never taking the fast path; (2) the test-runner's @std pre-build DEGRADES to whole-program shards on a fast-path failure (a [warn], not a failure) and the suite still passes green. This let the F4d.8 metadata_synthesize flip ship (from a prior session) with a SIGSEGV + wrong-output + 3x-slowdown on the fast path, undetected until it degraded a full make test to ~50min (snw0-style) and I traced it. FIX: add a spec test (fixture-stateful) that (a) builds a small producer package + emits its unit .meta.bin to a cache slot, (b) compiles a consumer that imports the producer's full surface with AVRA_USE_METADATA=1 so take_meta_fast_path fires, (c) asserts the consumer's runtime output is CORRECT (probe lines), and (d) asserts compile wall-time is within a sane bound (guards the 3x regression). This is the gate any future metadata_synthesize/stamp_stub_spans/synthesize_unit_body change must pass. Also consider making the test-runner's pre-build failure a HARD suite failure (not a silent degrade) when a canary env is set, so CI catches fast-path breakage.
notes:
Investigation (2026-07-07): cached_fixture_run (test_runner/mod.av:446) runs 'diagnose.sh --run <fixture>' and RESPECTS the ambient AVRA_USE_METADATA — it does NOT force the fast path. That's the masking mechanism: when the @std pre-build crashes, the run degrades (AVRA_USE_METADATA unset run-wide), so metadata_codec_test + every fixture compiles via the SLOW path → passes → crash invisible. build_lib_metadata_test covers only the PRODUCER (emit + metadata_show), and its fixture builds a DEP-FREE lib so it never exercises the dep/mod fast-path synthesize+stamp+resolve where the crash lived. THE FIX: a fixture that (1) builds a producer with an exported surface (model on build_lib_metadata_fixtures/sample.av), (2) compiles+runs a CONSUMER that imports+uses that surface with AVRA_USE_METADATA=1 EXPLICITLY set in the shell cmd (force the fast path regardless of ambient/degrade state) — either a cross-package 'use @pkg' (needs package-search-path setup) OR simpler a same-package 'mod producer' + entry that 'use's it (hits resolve_module_stmt's take_meta path, resolver.av:~1156, the site that crashed), (3) asserts consumer rc==0 (no SIGSEGV) AND correct runtime output (stubs compiled correctly). The producer must be built FIRST so its meta.bin is cached, then the consumer recompiled with the fast path forced. This forces the exact synthesize_unit_body→stamp_stub_spans→resolve path that the reverted metadata flip broke, independent of the global-degrade masking.
IMPLEMENTED in PR #656 (claude/y5um-f4d-finish). Fixture tests/metadata_fastpath_consumer_fixtures/sample.av + test tests/metadata_fastpath_consumer_test.av: builds a rich-surface producer (struct+enum+2fns+const), compiles a consumer using the whole surface with AVRA_USE_METADATA=1 forced inline (fast path immune to the global degrade), asserts fast-path-taken + build rc==0 + .ll emitted. Mutation-verified (stamp_stub_spans→[] flips 2 probes to FAIL). 4/4 on HEAD. This is now the gate for the F4d.8 metadata_synthesize redo. NOTE: v1 guards the CRASH class (build rc==0); runtime wrong-output is complementarily covered by metadata_codec_test when the fast path is engaged (bs2 build stops at .ll — running a linked binary needs llc+cc, deferred). Close 7hx3 when #656 merges.
close_reason: Implemented + merged in PR #656 (squash f695d49d): metadata fast-path consumer guard (fixture + test), mutation-verified 4/4. Closes the coverage gap diff-test structurally can't provide. Now the mandatory gate for any metadata_synthesize/stamp_stub_spans/synthesize_unit_body change (F4d.8 redo included).

comments.author: Claude
comments.text:
REPRO CONSTRUCTED (the ticket's stated blocker — deferred repro files were gone). A runtime statement quote ICEs at codegen:
  fn f() -> int { let s = quote stmts { let x = 5  let y = 6 }  3 }
  -> ./build/bs2 compile => F9999 'codegen error: undefined function @std::avrac::features::comptime::synth_stmt_ids'
(quote stmt { let x = 5 } hits the same; check passes, the ICE is at CODEGEN not typeck.)

ROOT CAUSE: dispatch_quote_kind (features/quote_expr/lower.av:334) lowers kind stmt/decl -> construct_stmt (single) / construct_stmt_ids (list) and kind stmts -> construct_stmt_ids (:343-344). Those emit calls to the synth_stmt / synth_stmt_ids shims (features/comptime/synth.av), which are COMPTIME-ONLY identity shims: eval intercepts them by name (call_is_synth_shim in features/eval/mod.av) and their body is synth_shim_unreachable. There is NO runtime codegen for them, so a statement quote reached by the CODEGEN path (a runtime quote, not comptime-folded) hits 'undefined function synth_stmt_ids'. The EXPR-quote path (construct_expr) is the sibling that works under comptime but standalone-runtime-ICEs differently ('undefined enum type @std::avrac::core::Expr' — the AST enum types aren't available outside a context that imports @std.avrac.core), so the true i0yg repro wants AST types in scope so the expr path is fine and ONLY the statement shim is the gap.

DESIGN DECISION (mine, as language designer): runtime statement quotes SHOULD WORK, by symmetry with runtime expr quotes (both construct AST values at runtime — the use case is metaprogramming / the compiler manipulating Stmt trees). So the fix is NOT a clean-error gate; it is to give the statement synth shims a RUNTIME lowering. The ticket's 'value-space/arena id reconciliation' is the crux: synth_stmt_ids is a value-space identity over List<StmtId>, but at runtime the constructed StmtIds must be reconciled with the CONSUMER's arena (the synthesized MatchExpr(Null,[arm]) tree at lower.av:~661 rows must re-ingest into the executing NodeStore, exactly as parse_body_source does for @comptime bodies). FIX DIRECTIONS: (a) codegen a real runtime body for synth_stmt/synth_stmt_ids (identity that threads the arena-ingested ids), OR (b) lower stmt/stmts quotes to direct runtime Stmt construction (like construct_expr does for exprs) without the shim. Prefer (b) if the expr path already avoids a comptime-only shim at runtime — check how construct_expr's synth_expr_id resolves at runtime codegen vs synth_stmt_ids. NEXT TICK: claim, pick (a) or (b), implement + a runtime-statement-quote spec test (the repro above), mutation-verify, gate + diff-test (likely an intended-ir-change if any compiler code uses runtime statement quotes — check). This deserves a fresh focused tick (fresh repro now exists; unblocked).

title: Resolver: module-private fns leak cross-module and locals fail to shadow them — closure-marker corruption
description:
A top-level (non-export) fn declared in one module resolves inside a DIFFERENT
module of the same package, and a LOCAL VARIABLE with the same name does not
reliably shadow it: the identifier compiles to a reference to the fn — a
closure array [0xDEADBEEF marker, fn_ptr] — instead of the local's value.
The corrupt value then flows silently until something renders/derefs it.

Two defects, both must be fixed:
1. Locals must always shadow fns in identifier resolution (lexical scope wins).
2. A module-private fn must not be visible from another module at all.

REPRO (found 2026-07-04 during F1c+F1d, y5um.8.4/.8.5): add
`fn struct_lit(type_name: string, inits: List<FieldInit>) -> Expr` to
features/quote_expr/lower.av — component_decl/expand.av:516 has a local
`let struct_lit = Expr.StructLit(type_name, name_init)` used in
`Stmt.Return(struct_lit)`. Rebuild bs2, then:
  cd packages/std-avrac && AVRA_USE_METADATA=1 AVRA_LIB_PKG_ROOT='@std::avrac' \
    ./build/bs2 compile --emit_metadata --module_path='@std::avrac' src/avrac.av
=> exit 99: non-exhaustive match in @std::avrac::core::render_expr, unmatched
tag -559038737 (the closure marker, codegen/types.av closure_marker()). The
component factory body carried the closure where the struct-lit Expr belonged.
Plain `bs2 compile avrac.av` from src/ does NOT reproduce (no manifest -> no
metadata path); the corruption only surfaces where the expanded component AST
is consumed.

The bug is baked into the seed's resolver too (v62 reproduces), so the fix
lands on its own PR and rides the seed train before any dogfooding.

This is the root cause behind the CLAUDE.md rule "never shadow fn/type names
with pattern vars" — fixing it makes that rule unnecessary. Capture a spec
test per rule 11: fn X in module A + local X in module B, assert the local
wins and the private fn is invisible cross-module (expect F3xxx once fixed).

Related but distinct: ogx0 (duplicate TYPE names), irh4 (test-shard type
namespace).
close_reason: Fixed + merged (#667, squash 67d16490). Name-qualifier now threads let/mut/const/destructure + For/ForIn loop-var bindings through rewrite_stmt_ids, so a local shadows a same-named use-alias/module-sibling fn instead of being qualified to it (which codegen materialised as the 0xDEADBEEF closure array = silent memory corruption). Byte-identical diff-test; 3602/3602 suite + selfhost fixed point; mutation-verified regression test (resolve/tests/local_value_shadows_import_test.av); proven end-to-end via a local seed cycle. Removes the root cause behind the CLAUDE.md 'never shadow fn/type names' rule (dogfooding deferred until the seed train advances past this fix).

comments.author: Claude
comments.text:
SCOPING (investigation, not yet started). Loci found:
- DEFECT 1 (local shadows fn): the RESOLVER Ident path (resolve/mod.av:446-462) ALREADY checks locals first — lookup_name(r.scopes) at :452 before lookup_fn(r.functions) at :459. So the resolver resolves the local correctly. The closure-marker corruption is therefore DOWNSTREAM: either codegen re-decides the Ident (local vs fn) and picks the fn, OR the resolver doesn't ANNOTATE the Ident as local so codegen must re-resolve and mis-picks. Next step: trace how codegen lowers Expr.Ident to a local load vs a fn reference (grep codegen for Ident + closure_marker), and whether resolve rewrites resolved locals to a distinct node. The fix likely lives in codegen's Ident lowering (respect the local binding) OR in resolve annotating the local.
- DEFECT 2 (module-private fn leaks cross-module): lookup_fn(r.functions, name) at :459 — r.functions includes fns from OTHER modules (the leak). Fix: scope r.functions to the current module + others' EXPORTED fns only. names.av already tracks per-item  (item_is_exported, ModuleItemEntry.exported) — thread that into how r.functions is populated so a non-export fn is only visible within its declaring module.

SCALE: substantial + subtle (resolver + codegen), and SEED-BAKED (v62 reproduces) -> lands on its OWN PR and rides the seed train before any dogfooding. Deserves a fresh focused tick (not rushed at a marathon session's tail). Repro in the description (add fn struct_lit to quote_expr/lower.av, metadata-path compile -> exit 99 unmatched tag -559038737).

So the resolver resolves the local correctly; the closure-marker corruption is DOWNSTREAM — either codegen re-decides the Ident (local vs fn) and picks the fn, or resolve does not ANNOTATE the resolved local so codegen re-resolves and mis-picks. comments.author: Claude
comments.text:
ROOT CAUSE FOUND + FIXED (branch claude/zo1a-fn-shadow-leak).

The bug is in the NAME-QUALIFICATION pass (resolve/names.av), not codegen.
`rewrite_ident` already checks `scope_has(ctx.locals, name)` first — but
`rewrite_stmt_ids` walked a statement sequence STATELESSLY (`list_map`),
so it never added the bindings a `let`/`mut`/`const`/destructure
introduced to `ctx.locals`. A later statement's reference to that local
was therefore rewritten to the same-named module sibling's (step 5) or
`use`-alias's (step 4) canonical path; codegen's emit_name_lookup then
missed env (keyed on the bare name), fell to get_fn(FQN), and built the
[0xDEADBEEF, fn_ptr] closure array where the local's value belonged.
`For`/`ForIn` had the same gap (loop var not bound into the body).

Why standalone repros "won" but the full build lost: a root-level file
has current_module=="" so step 5 never fires; the corruption only shows
when the local's name matches a sibling/alias (module context). The
original repro's `construct_type_param_list` local `struct_lit` collided
with the injected `fn struct_lit` sibling in quote_expr.

FIX: thread ctx.locals through rewrite_stmt_ids (bind_stmt_locals after
each stmt) + bind For/ForIn vars into their bodies. Centralised as
scope_add_local (shared with bind_params_ctx).

VERIFIED: byte-identical diff-test (no-op on collision-free compiler src);
regression test resolve/tests/local_value_shadows_import_test.av
mutation-verified (FAIL pre-fix, PASS post-fix); proven end-to-end via a
LOCAL seed cycle — the exact ticket repro (inject fn struct_lit, metadata
compile) crashes on the pre-fix seed and compiles cleanly on the fixed
seed. SEED-BAKED: bs2 built from the pre-fix seed still carries the
corruption in its own quote-lowering, so dogfooding (relaxing the CLAUDE.md
"never shadow fn/type names" rule; using colliding names in compiler src)
lands only AFTER the seed train advances past this fix.

title: diff-test: label-gated run-results-equivalence mode for INTENDED IR changes
description: The HRN gate has no path for landing an intentional IR change: CI diff-test (byte-identity vs the base ref) fails by design and the oracle only advances at merge — so e.g. the F1005 zero-fill→explicit-fields cleanup can never go green. Add --diff-test --run-equiv: when IR differs, fall back to RUN-RESULTS equivalence (compile+execute the corpus under OLD and NEW, compare outputs byte-for-byte; require the full suite green under NEW). CI invokes it only when the PR carries an intended-ir-change label; the label + the equivalence evidence become the documented oracle-advance procedure. Prerequisite for the F1005 cleanup train (681 sites); implemented in diagnose.sh per rule 10.
close_reason: Implemented and merged (#615, squash 200b7220). --diff-test --run-equiv: on IR divergence each divergent corpus artifact links+runs under OLD and NEW and must match stdout+exit (30s timeout); corpus skips forbidden in the mode; selfhost divergence records as intended (corpus run-comparison + rc-strict suite are its evidence). CI label-gated on intended-ir-change. Default mode verified byte-identical-unchanged; flag sanity PASS. First real divergence exercise = F1005 cleanup tier 1 by design.

comments.text:
SEQUENCING FINDING (diff-test / self-hosting): the F1005 gate cannot land in ONE PR with the cleanup. comments.author: Claude
comments.text:
F3b execution plan (post-F3a). Infrastructure is DONE (F3a built ExprArena, reexpr, exprs.get/add_leaf, ingest_expr, pos/span side-tables, the derive-walker id handling). F3b is mechanical: flip the Expr enum's own Expr/List<SExpr> children to ExprId/List<ExprId> (and Expr.Block's List<SStmt> -> List<StmtId>), thread the store through consumers. Staged by variant family (ticket sanctions this), each family a byte-identical checkpoint PR:

Family 1 — single-sub-expr wrappers: Grouping, Unary, Assign, Try, Spawn, Isolated, Splice, FieldAccess, OptionalChain, TupleIndex, IsCheck, FieldAssign (obj+value).
Family 2 — binary/logical/coalesce: Binary, Logical, NullCoalesce, Index, Slice, IfExpr.
Family 3 — call/args (List<SExpr>): Call, GenericCall, EnumCtor, OptionalMethodCall, InCheck.
Family 4 — collection literals (List<SExpr>): Tuple, ListLit, MapLit.
Family 5 — struct/with (List<FieldInit>): StructLit, With.
Family 6 — bodies: Block(List<SStmt>->List<StmtId>), Lambda, MatchExpr, When, ListComp, Catch, Quote, ChannelNew(capacity: Expr?).

Per-family: change enum fields -> update parser (native alloc via alloc_leaf/alloc_expr + record span) -> desugar/quote/marshal/eval-decode constructors -> codegen/typeck/eval/render/resolve readers (resolve child via store.exprs.get) -> derive walker auto-handles id fields. GATES each family: build from v66 (window),  byte-identical (the oracle — 07po showed the suite alone misses pos-regressions; watch reexpr/restmt inherit pos+span), full suite + selfhost, prepare-pr x3, PR, CodeRabbit, merge. The 07po lesson: every transform rebuild MUST use reexpr (inherits span), never a bare exprs.add_leaf, or source positions zero out. Container types (SExpr wrapper, FieldInit) stay until F4 (y5um.8.9).

title: B1 producer flip: parser builds the arena natively; boxed_view shim serves un-migrated passes
description: The keystone sub-increment (parent y5um design, B1). Parser allocs nodes into the NodeStore directly (every production returns a typed id); a boxed_view(id) shim (generalising program_from_store) reconstructs the SExpr/SStmt tree so all un-migrated passes are UNCHANGED. Deletes the ingest copy step (arena is no longer a mirror — it IS the producer). Struct-embedded children (ParamEntry, CompConfig, WhenArm, Variant, remaining containers) get ids NATIVELY here with structure stored — the industry-precedented rep (rustc hir::Arm-as-node / rust-analyzer id-field structs / Zig extra_data ranges): container children are labeled ids or explicit ranges, NEVER a flat unlabeled child list re-partitioned by counting. This subsumes v8op's residual and the descoped y5um.3 Stage 3 (2026-07-01 architecture decision, user-approved: stop extending the walker-shim's flat-list model — it has no industry precedent and collapses on multi-var-slot nodes like ComponentDef). Design questions to settle first (in this ticket, before code): container rep choice (own arena+id per struct vs id-field structs inline), NodeRef/AnyNode growth vs generic ref, span+provenance for container children. M3-gated: reconstructed boxed view byte-identical to today's parser output (diff-test oracle), suite + fixed point. NOT seed-gated (internal Avra; field TYPES not variant set). Unblocks ps3t.3.4 (error nodes), ps3t.3.5 (hash-consing).
notes: DESIGN DOC: docs/2026_07_02_B1_PARSER_BUILDS_ARENA.md. Decisions: 3a-BOXED (productions return typed ids, arena keeps boxed payloads, embed via store.get(id)); chokepoint-alloc rejected; boxed view = program_from_store; store scope = entry file + template sub-parsers; speculation truncates arena on restore; rebuild shells may orphan (non-quote-bearing, documented); NO seed cycle; migration oracle = serve-path equivalence probe (AVRA_B1_PARITY), dark-launch stages A-E each M3-gated; OUT: span cleanup, richer edges, container field changes (B-final). AWAITING USER SIGN-OFF.

title: L1 keystone increment B: id-children + parser-builds-arena (arena = single source of truth)
description: ps3t.3.7 increment (iv) / spine §14.1. The L1 pivot: nodes hold typed ids (ExprId/StmtId/PatId/TypeId) instead of boxed children, parser builds the arena directly, SExpr/SStmt deleted (spans+provenance already in arena side-tables from A1/A2). DEFINITION-OF-READY design ticket (this) decomposes B into M3-gated sub-increments. Surface: ~2219 node construct/match sites, 81 SExpr/SStmt files, codegen deepest. Staged via compat shim (NOT big-bang) per §14.6; recommended first step B1 = producer flip with a boxed-view reconstruction shim (passes unchanged, diff-test byte-identical). See design field for the full plan.
design:
B — id-children + parser-builds-arena (ps3t.3.7 increment iv / spine §14.1). The L1 PIVOT: arena becomes the single source of truth, not a read-side shadow.

== END-STATE ==
- Expr/Stmt/Pattern/ValueType variants hold TYPED IDS for child/cross refs, not boxed nodes:
  Binary(left: Expr, op, right: Expr) -> Binary(left: ExprId, op, right: ExprId);
  Block(body: List<SStmt>) -> Block(body: List<StmtId>); etc.
- SExpr/SStmt DELETED. Spans live in the arena span side-table (built by A2), provenance in the sparse table (A1). line/col recomputed on demand.
- Parser allocs into the arena and threads ids (every production returns an id). Passes read via arena.get(id).

== CURRENT STATE (post A1/A2) ==
Arena is a READ-SIDE SHADOW. Parser builds the boxed SExpr/SStmt pointer-tree; ingest_program flattens it into the arena (ids + cross-type edges + real spans for wrapped nodes); program_from_store reconstructs the boxed tree; all passes still read the boxed tree; AVRA_L1_INGEST gates the round-trip. So the arena is PROVEN to hold the whole walker-reachable tree faithfully (A1 edges + A2 spans) — but nothing reads ids yet.

== SURFACE (measured 2026-06-30) ==
~2219 Expr/Stmt/Pattern/ValueType `.Variant` construct+match sites (non-test); 81 files reference SExpr/SStmt; codegen is the deepest consumer (12 files). Far too large for an atomic flip.

== CENTRAL DESIGN FORK ==
- BIG-BANG (flip rep + parser + every pass at once): REJECTED for B. The build would be red across the flip and M3 (bs2==bs3 + HRN diff-test) is unmaintainable mid-flight. §14.6 explicitly prescribes staged; §12 "go hard WITHIN a buildable step".
- STAGED via compat shim (RECOMMENDED): arena is canonical; un-migrated passes consume a reconstructed BOXED VIEW; migrate passes one at a time; flip the variant rep + delete SExpr/SStmt last. The wrinkle: today's Expr/Stmt IS the boxed rep, so "both reps coexist" needs the shim to hand out a reconstructed boxed view (the inverse of A1 ingest — A2's spans make it lossless).

== RECOMMENDED DECOMPOSITION (each sub-increment M3-gated, byte-identical) ==
B0 (this ticket): Definition-of-Ready design — the fork + per-pass order + shim mechanism + seed analysis.
B1 — PRODUCER FLIP: parser builds the arena natively (allocs ids), a boxed_view(id) shim (generalises program_from_store) reconstructs the SExpr/SStmt tree faithfully; PASSES UNCHANGED. Makes the arena the producer without touching consumers — isolates+de-risks the producer change. M3: reconstructed tree must be byte-identical to today's parser output (diff-test is the oracle). NOT seed-gated (internal Avra).
B2..Bk — MIGRATE CONSUMERS pass-by-pass to read ids from the arena (resolve -> typeck -> desugar -> mono -> codegen; least-coupled first, codegen last). Shim bridges the un-migrated rest. Each migration diff-test byte-identical.
B(final) — FLIP THE VARIANT REP to ids + DELETE SExpr/SStmt + the boxed shim, once all passes read ids. The ~2219-site change, but mechanical by then (passes already use id-accessors).

== SEED-GATING ==
Per §10.A: the id-children refactor is an INTERNAL data-structure refactor written in CURRENT Avra (ids are int newtypes; arena.alloc/get are normal fns) -> NOT seed-gated. B changes field TYPES, not the variant SET, so the seed's match-traps over Expr/Stmt still match (no make seed-patch-traps needed). The only seed-gated work would be a sub-step that dogfoods NEW SURFACE in compiler src/ (none in B). CONFIRM empirically at B1 by building from the pinned seed.

== GATES ==
M3 at every sub-increment: suite green + bs2==bs3 byte-identical + HRN diff-test byte-identical. B1's reconstructed boxed view is the critical correctness proof (diff-test). Pass migrations must not change emitted IR. The final rep flip changes internal structure but MUST keep output byte-identical.

== RECOMMENDED FIRST IMPLEMENTABLE STEP ==
B1 (producer flip + boxed-view shim) — self-contained, de-risks the producer, M3-provable, not seed-gated. Start there after design sign-off.

== UNBLOCKS ==
ps3t.3.4 (error/missing nodes — needs parser-on-arena), ps3t.3.5 (hash-consing — needs centralised alloc), and subsumes v8op (struct-embedded nodes get ids natively when the parser allocs them). Feeds L6 (per-fn codegen cache reads the arena).

title: CI seed-cycle caching: persist seed binary + diff-test builds across runs; train skips redundant suite
description: The 4 heavy bootstrap workflows (window, diff-test, seed-train-verify, seed-train) have NO actions/cache, so every PR + merge cold-rebuilds the seed binary (llc -O2 over seed.ll, ~3-4 min) and the post-merge seed-train re-runs the PR's entire build+fixed-point+full-suite verify (squash merge => same tree). title: Cross-module monomorphization mangle collision: same-short-named generics in different modules clobber each other
description: Two modules each declaring a generic type with the same SHORT name but different layout (e.g. type Box<V> = {items: List<V>} vs type Box<T> = {val: T}), both instantiated at Box<int>, mangle to one flat name Box__int because mangle_name_ordered used type_short_name (stripping the module qualifier). Codegen registers one struct under that name and the other module references resolve against the wrong layout: codegen error unknown field. Manifests when both modules are in one compilation unit (a bundled test shard, or a program that mods both). Reproduced with plain fn params (no closures). Fix: monomorphizer qualifies a short name shared across modules (mod_a__Box__int vs mod_b__Box__int) only when a collision exists, so collision-free programs and the compiler itself stay byte-identical. Fixed alongside 452k in the closure-param PR (#571); regression: cross_module_generic_mangle_test.av.

title: L3 enforced rule + lint: no representation/layout decision from an under-determined type (resolve totally or hard-error)
description: The §6 enforced rule that the AST-source-of-truth epic was missing. CLASS: a representation decision (LLVM layout, payload load type, calling convention, mangled name) made from a type that does NOT uniquely determine a representation — at that boundary the compiler GUESSES (first-match instantiation, i64 fallback, ptr-for-Unknown) instead of REFUSING. Members: bare-generic first-match (sh0g segfault), i64 fallback for Bool/Float, string-typed annotation fallbacks (translate_type_ctx), Unknown surviving to codegen, monomorphizer first-match-wins. Layer 3 (typed identity) kills the name-based MECHANISM (string id -> interned/content-addressed id; §15.4 kill the vtype_eq name fallback; 5idg make mono structural). But identity != totality: interning makes 'are two types equal' correct, it does NOT force codegen to refuse an incomplete type. RULE (add to spine §6, CI/lint-gated): the type->layout boundary is TOTAL — codegen consumes only a fully-resolved type; an under-determined type (Unknown, unbound type param, under-applied generic, ambiguous name) is a hard compile error BEFORE codegen, never a guess. ENFORCEMENT: (1) typeck gating (spec Axis 20) rejects under-determined annotations with an F-code (sh0g does this for generics now); (2) structural: distinct ConcreteType/Layout consumed by codegen, constructible only via a total resolve(vt)->Result<Layout,TypeError> (parse-don't-validate) so the fallback has nowhere to live; (3) lint flags any rep-boundary fallback (first-match name lookup, i64 default, ptr-for-Unknown). sh0g is the concrete witness + the first tactical gate; 5idg is the structural dissolution. Spine doc: docs/2026_06_14_AST_SOURCE_OF_TRUTH_EPIC.md §6 + §15.
notes:
RESIDUAL from sh0g PR (#572): the F1004 gate is now type-param-aware at signature/decl/field/payload/trait positions (skips a name that is an in-scope type param shadowing a declared generic — CodeRabbit catch). But check_binding (let/mut/const) and lambda params still pass empty scope_tp, because the enclosing fn's type params aren't threadable to check_binding without changing the registry-shared check_stmt signature. So a TYPE-PARAM-SHADOWED local/lambda annotation (declared 'type T<U>' + 'fn f<T>() { let y: T }') still false-positives F1004. Triple-degenerate (you must name a generic type identically to a type param). PROPER FIX: make resolve_vtype type-param-scope-aware (track in-scope type params in TC scope) so a type-param name never resolves to a shadowing global nominal — fixes the gate AND any other consumer that mis-resolves a shadowed type param. Belongs with the totality/L3 work.
STANDALONE-LAMBDA SLICE LANDED via #697 (squash 537bed94, 2026-07-10): typeck F1006 gate rejects a bare `let/mut/const f = (x) -> …` (no fn-type context) at check_binding — resolve-or-hard-error for that under-determination site. Contextual lambdas (call-arg/typed-binding/struct-field/return) still resolve via existing mechanisms. Byte-identical (diff-test). RESIDUAL (ticket stays OPEN): delete the codegen body-scan heuristic + resolve CONTEXTUAL lambda params from the TYPE (not the body) — the return-position slice is BLOCKED by 8cyb (parser-FnTyped sparse-match bug); working contextual-threading codegen is stashed on claude/ps3t45-lambda-gate. Other under-determination sites (Bool/Float i64 fallback, first-match mono) also remain.

comments.text:
SCOPING (post ps3t.4.2 id-only + .4.3 Inc1). PRIMARY target: codegen/types.av:745
`.Unknown -> i64t` in llvm_type_for_full (and its sized twin) — the canonical
"representation/layout decision from an under-determined type" this ticket forbids.
Defaulting Unknown->i64 silently mis-lays a ptr-typed value as i64 (the CLAUDE.md
"wrong return type / -O2 alignment" silent-failure class).

NOT a naive one-liner (change i64t -> hard-error): the CLAUDE.md notes Unknown is a
typeck sentinel that "codegen paths that fall through pre-resolve hit" — i.e. Unknown
DOES legitimately reach llvm_type_for_full today. So .4.5 is two halves:
  1. RESOLVE TOTALLY: prove/ensure no Unknown (nor id==0 unstamped nominal) reaches a
     layout/repr decision — trace every caller of llvm_type_for_full that can pass
     Unknown, and resolve upstream (mono/typeck must pin the type). This is the bulk.
  2. HARD-ERROR (F-code, F2xxx borrow/memory range or a new F-code) + lint at the
     layout site once (1) guarantees it never fires on a valid program — so the gate

comments.text: ROOT-CAUSE for the lambda instance (2026-07-10, caught by user 'are you working around a bug?'). Confirmed typeck does NOT resolve lambda param types: tc_param_types just returns p.vtype (Unknown for un-annotated); tc_bind_params binds the body param to resolve_vtype(Unknown)=Unknown. So typeck leaves params Unknown and codegen guesses. (Note: the TYPED path — lambdas passed to fn(T)->U / .map/.filter — already gets correct param_types via emit_typed_lambda_arg; only UNTYPED-STANDALONE lambdas 'let f = (n) -> ...' hit the guessing heuristic.) REJECTED WORKAROUND (my first attempt, reverted): make infer_param_types honor annotations (drop the erroneous '!(p.vtype is .Int)' exclusion). Byte-identical + diff-test-PASS, but it POLISHES the heuristic instead of removing it — still leaves codegen inferring un-annotated params. Not shipped (rule 16 / no building on sand). CLEAN FIX (real 4.5): (1) typeck resolves EVERY lambda param's type — annotation, else expected closure type threaded from the binding/call context, else body inference — and stamps it; (2) codegen READS the resolved type, delete infer_param_types entirely; (3) a param still genuinely under-determined (un-annotated standalone, no expected type, ambiguous body) is a typeck HARD-ERROR ('cannot infer type of parameter x; add an annotation'), not an i64 guess. Per spec (fully static) lean require-annotation/full-inference, NOT the int default (the guess). SIZE: substantial typeck increment (closure param resolution + expected-type threading) + selfhost validation (confirm compiler src has no untyped-standalone lambdas that would newly error). title: Bare generic type as fn param picks wrong instantiation (first-match) when >1 instantiation exists — silent segfault
description: A function with a BARE generic type as a param/return (no type args, no fn type param), e.g. fn ge_show_int(opt: GenOpt) -> string, is NOT monomorphized: collect_generic_stmt only records fns with tp.length>0, and plain Call sites never generate instantiation requests (only EnumCtor/StructLit value sites do). So the function is codegen'd as ONE non-generic body, and rewrite_instance_vtype (mono.av:1057) rewrites its bare param via rewrite_type_name first-match. With ONE instantiation of the generic this happens to pick the right layout; with MULTIPLE (e.g. GenOpt__int AND GenOpt__string) it picks the global-first (GenOpt__string) regardless of the actual call arg. The match arm then extracts the payload with the WRONG type (loads a boxed int as a ptr) and string(v) derefs it -> SIGSEGV (accessed address 0x2a == 42). Pre-existing; reproduces in plain main() (no spec blocks): enum GenOpt<T>{None,Some(value:T)}; fn ge_show_int(opt:GenOpt)->string{match opt{.None->"none" .Some(v)->string(v)}}; fn main(){ge_show_int(GenOpt.Some(42)); GenOpt.Some("hi")} segfaults. Explicit args (opt: GenOpt<int>) work correctly. Currently latent in the test suite because spec/then conds were never type-annotated (the annotate pass skipped SpecBlock/GivenBlock); the hk70 fix that annotates them exposes generic_enum_test.av as a crash. 7 test files use bare-generic params (generic_enum_test, generics_test, generic_result_test, generic_combo_test, generics_example_test, generic_struct_expected_inference_test, pattern_generic_substitution_test) so it is an intended feature, not an accident. PROPER FIX: implicit-generic monomorphization — treat a bare/under-applied generic type in a fn signature as introducing implicit fn type params (fn f(opt:GenOpt) == fn f<T>(opt:GenOpt<T>)), infer the args from call sites, and specialize per call via the existing specialize_fn path. BLOCKS hk70 (spec/given annotate). Locus: mono.av collect_generic_stmt(1120)/collect_inst_expr_inner(1312) Call arm missing, rewrite_instance_vtype(1057).
notes:
RE-HOMED into ps3t.4 (L3 Typed identity): sh0g is a concrete witness of the L3 class — codegen picks a representation from an under-determined type by string first-match (rewrite_type_name->inst_mangled, mono.av:955/179). MECHANISM dissolved structurally by 5idg (make mono type round-trip structural, not List<string>) + L3 interned/content-addressed ids. INVARIANT (refuse incomplete type at the rep boundary) tracked by forge-crafting-intepreters-ps3t. THIS ticket = the tactical Axis-20 typeck gate (reject under-applied generics before codegen) — small, no seed cycle, unblocks hk70.
(correction) the general totality/lint rule is ps3t.4.5, not the top epic. sh0g = tactical Axis-20 gate (this work); ps3t.4.5 = the general enforced rule; 5idg = structural dissolution.
Tactical Axis-20 gate IMPLEMENTED + tested. F1004 (DiagCode.UnderAppliedGeneric) in typeck check pass: tc_check_signature_arity (params skip self + return) + check_binding (let annotations), recursing through container/wrapper types. 7 bare-generic test files corrected to explicit args. Negative test under_applied_generic_gate_test (12 cases, mutation-verified). No seed cycle (byte-identical selfhost). PR #572. Close on merge. Structural dissolution remains 5idg/L3; general lint remains ps3t.4.5.

title: vtype_eq nominal soundness: prefer FQN-name equality (counter TypeId diverges across registries)
description: ROOT (found 2026-06-24 while probing pyly): TypeRegistry still uses an incrementing counter (type_registry.av:84 'let id = infos.length + 1') — wc5w content-addressed TypeId is marked delivered but was NOT applied here. Counter ids are registration-order-dependent, so the SAME fully-qualified nominal (e.g. @std::avrac::core::ValueType) gets DIFFERENT ids in different package registries. vtype_eq (core/ast.av:664-685 Struct/Enum/Trait/Newtype/NarrowedEnum arms) does 'if id1>0 && id2>0 { id1==id2 } else { n1==n2 }' — it TRUSTS the divergent ids over the reliable FQN names, so two identical-FQN nominals compare UNEQUAL. Proven: a strict nominal gate at the enum-ctor site false-positives 75x on selfhost, every one 'expects X, got X' (identical FQN). This is the SHARED blocker behind pyly (nominal enum-ctor gating), 8x32 (nominal fn param/ret), and cpvo. FIX: make nominal equality '(id1>0 && id2>0 && id1==id2) || n1==n2' — equal if ids match OR FQN names match. FQN is unique so name-equality is sound; strictly ADDS correct equalities (fixes false-unequal) without removing the same-registry id fast-path. Verify: selfhost + diff-test (expect byte-identical — existing code shouldn't depend on the false-unequal) + full suite. Then pyly/8x32/cpvo nominal gates become sound. The proper long-term fix is completing wc5w (content-addressed ids), which also closes the dual false-EQUAL hole (different types, colliding counter ids cross-registry); this ticket is the sound, minimal interim.
notes: DEFINITIVE (2 empirical attempts 2026-06-24): piecemeal fixes are INSUFFICIENT — this needs content-addressed TypeId (wc5w), not a vtype_eq/stamping patch. ATTEMPT 1 (vtype_eq name-fallback '(id...)||n1==n2' on all 5 nominal arms): built+selfhosted clean, ZERO false-positive reduction — because the two sides are different KINDS (.Enum field vs .Struct arg), so the per-kind arms never match and the name-fallback is unreachable. ATTEMPT 2 (+ kind-correction in stamp_ids_vtype .Struct arm: emit .Enum when type_registry_is_enum(reg,id), + name-fallback): STILL zero reduction — the 148 'f=[Expr] a=[Expr]' identical-FQN cases persist. ROOT (final): the kind-correction at the post-resolution stamping layer DOES NOT REACH the arg types. Those a0 types come from check_expr DURING TYPECK (inference), produced as .Struct AFTER stamp_ids_vtype already ran — so any canonicalization at the stamping/resolution layer is bypassed. The .Struct-vs-.Enum (and FQN-vs-short, and id-divergence) representation inconsistency is PERVASIVE across type-production paths (parser, resolver, stamping, AND typeck inference), not fixable at any single site. CONCLUSION: the only sound fix is wc5w's content-addressed TypeId — a representation-independent id (blake3 of canonical type def) so vtype_eq compares ids that are stable regardless of Struct/Enum wrapper, FQN-vs-short name, or per-registry counter. That makes ALL facets moot by construction. wc5w (marked 'delivered' but type_registry.av:84 still uses infos.length+1 counter) must be genuinely completed. This op3w 'name-fallback' approach is SUPERSEDED — close/fold into wc5w. pyly/8x32-nominal/cpvo stay blocked on wc5w. All experiments reverted; tree clean.
close_reason: Sound nominal type identity LANDED via #551 (squash 95f52870). The fix: (1) vtype_eq compares plain Struct/Enum KIND-AGNOSTICALLY by FQN name (the parser defaults nominals to .Struct so the same enum is .Enum in decl position and .Struct in arg position — per-kind arms missed that); (2) the nominal payload gate compares by CANONICAL registry id (type_registry_id_for resolves FQN+short to one id, kind-agnostic) — sound where the counter TypeId (type_registry.av:84, still present) diverges across registries. NarrowedEnum/Newtype/Trait keep their per-kind arms (extra discriminators). Verified: suite 3291/3291, selfhost fixed point byte-identical, diff-test byte-identical (provably behavior-preserving — inert on all valid code). The counter-TypeId ROOT itself is unchanged (full content-addressed id = wc5w); this achieves SOUND COMPARISON around it, which is op3w's scope. Unblocks pyly (general class done), and the same primitives (tc_nominal_id) are available for 8x32/cpvo.

title: Add seed-train-verify PR gate: run the train's verify phase pre-merge
description:

title: Flaky 4szi.1 toolchain_fp_memo test blocks seed-train (shared write-once global memo)
description:
seed-train run 22 (#538 merge) and likely run 23 (#539) FAIL the suite step on 2 tests in test_runner/tests/toolchain_fp_memo_test.av (spec 4szi.1): 'first set/first get returns the value' and 'later sets are no-ops'. So the seed train is STUCK at v7 (no v8 published since #537); #538+#539 wild-store changes are not in the seed.

ROOT CAUSE (not related to the wild-store work): the memo g_test_toolchain_fp_memo (runtime.c:1701) is process-global + write-once. The REAL path read_or_compute_toolchain_fp (test_runner/mod.av:697) writes it via avra_test_toolchain_fp_set, and it is called by every fixture test (cached_fixture_capture). Under the d4jv shared-process parallel runner, any fixture test sharded BEFORE toolchain_fp_memo_test warms the memo with the real fp; the test's set(marker) is then a no-op (write-once) and get() returns the real fp, not the marker -> both assertions fail. Deterministic per shard ordering (passes locally, fails on the runner's core-count sharding).

FIX (ready): rewrite the test to assert the write-once IMMUTABILITY contract instead of a marker round-trip — set a probe value, capture get() (whatever was published first, ours or a sibling's), then assert a second distinct set leaves get() unchanged and non-empty. Deterministic regardless of warming (write-once => published value is immutable, no race). Test-only change, no compiler IR impact (diff-test unaffected). Needs a PR into the integration branch to unblock the seed train.

Source: discovered while merging #539. Pre-existing since #538.
notes: Fix committed (d025b25e), PR #540 open into feat/crafting-intepreters. title: Generic type-arg conflict → wild-pointer store (fn-side) + generic-struct assignability leniency
description:
Sibling of the struct-side fix in da7dee12 (PR #536). Two pre-existing typeck gaps let a generic type-arg conflict (a wrong annotation that disagrees with the data) escape detection and reach the monomorphizer, which produces a memory-unsafe type-confused store. Reachable only via INVALID programs (wrong annotations), but a wrong annotation must be a type error, never a wild pointer.

(1) FN-SIDE OVERRIDE (mirror of the struct bug, root: infer_from_params_with_expected, so07.7.16).
Repro:
  fn id<T>(x: T) -> T { x }
  fn main() { let y: string = id(9)  println(y) }
mono mangles id__string (expected return overrides the arg-bound T=int), and codegen emits:
  call ptr @id__string(ptr inttoptr (i64 9 to ptr))   ; int 9 passed as wild pointer 0x9
Fix direction: same 'fill gaps, never override a concrete binding' principle the struct side now uses (fill_unresolved_from_expected in features/generics/mono.av). The fn side threads expected via unify_param(tp, ret_vt, expected, arg_ta) — needs a 'skip already-resolved params' mode so the expected return only binds params the args left unresolved. Higher blast radius than the struct side (every generic call with an expected return), so gate on diff-test byte-identical.
