title: compiler: bs2 uses ~15GB to compile std-avrac (~10x a mature compiler) — memory footprint bounds the lib pre-build
description:
ROOT CAUSE behind gvi5's cold-tree fast-path failure. Compiling std-avrac (~50K source lines, 566K IR lines) as one unit peaks ~15.3GB RSS and OOM-kills in a 15GB box. Mature compilers (clang/rustc) compile comparable code in 1-2GB — bs2 is ~10x heavy.

EVIDENCE (measured, correct AVRA_LIB_PKG_ROOT='@std::avrac'):
- single-unit 'bs2 build --lib': peak ~15.3GB → Killed (standalone).
- '--per_module' does NOT help: it runs a MONOLITHIC _unit_meta phase first (compiles the whole package to derive per-unit metadata → produces avrac.av.ll), which is the 15GB step. jobs=4 and jobs=2 both peak ~15GB; per-unit logs show NO 'Killed' (the OOM is the meta phase, not a unit).
- features/ subdir alone is 26567 lines (5x the next); subdir-granularity TUs are still too coarse.

WHY IT MATTERS: the test-runner metadata fast-path (10x suite speedup) pre-builds each @std package into producer objs. In a memory-tight env that pre-build OOMs → fast-path disabled → slow whole-program fallback. The sibling jobs-cap (60ba291c) makes that fallback memory-SAFE (no crash), but the fast-path can't engage cold until this is fixed.

THE MATURE FIX (compiler-engineering, substantial):
1. True separate compilation: eliminate the monolithic _unit_meta phase so each TU's memory is bounded; archive per-TU .o's; consume the archive in collect_workspace_lib_objs. Bound concurrency by MEMORY (read MemAvailable / per-unit estimate), not just cores.
2. Reduce per-compile footprint: prime suspect is monomorphization deep-COPYING subtrees per instantiation (mono.av substitute_stmts ~1481/1613) in a generics-heavy program; also free ASTs/IR after lowering rather than retaining whole-program state across the 4 mono passes. Profile allocation during the std-avrac compile to pinpoint.

GATES: once footprint < ~half RAM, re-apply the gvi5 mkdir fix (cold-tree pre-build redirect) + switch the pre-build to per-module, and the cold fast-path works. Until then mkdir is net-negative (trades a fast redirect-fail for a 280s std-avrac OOM) and stays reverted.
close_reason: MISDIAGNOSIS — could not reproduce. Re-measured the std-avrac lib build in a CLEAN memory state (15GB box, 14GB free, no stray procs): peak process-tree RSS = 111MB, rc=0. The earlier '~15GB' readings were session-accumulated memory pressure (I'd killed several make-test runs; leftover procs + page cache), exactly the misdiagnosis snw0's description already warns about ('Standalone lib build is only 137MiB ... session-accumulated memory pressure ... masqueraded as code bugs'). bs2's per-compile footprint is normal, NOT 10x. The real memory lever — degraded-mode SHARDS compiling all of @std at ~10GiB — is already snw0 (lever b = reduce that shard's footprint; lever c = cap parallelism). No separate compiler-bloat ticket needed.

title: Generics/mono round-trip types through strings (turbofish type_args are List<string>) — make it structural
description: The monomorphizer and turbofish path represent and compare types as STRINGS, violating the 'no string-based type handling / use structural analysis' rule (CLAUDE.md rule 16). Concretely: (1) Expr.GenericCall(callee, type_args: List<string>, args) stores explicit turbofish type-args as bare name STRINGS, not List<ValueType>. (2) mono.av parses those strings back into ValueTypes via vtype_from_type_string, and round-trips generic type NAMES through strings: rewrite_type_name(ty: string), split_annotation_args + top_level_split_idx (comma-splitting 'Result<int, string>' strings to find args), explicit_to_type_args (vtype_from_type_string per turbofish arg). Symbol MANGLING legitimately produces strings (mangle_name_ordered/vtype_mangle_slug) — that part is fine; the problem is type IDENTITY/args flowing as parseable strings instead of structural ValueType. Fix: carry turbofish type-args as List<ValueType> on GenericCall (seed-gated AST change), and make mono's type-arg inference/substitution fully structural (it largely is post-2px2 via unify_param/substitute_vtype) so the string parse/split helpers can be deleted. Umbrella: ps3t.4 typed identity / wc5w content-addressed TypeId. NOTE: current generic-system work (2px2/jl8q/zuzv/wpqd) is structural and does NOT add string handling — this ticket is to REMOVE the pre-existing string round-trips.
notes:
EMPIRICAL VERDICT 2026-06-24 (worktree test, both paths measured): the standard seed-gated two-phase does NOT work for this change.
Q1 (seed-patch-traps + local cycle): FAILS. 'make seed-patch-traps' -> 'Patched 0 match traps' (no-op). 'make build' -> 32x F4006 + 1x F4000, bs2 not produced. Root cause: the F4006 is an EXPLICIT .Err('decode: non-string in string list') from the SEED's baked-in value_to_expr_node -> list_value_to_string_list (eval/mod.av:2499) during @derive(walker) expansion of ast.av — NOT a match-trap, so the trap-patcher (which only rewrites avra_match_unreachable blocks) can't fix it. The seed performs the field's macro decode itself and is one version behind.
Q2 (restructure: derive_walker emits plain Call, no turbofish, to un-gate): FAILS at typeck. 14x F1000 'match arms have different types: List<Expr> vs List<T>'. The walker helpers unwrap_node_list<W,T>/unwrap_node_opt<W,T> have T ONLY in the return type, so without the explicit turbofish T can't bind. The turbofish is load-bearing.
COUPLING (why even a polymorphic-decoder Phase A is insufficient): value_to_expr_node produces the FIELD's type. In Phase A (field List<string>) it produces List<string>; the v_next seed built from Phase A still produces List<string> data, which lands in Phase B's List<ValueType> slot -> type confusion. There is no feature-branch sequence from v18 (List<string> decode) to a seed with a List<ValueType> decode, because each intermediate seed's decode follows the field type at that point.
PATH FORWARD (NOT a normal PR): either (a) a maintainer-coordinated manual seed transition on integration where the full change + a hand-bridged seed land together, or (b) refactor value_to_expr_node to decode type_args REFLECTIVELY from the registered field type (decoupling the decoder from the hardcoded List<string>) — itself a macro-system change to scope. The full internally-consistent change is correct + complete (file map above); the sole blocker is bootstrap sequencing. PARKED pending that design.

title: Generic struct construction can't infer type params from empty fields / let-annotation
description: Constructing a generic struct whose fields are empty collections doesn't infer its type params, and a let-binding type annotation doesn't propagate into the struct literal either. E.g. type Arena<N,Id> = { nodes: List<N>, ... }; let a: Arena<Expr,ExprId> = Arena { nodes: [], ... } fails with F1002 'cannot infer type parameter'. Explicit struct generic args in a literal (Arena<Expr,ExprId>{...}) don't parse. Phantom params (Id appears only in method sigs) are wholly uninferrable. Together with mkwc, this blocks expressing the single generic Arena<N,Id>/DenseTable<Id,V>. Fix: propagate the binding/return-position type annotation into generic struct-literal type-param inference (and/or accept explicit struct type-args in literals).
acceptance_criteria: A generic struct with empty-collection fields constructs via a let/return type annotation (or explicit literal type-args); Arena<N,Id> and DenseTable<Id,V> are constructible; selfhost + diff-test green.
notes: RESOLVED on claude/amazing-cori-28v9fs (commit 17b6892). The titular case now works: a generic struct whose params can't be inferred from its fields — a phantom param (in no field) or a param behind an empty-collection field (nodes: []) — resolves from the let/return EXPECTED type instead of F1002. Arena<N,Id> and DenseTable<Id,V> are now constructible (proven by EiArena<N,Id> + EiTab<Id,V> regression tests). Impl: mono.av threads expected through collect_inst_expr_with_expected + rewrite_expr_with_expected (.StructLit arm), sharing infer_from_field_inits_with_expected — mirrors the fn-side so07.7.16. close_reason: All acceptance criteria met: empty-collection-field and phantom-param generic structs construct via let/return annotation (Arena<N,Id> + DenseTable<Id,V> proven constructible); selfhost byte-identical fixed point holds; diff-test byte-identical vs integration oracle. title: Generic-struct methods don't monomorphize per instantiation (blocks generic arenas/side-tables)
description: The L1 node model wants a single generic Arena<N, Id> / DenseTable<Id, V> instead of the four hand-duplicated arenas (ExprArena/StmtArena/PatArena/TypeArena in core/arena.av, each repeating ingest/get/children_of/span_of/count). This is the root blocker for ps3t.3.6 (DenseTable/SparseTable side-table infra) and the reason core/arena.av carries four near-identical copies. Fix: make mono specialize generic-struct impl methods per concrete instantiation (mirroring generic-fn mono). Until then the duplication is intentional and consistent (matches surrounding style), DRYed only where possible without generics.
acceptance_criteria: A generic struct with methods (e.g. Arena<N,Id> or DenseTable<Id,V>) compiles with each instantiation getting correctly-typed, separately-monomorphized methods; core/arena.av's four arenas collapse to one generic; selfhost + diff-test green.

- Impurity enters ONLY through the extern-fn FFI boundary (pure Avra can't do IO/syscall without FFI). So the check is principled, NOT a name-heuristic (rule 16): mark the effectful boundary, check transitive reachability.
- Impure extern set (ambient IO/FS/net/clock/proc), enumerated: avra_shell_exec, avra_process_forward/exec/spawn_bg/wait/is_alive/exit/env_get/env_unset, avra_file_lock_exclusive/unlock/mtime/size, avra_uptime_ms (clock). (+ audit for rand/net/stdout puts.)
- 28 compiler source files reference @comptime (many are macro-infra/doc, not fn decls) — the ACTUAL @comptime fn decls are the component/derive/expand macros. Whether any transitively reaches an impure extern is the SELFHOST-RISK crux; only the checker can answer it → build-and-observe.

IMPLEMENTATION (incremental, rule 7 — build/audit each step):
1. Add @impure annotation to the enumerated effectful externs (pure-additive, zero-behavior, builds clean). Centralize the marker; do NOT hardcode a name list in the checker.
2. Build the purity checker: for each @comptime fn, walk its transitive call graph (resolve callee names to fn decls incl. externs) and collect reachability to any @impure extern. New pass, likely in resolve/ or a new features/comptime/purity.av, run from run_comptime's prepare phase (before folding) OR at resolve time.
3. Run it NON-GATING (warning) first against the whole compiler to empirically answer the feasibility question (does any compiler @comptime macro reach an impure extern?). 
4. If clean → flip to GATING with new F-code F4008 ComptimeImpureCall (diagnostics/mod.av + error_def; F4007 now taken by ps3t.5.7, F4008 free) before folding, mirroring F4007's channel. If NOT clean → the reaching macros are genuine bugs or need the @embed carve-out; handle per-case (do NOT weaken the check to pass).
5. @embed read-only allowlist: @embed compile-time file read is ALLOWED (the one sanctioned FS touch). Audit whether @embed infra exists; if not, scope its allowlist entry minimally.
6. Resource limits (instr/alloc/time budget at JIT boundary) are ps3t.5.4, NOT here (design §82).

TESTS: a @comptime fn calling avra_shell_exec (or transitively) → F4008 before folding; a pure @comptime fn (arith/string/collection) → no error, folds; @embed read → allowed; transitive impurity (pure fn calling impure helper) → caught. Mutation-verify. diff-test: EXPECT non-byte-identical IF any existing program relied on an impure @comptime fold (audit); likely byte-identical since valid programs don't.

SEED: no cycle for the annotation/check (no new syntax, no new ValueType/Expr/Stmt variant). Dogfood after merge + train.

title: L2: ORC JIT integration
description: Spine: docs/2026_06_14_AST_SOURCE_OF_TRUTH_EPIC.md.
acceptance_criteria: @comptime fns compiled to machine code in-memory via LLVM ORC and called directly; replaces the interpreter for supported cases; output matches the interpreter on the comptime suite.
notes:
SLICE-A PLAN + ORDERING RESOLUTION (2026-07-10). The fold path: comptime/eval.av fold_call:69 runs eval_fn_with_resolved_args (interpreter) on LITERAL Value args (gated by literal_args_to_values), then value_to_expr turns the result Value into a literal Expr spliced back. CRUX the design under-specified: run_comptime folds POST-resolve, PRE-typecheck (comptime/mod.av), but JITing a @comptime fn needs it typechecked + codegen'd (codegen needs resolved types). RESOLUTION (design decision): a fold-time MINI-CODEGEN keyed+memoized on the comptime fn — a @comptime fn is self-contained (typed params/return, pure body), so typecheck+codegen it IN ISOLATION reusing the resolve-time type registries; emit into a throwaway LLVM module; MCJIT it once; cache the fn-address (folds ps3t.5.5 memoization). Do NOT reorder the whole pipeline — keep the fold pass where it is, just give it a lazy per-fn mini-Ctx. STEPS: (1) additive C primitive avra_llvm_jit_call(module, fn_name, argc, i64* argv) -> i64 in llvm_wrapper.c (model on avra_llvm_jit_run:1066 — reuse the MCJIT-engine init, GetFunctionAddress(fn_name), call with argv) + extern in core/llvm.av; (2) build_comptime_fn_module(reg, fn_def) -> module: minimal codegen Ctx from the program's type regs, emit just fn_def (+ transitive @comptime callees); (3) jit_fold_call: marshal List<Value>->i64[] (int/bool direct, float bitcast, string/enum ptr), jit_call, marshal i64 result -> Value by fn_def declared return type, then value_to_expr; (4) swap fold_call to try jit for return types {Int,Bool,Float,Str} else FALL BACK to eval_fn_with_resolved_args (g18a); (5) GATE: diff-test byte-identical (folded literals identical to interpreter) + comptime spec suite green. RISK: comptime powers @expand/@derive/@expand macros (load-bearing) — the fallback keeps all AST-returning + non-scalar cases on the interpreter, so day-one capability is unchanged. Feasibility unknown-until-tried: whether a minimal Ctx can codegen one fn standalone (setup.av builds the full-program Ctx) — validate the mini-Ctx path first.
SLICE-A SPIKE LANDED (PR #700) — step 1 + the mini-Ctx crux DONE + PROVEN. Landed: avra_llvm_jit_call + avra_i64_buf_* marshalling (llvm_wrapper.c); compile_and_jit_call (codegen/setup.av); codegen/tests/jit_call_slice_a_test.av 10/10 mutation-verified. VALIDATED codegen_program emits a single-fn subset (no main) reusing resolve-time type_reg; JIT round-trips 0..4 i64 args + control flow + transitive callee + negatives. FINDING: in-process MCJIT needs -rdynamic (JIT'd bodies calling any runtime fn — div-by-zero trap, string/list ops — fail materialization unless avra_* symbols are dynamic; MCJIT resolves via dlsym(RTLD_DEFAULT)); fixed in build/link.av for test shards. Gate: diff-test byte-identical selfhost 645038 lines + 14 corpus. STAYS OPEN. PR-B remaining: Value<->i64 marshal by declared ret type (bool low-bit mask/float bitcast/ptr for str-enum), build_comptime_fn_module, swap fold_call try-JIT-with-interpreter-fallback for {Int,Bool,Float,Str}, thread type_reg through run_comptime, bs2 -rdynamic (diagnose.sh link_ll).
close_reason: Functional acceptance MET via MCJIT: @comptime fns compiled to machine code in-memory + called directly, replacing the interpreter for supported scalar cases {Int,Bool,Float,Str} (int params, <=4 args, jit-safe bodies), output byte-identical to the interpreter (diff-test-gated). Delivered across #700 (mini-Ctx spike) + #711-716 (child 5.2.1: int/bool/float/string returns + transitive callees + try-JIT-with-interpreter-fallback + -rdynamic). The acceptance's literal 'via LLVM ORC' clause: impl is MCJIT (works, byte-identical, LLVM pinned). Per human design decision, the MCJIT->ORC modernization is split to standalone low-prio ticket forge-crafting-intepreters-78bn (deprecation hygiene, zero functional gain). Broader JIT coverage toward g18a continues in 5.8 + the epic.

comments.author: Claude
comments.text: INVESTIGATION (2026-07-11, v148). PR-B 'remaining' from the 2026-07-10 note is ALL DONE via the closed child 5.2.1 (#700 mini-Ctx spike + #711-716 int/bool/float/string returns + transitive callees + try-JIT-with-interpreter-fallback + -rdynamic). The functional acceptance ('compiled to machine code in-memory, called directly, replaces interpreter for supported cases, output matches interpreter') is MET by the current MCJIT impl (avra_llvm_jit_call/_f64/_str in llvm_wrapper.c via avra_jit_resolve; diff-test byte-identical gates it). The ONLY unmet literal is 'via LLVM ORC' — impl is MCJIT (deprecated in LLVM18). ORC migration is INVASIVE for ZERO functional gain: ORC needs the module in a ThreadSafeContext-owned LLVMContext (LLVMOrcCreateNewThreadSafeModule), but setup.av builds the jit module in a plain avra_llvm_context_create() context — so it's not a C-only wrapper swap; it needs a JIT-specific codegen path threading a TSContext through module creation + disposal-ownership care (crash risk). Same LLVM backend => byte-identical fold results. MCJIT not broken (seed pins LLVM). DECISION NEEDED (P1, architectural): (A) do the real ORC migration, (B) accept MCJIT as satisfying 5.2's functional intent + track ORC-modernization as a low-prio follow-up (recommended), (C) other. Asked the human.

description: Spine: docs/2026_06_14_AST_SOURCE_OF_TRUTH_EPIC.md.

comments.author: Claude
comments.text:
SCOPE FINDING (2026-07-09, honest re-scope). The notes frame this as a quick byte-identical lint over '47 name==/kind== smells'. Investigation shows the ACCEPTANCE part ('ids are only compared/looked-up, never inspected') for the REAL id types needs a foundational prerequisite, not a lint:
- .raw() is the general Newtype peel (features/struct_decl), not id-specific — a lint must be TYPE-AWARE (flag .raw() only where the receiver is an @opaque-marked newtype), else it false-positives on legitimate user-newtype peels (struct_decl tests do this).
- The invariant is ALREADY HELD: every id .raw() peel is confined to node-model modules (core/arena.av, core/side_table.av, core/ids.av); the two fn_decl/codegen.av hits are error-message strings. wc5w (content-addressed TypeId) already landed with zero call-site churn, so 'demonstrated' is effectively done; .4.4 is now a REGRESSION GUARD, not the 'land first' enabler.
- The peel-locality boundary is the hard part: the id newtypes are declared in ids.av but peeled in arena.av/side_table.av — different FILES, same PACKAGE. So the boundary is neither same-file (too narrow) nor same-package (the whole compiler is one package → useless). It needs a friend/capability mechanism.
- BLOCKERS for that: (1) typeck has NO current-module context (resolution FQN-qualifies names before typeck, so typeck is module-flat — no cur_module field); (2) no general module-level annotation exists (only @doc/@module_doc from //!). A post-typeck pass that walks Stmt.Module wrappers could recover module context without threading it through all of typeck — the tractable path — but still needs the friend/capability design + an @opaque newtype annotation + NewtypeReg extended with opaque-flag/declaring-module.
Net: feature-scale, comparable to .4.5, NOT a 30-min lint. Prereq: give the enforcement pass module-awareness (via Stmt.Module walk) + design the @opaque friend-capability. Left OPEN, unclaimed.

comments.author: Claude
comments.text: CLAIMED on branch claude/ps3t44-opaque-handles (base v161, post-#736). Friend mechanism: positional string args name friend MODULES — @opaque("core.arena", "core.side_table") — the declaring module is always an implicit friend. Named-arg form (friends: ...) does NOT parse and is not needed. ENFORCEMENT: .raw() on an @opaque-marked newtype receiver outside {declaring module} ∪ friends → hard compile error (next free F1xxx in the totality family). comments.author: Claude
comments.text:
INCREMENT 1 MERGED — squash 1571fa60 (PR #663) into feat/crafting-intepreters. Content-hash primitive over the 3 live arenas (expr/stmt/pat), per-arena kind discriminator (E:/S:/P:), render_pat_id added, 12 contract specs, mutation-verified, byte-identical, all CI green (diff-test/bootstrap-window/rc-strict/seed-train-verify) + CodeRabbit clean. comments.author: Claude
comments.text:
INCREMENT 2 DESIGN (decision, Plan phase) — a SIMPLER correct scheme than full occurrence-keying, grounded in the actual code.

SITE MAP (verified, .av source):
- arg_tys (SparseTable<ExprId,ValueType>): WRITTEN by typeck annotate — typeck/mod.av:4225,4362 via annotate_expr_stamped (which reexpr's → FRESH id, then set_arg_ty(new_id, ty)); COPIED by mono.av:1687. READ by mono generic-inference (mono.av:528,649,811) + typeck (3412,4287).
- provenance (SparseTable<StmtId,bool> from_macro): WRITTEN by comptime splice (expand_macro.av:533,555 mark_from_macro); READ by resolver rewrite_uses_macro_only (names.av:856,927 is_from_macro).

KEY INSIGHT: annotate_expr_stamped does reexpr → a NEW id, stamps arg_ty on THAT id, and the tree is rebuilt to use the new ids (annotate_expr_list_ids returns the new-id list; the Call is rebuilt with them). Mono reads arg_ty_of(annotatedId) — the fresh id, NEVER the parsed id. Likewise comptime splice produces NEW stmt ids and marks provenance on them. So the occurrence-dependent side-tables are ALREADY keyed by POST-PARSE, per-occurrence ids — not by the parsed node ids.

DECISION: confine interning to the PARSER's allocation (the canonical parsed AST = pure content; feeds structural-equality id-compare + L6 incremental + memory dedup). Post-parse node-synthesizing passes (comptime expand, typeck annotate/reexpr, desugar, mono) allocate NON-interned. Then arg_tys/provenance stay collision-free BY CONSTRUCTION: their keys are post-parse ids, which are unique per occurrence even when the parsed subtrees they derive from were interned to one id. This AVOIDS a full occurrence-keying refactor of arg_tys/provenance (spine §4's edge-keyed end-state remains the eventual L6 goal, but is not needed to make dedup safe now).

WHY correct: at PARSE time no arg_tys/provenance exist yet (typeck/comptime write them later), so interning two structurally-identical parsed args (f([]) vs g([]))'s [] to one id carries no conflicting side-data. The type divergence is added later by annotate as fresh per-occurrence ids. Structural-equality-by-id is only needed on the canonical parsed tree; passes needing structural equality on derived trees use the Inc 1 content-hash explicitly.

IMPLEMENTATION (next focused tick, each M3-gated byte-identical):
1. Add an interning mode to NodeStore alloc: parser's intern path dedups via the Inc 1 content-hash (fast-hash bucket + content-compare on collision, per §15.2 two-tier); passes' plain add_* stay non-interning. Mechanism: either a distinct intern_expr/intern_stmt the parser calls, or a store.interning flag set during parse only (prefer explicit methods over a mode flag).
2. Intern map: content-hash → List<Id> buckets in NodeStore (new side-table), consulted by the parser's alloc.

comments.author: Claude
comments.text: INCREMENT 2 WRINKLE (span-sharing) — found while re-examining. Enabling interning shares one span slot per interned id: two structurally-identical subtrees at DIFFERENT source lines intern to one id -> one ByteSpan -> one of them reports the WRONG error location. Diff-test stays green (spans aren't in codegen IR) and most compile-error tests assert F-codes not lines, so M3 passes — but it's a real diagnostics-quality regression, and shipping it violates 'don't ship a compromised foundation'. So Inc 2 decomposes: 2a = make spans occurrence-safe (edge-keyed per spine §4, OR exclude multi-location leaves from interning), 2b = enable interning. This is why Inc 2 is a careful multi-part effort, not a one-tick grind. Design still favors intern-at-parse-only (arg_tys/provenance stay collision-free by construction, per the prior comment); the span sub-problem is the added gate before 2b.

comments.author: Claude
comments.text:
INCREMENT 2 SEQUENCING (design decision). Inc 2 = actual node-MERGING interning in alloc(). Deferring it, deliberately, behind TWO gates — this is correct sequencing, not skipping:
1. Span-safety (the Inc-2 wrinkle recorded above): node-merging shares one span slot per interned id, so two structurally-identical subtrees at different source lines would collide -> one reports the wrong error location. Occurrence-keyed spans (spine §4) must land first.
2. A real consumer. Inc 1's content-hash ALREADY provides O(1) structural equality via hash-compare (FNV + content-compare on collision), which covers current L1 needs. The ADDITIONAL thing merging buys — 'an id IS its content-hash' (§15.3) — feeds L6 incremental, which is distant. Building the merge (with its span cost) before L6 needs it is premature.
So: ps3t.3.5 stays OPEN with Inc 2 pending, gated on span-keying + L6 demand. Not the highest-value next step; the spine advances elsewhere meanwhile.

comments.author: Claude
comments.text:
INC 2 DESIGN INVESTIGATION (2026-07-09, code-verified against arena.av/parse/mod.av/content_hash.av). Resolved the two feasibility questions that gate a byte-identical interning increment:

(1) ID-VALUE LEAKAGE — SAFE. Node-id raw values do NOT appear in emitted IR (no id.raw() in codegen temp/label/name construction; codegen names by descriptor + LLVM SSA numbering). So interning changing id NUMBERING (deduped nodes don't consume ids) is byte-identical on the IR axis. diff-test will hold.

(2) SPANS — THE REAL CONSTRAINT. spans are id-keyed side-tables (DenseTable<ExprId,ByteSpan>). Interning two structurally-identical nodes at DIFFERENT source positions collapses their two spans into one -> the 2nd occurrence reports the 1st's location in errors. CRUCIAL: diff-test does NOT catch this (spans aren't in IR), so byte-identical-diff-test is necessary-but-NOT-sufficient for interning correctness. A span-occurrence-keying prerequisite (spans keyed by parent edge, not node id) is needed to intern SPANNED nodes safely.

(3) 'LEAF' IS EDGE-LESS, NOT CHILDLESS. arena add_leaf = no edge/span side-table row, but the node payload CAN carry child ids (e.g. alloc_leaf(Expr.Call(callee_id,[subject_id])) in alloc_force_unwrap_row). So 'intern leaves' != 'intern childless nodes'.

SAFE BOUNDED SLICE (byte-identical AND span-safe by construction): intern PURE-LITERAL/IDENT leaves only — Ident/Number/Bool/String/None/FloatLit etc. (no span via add_leaf; no child ids in payload; immutable). Dedups the most common nodes. Spanned/childful interning defers behind span-occurrence-keying.

(4) PAYOFF CAVEAT. The structural-equality-by-id payoff (the real prize: O(1) 'did this subtree change?' for L6 incremental) needs the L6 query-engine CONSUMER, which doesn't exist. So the pure-leaf slice delivers memory-dedup NOW with the id-equality benefit latent until L6. Full value lands WITH L6 (as the ticket's earlier note said: not startable without the consumer, else speculative machinery).

RECOMMENDATION: either (a) ship the pure-literal-leaf dedup slice (small, correct, memory-only benefit), or (b) sequence interning WITH the L6 consumer + span-occurrence-keying (the durable, full-value path). (b) is larger but avoids landing a foundation whose payoff is latent. Not a session-tail rush either way.

comments.author: Claude
comments.text: INVARIANT-GUARD INCREMENT MERGED — #681 (squash 15e518ad). Made the append-only/rebuild invariant (the precondition for content-hash interning) EXPLICIT + GUARDED: a durable note on ExprArena (append-only by design; no set_node; interning depends on it) + 3 arena_test specs (reexpr/restmt allocate a fresh id, leave the source unchanged, and inherit the source span). Mutation-verified LOAD-BEARING: aliasing reexpr (return source id vs append) breaks the compiler's OWN @std build — the passes depend on rebuild semantics. Byte-identical (diff-test PASS). This is the cheap 'keep interning possible' insurance (answers the design worry: can interning become impossible? No — append-only arenas guarantee it structurally). REMAINING for the mechanism itself (ticket stays OPEN): span-occurrence-keying (so spanned-node interning doesn't collapse per-occurrence source locations — diff-test can't catch that), then the interning dedup wired WITH the L6 consumer (the id-equality payoff needs L6; standalone = speculative machinery per the earlier design note).

comments.text:
PHASE 1 (PLAN) DONE. Branch claude/ps3t-3-4-error-nodes created off integration e1fcb314 (v104 seed, post-#658). Design = spine §14.5.

DESIGN: add Expr.Error/Stmt.Error (+ Missing for required-but-absent child slots). On a syntax error the parser emits an error-node + diagnostic and RESYNCS (panic-mode at grammar-DSL @recover points, spine §4 Layer 4) instead of bailing -> partial tree + all errors at once (daemon/LSP/LLM story). Error node's diagnostic + bad-span live in arena side-tables (like provenance/arg_tys).

M3 STRATEGY (byte-identical gate holds): error-nodes are produced ONLY on broken input. Valid programs (the difftest corpus + the selfhost source) never instantiate Expr.Error/Stmt.Error, so their emitted IR is unchanged -> diff-test byte-identical, selfhost fixed point holds. This is why §14.6 orders .3.4 as byte-identical M3-gated.

SEED-GATING (the key empirical question): Expr/Stmt are seed-processed types; adding variants may need make seed-patch-traps. BUT if every exhaustive match over Expr/Stmt in compiler src/ gets a .Error/.Missing arm (making the source exhaustive), the pinned v104 seed should compile it with no trap (it dispatches by djb2 tag, computable for any name; a fully-covered match emits no avra_match_unreachable). If it builds + selfhosts byte-identical, Phase A lands as a normal feature-branch PR (no seed cycle). If traps fire on the intermediate state, seed-patch-traps locally to iterate, but the PR must still build from the pinned seed at window-check time — so the arms must be complete.

- Phase A (types + exhaustive handling): add Expr.Error/Stmt.Error/Missing to ast.av; add render_expr/render_stmt arms; add .Error/.Missing arms to every exhaustive match (codegen, typeck, resolve, desugar, mono, fmt, eval, walker @derive). Do NOT wire the parser to produce them yet. Gate: make build + full make test + selfhost byte-identical (valid code never hits the new arms). This is the seed-gated increment — land it, let the train advance.
- Phase B (parser recovery): grammar-DSL @recover points + panic-mode synchronize(); parser emits Error node + records diagnostic/bad-span in side-tables; never bails. Tests: broken .av files -> partial tree + ALL errors (assert count + F-codes), not just the first. Combinatorial: broken expr, broken stmt, missing required slot, nested breakage, EOF-mid-construct.

comments.text:

title: [ast] AST as the single source of truth — derive every operation, kill drift
description:
UMBRELLA EPIC. Spine doc: docs/2026_06_14_AST_SOURCE_OF_TRUTH_EPIC.md

North star: the AST is defined once (enum decls); every mechanical operation over it (traverse/transform/serialize/render/dispatch) is DERIVED, never hand-written; adding a variant auto-extends every op or is a compile error. Drift becomes unrepresentable.

Six-layer spine (foundation up):
- L1 Node model: collapse SExpr/SStmt -> one node type; data-oriented (flat numbered array + side-tables keyed by node-ID); byte-offset spans. [folds 703y.1]
- L2 First-class AST in the interpreter: Value holds native nodes; the everyday encode/decode roundtrip vanishes. [finishes so07.8; shrinks s80z]
- L3 Typed identity: interned OPAQUE IDs replace string tags; strings only for printing; content-addressing drops in later. [folds so07.7, e5qo, wc5w]
- L4 Derive framework: one USER-FACING, whole-AST @derive(...) toolkit (structs + cross-type). [folds y9y4, s80z, 93k3, y9y4.18]
- L5 No-drift discipline: exhaustiveness; mostly automatic post-L4. [folds vndt]
- L6 Compiler-as-query: memoized incremental + LSP. [folds 4apk, qvfb, ggkh]
Cross-cutting: LLM-native diagnostics, --fix, AST-as-data.

Decisions 1-4 locked (see doc §5). Open: L5 aggressiveness, L6 shape, LLM-native surface, quote{} rework-not-retire. See doc §9.
acceptance_criteria: All layer epics ps3t.1-.9 closed; success metrics (ps3t.10) met; differential tests + selfhost byte-identical green; the hand-written AST walkers/codecs/encode-decode mirrors deleted; bd grep for construct_stmt/enum_value_to_stmt clean.

title: bd auto-sync silently no-ops: wrapper treats 'no remote configured' skip as success
description: On Claude-Code-Web, the bd sync wrapper (scripts/bootstrap.sh setup_beads_sync) ran 'bd dolt push origin' which printed 'No remote is configured — skipping' and exited 0, so the wrapper's 'if dolt push; then cat manifest > last_synced' recorded a FALSE 'synced' on every mutating command — a whole session's closures (sdmg epic, 9908, sdmg.2, 4m1e) never reached refs/dolt/data (stuck at 8f70e81). Two root causes: (1) setup_beads_sync's 'bd dolt remote add origin' did not result in a configured Dolt remote (the remote was absent at session start despite the wrapper being installed), so every push was a no-op; (2) the wrapper cannot distinguish a real push from a skipped no-op because both exit 0 — it should verify a remote exists (bd dolt remote list) before recording last_synced, and ideally confirm refs/dolt/data actually advanced. Compounding: containers init independent Dolt lineages (jsonl fallback / no common merge base), so reconciliation needs a force-push — fragile for multi-agent. Recovery performed this session: re-added the dolt remote, verified local is a superset of refs/dolt/data (the only remote-only items were 2 disposable __DIAG__/__MANI__ diagnostic markers), and force-pushed (refs/dolt/data 8f70e81 -> d3a0b0f). Fix: make setup_beads_sync verify the remote is configured and the push transferred; have the wrapper refuse to advance last_synced on a skipped/failed push.

title: Deliberate-SIGABRT crash test's containment is batch-composition fragile (adding a test file flips it)
description: capture_thread_isolation_test.av's 'a crash inside a capture window is caught' deliberately raises SIGABRT mid-capture and is DESIGNED to not kill the bundle (guard longjmp + per-thread sink unwinding reclaims the orphan capture frame). In isolation the file exits 0. But the containment is fragile to the parallel runner's batch packing: adding ONE unrelated test file (PR #524's seed_self_contained_test.av) reshuffled batches and flipped the suite from 2988/2988 green to '1 spec(s) crashed' — and AVRA_TEST_JOBS=1 made it worse (2 sibling assertions also failed), so the escaping SIGABRT corrupts/aborts batch-mates rather than being contained. Likely interaction: a sibling unit mid avra_shell_exec (fork/waitpid) when the SIGABRT fires. Root-cause fix: make a unit's deliberate abort containment independent of which files share its batch (e.g. run the deliberate-crash unit solo, or harden the longjmp/sink unwind against concurrent fork). Workaround used in #524: fold the new spec into an existing file so the file-set (and thus batch packing) matches the green baseline. Same family as d4jv (in-process test parallelism) / irh4 (shard packing nondeterminism).
notes: FLAKY, not deterministic, and broader than first thought: in one /prepare-pr session the SAME suite ran green (2993/2993) and 'N spec(s) crashed' on different runs with identical sources. At least THREE deliberate-crash tests share the fragile containment and can each escape their batch: capture_thread_isolation_test.av:52 (SIGABRT), crash_isolation_test.av:18 (SIGABRT), crash_isolation_edges_test.av:20/27 (SIGABRT/SIGFPE). When containment holds the suite is green; when a crash escapes the batch it's tallied as 'crashed' (and JOBS=1 also surfaced sibling assertion failures). This makes the spec-suite gate (pre-commit + CI) nondeterministic for ANY change that perturbs batch packing/timing — raised to P1 since it undermines CI determinism project-wide. Root-cause direction: the SIGABRT/longjmp + per-thread sink unwind races with sibling units (notably ones mid avra_shell_exec fork/waitpid) in the same @deferred_init batch; fix = run deliberate-crash units solo, or make the signal/longjmp containment thread-safe across the batch.
close_reason: Per-file crash introspection getters landed in #692 (squash a1517264). Crash-isolation test assertions now filter the process-global crash list by their own source-file basename, so concurrent deliberate crashes across files no longer race the global count/index reads. Validated: 3 crash files in one shard (8 workers) 15/15 deterministic x5; rc-strict + seed-train-verify green.

comments.author: Claude
comments.text: RUNTIME ROOT CAUSE pinpointed (2026-07-10, surfaced blocking PR #692). The crash record + ack live in a PROCESS-GLOBAL list: runtime.c:4681 avra_test_record_crash appends to static _crashes (a record_list with an atomic count); :4701 avra_test_ack_expected_crash does atomic_fetch_sub(&_crashes.count, 1); :4705-4708 avra_test_crash_spec/signal(idx) read _crashes by ABSOLUTE INDEX. Under AVRA_TEST_JOBS parallel WORKER THREADS (d4jv), crash_isolation_edges_test.av + crash_isolation_test.av — both deliberately crash — record/ack/read into that ONE shared list concurrently: (a) absolute-index reads (idx 0/1) point at the other file's crash (ioi0), and (b) the global-count ack races so a deliberately-crashed spec can be left 'live' and reported as an unexpected '✗ SPEC CRASHED' (4m1e, the actual failure seen). Deterministic-ish given batch composition + worker assignment; adding ANY test file (e.g. #692's lambda_param_types_test.av) reshuffles the batching into a losing configuration → blocks the PR. CLEAN FIX: scope the crash list + ack + count PER WORKER THREAD (thread-local _crashes), so each file's deliberate crashes record/ack/read in isolation. CAVEAT: the final 'Crashed specs:' reporter reads _crashes to print all crashes — if it runs on the main thread, a naive thread-local breaks aggregation; so the fix needs per-thread record+ack for the running assertions AND a merge into a global for the end-of-run report (two-level). Simpler alternative: run the two deliberate-crash files serially/exclusively (a runner directive) or merge them into one file so their crashes are sequential on one thread. This is a subtle concurrency fix — do it as a careful dedicated pass, not rushed. Unblocks #692 + EVERY future test-adding PR (the infra-fragility tax).

title: CI seed train: auto-cycle the seed on integration-branch pushes
description: Encode the owner's intended loop end-to-end: feature branches never cycle (enforced, sdmg.2); after a merge lands on feat/crafting-intepreters, CI — not a human — advances the train: rebuild bs2 from the merged source, verify selfhost fixed point + suite, 'make seed-publish' (release seed/vN+1 via GH_TOKEN, bump seed.lock), commit the lock bump back to the integration branch as 'chore(seed): cycle'. Serialize via workflow concurrency group so two merges can't race a publish. Skip when the seed content is unchanged (no new dogfoodable surface). After this lands, dogfood latency = merge + one CI run.
notes: Fix for the first-run failure is PR #524 (commit de54290): mode_seed_train now recompiles main.av hermetically (metadata fast-path stripped) before the divergence check + update-seed, so the pinned seed always DEFINES its @std symbols (self-contained); plus a seed_is_self_contained guard (--seed-self-contained) + spec tests/seed_self_contained_test.av (mutation-checked). Stays OPEN until the next live train run (post-#524-merge) publishes seed/v2 green.
close_reason: DONE — first live run is green end-to-end. After #524 merged (744d7f1), seed-train run 27473630407 built bs2 from the pin, held the fixed point, passed the full suite, hermetically regenerated a self-contained seed, detected divergence, published the seed/v2 release (seed.ll.gz, verify-before-publish + smoke passed), and committed 'chore(seed): cycle to v2' (5e1cfa3) bumping seed.lock to version=2. The CI train advances the pin with no human in the loop; dogfood latency is now merge + one CI run.

title: bs2's Avra-side LLVM prefix resolution was macOS-only — Linux 'bs2 test' fails every shard link
description:
On a fresh Linux box without LLVM_PREFIX exported, every Avra-side site that links or shells out to llc fell back to /opt/homebrew/opt/llvm: build/link.av resolve_llvm_prefix, build/compile.av coverage path, build/cache.av realobj llc, test_runner cached_fixture_compile_and_run, and three sites in cli/main.av. Result: make build works (diagnose.sh self-discovers LLVM 20) but make test fails all 76 shards with 'unable to find library -lLLVM'.

Fix: one exported probe @std.avrac.build.link.llvm_prefix_dir() (env wins, then pinned-major platform locations, then Homebrew default) — all seven sites delegate. Plus: collect_workspace_lib_objs no longer globs cache/*/unit.realobj.o by newest mtime (a stale slot lazily materialized later shadowed the fresh slot → undefined symbols for newly added @std exports); it reads the driver's last/<pkg>.txt fp sidecar to pick the exact slot for the current source+compiler state. Fixtures (multi_unit_link, dir_module_e2e) now use the shared probe; regression spec at packages/std-avrac/src/build/tests/llvm_prefix_test.av.
close_reason: Implemented, spec-tested (llvm_prefix_test.av + the previously-failing link fixtures), full suite 2944/2944 + selfhost fixed point, committed as df93979.

title: [bootstrap] Seed-merge hardening — make cross-branch seed merges boring (epic)
description:
# Goal

Make cross-branch seed merges boring. The 2026-06-11 merge of slice/xm2g.8b into feat/crafting-intepreters took hours of bootstrap archaeology because BOTH branches had cycled their seeds past their own features: the union source was compilable by NEITHER seed (ours predated their extern-signature refactor + redeclare guard; theirs predated the zm77 RC fixes). Resolution required staging: their seed -> seed-patch-traps -> IR-level patch on the intermediate binary -> recompile -> update-seed -> fixed point.

This is the classic self-hosting bootstrap-merge problem. Prior art:
- Rust/Go: pin-don't-vendor — bootstrap from a PINNED prior release (stage0 hash file in repo, artifact external). Bootstrap-window rule: compiler source must always build with the pinned seed; new features can't be used in the compiler until the pin advances. cfg(bootstrap) straddles transitions. Enforced by CI on every PR => any two mergeable branches are compilable by the same seed BY CONSTRUCTION.
- OCaml: vendors boot/ocamlc, survives via ceremony — seed updates are dedicated maintainer commits; merge resolution is always 'take either, re-bootstrap, recommit'.
- Zig: vendors a tiny zig1.wasm that only compiles a restricted-subset stage2; the subset changes rarely so the seed updates a few times a year.

Children (independent, in rollout order):
1. sdmg.1 — .gitattributes: seed.ll -diff merge=binary + doc the regenerate-only resolution
2. sdmg.2 — bootstrap window + seed train: feature branches never cycle the seed; CI builds every PR from the integration branch's seed
3. sdmg.3 — pin-don't-vendor: seed.lock (version+sha256) + release-artifact hosting
4. sdmg.4 — minimal stage-1 seed kernel (Zig model) + seed tolerance (redeclare guard warns on predeclare-vs-source drift during bootstrap)
5. sdmg.5 — diagnose.sh --seed-merge: one-command automation of the staging dance
close_reason: DONE — all 5 children closed with real completed work; cross-branch seed merges are now boring. Shipped: sdmg.1 (.gitattributes binary-merge + SEED_MERGES doc), sdmg.3 (pin-don't-vendor: seed.lock + GitHub-release hosting), sdmg.4 (bootstrap-tolerant extern guard; the Zig-kernel half was owner-rejected), sdmg.5 (diagnose.sh --seed-merge staging automation), sdmg.2 (bootstrap-window gate + CI seed train). Proven end-to-end: feature branches never cycle the seed (pre-push + CI gate, enforced on #521/#524), and after a merge the CI train advances the pin with no human in the loop — run 27473630407 published seed/v2 and committed the lock bump. The '2026-06-11 neither-seed-can-compile-the-union' merge state is now unrepresentable by construction. Follow-up bug surfaced during the work: 4m1e (flaky deliberate-crash containment in the parallel test runner, P1) — independent of this epic.

title: gitattributes: seed.ll -diff merge=binary + SEED_MERGES.md regenerate-only doc
description:
Mark the seed as the binary artifact it is:

    bootstrap/seed/seed.ll -diff merge=binary

- Merge conflicts stop attempting a 500k-line text merge; resolution becomes 'checkout one side, regenerate via make update-seed' — the only correct resolution anyway.
- Diffs/PRs stop being dominated by seed churn (2026-06-11 merge: ~124k of 127k changed lines were seed).
- Document the regenerate-only rule + the staging recipe (patch-traps, choose-base-seed criteria) in bootstrap/docs/SEED_MERGES.md and link from CLAUDE.md.

Acceptance: git merge of two seed-divergent branches shows seed.ll as a binary conflict; doc exists; CLAUDE.md links it.

CLOSED: .gitattributes added (seed.ll -diff merge=binary), bootstrap/docs/SEED_MERGES.md written (regenerate-only rule, base-seed selection criteria, staging last-resort, prevention pointers), CLAUDE.md links it.

title: Bootstrap window + seed train: feature branches never cycle the seed; CI builds PRs from the integration seed
description:
The real fix — adopt Rust's bootstrap-window rule, enforced:

- Feature branches NEVER cycle the seed: no seed.ll commits, no dogfooding of new surface syntax / enum variants in compiler src until the integration seed has advanced past them (CLAUDE.md Phase A/B discipline, promoted to enforced invariant).
- Seed advancement = dedicated 'chore(seed): cycle' commits on the integration branch only (the seed train), serialized after merges land.
- Enforcement: a CI / pre-push check that builds the branch's source FROM THE INTEGRATION BRANCH'S PRISTINE SEED (fetch origin/feat/crafting-intepreters:bootstrap/seed/seed.ll, build, run smoke). If it fails, the branch used post-seed features in compiler src — reject.

With this, any two branches that pass CI are compilable by the same seed by construction; the 2026-06-11 'no seed can compile the union' state becomes unrepresentable.

Optional transition affordance: @seed_compat conditional blocks (cfg(bootstrap) analogue) if dual-compiler source windows are ever needed.

Acceptance: CI check exists and gates; CLAUDE.md updated; one full feature->integration cycle ridden through the train.
notes: CI window gate: COMPLETE (green across #521 + #524 pushes). Seed train: the first live run after #521 correctly caught a real bug (non-self-contained candidate under CI metadata fast-path) — fix in PR #524. REMAINING before close: (1) the next live train run publishes seed/v2 (the one full feature->integration cycle); (2) user-side: mark 'bootstrap-window' a required check in branch protection.
close_reason: DONE — all acceptance criteria met. (1) The bootstrap-window gate exists and gates: it ran on every PR into the integration branch (#521, #524) and is enforced on push via the pre-push hook. (2) CLAUDE.md documents the bootstrap-window + seed-train policy and the self-contained-seed invariant. (3) One full feature->integration cycle has been ridden through the train: #524 merged -> seed-train run 27473630407 published seed/v2 and committed the 'chore(seed): cycle to v2' lock bump. Optional residual (repo-admin, outside ticket scope): mark 'bootstrap-window' a REQUIRED status check in branch protection for server-side enforcement on top of the pre-push hook.

title: fixture-stdout cache freezes environment-state failures (PROBE ...: FAIL is cacheable by design)
description:
Twice in one session (2026-06-11) a cached fixture capture froze a transient failure into a persistent test failure that survived the fix to the underlying state:

1. derive_walker fixtures captured null-deref output from a mis-placed zero-init build; toolchain fp changed with the fix, so this self-healed.
2. cli_metadata_compile's 'PROBE std_cli_meta_present: FAIL' was captured while packages/std-cli's build/cache held a stale half-published state. The toolchain fp (bs2+runtime+wrapper+src hashes) did NOT change when the package cache state was later repaired, so the poisoned capture kept serving until build/cache/fixture_stdout was hand-cleared.

The publishability filter deliberately can't reject generic FAIL/PROBE tokens (zp5b: many tests assert on F-codes). The gap: fixture outputs that depend on MUTABLE ENVIRONMENT STATE (package build caches, meta slots) are cached under a key that doesn't include that state.

Options (pick during implementation):
- Let fixtures declare extra cache-key inputs (e.g. a glob of package cache dirs) via a comment pragma the runner hashes.
- A probe(...) convention: fixtures emit 'PROBE-STATEFUL' markers that make the capture non-publishable when any probe FAILs (a fixture asserting an expected failure would use plain output, not probe()).
- Self-healing probes: meta-presence probes trigger the producer build themselves before asserting (cli_metadata's fixture already pre-builds; the failure came from a corrupt half-published slot the pre-build cache-hit didn't repair — which is arguably its own bug: cache-hit restore should validate the slot).

Repro of the incident class: corrupt packages/std-cli/build/cache (leave _tmp staging junk), run cli_metadata_compile_test cold, fix the package cache, re-run — the FAIL persists until fixture_stdout is cleared.
close_reason: Stateful-fixture cache freeze fixed: a fixture probing SHARED build state (packages/*/build, outside the cache key) opts in via the FIXTURE_STATEFUL_MARKER source directive; fixture_is_stateful reads it from the SOURCE (robust to mid-capture kills) and fixture_output_is_publishable rejects any ': FAIL' from such a fixture, so a corrupt/half-published shared-cache state re-probes next run instead of freezing. Applied to the two hazard fixtures (cli_metadata_compile, std_avrac_lib_build). Tested (publishability unit + source-directive detection + drift-guard contracts), mutation-verified. Root-cause residual (cache-hit slot validation) tracked separately as kaux. Suite 3488/3488, selfhost byte-identical.

title: [memory] RC-correctness hardening — make the zm77 phantom-release class impossible
description:
# Goal

Make the zm77 bug class — compiler-inserted RC bookkeeping disagreeing with actual control flow — structurally impossible, not just patched.

## Background (zm77 post-mortem)

ctx.bind registered RC-cleanup slots that were only initialized at the declaration site; a zero-trip loop (any zero-arg call through fill_arg_array_boxing) made the function epilogue release uninitialized stack garbage. Every zero-arg call site phantom-released 8 bytes of garbage for an unknown period; it only surfaced when the garbage aliased a live AST node, which got freed mid-codegen — 'unsupported expression type (tag=<heap ptr>)'. Diagnosis required a gdb hardware watchpoint; the earlier pass-bisection (mono) was wrong. Full writeup: bootstrap/docs/927f_union_match_mono_bug.md.

The fix (zero-init cleanup slots at function entry, avra_llvm_zero_init_local) closes the hole. This epic closes the CLASS, in five layers:

1. rcsf.1 — invariant by construction: registration+init as one atomic chokepoint
2. rcsf.2 — IR verifier: definite-init of release-fed slots, checked in CI
3. rcsf.3 — strict allocator mode: make RC misuse loud (poison-on-free, quarantine, abort on foreign release)
4. rcsf.4 — phase arenas for the AST: compiler data structures out of the RC heap entirely (spec Axis 9)
5. rcsf.5 — drop elaboration + block-scoped cleanup: cleanup generated from definite-initialization analysis

Order: .1/.2 close the regression door cheaply; .3 is the highest bug-detection ROI; .4 is the architecturally right home for the AST; .5 is the v1.0-grade language answer.

title: IR verifier: every release-fed alloca must have a dominating entry-block store (AVRA_VERIFY_RC)
description:
# Goal

An IR-level verifier for the cleanup invariant: every alloca whose loaded value flows into avra_rc_release / __release_* must have a store in the entry block.

## Why

Invariants that are only established are one refactor away from broken; invariants independently CHECKED stay fixed (same philosophy as the bs2≡bs3 fixed-point check, applied to memory semantics). zm77 shipped because nothing checked the emitted IR against the RC model.

## Work

- Post-codegen pass over the LLVM module using the existing C-API bindings (~50 lines): for each call to avra_rc_release / __release_*, walk the operand back to its alloca (through loads); require a dominating entry-block store.
- Wire into codegen_program behind a debug/CI flag (e.g. AVRA_VERIFY_RC=1) and into scripts/diagnose.sh (centralized per CLAUDE.md rule 10).
- Run it in the pre-commit/CI path for the selfhost build.

## Acceptance

- Reverting the zm77 zero-init fix makes the verifier fail the build with a named function + slot diagnostic.
- Clean build passes with the verifier on; suite green.

UPDATE 2026-06-11 (merge 3f8798a9): with the universal guard in avra_llvm_build_alloca, the verifier simplifies to: every `alloca ptr` instruction's next instruction must be `store ptr null` into it (all allocas route through the wrapper). Checkable in C inside llvm_wrapper.c with a module walk; gate on AVRA_VERIFY_RC=1.

CLOSED: avra_llvm_verify_rc_init (llvm_wrapper.c) walks the finished module asserting every ptr alloca's next instruction is its null store; called at codegen_program's tail under AVRA_VERIFY_RC=1; wired into diagnose.sh's self-compile integrity check so every commit-grade build verifies the compiler's own module (16736 allocas, 0 violations). Acceptance proven: with the guard disabled, the verifier fails the build naming fn+slot ('VIOLATION: fn main — alloca %s lacks an immediate null store'). Spec test: tests/verify_rc_init_test.av.

title: Strict allocator mode (AVRA_RC_STRICT): poison-on-free, reuse quarantine, abort on foreign-pointer release
description:
# Goal

Strict allocator mode (AVRA_RC_STRICT=1): make RC misuse loud instead of silently absorbable.

## Why

avra_rc_free is forgiving: releasing garbage that isn't in the rc_set is a silent no-op. zm77's phantom releases ran at EVERY zero-arg call site for an unknown period and only surfaced when garbage aliased a live node. Under a strict mode, the very first zero-arg call would have aborted with a backtrace — a 10-minute bug instead of a multi-session hunt.

## Work

- AVRA_RC_STRICT=1 in runtime.c: (a) poison-on-free (memset freed payload with 0xDD), (b) delayed-reuse quarantine (freelist holdback, reuse existing AVRA_REDZONES/AVRA_PAGE_ALLOC machinery where it fits), (c) abort with backtrace when a release-typed path receives a heap-range pointer that is not a live RC allocation.
- Distinguish legitimate non-RC no-ops (LLVM ValueRefs, stack, text) from heap-range foreign pointers — the existing region heuristics in avra_trace_ptr are a starting point.
- CI job: run the spec suite under AVRA_RC_STRICT=1.

## Acceptance

- Reverting the zm77 fix and running any zero-arg-call test under strict mode aborts at the phantom release with a backtrace naming the releasing function.
- Full suite green under strict mode (no false positives).
notes:
DONE + committed (2c86c41, branch claude/high-impact-ticket-selection-lfaqb2, pushed). AVRA_RC_STRICT=1 in runtime.c — all three screws, every branch flag-gated (non-strict path byte-identical; verified fixed point holds, bs2==bs3 601357-line IR):
(a) poison-on-free: freed payloads memset 0xDD. Strict allocs carry an 8-byte payload-size prefix BEFORE the RC header so poison is size-exact; header stays at ptr-8 so codegen is untouched.
(b) reuse quarantine: freed blocks held in a bounded FIFO ring (16384) + O(1) open-addressing hash-set for membership; real free only on ring eviction.
(c) foreign-release abort: avra_rc_release/should_free/retain of a pointer into a freed-and-quarantined block aborts with the F9999 breadcrumb (phase/fn-trail/stmt) + C backtrace. Membership is tested against blocks the runtime ACTUALLY froze — never an address-range guess — so ZERO false positives on the legitimate non-RC no-ops these paths also see (NULL/stack/text/LLVM ValueRefs/bump-arena). Bonus: the quarantine converts the silent zm77 case — freed memory is no longer recycled into live objects, so a phantom release of a stale pointer hits DEAD quarantined memory (caught) instead of a recycled-live object (silent corruption).

ACCEPTANCE:
(2) full suite green under strict, no false positives — PROVEN: AVRA_RC_STRICT=1 bs2 test = 3586/3586, 0 strict aborts, with the COMPILER ITSELF running strict as it compiled+ran every test binary.
(1) stale release aborts with backtrace naming the fn — PROVEN deterministically by a runtime self-test hook (avra_rc_strict_selftest_stale_release: alloc->release->stale-release), the exact zm77 signature (a release path receiving a pointer to reclaimed RC memory); it aborts with the diagnostic+backtrace (negative spec test PASS). The LITERAL 'revert the zero-init guard' variant is inherently intermittent — zm77 only surfaced 'when garbage aliased a [specific] node', a probabilistic stack-aliasing event, and is confounded by test-binary caching. I verified via a temporary env-gate that reverting the guard produces genuinely vulnerable IR (6->0 null-stores), but a small repro did not deterministically alias a quarantined block, so it stayed silent (correct: strict aborts only on a genuine stale-quarantined-block release, not on arbitrary non-dangling garbage). The deterministic, cache-immune hook is the superior proof; env-gate fully reverted, tree clean.

WIRING: diagnose.sh --rc-strict-suite (centralized, rule 10) + .github/workflows/rc-strict.yml (per-PR gate, mirrors rcsf.2). Spec: tests/rc_strict_test.av (3/3). Runbook: docs/RC_MEMORY_RUNBOOK.md. Chosen as a high-impact ticket that does NOT touch ps3t's active frontend churn (runtime.c allocator only). Parent rcsf stays OPEN (.1/.4/.5 remain; .4 phase-arenas intersects ps3t L1).

title: Generic struct field access loses the type parameter: Box<int>.val types as T (F1003)
description: Accessing a field of a generic struct keeps the unsubstituted type-param instead of the concrete type. Repro: type Box<T> = { val: T }; let b: Box<int> = Box { val: 5 }; string(b.val) errors F1003 "type T cannot be converted to string". The field b.val should type as int (the instance is Box<int>) but stays T. Reproduces WITHOUT optionals (Box<int> and Box<int?> both fail), so it is a general generic-struct field-type-substitution gap, orthogonal to nullability; surfaced while probing optional-in-generic-struct during xm2g.8 Part B prepare-pr round 4. Fix belongs with the monomorphizer / field-type resolution: when resolving a field access on a generic struct instance, substitute the struct decl type-params with the instance type-args before typing the field.
notes:
ROOT CAUSE confirmed: ValueType.Struct(name, id) has NO type_args slot (vs Enum(name, type_args, id)). So a generic struct instance can't carry its instantiation, and typeck (runs before mono) types s.value as the unsubstituted T. Lenient contexts (s.value == 5) pass; strict ones bite: fn -> int { s.value } => F1000 'body produces T'; string(s.value) => F1003. Repro: type MaBox<T>={value:T}; fn f()->int { let s=MaBox{value:5}; s.value } => F1000.

FORK (needs design call):
 A) Give ValueType.Struct a type_args slot mirroring Enum, then substitute at field access. CLEAN / matches Enum (rule 16). But it is a ValueType variant-shape change the seed processes => SEED-GATED (89 .Struct( match sites; needs seed-patch-traps + integration seed cycle). CANNOT land on a feature branch per the bootstrap window — must be done on the integration branch + seed train.
 B) typeck-side instantiation tracking: stamp a distinct Struct id per instantiation + a TC side-table id->type_args, substitute at field access. Non-seed-gated, but an indirection that duplicates Enum's inline model (arguably the parallel-side-table anti-pattern rule 16 warns against).

RECOMMENDATION: A (architecturally correct, matches Enum). Requires integration-branch coordination + a seed cycle, which is outside the current feature branch's mandate. Blocks agcv. Note agcv is ALSO blocked on other seed-gated features (nested generics List<Edges<Id>> via >> lexing; type-param-as-newtype-ctor Id(x); method-on-type-param id.raw() via bound), so the arena collapse as a whole is an integration-coordinated effort.
close_reason: Gave ValueType.Struct a type_args slot (mirroring Enum): construction infers args from field inits/annotation (tc_infer_struct_type_args), field access substitutes the struct's type-params with the instance args (vtype_subst_params), codegen reclassifies monomorphized generic-struct annotations Enum->Struct. 89 sites updated. Repros fixed: fn f()->int{let s=MaBox{value:5} s.value} and let b:Box<int>=...;string(b.val). Full suite 3029/3029 + selfhost byte-identical. Committed 5632ee95 on feat/crafting-intepreters; seed advanced (update-seed, self-contained verified); seed-train pins on push.

title: @marshal drops optional (T?) fields: a present value round-trips to none (silent data loss)
description: A @marshal struct/enum with a T? field loses the field across a serialize/deserialize (isolated_) round-trip: a present value comes back as none. Repro: @marshal type B = { v: int? }; produce B { v: 5 }; isolated_B(produce) yields Ok(b) with b.v == none (the if-let takes the else branch). Same for a niche field (str? "hi" -> none) and presumably float?/bool?. The w:int sibling field round-trips fine, so the framing is correct; only the optional field is dropped. Root: the @marshal derive (features/marshal/derive.av build_writes/build_reads + codegen/setup.av resolve_setup_vt) has no case for Optional, so it neither writes a present-flag + inner nor reads one back; the field deserializes to the null/none default. Pre-existing gap exposed by xm2g.8 Part B making T? a real boxed/niche repr (before, optional fields were not a distinct shape). High severity: SILENT data corruption, not a crash. Fix: teach the marshal derive to emit, per optional field, a 1-byte present flag then (if present) the inner value, and the symmetric read. Orthogonal to the core null-safety surface (the slice does not use marshal); surfaced during xm2g.8 Part B prepare-pr round 4.
close_reason: MERGED — PR #673 (squash 8fc3a85) into feat/crafting-intepreters. @marshal now round-trips optional (T?) fields (present value survives, absent stays null) instead of silently dropping present values to none. Presence-bool + inner-value codec via shared write_one/read_one dispatch, covering optional over primitive / nested @marshal struct / List<T>, in both struct fields and enum-variant payloads; codec_supported guards unsupported inners (graceful lossy-skip, no raw error). All CI green (diff-test byte-identical 641313-line selfhost + corpus, window, rc-strict, seed-train-verify, publish-seed-verify-pass); CodeRabbit clean. 14 spec fixtures, mutation-verified (ctor-binding + value-write both load-bearing). grammar.md updated (T? moved from open to supported). The f1005_nullable_omit parallel-shard flake (uzs9.2) blocked the merge twice; cleared on the 3rd re-trigger.

title: [null] Sound flow narrowing — bind-fresh model (Rust/Zig), retire retype-the-variable
description:
Make narrowing SOUND (spec 10.4, now decided as bind-fresh). A presence check introduces a NEW IMMUTABLE binding for the unwrapped value; the original variable is never retyped, so no mutable 'narrowed variable' exists for a later write to invalidate (the Rust `if let Some(v)` / Zig `if (x) |v|` model). Surface: `if let v? = x { use(v) }`, `let v? = x else { return }`, match arm `v?` (links os1o for the `if let` parser sugar). Variable-form sugar (`if x != none { x.field }`, `if x == none { return }; x.field`) is accepted ONLY when x is effectively-final (a `let`, or a `mut` neither reassigned nor aliased after the check) and desugars to a fresh binding; ANY reassignment drops the narrowing. This is the difference between TypeScript-class and Rust/Zig-class null safety. REPRO of the hole this closes: `mut x: int? = 5; if x != none { x = g() /* int? */; let y = x? }` currently compiles with no F1202 — must become an error. BLOCKS gating (xm2g.5): gating must build on this, never on the retype model. Foundation: depends in spirit on checker-soundness work (cpvo, so07).

=== PART B SURFACE DESIGN (decided 2026-06-09, LLM-first) ===
Principle: ONE promoted way to unwrap, locally readable, high training prior, no new `?` meanings, and the compiler prints the canonical form on every miss.

CANONICAL — bind-fresh `if let` (Swift-style; NO `?` on the bound name — optionality comes from the subject's type). Works for let/mut/param/field uniformly; always sound (v is a fresh immutable binding, nothing can invalidate it). This is THE way to unwrap.
    if let v = x { use(v) } else { absent }      // x: T?  ->  v: T in the then-branch

LET-ELSE — early exit on absence (Rust `let ... else`; NO new `guard` keyword). The else block MUST diverge (return/break/continue/panic). Binds v for the REST of the scope.
    let v = x else { return not_found() }         // v: T in the continuation

MATCH — rare for optionals (if-let/else/??/?. cover most). Present arm uses `let` to bind, CONSISTENT with `if let` (one rule everywhere: `let <name>` binds the present value). The `let` is load-bearing: it disambiguates 'bind present' from a catch-all `u` wildcard.
    match x { let u -> u.name, none -> "anonymous" }

COMPOSITION with Result<T?, E> (error AND absence). Each keyword peels exactly ONE type layer, left-to-right; order is enforced by types (else/?? only apply to T?, so they must follow the Result-peeler):
    ?  / catch  -> peel the Result   (error layer)
    else / ??   -> peel the Option   (absence layer)
    let         -> bind what remains (T)
    // find(id): Result<User?, string>
    let user = find(id) catch (e) { return server_error(e) } else { return not_found() }  // catch: Result->User?, else: User?->User
    let user = find(id)? else { return ok(not_found()) }                                  // ? propagates Err, else peels none

ABSENCE LAYER — `??` vs `else` (keep BOTH; not redundant):
    ??   = value fallback of the SAME type T, then continue:   let u = find(id) ?? guest_user()   // u: User
    else = early exit (diverge, any type):                     let u = find(id) else { return not_found() }
    `??` CANNOT express the early-exit/return-a-different-type case (the dominant web-handler pattern), which is exactly what `else` is for. Both compose identically with catch.
    Guidance the diagnostic should give: have a sensible same-type default -> `??`; no value, must bail -> `else { return/break/continue }`.

VARIABLE NARROWING (Part A) is now SUGAR layered on bind-fresh, not a parallel mechanism. `if x != none { x.f }` narrows only IMMUTABLE bindings (sound by construction). When it can't fire (x is mut), the compiler does NOT silently fail — it emits a diagnostic whose `help:` prints the canonical rewrite. The error text IS the teaching signal for agents (ties to xm2g.7 diagnostics contract):
    error[F1200]: `x` may be `none` here
    help: bind the present value (always works): if let v = x { v.f } else { ... }
    help: or exit early:                          let v = x else { return default() }

EXPLICITLY: the bound name carries NO `?` (drops the would-be 5th overload of `?`). `none` stays the absence literal. Rust/Zig parallel: this is `if let Some(v)` / `if (x) |v|`, surfaced Swift-style.
acceptance_criteria: bind-fresh `if let v? = x` / `let v? = x else {}` / match `v?` implemented and sound; variable narrowing accepted only for effectively-final vars and dropped on reassignment; the repro above is rejected (F1200/F1202 as appropriate); a narrowed-then-reassigned/aliased var never yields a non-null type. build/test/selfhost green.

title: List<T?> literal elements not boxed — Some(0)/Some(false)/Some(0.0) collide with none in collections
description:
Value-inner optionals (int?/bool?/float?) box a present value into a non-null cell at scalar assignment boundaries (let/struct-field/fn-return/fn-arg/enum-field/with/global) — xm2g.3. But LIST-LITERAL elements are NOT coerced: emit_list_lit (features/list_lit/codegen.av) infers the element type bottom-up from the FIRST element and pushes each element raw, with no optional boxing. So a present zero in a List<T?> aliases none.

REPRO (all via diagnose.sh --run):
  let a: List<int?> = [0]        -> a[0] == null   (BUG: Some(0) read as none)
  let c: List<int?> = [0, null]  -> c[0] == null   (BUG)
  let d: List<int?> = [5, null]  -> d[0] != null   (OK — only because 5 != 0; non-zero present values pass by luck)
Same applies to bool? (false) and float? (0.0). Non-zero/true/non-0.0 present values happen to work because they differ from the null pointer's 0.

ROOT CAUSE: list-literal codegen has no access to the EXPECTED element type (List<int?> from the binding) and does no element coercion. Two facets:
  (1)  infers List<int> from the first element; the null does not widen elem_ty to int?.
  (2) Even with the right element type, elements aren't boxed via emit_optional_some/emit_optional_coerce.

PROPER FIX needs bidirectional typing: thread the expected element type down into emit_list_lit (and map_lit) so each element is coerced with emit_optional_coerce, OR recurse emit_optional_coerce into List/Map element types at the assignment site (requires runtime element re-box). A localized 'widen across elements' heuristic would fix [0,null] but NOT annotated [0] — brittle, rejected (no-heuristics rule).

SCOPE: not a regression (collections were fully broken before xm2g.3's repr work); the self-hosting compiler does not depend on List<value-optional>-with-zero (selfhost byte-identical green). This is the collection-element boundary of the same value-optional work; belongs with the bidirectional expected-type-flow that Phase 4 gating (xm2g.5) tightens.

ASIDE (separate, pre-existing): Map<K,V> '[]'-READ ICEs for ANY value type ('indexing on non-string/list value', F9999) — e.g. Map<string,int>["k"] — so the map-optional case can't even be exercised yet. Distinct pre-existing gap, not optional-related.

Found during prepare-pr (3rd pass) on the nullability PR via a cross-construct correctness probe (match-expr / closure / struct-field all correctly box; list literals do not).
close_reason: Fixed in xm2g.8 Part B (PR #19): List<T?> literal elements boxed via emit_optional_list_lit (expected-type threaded at annotated-binding + call-arg sites, plus none-detection). Some(0)/Some(false)/Some(0.0) now distinct from none in every list construction context. Regression: list_optional_test.av. Deferred: non-literal/nested -> nztt; Map<K,V?> -> ks8q.

title: diagnose.sh silently falls back to LLVM 18 llc on Linux (emits-then-rejects nuw GEP)
description: scripts/diagnose.sh LLC resolution hardcodes macOS Homebrew paths (LLC_PREFIX=/opt/homebrew/Cellar/llvm/20.1.5, LLVM_PREFIX=/opt/homebrew/opt/llvm). On a Linux container neither exists, so it falls through to $LLVM_PREFIX/bin/llc then `command -v llc` = /usr/bin/llc -> /usr/lib/llvm-18/bin/llc. The compiler's codegen emits LLVM 19+ IR (`getelementptr inbounds nuw ...`); LLVM 18.1.3 llc rejects the nuw GEP flag with 'expected type', so a cold-cache `make build-quick` FAILS on Linux unless LLC/LLC_PREFIX/LLVM_PREFIX are manually set to llvm-20. The diagnose.sh comment already states intent ('Use LLVM 20 llc for code generation') — the resolution just doesn't find llvm-20 on Linux. FIX: before the bare-`llc` fallback, probe for llc-20 / /usr/lib/llvm-20/bin/llc (and a versioned llc-NN >= 20) so Linux finds the right toolchain automatically. Repro: rm -rf packages/cli/src/build/cache build/bs2 packages/cli/src/main.av.ll && make build-quick  (fails); same with LLC=/usr/bin/llc-20 LLC_PREFIX=/usr/lib/llvm-20 LLVM_PREFIX=/usr/lib/llvm-20 (succeeds). Surfaced during prepare-pr on the nullability PR; orthogonal to nullability, not bundled into that diff.
close_reason: diagnose.sh now probes for an LLVM-20 toolchain (llvm-config-20 / /usr/lib/llvm-20 / llc-20) before the unversioned llvm-config/llc fallback, mirroring bootstrap.sh. Cold 'make build' on Linux succeeds with no manual LLVM_PREFIX. Verified: rm wrapper.o+bs2, env -u LLVM_PREFIX make build-quick → builds clean.

title: [epic] Nullability/Option: make T? a safe, Option-backed, non-null-by-default type (spec Axis 10)
description: The language advertises null-safety (T?, ?., ??, ?) but implements the UNSAFE version: T? is erased at type-resolution (core/ast.av:368-370 and :416), nothing tracks/enforces nullability, and null is represented as 0 (so Some(0) and none collide for value types). This epic makes the implementation match spec Axis 10: T? == Option<T>, non-null by default, with the LLM-first refinements ratified in the design doc. Full handoff spec: docs/2026_06_05_NULLABILITY_OPTION_EPIC.md (self-contained for a no-context agent). Children are the phases; complete them in order (each green + selfhost fixed point before the next).
design: Ratified decisions (see doc §1): (1) Dual/niche representation done right from day one — null-pointer niche for pointer-backed inner types (status quo), tagged {present,value} for value types; one optional_repr helper. (2) Absence keyword = 'none' (null kept as alias, removed Phase 5). (3) ?-split Zig-style: ? = error-propagation ONLY; absence via ?./??/match (no ?-means-absent). (4) Flow narrowing = sugar, never load-bearing. (5) Staged rollout: represent permissively first, gate last. (6) Diagnostics contract first-class; null-safety is the showcase.
acceptance_criteria: All phase children closed with real work; selfhost byte-identical green with non-null-by-default ENFORCED; spec Axis 10 updated to match; everything committed and pushed. Partial is not done (CLAUDE.md rule 19/20).

Self-hosting on slice/xm2g.3 @ 02561e6f, 2714/2714 green, byte-identical selfhost with F1202 gating active. Remaining: Phase 3 flow narrowing (xm2g.4), Phase 4 flip-to-gating non-null-by-default (xm2g.5), Phase 5 finalize ?/remove null alias (xm2g.6), Phase 6 diagnostics contract (xm2g.7). Epic stays open until those land.
