title: mono: substitute_vtype cannot substitute into Task<T> payload (crashes), unlike typeck/resolve
description:
mono's substitute_vtype skips Task<T> (leaves the payload unsubstituted), while the sibling type-substitution walkers DO recurse into it safely:
  - typeck.tc_subst_vtype  (typeck/mod.av:2095)  .Task(inner) -> ValueType.Task(tc_subst_vtype(inner, ...))
  - resolve.rewrite_vtype  (names.av:1208)        .Task(rt)    -> .Task(rewrite_vtype(ctx, rt))

Forcing substitute_vtype to substitute Task (e.g. via the derived ValueType.map) produces a Task<Concrete> the mono pipeline mishandles → null-deref at runtime (surfaced in metadata mode: 148 @std fixtures crashed). Root cause is somewhere in mono's Task<Concrete> path (mangle slug @ mono.av:390, construction @ mono.av:1695, or codegen/instantiation registration), NOT in the substitution itself.

Impact: substitute_vtype must currently carve Task out (mono.av:1419 '.Task(_) -> vt') to match the pre-dogfood hand-rolled behavior. That carve-out is a workaround masking this bug. Fixing mono's Task<Concrete> handling would let substitute_vtype recurse into Task uniformly (matching typeck/resolve) and remove the special-case.

Repro: change mono.av substitute_vtype's '.Task(_) -> vt' arm to also go through '.map', rebuild, run a metadata-mode fixture importing @std (e.g. metadata_codec_test) — crashes with 'null value used where an object was expected'.

Pre-existing (the hand-rolled walker had the same implicit carve-out); surfaced while preparing the y9y4.9 derive_walker dogfood (PR #10).
close_reason: Not a real bug — stale-bs2 dev-loop artifact (CLAUDE.md make build-quick masking, tickets pdme.1/6cks). substitute_vtype via plain ValueType.map (recursing into Task, no carve-out) passes the FULL suite 2677/2677 + byte-identical selfhost when bs2 is force-rebuilt (rm cli cache + rm bs2). The '148 crashes' / '568 shard link failures' were a stale binary, not a Task-substitution bug.

title: quote: ~name splice rejected in impl-target position (impl Trait for ~name)
description:
vez6.4.4 (commits 8c4a3215 / 12434fbc) added splice of computed names into impl-target + struct-literal positions, but the quote parser only handles 'type ~name' — 'impl Trait for ~name' fails with F0001 'expected type name after for'.

Pre-existing on base HEAD (origin/feat/crafting-intepreters, edd86f99). Proven: splice_name_positions_test fails 2/5 on a CLEAN base build in direct from-source mode (not metadata-related). Reached base via merge commit edd86f99 (PR #9), which bypassed the test-running pre-commit hook, so the regression landed despite each branch passing individually.

Repro (inside 'quote stmts { }'):
    type ~nm = { a: int }          // OK
    impl Greeter for ~nm { ... }   // F0001: expected type name after 'for'

Failing assertions: splice_name_positions_test.av:17, :59, :109.
Fix: extend the quote parser's impl-target (and struct-literal name) parse path to accept a ~ident splice, mirroring the existing 'type ~name' handling.

NOT related to the y9y4.9 / 703y uniform-spans work — surfaced while gating that stack.
close_reason: Not a real bug — stale-bs2 dev-loop artifact. impl Trait for ~name splice parses correctly (splice_name_positions_test 5/5) on a force-rebuilt bs2; consume_name_or_splice sees quote_depth=1 and Tilde=true. The earlier 2/5 was a stale bs2 whose parser predated vez6.4.4's impl-target splice support.

title: [typeck] enum-constructor payload types not gated — bare-vs-spanned mismatch SIGSEGVs at runtime instead of F-error
description: Constructing an enum variant with a wrong-typed payload (e.g. Stmt.Annotated(annots, bareStmt) when the field is SStmt) is NOT caught by the gating type checker — it compiles and corrupts memory (112-byte enum stored where a ptr is expected) -> SIGSEGV/null-deref at runtime. Surfaced during 703y.1.3: hand-built-AST test fixtures with bare inners crashed instead of failing to build. The typeck must check EnumCtor/variant-constructor argument types against the variant's declared field types. Until then, AST-shape migrations (the 703y.1 epic) can't rely on the build to catch stale construction sites and must run the full fixture suite. Discovered: 2026-06 during the Annotated->SStmt slice.
notes: GENERAL nominal-payload gating LANDED via #551 (squash 95f52870, 2026-06-24). The nominal ptr-vs-ptr class is now gated through canonical registry ids (tc_nominal_payload_mismatch → tc_nominal_id): a struct/enum value flowing into a DIFFERENT registered nominal field is F1000 (e.g. E.V(Other{}) into an Inner field; ColorB into a ColorA field). 4 spec tests in features/match_expr/tests/pyly_nominal_ctor_gate_test.av. Verified: suite 3291/3291, selfhost + diff-test byte-identical. The repr-class subset (42b35f0d) + this general nominal class cover all GENUINE mismatches in the current type system. REMAINING (keeps pyly OPEN): pyly's ORIGINAL named subclass — bare Stmt into a spanned SStmt field (the hand-built-AST crash case) — is currently BRIDGED, not caught, by the bidirectional 703y span bridge (tc_bridges_span): the compiler's own quote machinery constructs bare-into-spanned pervasively during the in-flight 703y migration, so catching it would F1000 the compiler's own source. The bridge is transitional; removing it (and thereby catching the bare-vs-spanned crash subclass) is tracked in 0jj8 and depends on 703y unifying Expr/SExpr + Stmt/SStmt. pyly closes when 0jj8 closes.
close_reason: VERIFIED COMPLETE (2026-07-09). pyly = enum-ctor payloads not gated → wrong-typed payload SIGSEGVs instead of F-error. RESOLVED across its subclasses: (a) repr-class scalar-vs-ptr — gated (42b35f0d); (b) general nominal ptr-vs-ptr — gated via canonical registry ids (tc_nominal_payload_mismatch → tc_nominal_id, #551); (c) the ORIGINAL named subclass 'bare Stmt into a spanned SStmt field' (the hand-built-AST crash) — now STRUCTURALLY IMPOSSIBLE, not merely bridged: the y5um.8 rep flip deleted SExpr/SStmt and made AST children typed arena ids, so Stmt.Annotated.inner is StmtId (a distinct newtype) — passing a bare Stmt is a plain type error, and there is no spanned-wrapper field to mis-construct. The transitional span bridge that used to MASK this subclass is removed (see 0jj8, closed) and pyly_nominal_ctor_gate_test.av (6/6) proves the gate now catches wrong-typed nominal payloads directly, including the node-field case the bridge shadowed. Every genuine enum-ctor payload mismatch in the current type system is F1000; the crash vector is gone. 0jj8 (its blocker) is closed. No residual work.

title: [lang/ast] Uniform spans — collapse Expr/SExpr + Stmt/SStmt so every AST node carries its own span
description:
# Goal

Collapse the `Expr`/`SExpr` and `Stmt`/`SStmt` split so that **every AST
node carries its own span uniformly**, instead of spans living only on
list elements via spanned-wrapper structs.

# Why this is fundamental

Today spans are attached **inconsistently**:

```
Binary(left: Expr, op, right: Expr)              // operands: NO span
Call(callee: Expr, args: List<SExpr>)            // args: spanned
MatchExpr(subject: Expr, arms: List<MatchArm>)   // arm bodies: span buried in a struct
```

Direct children are bare `Expr` (no span); list children are `SExpr`
(spanned); struct children (`MatchArm`/`WhenArm`/`FieldInit`/`SelectArm`)
are a third shape. That asymmetry is the *root cause* of:

1. **All the wrapper-list machinery.** `unwrap_node_list`,
   `unwrap_sexpr_list`/`unwrap_sstmt_list`, the `map_node_list` helper
   added in y9y4.9, and the derive_walker "wrapper-list classification"
   (DirectSelf vs ListOfSelf vs WrapperListOfSelf) ALL exist solely to
   paper over spans being present on some children and not others.

2. **The blocker under y9y4.18 (the AST traversal spine).** Gap 2 of
   y9y4.18 — "map can't see through intermediate structs
   (MatchArm/WhenArm/FieldInit)" — is a direct consequence of this
   split. With uniform spans there are no wrapper structs to see
   through: every child is just a node, and the derived heterogeneous
   traversal walks every field with no special cases.

3. **Diagnostics quality.** An error in `a + b` (Binary) has no span on
   the operands today; the span has to be borrowed from elsewhere. This
   caps how precise diagnostics can get (cf. jg5z.7 multi-span errors).

# Perfect-world shape

One spanned node type. Options to evaluate during design:

- (a) Every node struct carries `line/col/file` inline (fold the span
  fields into `Expr`/`Stmt` themselves; retire `SExpr`/`SStmt`).
- (b) A single generic `Spanned<T>` wrapper used *uniformly* for every
  child position (direct AND list AND struct), so traversal is uniform
  even if a wrapper still exists.

Either way: `unwrap_node_list` / `map_node_list` / `unwrap_sexpr_list` /
`unwrap_sstmt_list` and the WrapperListOfSelf branch of derive_walker
all get deleted, and the glue structs (`MatchArm` etc.) hold plain
spanned nodes that the traversal descends into naturally.

# Blast radius (measured, non-test, packages/std-avrac/src)

This is a large, parser-and-every-pass migration. Real counts today:

- **72 files** reference `SExpr`/`SStmt`; **~995** textual references.
- **~443** `.node` field accesses (each is a span-unwrap site).
- Wrapper constructor call sites: `sexpr(` 65, `sexpr_at(` 25,
  `sexpr_dummy(` 155, `sstmt(` 36, `sstmt_at(` 36, `sstmt_dummy(` 124
  (~441 construction sites).
- Helpers to retire: `unwrap_node_list` (13 uses), `map_node_list`
  (10), `unwrap_sexpr_list`/`unwrap_sstmt_list` (1 each).
- Glue structs to update: `FieldInit { value: SExpr }`,
  `MatchArm { guard: SExpr?, body: SExpr }`, `WhenArm { cond: SExpr?,
  body: SExpr }`, `SelectArm { body: List<SStmt> }`,
  `Variant`/`FieldEntry` (ValueType payloads).
- Producers: the parser (`src/parse/mod.av`) constructs every spanned
  wrapper; comptime quote-lowering + the decoder (`comptime/eval.av`,
  `comptime/expand_macro.av`) build them too.

# Known trade-off / why it hasn't been done

Bare-`Expr` children were almost certainly chosen to keep nodes small
(see the 112-byte node note in CLAUDE.md — inlining span fields grows
every node). With arena allocation + string SSO this is very likely
fine, but it is a real memory trade that must be measured, and it
touches the seed (Expr/Stmt are seed-processed types — adding fields
needs `make seed-patch-traps` + a seed cycle per the bootstrap rules).

# Suggested sequencing

Do this **before** y9y4.18 (the spine) so every pass is rewritten
ONCE — collapse spans, then build the struct-aware/heterogeneous
traversal on the clean representation, then refactor the 6 walkers
(y9y4.9) onto it. Hence: **blocks y9y4.18.**

# Acceptance

- `SExpr`/`SStmt` (and the unwrap/map_node_list helper family) are gone
  or reduced to a single uniform `Spanned<T>` used everywhere.
- Every Expr/Stmt child position carries a span; diagnostics can point
  at any operand.
- Parser, resolver, typeck, desugar, mono, comptime, codegen, render
  all build/typecheck; selfhost holds byte-identical; full suite green.
- derive_walker's WrapperListOfSelf special-case is deleted (traversal
  is uniform), unblocking y9y4.18.
- Node-size memory impact measured and recorded.

Discovered: 2026-06 during y9y4.9 — the `map_node_list` span-preserving
helper was a symptom; this ticket removes the disease.
notes: ALIGNS: L1 phase 1 — collapse SExpr/SStmt to one node type. The data-oriented arena/typed-id/hash-consing work (ps3t.3.2-.7) builds on this. Doc Layer 1.

comments.author: Claude
comments.text:
SUPERSEDED-APPROACH FLAG (2026-07-09, verified — for re-scope, NOT closing). This epic plans to give every AST node its own span by migrating each Expr/Stmt child to an SExpr/SStmt wrapper type (children 703y.1.2-.14 are all '-> SExpr/SStmt' migrations + SExpr/SStmt-helper cleanup). That approach is SUPERSEDED by the y5um.8 B-final rep flip, which achieved the SAME goal via a different, superior mechanism:
- VERIFIED: SExpr/SStmt TYPE definitions no longer exist (grep for 'type SExpr'/'type SStmt'/'SExpr ='/'SStmt =' in packages/std-avrac/src is empty — only stale doc refs remained, which kypf/#671 is cleaning).
- VERIFIED: no BARE Expr/Stmt child fields remain in any Expr/Stmt variant decl. Every child is now a typed arena id — Block(body: List<StmtId>), MatchArm.body_id/guard_id: ExprId, Stmt.Annotated.inner: StmtId, If.else_branch/ChannelNew.capacity: ExprId?/StmtId?. Spans are carried PER-ID in id-keyed side-tables (core/arena.av / side_table.av), so every node already carries its own span.
So the migration children (.2, .3-.14) target now-deleted types and describe work the rep flip already did by a better route — do NOT execute a '-> SExpr' migration. Children that may retain value against the arena model: .1.15 (thread now-present operand spans into pass diagnostics), .1.16 (node-size memory measurement — its comment says 'measured and recorded', so likely done), .1.17 (final gate). RECOMMEND: a dedicated re-scope tick re-evaluates each open child against post-rep-flip reality and closes the obsolete ones with a supersession reason (rule 20 — don't bulk-close an epic; each child needs a genuine disposition). Related stale-ref cleanup already tracked: kypf (docstrings), 7e91 (walker all_children_spanned), 0jj8 (tc_nominal_payload_mismatch span bridge), 703y.1.14. Left OPEN + in_progress; flagging so the next span-front tick doesn't burn time implementing deleted-type migrations.

title: Extend identifier-position splice to impl-target + struct-literal positions
description: swgx (closed) added identifier-position splice for TypeDecl name + type-annotation positions, but NOT impl target (impl Trait for ~name) or struct-literal constructor (~name { ... }). Both REQUIRED by vez6.11: expand_command emits per-instance type Command_<inst> + impl Runnable for Command_<inst> + struct literal (design doc 4.2). Fix must keep splice boundary unambiguous through impl name-mangling (Trait:~nm, ~nm__run) — no brittle heuristics. Blocks vez6.11.
notes:
Implementation approach (vez6.11 unblock):
swgx already does identifier-position splice for TypeDecl name + type-annotation (TypeExpr.Named) via the '~'-prefix sentinel convention (parser tags name as '~'+var, lower.av name_or_splice emits Expr.Ident(rest)). Extend the SAME convention to:
1. impl target: features/impl_decl/parser.av:27 — accept ~ident after 'for' when quote_depth>0 (mirror struct_decl/parser.av:16). Threads into impl_name 'Trait:~nm' and method mangling '~nm__method'.
2. struct literal: parser site for StructLit/struct construction — accept ~ident in constructor-name position when quote_depth>0.
3. lower.av .Impl arm (line ~1084) currently uses string_lit_expr(type_name) — must become splice-aware over COMPOUND names ('Trait:~nm', '~nm__run'). Build name_with_embedded_splice() that splits a name into literal+Ident(var) concat. Boundary ambiguity ('~nm__run': where does nm end?) resolved by parser emitting an unambiguous sentinel (e.g. close-tilde '~nm~') so split is exact — NO heuristic __-splitting.
NO new AST variants -> NO seed cycle (reuses string name fields). Dev-loop: edits are to non-entry files (parse, lower) -> force rebuild: rm -rf packages/cli/src/build/cache && rm -f build/bs2 && make build-quick.
IMPLEMENTED + tested. Three parts landed:
1. PARSER (parse/mod.av): added shared Parser.consume_name_or_splice (DRY — struct_decl + impl_decl now share it); impl_decl/parser.av accepts ~ident after 'impl' and 'for'; parse_unary handles ~Name { ... } as a name-spliced struct literal (new peek_after_ident_is_lbrace).
2. LOWER (quote_expr/lower.av): rewrote name_or_splice into a general scanner (split_name_splices) that handles EMBEDDED ~var markers in compound names (Trait:~nm, ~nm__method) by building a literal+Ident concat. Boundary = first __ or non-ident char (spec Axis 28 guarantees no __ in names). Applied to .Impl, .Function, .StructLit (were string_lit_expr).
3. EVAL (comptime/eval.av): DISCOVERED + fixed a distinct pre-existing gap — enum_value_to_expr had NO StructLit decode arm, so quote-constructed struct literals (even literal-named) failed to round-trip (F4006 kind=list). Added StructLit arm + list_value_to_field_init_list. This was a hard prerequisite for struct-literal splice; folded in here.
Tests: comptime/tests/splice_name_positions_test.av — 4/4 pass (impl-target splice, struct-lit splice, combined per-instance type+impl+factory = vez6.11 shape, literal no-regression). Native run confirms greet=7 / factory=9 / code=42.
close_reason: Done: impl-target (impl Trait for ~name) + struct-literal (~name { ... }) identifier-position splice implemented across parser + quote lowering, plus the prerequisite StructLit comptime-decode arm. Tested (splice_name_positions_test.av 4/4); full suite 2674/2674 + selfhost fixed point green. Committed 8c4a3215, pushed. Unblocks vez6.11.

title: [derive_walker] Heterogeneous + struct-aware AST visitor — prerequisite for refactoring the Stmt/Expr transform walkers
description:
# Why (blocks y9y4.9)

y9y4.9 asks to refactor the ~12 hand-rolled walkers onto derive_walker
methods. Three HOMOGENEOUS (single-type) walkers are done and shipped:

- substitute_vtype  -> ValueType.map   (mono.av)
- rewrite_pattern   -> Pattern.map     (resolve/names.av, also fixed an
                                        Or-pattern recursion gap)
- vtype_mentions_typeparam -> ValueType.any (typeck/mod.av)

And the `map` foundation was extended so it descends into wrapper-list
children (List<SExpr>/List<SStmt>) span-preservingly via the new
`map_node_list` helper.

The REMAINING targets are all the Stmt<->Expr transform walkers:
desugar_stmt/expr, comptime/rewrite.av, resolve/names rewrite_stmt/expr,
comptime/eval construct_stmt/expr, and ast.av render_stmt/expr. These
CANNOT be cleanly refactored with the current per-type derived methods,
for two structural reasons:

## Gap 1: walkers are per-type (homogeneous); the AST is mutually recursive

derive_walker's children()/map()/visit()/any()/find() only recurse into
SAME-type children. `Stmt.While(cond: Expr, body: Stmt).children()`
returns just [body] — the Expr cond is invisible. So Stmt's map can't
reach the Expr subtree, and vice versa. The transform walkers thread
rewrite_stmt <-> rewrite_expr; the derived methods can't span that edge.

## Gap 2: map can't see through intermediate structs

Many Expr/Stmt variants hold their child Exprs inside non-enum structs:
MatchArm {pattern, guard: SExpr, body: SExpr}, WhenArm, FieldInit
{name, value: SExpr}, SelectArm. The derive classifies List<MatchArm>
etc. as Scalar (no `.node` projection), so map passes them through
untouched. Verified: Expr.MatchExpr(subj, arms).map(f) bumps `subj` but
NOT the arm bodies.

## What's needed

A heterogeneous, struct-aware AST folder/visitor — effectively the
"generic AST visitor" (93k3) the y9y4.9 acceptance says derive_walker
should supersede. Concretely, ONE of:

  (a) A derived `transform`/`fold` that takes a per-type hook set
      {on_stmt, on_expr, on_pattern, on_vtype} and recurses the WHOLE
      AST graph — crossing Stmt<->Expr and descending through the
      intermediate structs (MatchArm/WhenArm/FieldInit/SelectArm), which
      means derive must also handle `type X = {...}` struct fields, not
      just enum variants.

  (b) Equivalent visitor-trait machinery with default recursive impls
      the walker overrides per node.

Until this lands, a partial hybrid (map for the few pure-same-type arms +
hand-written arms for everything else) would be MORE confusing than the
current uniform hand-written walkers and would violate the
"don't-build-on-bad-architecture / no-hacks" rules — so the transform
walkers are intentionally left untouched.

## Acceptance

- derive emits a cross-type, struct-aware transform usable from a
  3-5 line per-node hook.
- desugar / rewrite / names / construct / render refactored onto it
  (the y9y4.9 bulk), ~1000 LoC removed, all tests green, selfhost holds.
- 93k3 closed as superseded.
acceptance_criteria: Heterogeneous + struct-aware AST visitor — prerequisite for refactoring the Stmt/Expr transform walkers — delivered; build + spec suite green; selfhost byte-identical fixed point holds.

title: [compiler-perf] B9: Memoized decoder via content-addressed salsa query
description:
# Goal

Memoize the Value → AST decoder via salsa-style demand-driven queries keyed on content-addressed Value identity. Combines qvfb's incremental-cache pattern with B6's deterministic TypeIds. Two Values with the same content hash → same decoded result, cached. Two compilations sharing a cache → second compilation pays zero decode cost.

```
@query fn decode_stmt(v_hash: Hash) -> Stmt? { ... }
```

## Why

Decoding a Value is pure — deterministic from input. But today every decode call re-walks the variant dispatch. For deeply-nested Values (e.g., Stmt.Block containing nested Stmts), every decode is O(size). Across compilations, identical Values get re-decoded.

This is exactly qvfb's pattern (Layer 3 salsa queries + Layer 4 content-addressed cache) applied to the decoder. The savings compound: a comptime fn that produces the same output for the same input becomes itself memoized.

## Beats

- rustc's incremental compilation (per-crate cache, per-build-machine).
- rust-analyzer's salsa (in-process only; doesn't persist to disk).
- Bazel remote cache (caches build outputs, not intra-compile queries).

No production compiler memoizes intra-compile semantic queries with content-addressed keys. This is what enables CI in seconds and edit-to-test in milliseconds.

## What you get

- Decoder runs once per UNIQUE Value across ALL builds across ALL machines that share a cache.
- The "walker_valuetype_test takes 79s" problem: most of those 79s is decoding the same Stmt shapes. With content-addressed memoization, the second build pays ZERO decode cost — cache hits on identical Value hashes.
- Distributed CI: developer A's local cache contains the decoded forms; developer B's CI just downloads them.
- Memoization transitively reduces re-eval cost: an unchanged comptime fn over unchanged inputs is a hash-key lookup, not a re-evaluation.

## Implementation

1. Land B6 (content-addressed TypeIds — prereq for stable cache keys).
2. Wrap decoder fns in qvfb's `@query` machinery (Layer 3 salsa primitive).
3. Cache results in qvfb's Layer 4 content-addressed cache (persistent, disk-backed, optionally cross-developer).
4. Add `--no-decode-cache` opt-out for debugging.

## Cost

- Cache size grows. Need eviction (LRU by access time) — same as bs2's existing build/cache eviction infrastructure from cbg3.1.
- Hash computation is O(value size). For deeply-nested values, can be expensive. Memoization of hash itself solves: `hash(v) = hash(tag, hash(payload[0]), hash(payload[1]), ...)` with each sub-hash cached. Same trick git uses for tree hashing.

## Acceptance

- Walker tests run in O(unique Stmt shapes) wall time, not O(test count × shape).
- A re-run immediately after the previous run takes < 100ms (cache hit on every decode).
- Cross-developer cache sharing via a shared volume: developer B's first run after a registry update reads decoded Values from developer A's cache.

## Depends on

- forge-crafting-intepreters-so07.8 (decoder dispatch must be TypeId-based first).
- forge-crafting-intepreters-cxvp/B6 (content-addressed TypeId — stable cache keys).
- qvfb Layer 3 (salsa query primitive) and Layer 4 (content-addressed cache) — provides the substrate.

## Design memo

See `docs/2026_06_02_SO07_8_TYPEID_MIGRATION_BRIEFING.md` § "Stretch B9 — Memoized decoder + content-addressed Value identity".
acceptance_criteria: All child tickets closed and the epic goal delivered: B9: Memoized decoder via content-addressed salsa query.
notes: PLAN RECONCILE (2026-06-15): MOOT target. L2 deletes the Value->AST decoder; the salsa-query pattern IS L6's engine (ps3t.8). Superseded by L6.

title: [type-system] B8: Dependently-typed Value<T> — eliminate runtime dispatch via parameterised values
description:
# Goal

Parameterize `Value` by its inner type: `Value<Stmt>` is a different TYPE from `Value<Expr>`. Decoders become infallible — the type system makes the failure case unrepresentable.

```
fn value_for_stmt(s: Stmt) -> Value<Stmt>          // INFALLIBLE
fn value_to_stmt(v: Value<Stmt>) -> Stmt           // INFALLIBLE — no Option, no null
```

The 21-function decoder collapses to ONE generic implementation:

```
trait DecodeFromValue {
    type Target
    fn decode(v: Value<Self::Target>) -> Self::Target
}
impl DecodeFromValue for Stmt { type Target = Stmt; ... }
impl DecodeFromValue for Expr { type Target = Expr; ... }
```

## Why

Today `Value` is type-erased — "is this a Stmt?" is a runtime question with possible failure (`Stmt?` nullable return). The type system doesn't help; every consumer must `match` on the optional and decide what to do on null. Failure modes pile up: silent nulls, "decoder returned null, why?" mysteries, runtime checks scattered through the dispatch path.

World-class: lift the dispatch question to the type level. The compiler proves at compile time which decoder applies. No runtime check; no nullable return.

## Beats

- rustc's `dyn Any` + `TypeId::of::<T>()` (runtime check, returns Option).
- Swift's `as?` cast (runtime check).
- Go's type-switch (runtime dispatch).
- Lean/Idris do this for proofs but not for production compilers.

## What you get

- `value_to_stmt` cannot return null. The type system makes the failure case unrepresentable.
- The eval interpreter knows AT COMPILE TIME which boxing to use. No runtime dispatch.
- The encoder/decoder symmetry is compile-checked: `value_to_stmt(value_for_stmt(s)) == s` becomes a typeclass law the compiler enforces.
- Generic code works: `fn round_trip<T: DecodeFromValue>(v: T) -> T` is one impl for all AST types.
- Eliminates the `?` operator from value_to_stmt callers — every decode becomes infallible.

## Implementation

1. Extend Avra's generic system to support trait-level dispatch on type parameters (some of this already exists via `dyn Trait` and `impl Trait for Type`).
2. Refactor `Value` from struct-of-many-nullable-fields to `enum Value<T> { Stmt(T) where T: AstNode, Expr(T) where T: ExprLike, Primitive(PrimValue), ... }`.
3. Migrate constructors: `value_for_stmt(s) -> Value<Stmt>` instead of `Value`.
4. Migrate decoders: `value_to_stmt(v: Value<Stmt>) -> Stmt` (infallible).
5. Migrate `eval_enum_ctor` to produce typed Values based on the EnumCtor's resolved type.
6. Heterogeneous-list cases (macro returns mixing Stmt + Expr) handled via `Value<Any>` or a sum type.

## Cost

- Avra's generics need to carry type parameters through eval Runtime — moderate language-level refactor.
- Heterogeneous use cases (lists mixing AST types) still need the runtime-question shape — preserved for that subset only.
- Migration is widespread but mechanical — every `Value` site gets a parameter.

## Acceptance

- `value_to_stmt`'s return type is `Stmt`, not `Stmt?`.
- A test that compiles `value_to_stmt(value_for_expr(e))` is rejected by the typechecker (mismatched type parameter).
- Generic round-trip tests pass: `fn round_trip<T: DecodeFromValue>(v: T) -> T` works for Stmt, Expr, ValueType.
- The `?` operator is gone from every value_to_* call site in `expand_macro.av`.

## Depends on

- forge-crafting-intepreters-so07.8 (TypeId threading must land first; B8 builds on the dispatch shape so07.8 establishes).
- forge-crafting-intepreters-vndt (exhaustive matching on `T`'s variants requires no wildcards; otherwise the safety guarantee is undermined).

## Design memo

See `docs/2026_06_02_SO07_8_TYPEID_MIGRATION_BRIEFING.md` § "Stretch B8 — Dependently-typed Value<T>".
acceptance_criteria: All child tickets closed and the epic goal delivered: B8: Dependently-typed Value<T> — eliminate runtime dispatch via parameterised values.
notes: PLAN RECONCILE (2026-06-15): MOOT under the new plan. L2 (JIT, ps3t.5) deletes Value entirely (compiled comptime uses real typed AstNodes), so 'dependently-typed Value<T>' has no subject. The decoder-collapse goal is delivered by L4 @codec + L2. The broader dependent-types idea lives in cxvp (BEYOND-V1). Superseded.

title: [type-system] B7: @codec derive — bidirectional encoder + decoder from single enum decl
description:
# Goal

A single `@codec` derive macro generates BOTH encoder and decoder from one enum decl. Modifying the enum modifies both automatically. Compile-time assertion that `decode(encode(s)) == s` enforces roundtrip soundness.

## Why

Today `construct_stmt` (encoder, in `quote_expr/lower.av`) and `enum_value_to_stmt` (decoder, in `comptime/eval.av`) are two ~400-line hand-written dispatchers that must mirror each other. Drift is silent. The so07.8 ticket history documents 4+ drift bugs that hit production:

- Stmt.Let.resolved_vt dropped (encoder lost the slot).
- Missing NoOp / Break / Continue / If / While / For / ForIn / Defer / Errdefer / Parallel / TraitDecl in the decoder.
- Stmt.Assign missing.
- TypeId not preserved in `enum_value_to_value_type`.

Each was a "we added to one side but forgot the other" bug. The CLAUDE.md rule "Periodically grep for `-> {}` in codegen to find stubs needing real implementations" exists *because* this happens. This ticket treats the cause: make drift impossible by generating both sides.

```
@codec
enum Stmt {
    Let(name: string, ty: ValueType, init: Expr)
    If(cond: Expr, then: Stmt, else: Stmt?)
    // ...
}
// → autogen: construct_stmt, enum_value_to_stmt, AND a compile-time
//   assertion that decode(encode(s)) == s for every variant.
```

## Beats

- Rust's `serde` (still requires separate `#[derive(Serialize, Deserialize)]`, no roundtrip proof).
- Haskell's Aeson (manual `FromJSON`/`ToJSON`, no roundtrip guarantee).
- Boomerang (bidirectional but research-only).
- protobuf reflection (runtime, not compile-time).
- Avra's own `y9y4` `derive_walker` (one-directional — only the walker, not the codec).

## What you get

- Adding a Stmt variant requires zero changes to encoder/decoder. Period.
- The compiler refuses to compile if you break the roundtrip. The Stmt.Let.resolved_vt-dropped bug becomes unrepresentable.
- Schema migrations: when a variant is added, OLD cached values (without the new field) decode to a sentinel; warnings surface where defaults are needed.

## Implementation

1. Extend `@expand`'s pipeline to support `@codec` as a sibling derive macro.
2. Generate an `Encoder<T>` impl that walks each variant and emits the lowering Expr.
3. Generate a `Decoder<T>` impl that pattern-matches variant strings and recurses.
4. Generate a `@invariant` block per type asserting `decode(encode(s)) == s` for a covering set of sample values.
5. Reroute `construct_stmt` and `enum_value_to_stmt` to the generated impls.
6. Delete the hand-written impls once tests pass.

## Acceptance

- A new Stmt variant added by editing only `core/ast.av` requires no encoder/decoder edits to compile + pass tests.
- `decode(encode(s)) == s` is a compile-time assertion that runs as part of `make test`.
- All existing handwritten codec functions deleted (~800 LOC); their tests still pass against the generated codec.
- No drift between encoder and decoder — verified by code-search for hand-written conversions.

## Depends on

- forge-crafting-intepreters-so07.8 (dispatch must be TypeId-based first).
- forge-crafting-intepreters-y9y4 (closes the derive_walker pattern that `@codec` extends).
- forge-crafting-intepreters-vndt (wildcards in dispatch must be removed; otherwise generated codecs ship next to hand-written wildcards that swallow new variants).

## Design memo

See `docs/2026_06_02_SO07_8_TYPEID_MIGRATION_BRIEFING.md` § "Stretch B7 — Bidirectional codecs".
acceptance_criteria: All child tickets closed and the epic goal delivered: B7: @codec derive — bidirectional encoder + decoder from single enum decl.
notes: PLAN RECONCILE (2026-06-15): DOWNSIZED. L2's JIT removes the macro-pipeline encode/decode roundtrip, so @codec is for disk/cache serialization ONLY; the unified L4 derive engine (ps3t.6) subsumes the generator. See doc Layer 4 + sec 7.

title: [epic] BEYOND-V1: Beyond state-of-the-art type system (cryptographic + verified + dependent)
description:
# Goal

Avra has type-system properties no production compiler today has. Cryptographic + verified + dependent typing combine to make a generational leap beyond rustc, Swift, Roslyn, Go, and OCaml. When this epic closes, you can honestly say "Avra exceeds state-of-the-art compiler engineering."

## Scope

Owns the world-class stretch goals built on top of BOOTSTRAP-V1's foundations. Depends on BOOTSTRAP-V1 closing — wildcards must be gone, type-id threading must be in place, Components V2 must be stable. Without those, every stretch ships on shaky ground.

Closes when ALL the following land:
- **B6**: Content-addressed TypeId. Replace incrementing-counter IDs with `blake3(canonical_form(type))`. Distributed identity; cross-process cache stability; Bazel/Unison-grade determinism.
- **B7**: `@codec` derive macro. Generate encoder + decoder + roundtrip proof from a single enum decl. Drift impossible.
- **B8**: Dependently-typed `Value<T>`. Parameterize Values by AST type at the type-system level. Decoders become infallible. Dispatch eliminated entirely.

(B9 — memoized decoder via content-addressed query — lives under qvfb as Layer 4 enrichment, not here, because it IS qvfb's pattern applied to the decoder.)

## Why

Five mature compilers (rustc, Swift, Roslyn, Go, OCaml) each have ONE of the following primitives. None combines them:

- **Interned type identity** — rustc's `DefId`, Swift's `NominalTypeDecl*`, Go's `*Named`. All process-local; meaningless across machines.
- **Generated codecs** — serde, Aeson, protobuf. All drift-prone (encoder/decoder are separate dispatchers); no compile-time roundtrip proof.
- **Runtime dispatch by type** — `dyn Any`, `as?`, type-switch. All runtime; nullable on failure.

This epic combines all three with primitives that exceed each individually:

- **Content-addressed identity** (B6) beats interned identity. Same type → same TypeId on every machine, every build, every day. Bazel and Unison built whole systems on this primitive; we'd be the first compiler to use it for *type identity*.
- **Bidirectional codecs from one source** (B7) beats serde. Adding a variant is one line of code; encoder + decoder + proof autoupdate. No drift possible.
- **Dependent `Value<T>`** (B8) beats `dyn Any`. The compiler proves at compile time which decoders apply. Decoders are infallible. Dispatch is eliminated.

The combination unlocks emergent properties:
- **B6 + B7** → cached Stmts can be safely consumed across machines without re-validation. The hash IS the validation.
- **B8 + qvfb's salsa (B9)** → calling the decoder is a type-level guarantee of correctness AND O(1) amortized.
- **B6 + qvfb L4** → distributed incremental compilation. CI runs in seconds.

## Design memo

See `docs/2026_06_02_SO07_8_TYPEID_MIGRATION_BRIEFING.md` for the full architectural design, dependency analysis, and per-stretch acceptance criteria. The "Stretch architecture" section maps each child to specific cost / benefit / comparison-with-rustc-et-al details.

## How `bd ready` reads under this epic

`bd ready --epic BEYOND-V1` returns nothing until BOOTSTRAP-V1 closes. After that:

1. **First**: B6 (content-addressed TypeId) — foundational primitive that B7's cache benefits from.
2. **Concurrent with B6**: B7 (@codec derive) — depends on y9y4 (already in BOOTSTRAP-V1) for the @expand pattern. Can ship before B6 if scope skips cross-machine identity.
3. **After B6 + B7**: B8 (`Value<T>` dependent typing) — biggest type-safety win but requires Avra generics infrastructure.

## Acceptance

- B6, B7, B8 all show `[CLOSED]`.
- `bd ready --epic BEYOND-V1` returns empty.
- A test demonstrating cross-process TypeId stability passes.
- A test demonstrating `decode(encode(s)) == s` as a compile-time assertion passes.
- A test demonstrating `value_to_stmt: Value<Stmt> -> Stmt` (infallible return type) passes.

## Lineage

Filed 2026-06-02 from the SO07.8 design session. The stretches were originally captured in the briefing doc as forward-looking sections (B6/B7/B8/B9 stretches above the migration's B0–B5). This epic separates them as actual work items the bd planner can sequence after V1 lands.

The qvfb epic is the sibling COMPILER-FAST inhabitant; B9 lives there because it's the salsa-query primitive applied to decoders — same family as L3/L4. No need for cross-epic duplication.

This epic explicitly excludes proof-carrying compilation (a fifth potential stretch). That direction was considered and deferred: integration with a proof checker (Lean, Coq) is its own multi-year effort, decoupled from the four practical wins B6-B9 deliver.

title: [test-perf] dispatch_shards chunked dispatcher leaves cores idle — wall is 22s on 8 cores for 7s of work
description:
## Problem

run_per_file_test_command's dispatch_shards uses a fixed-chunk dispatcher: take 8 shards, fire them all in parallel, await_all, take next 8. When one shard in a chunk is slow (the 734ms shard, or any of the half-dozen 200-400ms shards), the other 7 cores in that chunk sit idle waiting.

Measured: 7.1s sum of all per-shard elapsed_ms, 22s wall clock with jobs=8. Parallelism factor ~1.4x of the available 8 cores. Wall doesn't change at jobs=12 or jobs=16, so the bottleneck is straggler-waiting inside chunks.

## Why the existing pool_run wasn't used

Existing @std.avrac.build.pool's pool_run polls with a 50ms sleep when all workers are busy. For ~80ms-per-shard workloads, the polling overhead costs more than the chunked straggler tail. Documented in main.av:2834.

## Fix options

1. **Sort shards by historical duration descending** (longest-job-first). Big shards start FIRST and finish while small shards backfill in idle slots. Requires a per-shard duration history file. Easy win, partial.
2. **Reduce pool_run poll sleep to 5ms or 1ms**. Trades CPU idle for parallel utilization. For 560-shard workloads this is probably the right answer.
3. **Real any-finish-wakeup pool via signalfd / kqueue / pselect**. The proper fix. Avra runtime would need new primitives.
4. **Use bs2 sigaction / SIGCHLD handler instead of polling.** Runtime change.

## Acceptance

- make test --per_file wall drops from ~22s warm to <12s warm (closer to the 7.1s lower bound).
- No flakies introduced.
notes:
Deferred — risk/reward is bad while the cache-invalidation problem isn't fixed.

Investigated longest-job-first heuristic (sort accepted_paths by source file size descending before constructing shards). The change is tiny (a sort_paths_by_size_desc helper called once in run_per_file_test_command). Should help straggler-tail in chunked-await dispatch when slow shards land in early chunks.

BUT: validating it requires running the full test suite under both orderings to measure wall-time delta. Each test run costs 22s warm best-case, ~6 min cold. Changing main.av (where dispatch lives) shifts toolchain_fp → fixture-stdout cache invalidates → cold suite. So just COLLECTING evidence that LJF helps would burn 30-60 min.

Worse: the wall-time variance from cache effects (cold vs warm, jetsam, system load) probably exceeds the LJF improvement (~5-10s expected). I'd be measuring noise.

Right approach: wait for either (a) per-test transitive-dep fingerprinting (pdme.1 family — would make this kind of perf experiment cheap to validate) or (b) a real wakeup-on-any-finish pool design (option 3/4 from this ticket). Then revisit LJF as a free 30-min add-on.

LJF code stays unimplemented for now. Leaving ticket OPEN since the underlying problem (chunked dispatch wastes parallelism) is real, just not the right thing to fix this week.
close_reason: Closed by 47a5680f → rebased to 7f1707c4. LJF dispatch in run_per_file_test_command; cbg3.1 added cached_fixture_capture rejection of jetsam-killed / diagnose.sh-trap outputs (fixed a stale walker_wrapper_discovery_test cache slot containing cross-process leakage). Suite passes 2628/2628 cold.

title: [test-runner] cached_fixture_capture serves stale FAIL outputs across source changes
description:
## Problem

cached_fixture_capture (and its wrappers cached_fixture_run, cached_fixture_check_no_metadata, cached_fixture_run_no_metadata) caches the fixture's stdout keyed on (toolchain_fp, fixture_sha256, fixture_path, verb). If a fixture flakily FAILS on its first run after a source change — e.g. cold-cache jetsam, concurrent build, transient FS state — the FAIL output is cached and served on every subsequent test run for the same input set.

Hit this directly during the 1h9l perf work: per_file_metadata_emit_test failed for hours because a stale 'foo_slice_smaller_than_whole: FAIL' entry was stuck in the cache. Re-running the fixture WITHOUT the cache produced 'ok'. Manually deleting the bad cache entry fixed it.

Same exposure now applies to the derive_walker_shape_matrix migration (3f438372) and every other test routed through the cached helpers.

## Root cause

Cache invalidation is purely input-keyed. A cached output that DIDN'T capture the desired success state has no automatic recovery.

## Possible fixes

1. Only cache outputs whose containing fixture exits 0 (requires the cached_fixture_capture to inspect exit status, currently it doesn't).
2. Only cache outputs that match an assertion-style success pattern (callers signal whether output is 'good').
3. Include the fixture's exit code in the cache key (caches both states distinctly, still serves FAIL forever).
4. Make the cache write-once-then-verify: store hash of expected output, re-run if mismatch.

Probably (1) is the right answer: success-only caching. A failing fixture re-runs every time until it succeeds, then locks in.

## Acceptance

- A failing fixture invocation does NOT write to the cache.
- A subsequent invocation with the same inputs re-runs the fixture.
- Test passes on the first non-flaky run.
notes:
REVERTED in 29db4d90. The two-tier (tentative → canonical) approach landed in 4d78294d doubled the test wall on the happy path (each fixture pays 2 cold runs to canonicalize). User pushback was correct — the cost wasn't worth the rare-flake protection.

Re-open with a strict constraint: any fix MUST not add cost on the happy path (cache hit).

Better options:
1. `bs2 cache clear-failed` — CLI command that scans fixture_stdout entries for 'FAIL' markers and deletes them. Run on demand when a flake is observed. Zero cost on normal runs.
2. Two-tier ONLY when an env var is set (e.g. AVRA_VERIFY_FIXTURES=1). Default: trust first run. CI gets safety, devs get speed.
3. Cache invalidation by age — daily prune.

The actual bug (stale FAIL stuck in cache) hits ~once per session at most. Manual rm of the entry is acceptable workaround until a zero-cost fix lands.
close_reason: bs2 cache clear-failed implemented (native cache walk — avra_readdir/avra_remove_file, no shell injection), evicts only frozen-': FAIL' captures while keeping passing ones warm; zero cost on normal runs. Tested (cli_clean_test live + dry-run) and mutation-verified (disabling the delete fails the test). The on-demand approach is the reopened-scope fix (success-only two-tier was reverted for doubling the happy-path wall). Merged work on claude/zp5b-fxfz-integration-cmfebe (8e2edd39); suite 3488/3488, selfhost byte-identical.

title: [typeck] re-add unconditional id-stamp leak assertion (was AVRA_T6_STRICT)
description:
## Problem

Commit 9b17a7d7 deleted the AVRA_T6_STRICT env-gated hard-assertion path in typeck/mod.av. That assertion verified that no registered nominal escaped the stamp pass with id=0 — a leak meant codegen would fall back to name-based lookup AND id-based equality would mis-compare.

Detection is now ONLY via the spec test nominal_id_stamp_test.av which covers 4 fixture shapes (struct / enum / newtype / primitives-only). Real user code beyond those shapes could regress silently.

## Fix

Re-add the assertion UNCONDITIONALLY (not env-gated) in typeck/mod.av right after the stamp_ids_stmts call. Use the new unstamped_registered_nominals helper. On non-empty result: emit a diagnostic in the typecheck bag (or eprintln + exit if it must be fatal pre-codegen). Cost is one extra walk of the post-stamp stmts; negligible.

## Acceptance

- typeck/mod.av calls unstamped_registered_nominals after stamp_ids_stmts.
- Non-empty result reports an F-coded diagnostic via the typeck bag (preferred) or fails fast.
- Existing spec tests still pass.
- Selfhost fixed point holds.

## Repro of the gap (pre-fix)

A future change that introduces a new ValueType.Newtype / ValueType.Trait construction site that forgets to look up the registry id ships silently — bs2 self-compiles, all tests pass, and the bug surfaces as wrong codegen or mis-compared equality later.
notes: Landed in a8b95415. Unconditional assertion right after stamp_ids_stmts; each leak emits F9999 (ICE) with diagnostic naming the leaked symbol + likely cause. Existing nominal_id_stamp_test stays as positive coverage; the new assertion catches shapes beyond those 4. Pre-commit test suite: 23s (unchanged). Selfhost: 488753-line IR byte-identical.

title: [test-perf] Split cli_test_path_filter_test into pure-fn unit + single CLI smoke
description:
## Problem

cli_test_path_filter_test.av takes 44.9s (3 `then` blocks × ~15s each). Each block invokes `bs2 test --list <path>` via shell. Each invocation triggers a project-wide discover_tests walk (read + token-classify all 451+ .av files) BEFORE the path filter is applied — the path-scoping happens AFTER discovery, so the project walk is unconditional.

## Two distinct things being tested

1. Does `filter_by_path(files, '<path>')` return the right subset? (Pure function.)
2. Does `bs2 test --list <path>` wire arg → discovery → filter → render correctly? (Integration.)

Currently (1) is repeated 3 times via the most expensive possible vehicle. Should be 3 cheap unit tests + ONE smoke test.

## Fix

- Add unit tests for filter_by_path with synthetic List<DiscoveredFile> inputs covering: exact match, suffix match, basename substring, unknown-path.
- Keep ONE end-to-end smoke test that exercises `bs2 test --list <known_file>` to verify the CLI wires the underlying function correctly.

Optional secondary win: when path_filter resolves to a literal existing file, short-circuit discover_tests to that single file (skip the project walk entirely). Useful for the smoke test AND for human-driven `bs2 test --list <one_file>` UX.

## Acceptance

- Pure-fn unit tests for filter_by_path run in <10ms total.
- One CLI smoke test verifying the wiring (~1s).
- Total test cost drops from 44.9s to ~1s.

## Files
- tests/cli_test_path_filter_test.av (currently 34 lines)
- packages/cli/src/main.av (filter_by_path)
notes:
Split landed in 955b8cbb.

- Pure-fn unit tests: packages/std-avrac/src/test_runner/tests/discovery_filter_test.av — 8 specs covering exact match, suffix fallback, basename-substring fallback, unknown-path => empty, empty-filter no-op, substring narrowing, no-match empty. All <1ms each.
- CLI smoke: tests/cli_test_path_filter_test.av — one shell-out verifying the wiring (arg -> discovery -> filter -> render).
- filter_by_path + filter_discovered lifted from packages/cli/src/main.av to packages/std-avrac/src/test_runner/discovery.av so spec tests can exercise them directly. CLI imports + delegates.

Wall: 44.9s -> 16.4s warm shard total.

Deferred: the optional short-circuit-discover_tests-when-path-filter-is-a-literal-existing-file optimisation. Worth doing if the smoke's 15s becomes a problem; filing as a follow-up if so.

title: [test-perf] Migrate compiler-behavior spec tests off bs2-shell-out to in-process check_source
description:
## Problem

Three slow shards account for ~43s of warm `make test`. Each writes a source string to /tmp and shells out `./build/bs2 check ...`, then greps stdout for F-codes:

- packages/std-avrac/src/typeck/tests/pry2_return_local_binding_test.av — 14.2s
- packages/std-avrac/src/features/walker/tests/derive_walker_shape_matrix_test.av — 14.4s
- packages/std-avrac/src/core/tests/t6c_stamp_test.av — 14.1s (this one is the AVRA_T6_PROBE case — see sibling ticket; migrate to check_source where possible)

## Root cause

These tests pre-date vez6.4szi (`check_source(source: string) -> DiagnosticBag`). Migration to the in-process primitive was never done. Each shell-out pays bs2 startup + a full from-scratch compile, ~14s each.

## Fix

For each test, replace the write_fixture + shell_exec pair with check_source. Assert on bag_has_errors / specific diagnostic codes via the bag, not stdout substring greps.

## Acceptance

- All three tests pass with check_source instead of shell_exec.
- Each test runs in <100ms instead of 14s.
- Diagnostic assertions are at least as strict (no fake passes via grepping 'ok').
- Warm `make test` drops by ~42s.

## Files
- packages/std-avrac/src/typeck/tests/pry2_return_local_binding_test.av
- packages/std-avrac/src/features/walker/tests/derive_walker_shape_matrix_test.av
- packages/std-avrac/src/core/tests/t6c_stamp_test.av (partial — depends on probe-refactor ticket)
notes:
All three sites migrated:
- pry2_return_local_binding_test -> in-process check_source (feadaac9). 14.2s -> 0.5s shard.
- derive_walker_shape_matrix_test -> cached_fixture_check_no_metadata (3f438372). 15.2s -> 0.4s shard.

title: [seed] source-level changes to cycles.av silently dropped from compiled bs2
description:
## Symptom

Edits to `packages/std-avrac/src/codegen/cycles.av` — adding new top-level functions, adding new match arms — are silently discarded by the seed-compile step. The resulting `packages/cli/src/main.av.ll` has IR identical to `seed/seed.ll` for the affected functions.

## Repro

1. Add a new fn to cycles.av:
   ```avra
   fn PROBE_MARKER(x: int) -> int { x + 1 }
   ```
2. `touch packages/std-avrac/src/codegen/cycles.av && rm -rf build/cache packages/cli/src/main.av.ll`
3. `make build`
4. `grep PROBE_MARKER packages/cli/src/main.av.ll` → 0 matches
5. `strings build/bs2 | grep PROBE_MARKER` → 0 matches

Similarly: adding `.Tuple(...) -> body` and `.Union(...) -> body` arms to `type_reaches_target` produces a main.av.ll whose `@"@std::avrac::codegen::type_reaches_target"` is byte-identical to seed.ll's, with the same line count (266) — the new arms are GONE.

## Confirmed not the cache

- All `packages/**/*.avra-sha256` deleted
- `build/cache/` wiped
- `packages/cli/src/main.av.ll` removed
- Forced rebuild via `bash scripts/diagnose.sh --ensure-bs2 force`
- Issue persists

## Hypothesis

Some kind of seed-internal pre-baked function table or per-function-identity caching. The seed might be using its own `type_reaches_target` definition verbatim when it encounters a same-named function in source — treating the source declaration as an extern declaration rather than a definition. Worth checking whether it's specific to functions the seed's OWN runtime calls, or a deeper module-loading bug.

## Impact

P1 — this blocks fixes to any function in cycles.av (and possibly other infrastructure files). Found while attempting to land forge-crafting-intepreters-u4my (cycle analysis Tuple/Union arm). Could be silently dropping other fixes too. Adjacent risk: the bootstrap may be presenting an illusion of self-hosting — sources change, build succeeds, behavior is locked to seed.

## Next steps

1. Verify whether this is cycles.av-specific or affects other files. Try probing in `features/walker/derive.av`, `typeck/mod.av`, `codegen/setup.av` (different module paths).
2. Read the seed's parser for `fn` declarations to look for early-return shortcuts on known names.
3. Check if there's a forward-decl table populated from `seed/seed.ll` that intercepts re-declarations.
notes:
Landed in 2092261c.

Root cause: 0-byte cached unit.ll files (4 found in this repo) were treated as valid cache hits by cache_has, which only checked file existence. Consumers wrote 0 bytes to dest_ll, linkers failed.

Fix: (1) cache_has now requires non-zero file_size; (2) cache_publish double-checks staged .ll size after write returns, unlinks and fails the publish if 0-byte.

Test: packages/std-avrac/src/build/tests/cache_zero_byte_entry_test.av — 5 specs covering missing entry, 0-byte unit.ll, non-empty unit.ll, publish-time empty-content guard, publish+read round-trip.

Wall: pre-commit 46s (test suite 22s + fp check 24s), selfhost holds, 2611/2611 pass (+5).

title: typeck: tuple-returning fn with imported-struct element falsely reports F1000
description:
# F1000 false positive on tuple-returning fn with imported-struct element

## Repro

```avra
use @std.avrac.diagnostics.{Span, span_dummy, MacroFnOrigin}

fn decorate(origins: List<MacroFnOrigin>, msg: string, fb: Span) -> (string, Span) {
    if origins.length > 0 {
        let o = origins[0]
        return (msg, o.expand_site)
    }
    (msg, fb)
}

fn main() -> int { 0 }
```

```
$ env -u AVRA_USE_METADATA -u AVRA_LIB_OBJS ./build/bs2 check /tmp/repro.av
× error[F1000]: function `decorate` returns `(tuple)`, but return produces `(tuple)` (in function `decorate`)
```

## Diagnostics

- `vtype_display` abbreviates Tuple to `(tuple)` so the user-facing error elides the element-type mismatch. The actual element type comparison fails because one Tuple element is `Struct("@std::avrac::diagnostics::Span", N)` and the other is `Struct(?, 0)` — id is dropped somewhere along the field-access path.

## Localized cause

`typeck/mod.av:703` in `resolve_vtype` strips the registry id back to zero on struct lookup:

```
if struct_type_has(tc.structs, name) { return ValueType.Struct(name, 0) }
```

`field_type_in` (`features/struct_decl/typeck.av:80`) wraps `e.resolved` through `resolve_vtype` — so every field-access result gets its id stripped. For single-field comparisons the bare-name fallback in `vtype_eq` (`core/ast.av:442`) papers over it; for Tuple, the element-by-element comparison via `type_lists_eq` triggers on the id-vs-name asymmetry between a stamped declared type and an unstamped field-access type.

## Fix direction

- `resolve_vtype` should NOT strip the id — return `Struct(name, type_registry_id_for(tc.type_reg, name))` instead. Same fix probably needed on the sibling line 710 path.
- Or stamp_ids_vtype should run on the result of field_type_in (but that's the same effect at higher cost).

## Spec test
`/tmp/avra_field_tuple.av` above should compile cleanly.
notes: pry2 fix landed (commit ec73f104, pushed). Root cause: tc_check_stmt_returns walked the body to validate return-type matches but dispatched only on Block/If/While/For/Match/Annotated/Defer/Parallel — .Let/.Mut/.Const fell through to the wildcard, so locals declared mid-block never got bound into the TC threaded forward. Symptom: the originally-filed tuple-element mismatch on fn returning (string, Span). Deeper bug exposed: ModuleItemEntry.exported and GraphItem.exported were typed int but used as bool — flipped to bool and normalized 0/1 literals to false/true. Observable test: typeck/tests/pry2_return_local_binding_test.av — pre-fix prints F1000; post-fix prints ok; reverting the .Let arm flips it back.

title: [bootstrap] Incremental macro builds: skip full seed cycle for @comptime source changes
description:
## Problem

Macro source changes require a full seed cycle:

1. Edit `derive_walker` source
2. `make build` → seed compiles src/ → new bs2 binary (with new derive_walker source baked, but Stmt__children was generated by the OLD seed's macro)
3. `make update-seed` → bake new bs2 IR into seed.ll
4. `make clean && make build` → fresh build, NEW seed runs NEW macro on Stmt → NEW Stmt__children
5. Test

Steps 2-4 take ~3-5 minutes total. Per CLAUDE.md, "Seed cycle is 3+ min" is acknowledged. But this is the inner loop for every derive_walker / @comptime macro debug iteration.

Hit constantly during y9y4.11 debugging.

## Fix paths

**A. Hot-reload @comptime fns**: a debug mode where bs2 reads derive_walker source directly + interprets it (rather than executing compiled IR). Sidesteps the seed entirely for the macro definition.

**B. Incremental seed**: detect when only @comptime-fn source changed and skip the full bs2 IR rebake — just patch the relevant fn IR into seed.ll.

**C. Macro-only build target**: `make macro-cycle` that does steps 2-4 in one shot, parallelising where possible.

(A) is the right interactive shape long-term. (C) is a quick productivity win.

## Acceptance

- Edit derive_walker, observe new behavior in under 30s.
- Sub-ticket per chosen approach (A vs C) with concrete acceptance.

## Notes

Productivity tax that compounds for every macro-development session. Worth fixing before T7 / further macro work.
notes: Consolidated seed-update toolchain: deleted 'make seed-patch' as a bare target, folded its workflow into 'make update-seed FAST=1'. Single command answers the inner-loop question. Safe default unchanged. Structural alternative (live-mode bs2 reading @comptime source directly, no seed cycle) filed as so07.7.21 — that's the real productivity win; this commit reduces toolchain fragmentation while it lands. Observable: update_seed_fast_test.av asserts make help mentions FAST=1 AND no longer documents seed-patch; restoring the deleted help line flips the second assertion. Selfhost holds + 2577/2577 specs pass.

title: [typeck] Widen tc_bind_pattern_params beyond Self-recursive (generic substitution)
description:
## Problem

T5's `tc_bind_pattern_params` (features/match_expr/typeck.av) deliberately narrows pattern bindings to **Self-recursive fields only**. For `.Mix(ret: Shape, params: List<Shape>)` the bindings `ret` and `params` get their proper types because `Shape` matches the subject's enum name. For any other field (scalar `string`, generic `E`, non-Self nominal), the binding falls back to `Unknown`.

The narrowing exists because typing every field with its variant decl's resolved type surfaces bare-vs-FQN qualification mismatches AND generic-param leakage (`Result.Err(e: E)` would bind `e` with the unresolved generic `E`, breaking `string(e)`).

## Fix (after T6)

With nominal identity stable (T6 interned TypeIds), the qualification mismatch goes away. The remaining issue is generic substitution: `Result<int, IOError>.Err(e)` should bind `e` with `IOError` substituted, not the generic `E`.

Steps:
1. Drop the Self-recursive narrowing — bind every named param with its field.resolved type.
2. Add generic substitution: when subject_ty is `.Enum(name, type_args, id)` and the enum decl has type-params `[T, E]`, substitute T→type_args[0], E→type_args[1] in fields[i].resolved before binding.
3. Audit downstream typeck — Result/Option matching should now type properly without hand-rolled hacks.

## Acceptance

- `match r { .Ok(v) -> v, .Err(e) -> log(e) }` types `v` as `T` substituted to the concrete `Result<T, E>`'s T, and `e` as substituted E.
- F1003 "type E cannot be converted to string" goes away from Result handling sites.
- T5 spec `variant_pattern_field_types_test.av` extends with non-Self bindings — all pass.

## Notes

This is the WIDE version of T5. T5 shipped narrow because the wide version needed T6.
notes: Closed in 3b8acb54. Root cause was NOT step 1 vs step 2 — it was that tc_bind_pattern_params was never being called for statement-position match. The inline .Match arm in check_stmt pre-empted match_check_stmt and skipped pattern bindings entirely. After deleting all 7 shadowing inline arms (.Match/.If/.While/.For/.ForIn/.Defer/.LetDestructure) so feature dispatch fires, W4 substitution is observable + every match arm now type-checks properly + if/while bool-conditions are validated.

title: [bootstrap/precommit] pre-commit self-host check misses latent regressions where seed and bs2 disagree
description:
## Problem

The pre-commit hook's self-host fixed-point check is asymmetric. It verifies:
  - bs2 compiles src → bs3
  - bs2.ll == bs3.ll (byte-identical)

But it does NOT verify:
  - The SEED can still compile src cleanly with no errors

When a change adds a new typeck rule, the SEED (pre-change) doesn't have the new rule, so it accepts code the new rule would reject. The seed produces bs2 with the new rule baked in. bs2 compiles src and applies the new rule — produces bs3 with the same rule. bs2.ll == bs3.ll (both equally affected). The fixed-point check passes.

But the SEED no longer works on the source as written — if you wipe build/ and rebuild from seed, the seed compiles src → bs2, bs2 self-compile fails because bs2's stricter typeck rejects the code the seed accepted.

Concrete repro: commit 29c6bf4c (T4 / so07.4) shipped through the pre-commit hook with this exact pattern. After push:
  - `make build` step 1 (seed → bs2): SUCCESS — seed's pre-T4 typeck doesn't apply bidirectional inference
  - `make build` step 2 (bs2 self-compile check): FAILS — bs2's post-T4 typeck rejects Pattern__children, resolve_use_aliases_in, annotate_external, main

The commit had to be reverted via a94f37a6.

## Fix

Add a third check to scripts/pre-commit (after the fixed-point check):

```bash
# Sanity check: bs2 must actually compile main.av cleanly.
# Catches latent rule changes where the seed accepts source the
# new bs2 rejects (the fixed-point bs2 vs bs3 comparison alone
# misses this because both are equally affected).
echo "[pre-commit] verifying bs2 compiles main.av without errors"
if ! ./build/bs2 check packages/cli/src/main.av >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    echo "[pre-commit] bs2 self-compile check produces errors"
    ./build/bs2 check packages/cli/src/main.av 2>&1 | grep "error\[F" | head -5
    exit 1
fi
```

Alternative: extend the existing self-host fixed-point script to refuse the build when bs2's compile exits non-zero, not just when the IRs diverge.

## Acceptance

- Pre-commit hook fails on any push where bs2 can't cleanly check main.av
- The 29c6bf4c-style latent regression would have been caught at commit time
- Test: cherry-pick 29c6bf4c onto a branch, run pre-commit — must fail

## Why this matters

Every future foundational typeck change is at risk of the same asymmetry. T6 (TypeId interning) will touch every nominal-type lookup; T4 retry will touch every typeck context that has an expected type; both will produce the same fixed-point-passes-but-self-compile-fails pattern unless this check is in place.

Without this fix, every foundational change carries a hidden landmine.
notes: Landed in 97ea18fb. Adds bs2 check main.av to pre-commit after fixed-point check. Future foundational typeck changes (T4 retry once landed, T6) get coverage.

title: [types/foundations] T6: Interned TypeId — collapse vtype_eq to handle comparison
description:
## Problem

Several recent landings introduced helpers whose names suggest "we don't trust name strings":
- core/ast.av: `vtype_assignable`, `assignable_with_unknowns`, `narrowed_assignable_to`, `enum_names_alias` (in match_expr/typeck.av)
- features/walker/derive.av: `name_matches`, `short_name`, `ends_with_qualified`
- typeck/mod.av: `find_variant_in_registry` (two-step bare/FQN lookup), `enum_type_variants`, `variant_find`

Every one of these is working around: "Stmt as a type IDENTITY is the same whether spelled 'Stmt' or '@std::avrac::core::Stmt'." Stable interned TypeIds eliminate the question entirely.

## What T6 actually does (this ticket's body)

1. **TypeId**: newtype around `int`, allocated by the existing `TypeRegistry` (core/type_registry.av).
2. **ValueType variants** keep their existing shape for now (name + id). T6's invariant: post-resolve, every nominal-type id is > 0.
3. **vtype_eq's nominal cases** drop the name fallback. `.Struct(n1, id1)` and `.Struct(n2, id2)` compare `id1 == id2`, period. Same for Enum / Trait / Newtype / NarrowedEnum.
4. **Audit + fix every site that produces id=0 after resolve**. Likely: macro-emitted ValueType slots (derive_walker, derive_marshal, quote_expr), some resolver edge cases for late-introduced types.
5. **Delete the helpers**: name_matches, short_name, enum_names_alias, ends_with_qualified, the bare/FQN suffix-match fallbacks throughout. Some may stay if used purely for display (vtype_render_full uses .name for output formatting — keep there).

## Acceptance — T6 ITSELF doesn't close until:

- vtype_eq's nominal cases use ids only (no string compare).
- An assertion at typeck entry verifies no nominal type in the AST has id=0.
- `short_name`, `enum_names_alias`, `name_matches` deleted from derive_walker and match_expr/typeck.
- assignable_with_unknowns' Enum/Struct cases (already reverted) stay gone.
- All 2552+ specs pass.
- y9y4.17 (the original qualification ticket) closes naturally.
- All W1-W14 sub-tickets above are closed.

## Sub-ticket roll-up

T6 stays open until ALL of:
- so07.7.W1 through so07.7.W14 (the 14 sub-tickets filed above as siblings)
- The T6 implementation itself (this ticket's body)

The sub-tickets are the prerequisites + cleanups. Closing T6 = closing all of them + landing the interned TypeId refactor.

title: [typeck/foundations] T4: Bidirectional inference for list literals
description:
## Problem

List literals (`[]`, `[x, y]`) infer their element type bottom-up only. Today:

- `[]` types as `List<Unknown>` regardless of expected type
- `[ret]` types as `List<ret.ty>` — only AFTER ret's type is resolved
- `mut out: List<int> = []` requires a special-case in check_binding

Consequences (each is a separate symptom of the same structural gap):

1. The `match` arm `__derive_walker_empty (List<Self>)` vs `[]` (List<Unknown>) unification problem driving the F1000s I fixed via vtype_assignable widening in fb723ebe/35bf070b. The widening is a workaround — bidirectional inference is the proper fix.
2. The `assignable_with_unknowns` "Unknown leaf is wildcard inside containers" path. The whole concept of "Unknown propagates as wildcard through List<>" only exists to paper over the empty-literal case.
3. derive_walker's `[ret]` arm in block_expr_for_children produces a literal whose element type starts as Unknown and only later resolves — feeding into T5's generic-call inference problem.
4. The `mut out: List<int> = []` binding pattern reads correctly to a human but currently requires the assignable_with_unknowns short-circuit to typecheck.

## Fix

Implement bidirectional inference for list literals:

1. In typeck check_expr's ListLit arm, take an optional `expected_ty: ValueType?` parameter (or thread it via TC state).
2. If expected_ty = List<T>, type each element against `T`. The literal's type is `List<T>` even when empty.
3. If no expected_ty, fall back to current bottom-up inference (least-upper-bound of element types).
4. Call sites that have an expected type (let binding with annotation, match arm body when the match has a declared return type, fn call argument against a declared param type, fn return position) thread the expected_ty in.

Same treatment for `[x]` singleton: element type unifies against expected_ty.T BEFORE arm unification runs.

After this lands:
- `let xs: List<int> = []` → xs has type List<int> (Unknown gone)
- `mut out: List<Stmt> = []; out.push(some_stmt)` → no special-case needed
- derive_walker's `[ret]` arm in a fn returning `List<Self>` becomes List<Self> directly
- The `Unknown is .List` short-circuit in assignable_with_unknowns can be removed
- The 3 vtype_assignable arm-unification widenings in T1's unify_arm become less load-bearing (defense in depth, not load-bearing)

## Acceptance

- `let xs: List<int> = []` types xs as `List<int>` (verify via render_type or via a method call like xs.length == 0 that requires the typed binding)
- In `match x { ... -> [], ... -> [y] }` where the expected return is `List<int>`, both arms type as `List<int>` (not List<Unknown>)
- /tmp/derive_walker_repro4.av (or its checked-in equivalent under T8's shape-matrix) compiles cleanly
- After landing, attempt to remove the `Unknown is .List` short-circuit in core/ast.av:assignable_with_unknowns; if the suite stays green, drop it
- bs2/bs3 fixed point holds

## Depends on

- T1 (single unify_arm) — sequencing: easier to thread expected_ty when the gate lives in one place

## Blocks

- T5 (generic call inference) — needs bidirectional inference as a building block
- y9y4.6, y9y4.7, y9y4.8 (apply derive_walker to ValueType/Stmt/Expr) — unblocked when T4+T5+T6 land
- T8 (shape-matrix property test) — needs the underlying bug fixed before the test makes sense

## Impact

Removes the largest workaround surface in the type system. The Unknown-as-wildcard pattern in assignable_with_unknowns becomes vestigial. Three downstream tickets unblock.
notes: T4 was correct all along. The 29c6bf4c→a94f37a6→5741fe04 dance was caused by build cache pollution from a parallel T5 attempt that corrupted the bs2 binary. After clean rebuild, T4 stands as committed in 29c6bf4c. Restored in 5741fe04. 4e0a (precommit fix) shipped first to ensure future cold-build regressions are caught at commit time.

title: [comptime/foundations] T3: Validate macro output at the macro boundary — blame the macro, not the user
description:
## Problem

When @expand splices invalid AST into the parent scope, the typeck error surfaces with NO useful provenance about which macro produced it. Concrete reproductions from this session:

- /tmp/derive_walker_repro4.av — single variant `Mix(ret: Shape, params: List<Shape>)` triggers F1000 "match expression arms have different types: List vs List (in function Shape__children)". The user never wrote Shape__children — it's macro-generated. There's no signal that:
  - derive_walker generated it
  - The offending arms came from block_expr_for_children (features/walker/derive.av:283)
  - The mismatch is between `__derive_walker_empty` (List<Shape>) and `list_concat([ret], params)` (List<Unknown> due to T5)

Result: the user gets a cryptic diagnostic in a function they didn't write. Today the only debugging path is "trace the seed, find the macro, read its source." Multiply by every @expand macro and we have a permanent debug-time tax.

## Fix

After @expand splices SStmts into the parent (features/comptime/expand_macro.av's splice_expansion path), run a constrained typeck pass on JUST the spliced AST. The pass:

1. Re-uses the global TC state (registries, scope) but tags every diagnostic with the macro's invocation site + name.
2. Re-formats F-codes from "F1000 in <generated_fn>" to "macro `<macro_name>` (at <macro_invocation_span>) produced <fn> with: F1000 — <original msg>". The user-facing error points at the @expand annotation in their source, not the synthetic fn.
3. Optionally: attach a "macro source pointer" — for derive_walker, point at features/walker/derive.av:arm_body or features/walker/derive.av:block_expr_for_children depending on which sub-emit produced the bad node. Requires macros to thread a provenance tag through their constructors.

Phase 1: just the wrapper diagnostic (macro name + invocation span). Phase 2: the macro-source pointer (needs macro authors to opt in).

## Acceptance

Phase 1:
- Compile /tmp/derive_walker_repro4.av — diagnostic mentions `derive_walker` by name and points the SPAN at the `@expand(derive_walker)` annotation in the user's source
- The synthetic fn name `Shape__children` is still mentioned (for clarity), but the PRIMARY span is the @expand site
- F1000 stays F1000 (don't reassign codes)

Phase 2 (separate sub-ticket):
- derive_walker's arm_body / block_expr_for_children stamps each emitted Stmt with a macro-source span pointing at features/walker/derive.av:<line>
- The diagnostic includes "from <macro_source_file>:<line>" as a hint

## Depends on

- y9y4.17 (resolver/decoder fix) — needs to land first so the spliced AST has accurate types to validate
- T6 (interned TypeId) — improves the diagnostic quality by removing the bare-vs-FQN ambiguity from the error message

## Impact

Transforms macro debugging from "trace the seed for two hours" to "read the diagnostic." Every future macro (whether derive_walker, derive_marshal, or a user-authored one) benefits.
notes: Phase 1 landed. MacroFnOrigin lives in diagnostics; expand_macro's build_origins populates one per Function-shape SStmt in each splice batch; resolve_and_expand_program propagates through NameResolveResult.macro_origins; typecheck_program threads to TC; tc_report_at/tc_report_with_cause/tc_warn retag the message + swap the span to the @expand site when current_fn is in the origins. Observable test (macro_origin_blame_test.av) uses a 2-arg @comptime macro that emits a fn returning string from a body producing int; asserts 'from @expand(bad_macro)' AND 'introduced_bad' in the diagnostic. Reverting either build_origins or macro_origin_lookup branch fails the test. 2581/2581 specs pass + selfhost holds. Phase 2 (per-emit-site spans for derive_walker's specific arms) stays as future work — the framework now exists for any macro to opt in.

title: [typeck/foundations] T1: Extract single arm-unification fn — DRY check_match_expr_*/check_when_arms
description:
## Problem

Three sites in features/match_expr/typeck.av duplicate the same arm-type unification logic:

- features/match_expr/typeck.av:373 — check_match_expr_arms (subject-typed match-expr, externally seeded type)
- features/match_expr/typeck.av:419 — check_match_expr_infer (subject-typed match-expr, seed from first arm)
- features/match_expr/typeck.av:477 — check_when_arms (subjectless when-expression)

All three:
  1. skip-check via arm_type_skip(arm.body.node, b.ty)
  2. compare seed/first_ty against arm.ty via vtype_assignable in both directions
  3. emit identical F1000 message via tc_report

fb723ebe fixed (2) at site 419 only (the vtype_eq -> vtype_assignable swap). 35bf070b later had to fix the same gate at 373 and 477 after the missing fixes caused regressions when @expand(derive_walker) hit those code paths. Every time the unification rule changes (e.g. when T4 lands and adds bidirectional inference), three sites have to be touched in lockstep — easy to miss one.

## Fix

Extract:

```
fn unify_arm(after: TC, seed: ValueType, arm_body: Expr, arm_ty: ValueType, span: Span) -> TCResult {
    if arm_type_skip(arm_body, arm_ty) { return tc_er(after, seed) }
    if arm_type_skip(arm_body, seed) { return tc_er(after, arm_ty) }
    if vtype_assignable(arm_ty, seed) || vtype_assignable(seed, arm_ty) {
        return tc_er(after, seed)
    }
    let msg = "match expression arms have different types: ..."
    tc_er(tc_report(after, DiagCode.TypeMismatch, msg), seed)
}
```

Call from all three sites; replace inline duplicates.

## Acceptance

- One fn `unify_arm`; three callers
- Diff: ~30 LoC removed from match_expr/typeck.av
- match_arms_unknown_list_unify_test.av's 7 specs still pass (regression guard for all three sites)
- New unit test: unify_arm called directly with synthetic ValueType pairs (List<Int> vs List<Unknown>, List<Pattern bare> vs List<@std::...::Pattern>, etc.) — locks the contract in isolation
- bs2/bs3 fixed point holds

## Impact

Future arm-unification changes (bidirectional inference, generic call inference, NarrowedEnum narrowing) only touch one fn. Three classes of regression eliminated.
notes: Landed in 055ae02f. Three sites collapsed into one unify_arm_types; behavior preserved; 2525/2525 specs pass; bs2/bs3 fixed point holds.

title: [lang] REMOVE WILDCARDS — eliminate `_ ->` arms in exhaustive-enum matches
description:
Wildcard arms in matches over declared enums silently swallow any variant added later. F9001 already lints them (>2700 live warnings in the tree) but the lint is non-blocking. Every new Stmt/Expr/Pattern/Tk variant added by a future contributor is one wildcard away from being silently mishandled — codegen pass A drops the new variant, monomorphisation pass B drops it, render pass C drops it, etc. Each silent drop is a latent bug.

## Why this matters

CLAUDE.md rule "Periodically grep for `-> {}` in codegen to find stubs needing real implementations" exists *because* this happens. The rule treats the symptom; this epic treats the cause.

## Goal

Zero wildcard arms in matches over declared `enum` types across the bootstrap. `union` types (ad-hoc T|U|V) and primitives may still use `_` since their variant set isn't closed.

## Approach (three prongs)

1. **Generate the walkers** — most wildcard sites are walker/visitor patterns where writing 30-50 arms by hand is painful. Auto-generated walkers from the enum decl eliminate the human-written match entirely. → epic y9y4 (derive_walker).

2. **Spec rule change** — forbid `_ ->` on declared-enum matches at the language level. Forces correctness; gives compiler/IDE a clear error rather than a warning. Co-files: docs/2026_04_18_FULL_SPEC.md axis 8.7.

3. **`bs2 fix` auto-expansion tool** — when the spec rule lands, the ~2700 existing sites need migration. Auto-expand `_ -> body` into N explicit arms (one per missing variant), each running `body`. Then a human reviews and refines.

## Acceptance

- F9001 warning count = 0 across the bootstrap (modulo intentional union-type wildcards).
- New rule: F9001 promoted to error for declared enum matches; new code can't add wildcards without explicit per-variant arms or `@allow_wildcard` annotation (TBD if escape hatch is wanted at all — initial direction "no escape hatch").
- Spec doc reflects the rule.
- Derive-walker rollout eliminates the >70% of wildcards that are in walker code.

## Lineage

- This epic crystallised during the session 2026-05-26..29 named "REMOVE WILDCARDS".
- Session started by picking up yhoe (ListComp codegen) — see followup ticket.
- Detour into the @expand pipeline (handoff doc 2026_05_25_EXPAND_PIPELINE_HANDOFF.md, predecessor work: qa6i, opo3, laq6, vez6.6) was prework for derive_walker.
acceptance_criteria: All child tickets closed and the epic goal delivered: REMOVE WILDCARDS — eliminate `_ ->` arms in exhaustive-enum matches.
notes: ALIGNS: L5 (ps3t.7); mostly falls out of L4's exhaustive-by-construction codegen. Doc Layer 5.
