title: comptime purity: method-mediated impurity (type-aware receiver resolution)
description:
The ps3t.5.3 comptime sandbox (purity.av, first PR) is SOUND for the FREE-FN call graph: a @comptime fn that reaches an impure extern directly or through helper FREE fns is rejected (F4008). Reachability expressible ONLY through a METHOD dispatch is NOT yet covered: `x.foo()` is `Call(FieldAccess(x,"foo"), ..)`, and which impl `foo` resolves to depends on x's type, which the pre-typeck purity pass doesn't have. So a @comptime fn that reaches an impure extern solely via a method whose impl body calls it is currently uncaught.

Why deferred, not hacked: a name-keyed over-approximation (recurse into ALL impls' methods named `foo`) is unsound-to-precise and risks false-positives that would break selfhost (macro-used method names like get/add/push collide with unrelated impls). The correct fix resolves the receiver type (reuse typeck/monomorphization's method resolution) so `x.foo()` maps to the ONE impl method, then extends the call-graph walk with method edges.

Acceptance: a @comptime fn reaching an impure extern via a method call is rejected (F4008); a pure method call is not; no false positives (selfhost stays green). Parent ps3t.5.3 stays OPEN until this lands (rule 19: "no ambient IO/syscalls reachable" includes method paths).

Also note: @embed is not yet implemented, so the design's "@embed read-only allowlist" carve-out is moot today; add the allowlist entry when @embed lands.
close_reason: Done + merged. PR #717 squash-merged as f9dc48bf into feat/crafting-intepreters. Method-mediated comptime purity: a @comptime fn reaching an impure extern via a method (x.foo() incl. self-chains, match-buried, method->helper) is now F4008; conservative receiver resolution (params incl. self + annotated/struct-lit lets; shadowed/nested-fn-param/non-nominal receivers skipped) => zero false positives (selfhost byte-identical + green diff-test/rc-strict/window CI). 10 specs. CodeRabbit nested-fn-param false-positive caught + fixed in the same PR.

comments.author: Claude
comments.text:
GROUNDED PLAN (investigated 2026-07-11, v147 — purity.av + comptime/mod.av). Concrete findings:
- Pipeline: resolve_names -> run_comptime -> typecheck. So purity runs POST-resolve, PRE-typecheck. Names are resolved; full type inference is NOT done, but run_comptime already INJECTS the resolved TypeRegistry (reg.type_reg, mod.av:50-53) — so type DEFINITIONS + impls are available.
- The walk: check_comptime_purity builds a free-fn FnGraph (build_fn_graph), then reach_impure_from DFS's over callee NAMES from collect_calls_in_stmts. That collector gathers ONLY Call/GenericCall whose callee is a bare Ident/QualifiedIdent; a method call x.foo() = Call(FieldAccess(x,"foo"),..) is SKIPPED (reach_impure_from:188 treats unknown callee as pure). Impl methods are NOT indexed in FnGraph (purity.av:96).

IMPLEMENTATION:
1. New collector collect_method_calls_in_stmts (mirror collect_calls_in_stmts' complete traversal) that gathers (receiver_expr_id, method_name) for every Call(FieldAccess(recv, m), ..). Keep the free-fn collector as-is.
2. Receiver-type resolution: thread a local var->ValueType env per fn body, seeded from the fn's PARAM types + let/const bindings that carry an annotation or a resolvable init type. PREFER reusing typeck/monomorphization's existing method-resolution helper (grep typeck for find_method / method-for-type / impl lookup by (TypeId, name)) over a bespoke resolver — the ticket says 'reuse typeck/mono method resolution'. Resolve recv's ValueType, then look up the ONE impl method for (type, method_name) via reg.type_reg.
3. Extend the graph walk with METHOD EDGES: when a method resolves, descend into that impl method's body (index impl methods by a mangled key e.g. 'TypeFQN::method' so the visited-set + graph_lookup work). The method body's own free-fn AND method calls recurse.
4. CONSERVATIVE on unresolvable receivers (inferred/complex type not derivable pre-typecheck): SKIP (false-NEGATIVE, never false-POSITIVE). This is the crux — a name-keyed over-approximation (recurse ALL impls named foo) is BANNED: get/add/push collide with unrelated impls and would false-positive selfhost. Only descend the resolved impl.
5. Tests (features/comptime/tests/): (a) @comptime fn reaching an impure extern via a method whose impl body calls it -> F4008; (b) a pure method call -> folds clean, no F4008; (c) selfhost stays green (NO false positives — this is acceptance-critical; run diff-test + full suite). Mutation-verify: break the method-edge resolver -> impurity test stops catching.
6. Close ps3t.5.3.1, then parent ps3t.5.3 if no other open children (rule 19: 'no ambient IO reachable' includes method paths). Note @embed allowlist carve-out is still moot (@embed unimplemented).
KNOWN LIMITATION to document (not a blocker): fully type-INFERRED receivers (no annotation, needs typeck) stay uncaught pre-typecheck — better than today (0 method coverage), no false positives. If that gap matters, the alternative is running a purity re-check post-typecheck; out of scope for this ticket.

title: run_comptime silently swallows @comptime constant-fold errors — no diagnostic channel on the fold path
description: run_comptime → rewrite_program_ids → fold_call returns Expr? (null on ANY fold failure), and run_comptime returns List<StmtId> with NO DiagnosticBag. A fold that genuinely ERRORS (a runtime error in the fn body, or the ps3t.5.4 loop-budget trap) is silently swallowed: the @comptime call stays unfolded and compiles as a runtime call, no diagnostic. The @expand path surfaces eval errors as F4005 (invoke_macro); the fold path has no equivalent — this is why 5.4's loop trap is clean on @expand but silent on the fold path.
acceptance_criteria: run_comptime threads a DiagnosticBag its 3 callers merge into the compile bag; a genuine fold ERROR surfaces an F-code; 'not foldable' (non-literal args) stays unfolded with no error. Unblocks the ps3t.5.4 fold-path diagnostic.
notes: IMPL PLAN (scoped, ready to execute): The genuine-error case is DISTINGUISHABLE — try_fold_call returns none for 'callee not a comptime fn' (fn_def_opt==none) and 'args non-literal' (arg_values_opt==none), both correctly stay unfolded; a null from fold_call() AFTER a known comptime fn + literal args is the real error (budget trip / body runtime error). Plan: (1) add fold_errors: ptr to CompTimeRegistry (a C-side accumulator, mirrors fold_cache) — record (message + call-site span) when fold_call returns null on the found+literal path. Capture the span at rewrite_expr_id (has the ExprId → store position side-table); thread the id into the fold call or record at that level. (2) change run_comptime -> { stmts: List<StmtId>, bag: DiagnosticBag } (or return a small result struct); build the bag from fold_errors after rewrite_program_ids, one diag per error (new F-code, F40xx range, e.g. F4007 ComptimeFoldFailed). (3) update the 3 callers (build/compile.av:89, check/mod.av:87, cli/main.av:3844) to merge the bag + guard on errors. (4) tests: a @comptime fn used as a constant fold that errors at fold time (e.g. AVRA_COMPTIME_LOOP_LIMIT low + a runaway loop via the FOLD path, not @expand) surfaces the new F-code; a non-literal-arg call (sq(runtime_var)) stays unfolded with NO error; a normal fold is unaffected. Byte-identical NOT expected if any existing test relied on a silent fold failure — audit; likely byte-identical since genuine fold errors don't occur in valid programs. This unblocks the ps3t.5.4 fold-path diagnostic residual.
close_reason: Merged #708 (squash c7150c01). run_comptime returns ComptimeResult { stmts, bag }; genuine @comptime constant-fold failures (body runtime error / loop-budget trap) surface as F4007 ComptimeFoldFailed instead of being silently swallowed — the fold-path sibling of @expand's F4005. Native List<ComptimeFoldError> accumulator (no C-side workaround); distinct from 'not foldable' (non-@comptime callee / non-literal args stay unfolded, no error). All 6 callers handled (check/test/compile + build_binary gate; check merges; fmt best-effort; bs2 run interprets, never folds). Byte-identical IR for valid programs (diff-test 647206-line selfhost + corpus, hermetic CI green); 6/6 mutation-verified specs; full suite + selfhost + all CI (seed-train-verify, diff-test, window, rc-strict, publish-seed-verify) green. title: beads-sync: metadata-table merge conflict blocks concurrent multi-agent reconcile (beads#2466)
description: Residual after #694 (which fixed the proxy-403 push). When two agents write concurrently, 'bd dolt pull' hits a merge conflict on the metadata table's machine-local rows (dolt_auto_push_commit / dolt_auto_push_last) — upstream beads#2466. dolt rolls the merge back, so the puller never integrates the other agent's issue changes and its own push then non-fast-forwards. No clean automatic fix reachable here: bd exposes no merge-strategy flags, 'bd sql' is unsupported in embedded mode (so dolt_ignore of the metadata table isn't settable), and push --force / reset --hard are lossy. Manual recovery (proven this session): back up (bd export), adopt remote (mv embeddeddolt aside + bd bootstrap clone), diff backup vs remote to find own delta, re-apply own closes/comments, push direct. Proper fixes need upstream: add metadata to dolt_ignore, auto-resolve metadata conflicts, or a bd version bump (gated by this repo's pinned Dolt schema — see bootstrap.sh BD_VERSION guard).

  export local (1242) -> diff: 4 local-only, 39 remote-only, 23 local-newer,

notes: Follow-up from jvw7. The V2 command model (expand_command) handles flag + arg children only; App.run_argv passes empty options to parse_tokens. Legacy Cli has options (cli_add_option, option component in main.av), so V2 needs parity before vez6.12 main.av migration. Commit 60bd854d (PR #669): expand_command reads 'option z {}' children -> generates 'let z = result_get_option(args, "z")' run binding + option_names() accessor; Runnable gains option_names(); App.run_argv builds the OptionDef schema (option_defs_for) from it and classifies --z=value against the command. title: Components V2: App.run(argv) parse needs per-command flag/arg schemas unreachable through dyn Runnable
description:
The design (docs 2026_05_08_COMPONENTS_V2_DESIGN.md §4.2) sketches:
  impl Cli { fn run(self) -> int { let parsed = parse_argv(self); for cmd in self.commands { if cmd.name()==parsed.command { return cmd.run(parsed) } } print_help(self); 1 } }

parse_argv must produce a CliResult whose positional args are NAMED (result_get_arg(args, "target") looks up by name), which requires each command's ARG SCHEMA (positional order -> names) and, for good errors, its FLAG schema. But the App stores commands as List<dyn Runnable>, and the Runnable trait exposes only name()/run() — the per-command flag/arg schemas the macro discovered are baked into the run body as result_has_flag/result_get_arg calls, NOT stored anywhere reachable at parse time. So parse_argv(self) cannot see them.

DESIGN OPTIONS (needs a decision before the parse/--help/--version machinery can land):
  (a) Extend Runnable with a schema accessor, e.g.  returning its flags/args; expand_command generates it from the declared children (it already collects flag_names/arg_names). App.run matches the command, uses its schema to parse, dispatches. Cleanest; keeps commands self-describing.
  (b) expand_cli stamps a parallel  onto the App alongside the dyn boxes (name-keyed), and parse uses that. Avoids a trait method but duplicates the command list.
  (c) Schema-less parse (generic --flag / positional classification) — but positionals can't be named without a schema, so result_get_arg breaks. Rejected.

Recommend (a). Blocks the bead's 'parse argv, --help, --version work' acceptance. The core (per-instance types + dyn dispatch + flag/arg/global bindings) already dispatches on a pre-built CliResult (done, tested); this is the argv-front-end. Found-by vez6.11. Blocks: vez6.11 full acceptance, vez6.12 (main.av rewrite depends on App.run(argv)).

title: Top-level let bound to a struct value is broken at top-level use sites (mis-typed unannotated; null field annotated)
description:
A module top-level 'let x = SomeStruct { ... }' does not behave as a struct at a later top-level use site:
- UNANNOTATED ('let x = App { ... }'): a top-level 'x.method()' fails codegen with 'method call on non-struct/enum value (ty=int)' — x is typed int, not the struct.
- ANNOTATED ('let x: App = App { ... }'): compiles, but at runtime a field read (e.g. iterating x.commands) hits 'index on null list' — the struct's fields are null/uninitialized when read at top level.

Both isolated with @std.cli.App (a plain struct with a List<dyn Runnable> field), no macros. The SAME construction inside a fn body works (build + method-call + dispatch all correct). So top-level 'let' bound to a struct value is the broken axis — likely the module-init lowering for top-level lets (CLAUDE.md notes 'export let compiles to local allocas') doesn't materialise struct values / their types for top-level consumers.

This is the concrete form of the design's § Non-goals line 14 ('cli avra { … } produces mut avra = 0, not an avra value; you can't write avra.run()') — Components V2 is supposed to FIX that. vez6.11 expand_cli sidesteps by emitting a builder 'fn <inst>() -> App' (function scope works) instead of a top-level 'let <inst> = App{}', but the design's ergonomic top-level 'let avra = …' + 'avra.run()' needs this fixed.

Found-by: vez6.11 (Components V2 expand_cli). Related: vez6.11, 966j.
close_reason: Fixed: declare_globals infers an unannotated top-level struct/enum let's type from its initializer at declare time (infer_global_init_ty), so top-level use sites see the struct/enum, not int. Merged #679 (squash 540bf513). diff-test byte-identical; 5-case test mutation-verified. Annotated half was resolved by 966j. const case is a separate intentional typeck rejection (no twin).

title: Stmt.Impl stringly-typed 'Trait:Type' encoding — mangled render + fragile split on qualified traits
description:
Stmt.Impl encodes a trait impl as a single 'type_name' string of the form "Trait:Type" (single-colon), parsed at features/impl_decl/parser.av:48-52 and consumed by resolve/typeck/codegen by splitting on the colon.

CODE SMELL: stringly-typed AST. A trait impl's two identities (the trait, the implementing type) are packed into one magic-delimited string instead of structured fields. This collides with '::' in qualified names: when the trait resolves to a qualified path (e.g. @std::cli::Runnable), the impl string becomes '@std::cli::Runnable:Command_build', and render_stmt (core/ast.av) splits on the FIRST ':' — producing the mangled 'impl @std for :cli::Runnable:Command_build' instead of 'impl Runnable for Command_build'.

IMPACT (today): cosmetic only — resolution + codegen + dyn-dispatch are correct (verified: a macro-generated Stmt.Impl("Runnable:Command_build", ...) typechecks, links, and dispatches through 'dyn Runnable' returning the right value via 'make run'). But the mangled render misleads anyone reading 'bs2 expand' output or impl-related diagnostics, and blocks robust render-string assertions in Components V2 macro tests (must assert on the 'Runnable:Command_build' substring, not the pretty form).

PROPER FIX: give Stmt.Impl structured fields — e.g. Impl(trait_name: string (empty for inherent impls), type_name: string, methods) — instead of the packed 'Trait:Type' string. Touches parser (impl_decl), resolve, typeck, codegen, and render. Core change (outside vez6 pure-consumer scope). Surfaced by vez6.11 expand_command.

Found-by: vez6.11 (Components V2 expand_command). Related: pqyp (hygiene un-rename of generated impl names).

title: f1005_nullable_omit_test flakes intermittently under parallel shards (blocks byte-identical merges)
description:
The spec 'F1005: a nullable field may be omitted from a struct literal (6y4y)' / then 'the omitted nullable field defaults to null' (packages/std-avrac/src/features/struct_decl/tests/f1005_nullable_omit_test.av:13) FAILS intermittently in the full parallel-shard suite (seed-train-verify / bundled run) while PASSING 3/3 in isolation (./build/bs2 test <file>).

RECURRENCE: hit twice on BYTE-IDENTICAL PRs where the change cannot have caused it — #671 (kypf, comment-only) and #673 (sfa5 marshal, diff-test byte-identical, 3636/3637). Both times diff-test proved identical emitted IR, so the compiled test binary is identical → the failure is non-deterministic at RUNTIME under parallel shard execution, not a source regression. Both cleared on a plain CI re-trigger.

CLASS: parallel-shard resource/ordering intermittent — the snw0/uzs9 territory (per-file runner runs test FILES as @deferred_init units across AVRA_TEST_JOBS worker threads with process-level shared runtime state). It is a struct-literal nullable-default RUNTIME value assertion, so a shared-state / RC-ordering race under concurrent shards is the leading hypothesis (vs a deterministic codegen bug, which would fail in isolation too).

IMPACT: intermittently reds seed-train-verify (a required merge gate) on unrelated byte-identical PRs, forcing a manual re-trigger each time. WORKAROUND: re-trigger CI (empty commit; rerun API 403s for the integration token).

NEXT: reproduce under AVRA_TEST_JOBS>1 with the shard batch that includes this file (log showed it in a 34-test shard); AVRA_TEST_STALL_MS / per-thread sink inspection. Determine whether it is a runtime RC/shared-state race (fix the leak) or a test-runner harness issue. Do NOT just quarantine the test — the flake is the signal.

title: quote/comptime: construct_stmt silently emits Stmt.NoOp for unhandled variants — violates design §3.4 (wrong splice = compile error), should be a comptime diagnostic
description: CODE SMELL (design review 2026-07-09). features/quote_expr/lower.av stmt_passthrough (~line 1290) returns Stmt.NoOp for any Stmt variant construct_stmt doesn't handle (Match with arms, and other decls). This is the CLAUDE.md 'empty match arm silently swallows behavior' anti-pattern: a macro that quotes an unsupported construct gets a SILENT NoOp with no diagnostic — the generated code silently drops a statement. It also contradicts the design's own §3.4 principle ('Splicing a wrong-typed value into a hole is a compile-time error at macro-expansion time'). construct_stmt is a pure AST transform with no diagnostic channel today, which is WHY it emits NoOp — the fix is to thread a comptime diagnostic (an F-code naming the unsupported variant) through the quote-lowering error path, or reject at typeck of the quote body. Partially tracked by vez6.3.10 (quote decl completion) but the SILENT-ness is a separable hardening bug. Found during design review.

comments.author: Claude
comments.text: SCOPED (2026-07-09): the fix is a moderate refactor, not a one-liner. construct_stmt (quote_expr/lower.av:1198) returns a bare Expr with NO diagnostic channel; stmt_passthrough (:1283) NoOps unhandled variants (Match, Use, Module, ShapeDecl, NewtypeDecl, UnionAliasDecl, Select, Spec/Given/Then, ComponentDef, AssocType, LetDestructure, ...). Threading a diagnostic means either (a) construct_stmt -> Result<Expr, Diag>, rippling ? through construct_stmt_id/construct_stmt_ids + every recursive arm (Block/While/For/If/Impl/Function/EnumDecl/...) + external callers (comptime/eval.av:134,197) — ~30 sites; or (b) a typeck-side rejection of unsupported quote-body stmts BUT quote lowering runs as a pre-typeck transform, so by typeck the NoOp is already baked in — would need lowering restructured so typeck sees the raw quote body, OR the diagnostic channel added to the lowering pass. Either is a real design decision + moderate change; not a session-tail rush. Recommend a dedicated tick.

title: F4 followup: retire walker all_children_spanned/with_children wrapper-branch handling
description: After deleting SExpr/SStmt (F4f), walker/derive.av still has WrapperOfSelf/WrapperListOfSelf/OptionalWrapperOfSelf handling in the all_children_spanned + with_children generators (spanned_one_wrapper_fn/box_wrapper_list_spanned_fn/node_opt_spanned_fn + wc_child_rebuild_fn respan branches) that return string names of now-deleted @std helpers (spanned_one_sexpr, box_sexpr_list_spanned, node_opt_spanned_sexpr, respan_*). These are DEAD: no AST enum has a wrapper field anymore, and user-wrapper enums hit the poison-name path (proven harmless — walker wrapper tests pass via children()/map() on the generic unwrap_node_list, independent of these branches). Remove the wrapper FieldKind branches from the spanned/with_children generators (keep children()/map() wrapper support via unwrap_node_list). Parent: y5um.8.9 F4.

title: typeck: if-expr branches with incompatible layout types (List<StmtId> vs List<SStmt>) not rejected
description: An `if`-expr whose two branches have incompatible LAYOUT types (e.g. fast-path returns List<StmtId>, else returns List<SStmt>) type-checks silently instead of erroring F1000. A direct call arg with the same mismatch IS caught. This gap let F4d.8 (31cb0d09) ship a resolver metadata-fast-path SIGSEGV (fixed in bbbaa240 by bridging via sstmts_of; the root typeck hole remains). Repro shape: `let x = if cond { list_of_ids } else { list_of_sstmt }` where downstream treats x as List<SStmt>. Fix: if-expr branch unification must apply the same layout-conflict check (check_assign_layout family / vtype layout compare) between the two arm types, not just structural nominal equality. Also audit match-expr arm unification for the same hole.
close_reason: Fixed: if-expr branch unification now applies generic_args_layout_conflict (the same nested check the call-arg/binding gates use), so two branches with memory-incompatible CONTAINER layouts (List<int> scalar vs List<Node> ptr elements) are F1000 instead of silently unioned. Scoped to the container/generic-args conflict on purpose — a top-level scalar↔ptr difference (int vs string) stays a legit inferred ad-hoc union; vtype_eq fast path for same-type branches. Match-expr arms AUDITED (ticket's 2nd ask): already safe — unify_arm_types rejects differing non-assignable types via vtype_assignable; pinned with a parity test. This closes the typeck root cause that let the reverted F4d.8 metadata flip reach a resolver SIGSEGV. Merged as #685 (squash d29b4629). Regression if_expr_branch_layout_conflict_test.av 9/9 (List/inverse/nested/Map conflicts F1000; int|string + two-struct unions + matching containers not over-gated; live + match-parity controls); mutation-verified; diff-test byte-identical; dogfood typeck 240/240, if_stmt 25/25, match_expr 135/135, null_safety 218/218. First landed increment of the B-final safety net.

title: Flaky: crash_isolation_edges_test reads global crash list by absolute index (races crash_isolation_test)
description: crash_isolation_edges_test.av asserts avra_test_crash_spec(0/1) == 'first/second deliberate crash' — reading a PROCESS-GLOBAL crash list by absolute index, assuming it is the only crashing spec. When bundled with crash_isolation_test.av (also deliberately crashes) under parallel workers (AVRA_TEST_JOBS), both tests' crashes race into the shared list, so indices 0/1 may point to the OTHER file's crash → 'crashed spec N name captured' fails. PASSES in true isolation (6/6); FAILS in the spec_test/tests directory bundle (3 failed) and intermittently in the full suite (ordering-dependent — phase-1 passed on lucky order). Pre-existing (test last changed seed v7). Fix: scope the crash list per test-file/unit, or make the assertions match by spec-name rather than absolute index. NOT related to any annotation/AST work. Surfaced during F4d y5um.8.9.4.4 phase 2 (byte-identical, all annotation tests green).
close_reason: Same root cause as 4m1e, fixed by the same change (#692, squash a1517264): crash_isolation_edges_test no longer reads the global crash list by absolute index — it uses avra_test_crash_{count,spec,signal}_for_file keyed on its own basename, so it can't race crash_isolation_test's entries. Deterministic under 8 parallel workers.

title: F4b cleanup: drop boxed guard/body value-tolerance in value_to_match_arm
description: value_to_match_arm (features/eval/mod.av) stays tolerant of BOTH the boxed guard/body value shape and the id guard_id/body_id shape during the F4b seed-migration window: the diff-test selfhost oracle compiles the PREVIOUS compiler source, whose derive_walker still emits boxed-shape MatchArm values, so the phase-2 compiler must accept them (converting to arena ids via value_to_expr_id). Symmetric to F4b phase-1 (which taught the seed the id shape). Once the seed train advances PAST the F4b flip, the base source's derive_walker + construct_match_arm emit id-shape only, so the boxed guard/body match cases become dead and can be removed (diff-test stays byte-identical because the new base is id-shape). Drop the two boxed cases + the comment note. Naturally subsumed by F4f (SExpr/SStmt deletion) if not done sooner.
close_reason: Merged in #658 (squash 6ea8f8d1). Dead boxed guard/body fallback in value_to_match_arm removed (id-only since F4b, no producer emits boxed shape). make test 3547/3547, selfhost byte-identical.

title: Complete walker coverage for flipped Expr subtrees (CodeRabbit #629 findings)
description:
Three pre-existing walker-coverage gaps surfaced by CodeRabbit on PR #629 (B-final Batch B). All verified pre-existing on the base (fca4c44f) — the byte-identical flip preserved the exact incomplete behavior, so they can't be fixed in a byte-identical-gated PR (the fix changes emitted IR). Land as a follow-up with tests, via the --run-equiv/intended-ir-change path if needed.

1. [Major] features/generics/mono.av rename_self_calls_expr (~1678-1706): does NOT recurse into .With/.ListComp/.Catch/.Quote/.StructLit/.EnumCtor/.MapLit (falls to _ -> expr). A self-recursive generic call inside one of those subtrees stays unmangled → can resolve to the dropped generic symbol. The sibling passes (rewrite_expr, substitute_expr, collect_inst_expr) already cover these; rename_self_calls_expr is the outlier. Fix: add the missing arms threading rename_self_calls_expr_id / rename_self_calls_expr_ids / arm+field-init walkers.

2. [Minor] features/closures/parser.av expr_contains_it (~34-39): .With(obj, _) checks only obj, .MatchExpr(subj, _) checks only subj — inits/arms ignored. So xs.map(p with { x: it }) or xs.map(match v { _ -> it }) can skip the implicit (it)-> lambda wrap, leaving 'it' unbound. Fix: add field_inits_contain_it / match_arms_contain_it recursion.

3. [Major] typeck/mod.av annotate_expr (~4207-4220): .ListComp and .Catch recurse with the OUTER tc — the comprehension var and the catch binding b are NOT bound, so nested refs to var/b annotate against the outer context and can receive a wrong .ty (the feature check hooks list_comp_check_expr/check_catch DO bind them; annotate_expr must match). Fix: bind var/b (tc_bind/tc_bind_params-style) before recursing into body/filter/inner.

Tests to add: (1) generic fn with a self-call inside a StructLit/With/match-arm body → mangled correctly; (2) xs.map(p with { x: it }) and xs.map(match v { _ -> it }) → it wrapped; (3) list-comp/catch where a nested var/b ref's type drives codegen → correct lowering.

title: typeck: List<SExpr> vs List<ExprId> layout-conflict not caught on fn-return args (only on annotated locals)
description: During the EnumCtor B-final flip (y5um.8.8), EnumCtor.args changed List<SExpr> -> List<ExprId>. Two tests hand-built EnumCtor with List<SExpr>: comptime_eval_test used an annotated local (let arg: List<SExpr> = [...]; Expr.EnumCtor(..., arg)) and was CORRECTLY caught as F1000 (layout conflict); enum_value_test used Expr.EnumCtor(..., one_arg_se(e)) where one_arg_se returns List<SExpr> and was NOT caught -- compiled and crashed at runtime (SIGABRT, SExpr ptrs used as ExprId indices into an empty store). Same mismatch, inconsistent gating: the layout-conflict check fires on the annotated local but not on the fn-call return threaded into the ctor field. Fix: make the gating consistent so a fn-return of the wrong list-element type into a struct/enum field is F1000, not a runtime crash. Discovered while updating tests for #627; all affected tests fixed there. Related leniency: 26ql.
close_reason: Duplicate of forge-crafting-intepreters-t8ny (identical bug: List<SExpr>-vs-List<ExprId> layout-conflict gate fires on annotated locals but not fn-return args into a ctor field; same repro, same fix). Consolidating onto t8ny.

title: typeck: List<SExpr> vs List<ExprId> layout-conflict caught on annotated locals but not on fn-return args
description:
During the EnumCtor B-final flip (y5um.8.8), a variant field EnumCtor.args changed List<SExpr> -> List<ExprId>. Two test files hand-constructed EnumCtor with List<SExpr>:
- comptime_eval_test.av: 'let arg: List<SExpr> = [...]' then Expr.EnumCtor(..., arg) -> CORRECTLY caught as F1000 (generic argument layout conflict) at compile time.
- enum_value_test.av: Expr.EnumCtor(..., one_arg_se(e)) where one_arg_se returns List<SExpr> -> NOT caught; compiled and crashed at runtime (SIGABRT, 'index <ptr> out of bounds' — SExpr pointers used as ExprId indices into an empty store).

Both are the same List<SExpr>-where-List<ExprId>-expected mismatch, but typeck's layout-conflict check only fires on the explicitly-annotated local, not on the fn-call return value threaded into the ctor field. The gating check should be consistent: a fn-return of the wrong list-element type into a struct/enum field must be F1000, not a runtime layout crash. Repro: construct any flipped-payload variant (Call/EnumCtor/...) passing a helper that returns List<SExpr> for a List<ExprId> field. Related leniency family: 26ql, scalar int->string assignability.
close_reason: Resolved: the enum-ctor payload layout gate (tc_check_enum_ctor_args, typeck/mod.av ~2846) was made position-independent by q6p4/pyly — it checks each arg's TYPE vs the variant field type regardless of binding, so fn-return/annotated/direct-literal are gated uniformly (verified). Added the fn-return regression case (the position q6p4's test left unpinned) + annotated companion, mutation-verified. Merged #680 (squash 20712718). 3h6r closed as dup; filed vdh3 (P3, duplicate-diagnostic emission).

title: Comptime fold: route Expr Values through flip-aware construct_expr (Call args latent conflict)
description: value_to_construct_expr (features/comptime/eval.av) routes only STMT fold-Values through the flip-aware construct_stmt; EXPR Values stay on the generic Expr.EnumCtor(type, variant, payload_to_args) rebuild. That generic rebuild reconstructs a flipped Call's args as List<Expr>, which trips the enum-ctor generic_args_layout_conflict check (List<Expr> vs the flipped Call.args: List<ExprId>) ONLY when the fold result is COMPILED into a program. The Stmt path covers the qa6i case (a quote stmt returned through a sibling @comptime helper, expand_body_eval_still_works_test). LATENT: an Expr-returning @comptime macro that folds to a bare Call (or any Expr variant with a List<ExprId> field) THROUGH A HELPER and is compiled would hit the same conflict — currently untriggered by any test (comptime_eval:220 renders, doesn't compile; expand_macro_expr_sum folds a Binary whose ExprId scalar fields don't trip the generic-arg check). Proper fix: make the Expr-Value decoder (value_to_expr_node) robust on hand-built EnumCtor Values (it currently SIGABRTs on comptime_eval mk_make_call_fn's value — which is why the Expr route was reverted), then route Expr Values through construct_expr too, symmetric with the Stmt path. Note: scalar id-fields (Binary.lhs: ExprId) do NOT conflict under generic reconstruction, so this is scoped to List<ExprId>-bearing variants (today: Call).

title: F3b: comptime-fold-constructed compound flipped Expr not renderable via a fresh store
description: After the B-final Expr-payload flip, a @comptime fn that folds to a COMPOUND flipped Expr (e.g. `quote { 1 + 2 }` → Expr.Binary) yields a node whose operand ExprIds live in the fold's construction store, not the caller's. Rendering it with a fresh NodeStore (`render_expr(new_node_store(...), e)`) can't resolve the operands → renders as null. LEAF comptime-Exprs (`quote { 42 }` → Number) still render fine (no child ids). The value_to_construct_expr fold path (features/comptime/eval.av) reconstructs children via synth_expr_id identity shims, which are Expr-as-id at eval time — not arena rows in a store the caller can pass to render. General B-final comptime/AST-API coherence gap (affects ALL compound flipped variants, surfaced by Binary being the first with a fold-render test). Fix likely threads the construction store to the caller, or renders comptime-produced nodes against their own store. Not Family-2-scoped: the 6 Expr-payload flips are diff-test byte-identical; this is the comptime-fold-render interaction. Parent y5um.8.8.

title: F3b metadata path: emit_expr reads flipped Expr ExprId payloads as bare int (F1000 in --emit_metadata re-check)
description:
During F3b (Expr-payload flip to ExprId), the metadata lib build smoke reports F1000: ExprArena__get parameter id expects ExprId, got int (in codegen::emit_expr) — one per emit_expr arm reading a flipped Expr payload (Grouping/Unary/Assign; grows as Family 2 flips Binary/Logical).

ASYMMETRY: Stmt's ExprId fields (Let.initializer via emit_statement exprs.get) are NOT flagged; only Expr's. Stmt has @expand(derive_walker); Expr does not. Metadata preserves the ExprId newtype for @expand'd enum fields but transparentizes ExprId->int for the plain Expr enum's variant fields. Newtype serialization (build/metadata.av:420) is correct, so the field vtype is already bare Int by emission (resolver/extract drops the ExprId newtype on Expr variant field annotations).

NON-BLOCKING: exit 0, .ll written, make test passes every tranche, diff-test byte-identical (real emit_expr codegen correct) — a metadata self-consistency re-check false-positive, not a codegen defect. Present since F3b tranche 1, cumulative.

REPRO: cd packages/std-avrac && rm -f src/avrac.av.ll && AVRA_USE_METADATA=1 AVRA_LIB_PKG_ROOT=@std::avrac ../../build/bs2 compile --emit_metadata --module_path=@std::avrac src/avrac.av 2>&1 | grep F1000

FIX: resolve/serialize Expr variant field ExprId newtype like Stmt's (resolve enum-variant field vtypes uniformly regardless of @expand, or preserve Newtype in metadata_extract for non-@expand enums). Check Expr.Block's StmtId (Family 6) doesn't hit the same.
notes: ROOT CAUSE CORRECTED (was misdiagnosed as a metadata newtype-strip). The failure is NOT in metadata serialization — metadata round-trips ExprId faithfully, and the resolver keeps the field as Struct(ExprId). The real defect is a TYPECK SCOPE LEAK in tc_check_match_arm_returns (features/match_expr/typeck.av): it threaded one accumulator across every match arm and checked each block arm's returns via tc_check_explicit_returns WITHOUT a per-arm scope. emit_expr's .Number arm does 'let value = parse_int_literal(text)' (int); with no scope isolation that binding leaked into the LATER .Assign(name, value) arm, shadowing its ExprId pattern var, so store.exprs.get(value) type-checked against the stale int -> F1000. The 'metadata only / Stmt survives' framing was an artifact: the repro path (bs2 check with AVRA_USE_METADATA stripped, via the test's cached_fixture_check_no_metadata) compiles @std from source, and the leak only bites the specific arm ordering (int let before a same-named ExprId pattern var). Latent pre-flip (int->ptr is lenient); the newtype arg gate made it hard. FIX: wrap each block arm's return-check in tc_enter/tc_exit. Regression test: features/match_expr/tests/arm_let_no_leak_into_sibling_test.av (mutation-verified: fails pre-fix with 'expects MyId, got int'). Fixed on claude/y5um-bfinal-f3b (commit a11d1846). Full cold suite 3640/3640 GREEN (shape_matrix + pry2 both pass), diff-test byte-identical.
close_reason: Fixed: match-arm return-check scope leak (not a metadata bug). tc_check_match_arm_returns now isolates each block arm's scope so a sibling arm's local let can't shadow a later arm's pattern var. Regression test added + mutation-verified; full cold suite green; diff-test byte-identical. Committed a11d1846, pushed to PR #621.

title: lib build: stale entry .ll satisfies the post-compile output check — failed child compile reports Built
description:
cli/main.av Miss-path (~line 2051): after the child `bs2 compile` subprocess
runs, success is judged by `file_exists("${entry_path}.ll")`. A stale .ll left
by ANY earlier successful run satisfies the check even when the child just
CRASHED (observed 2026-07-04: child died rc=99 with closure-marker corruption,
parent printed `Built 38d0337c8165` and exited 0, publishing the stale IR).
A trust-by-existence gate on a non-atomic, reused path — same class as
zp5b/fxfz/kaux/rrio (validate completeness/freshness on reuse).

Fix direction: check the child's exit code (run_with_progress must surface
it) and/or have the child emit to a per-pid temp + rename, with the parent
consuming only the fresh artifact. Spec test: plant a stale entry .ll, make
the child compile fail deterministically, assert the build FAILS.

title: test DSL: return inside a then-block silently drops sibling then registrations
description: A bare 'return X' inside a spec/given/then block returns out of the synthesized @deferred_init unit fn, so the then's own result AND some sibling specs' thens never register — the suite shrinks and shows green (observed: 4-then file reported 2/2 PASS). Should be a compile-time F-code (return not allowed in then-blocks) or scoped semantics. Discovered by an F1a mutation check that 'passed' because its failing thens vanished. Idiom until fixed: helper fns own the early returns.
close_reason: Implemented F0901 (DiagCode.ReturnInSpecBlock): a closure-boundary-aware typeck walker in the spec_test hooks rejects any escaping `return` inside a spec/given/then block (descends all control flow, stops at fn/lambda/spawn/isolated/quote and nested test blocks, reports exactly once). Merged as #682 (squash 511da9fb) into feat/crafting-intepreters. Dogfood: the gate caught 3 existing test files (isolated_dx_test, isolated_keyword_test, shared_store_test) using the exact latent trap; all rewritten to the non-escaping idiom. Regression test pins 7 escaping forms + no-double-report + 2 legit-accepted forms; mutation- and diff-test-verified (byte-identical IR). CI fully green.

title: runtime avra_str_char_at does strlen(s) per call — per-char scans (lexer, scanners) are quadratic per file; ~60% of every compile is strlen
description: Callgrind on bs2 check (2026-07-02, while landing B1 Stage A+B): __strlen_avx2 is ~63% of ALL instructions in a full compile, and the dominant edge is avra_str_char_at -> strlen (37% of the program, ~1500 instr per call on a ~19KB file — the bounds check re-derives strlen(source) per character). Every per-char consumer pays it: the lexer's advance_token, peek helpers, template scanning. build_line_index was the same pattern and was fixed in the B1 Stage A+B PR with a one-pass C scanner (avra_str_line_starts) — that PR left the general case untouched. Fix directions (pick one): cache length in the string rep (header-carried length, aligns with the spec's SSO plan), or a length-aware char_at variant the lexer threads its known source length through, or convert hot scanners to C-side one-pass primitives. Parent: 4apk (COMPILER-FAST). Expected win is large: strlen is more than half of every bs2 compile.
close_reason: Lexer per-char + per-token strlen eliminated: source length measured once at parser construction (source_len field) and threaded through length-aware avra_str_char_at_len / avra_str_substring_len primitives, routed via char_at/slice choke points in lexer.av + mod.av + component_decl lookahead helpers. Callgrind: __strlen_avx2 63% -> 0.17% of instructions on a 50KB compile. Behaviour-preserving: suite 3789/3789, selfhost fixed point holds, diff-test byte-identical IR (selfhost+corpus), bootstrap window holds. Regression test added (lexer_source_len_test.av). Commits bf6f035d + f06a57e3.

title: newtype identity lost through if-expression: .raw() on the result ICEs (undefined method)
description: Repro A (if-expr): type NrId = int; fn f(a: string, b: bool) -> NrId { if b { NrId(a.length) } else { NrId(0) } }; f(..).raw() -> F9999 ICE 'undefined method NrId.raw'. Repro B (early return): fn f(...) -> NrId { if b { return NrId(a.length) } NrId(0) } — same ICE. Any mixed-control-flow body drops the newtype identity of the return; only a single trailing ctor expression keeps it. The declared return annotation should re-stamp the newtype regardless of body shape. Pre-existing on the integration oracle (verified 2026-07-02). Related: 37at (cross-module .raw), e1sm (int(newtype)).
close_reason: Fixed: newtype .raw() now resolves via the type registry (kind-agnostic) on the method-dispatch failure path, so it survives a fn return regardless of how the receiver's type was produced. The ticket framed it as if-expr-specific; it was any fn return (single trailing ctor included). Merged as #684 (squash c2d08da7). Regression test newtype_raw_through_return_test.av 13/13 (every return body shape + string newtype + newtype-with-impl no-shadowing); mutation-verified; diff-test byte-identical. Merged through the known f1005_nullable_omit seed-train flake (wi2l) — rc-strict+diff-test+window green. Related open: e1sm (int(newtype)), 37at (cross-module .raw).

title: B2 consumer: typeck slice 1 — item-level walk reads nodes by id from the arena
description: The big reader (read-only, gating — no tree output, so byte-identical is trivially provable via diff-test + identical diagnostics). Slice 1 = the item-level walk (top-level + fn-item iteration) reads nodes by id, mirroring the y5um.1 resolve_program pattern (local re-ingest from typeck's own input tree; positions from wrappers). DO NOT attempt deep expression-level migration in slice 1 — typeck reads params/ret types heavily (ParamEntry.vtype is not edge-covered until y5um.4) and the deep walk is large; slice deeper only after y5um.4 lands, sized per-slice then. Gates: suite + fixed point + diff-test; mutation-verify an item-level F1xxx diagnostic.
close_reason: Closed with y5um.6 (user-approved, 2026-07-02): typeck slice 1 (item-level walk by id) is feasible but symbolic — it would repeat y5um.1's already-made proof on a different pass while the deep walk (the actual value) is flip-blocked for the same role-dependence reasons as the resolver (and params/ret types additionally need y5um.4's container coverage). Rather than ship a ceremonial PR, the typeck migration happens mechanically at the rep flip. Re-homed to y5um.8 (B-final).

title: B2 consumer: resolve_program deep walks (expr/pattern) read children via arena edges
description: Extends y5um.1 (top-level roots by StmtId, merged #596) downward: resolve_stmt/resolve_expr recursion reads children via children_of + the y5um.2 unwrap helpers instead of boxed fields, positions via per-kind linecol accessors where the wrapper position is needed. The resolver builds its store locally from its own input (the y5um.1 pattern — its tree is post-desugar/post-rewrite, NOT the parse-time store). Scope guard: where the resolver reads STRUCT-EMBEDDED node children not yet edge-covered (ParamEntry declares by NAME only — scalar, fine; verify match-arm walks use the now-covered arm edges), keep that sub-walk boxed rather than lose coverage; full depth after y5um.4. Byte-identical (diagnostics-only pass). Gates: suite + fixed point + diff-test; mutation-verify diagnostic position + order.
close_reason: Investigated 2026-07-02 (user-approved close): the resolver's deep walk is semantic through and through — role-dependent arms (Assign checks name mutability AFTER value; Call runs callee-shape-specific mutating checks; Block enters/exits scope), deliberate skips (uppercase idents, QualifiedIdent, the load-bearing _ -> feature-dispatch fallback that silently returns when no hook exists), and early exits (resolve_field_init_list stops at first error — diagnostic count/order depend on the exact walk). Flat children_of edges carry no role labels, so an edge-driven deep walk is either a split-brain half-measure redone entirely at the rep flip, or a behavior change (visits deliberately-skipped positions -> spurious diagnostics; not byte-identical). The correct deep migration is MECHANICAL at the flip (labeled id fields; arms keep their semantic shape, only field reads change). Re-homed to y5um.8 (B-final rep flip). No pre-flip slice exists below the top level (y5um.1 did that).

title: B2 consumer: lower_quotes presence-scan reads the parse-time arena (threads NodeStore out of parse_or_fail)
description: First pass to consume the PARSE-TIME store (it runs before any tree rewrite, so no divergence). Two parts, landed together so the plumbing is load-bearing (not inert scaffolding): (1) parse_or_fail returns {stmts, store} and call sites thread it (~8 sites in cli/main.av + check/mod.av + build/compile.av fallback for non-parse_or_fail callers); (2) any_quote_in_stmt_list drives off store.roots/children_of instead of the boxed walk. UNBLOCKED by y5um.3 Stages 1-2 (match-arm + field-init edges now exist — the cai8 class). PRECONDITION inside this ticket: audit every node position the boxed scan visits (any_quote_in_stmt/expr incl. ComponentDef config/children slots, ThenBlock, Defer, etc.) against arena edge coverage — any Expr-bearing struct NOT yet edge-covered means the arena scan would miss quotes there (cai8 regression); if any gap exists, either keep that sub-walk boxed or defer to after y5um.4. Byte-identical (scan returns a bool; lowering unchanged). Gates: suite + fixed point + diff-test.
notes: PR #604 opened (branch claude/y5um-b2-quotescan-arena). Audit done: boxed-scan positions strictly subset of arena expr rows (arms+inits covered by #599/#602); CompConfig/CompConfigPair = equal pre-existing blind spots both sides (not scope-crept). parse_or_fail -> ParsedProgram{stmts,store}, 8 sites threaded; 3 raw-parse sites + unwrapped compile use flat store scan; --module_path (sibling merge) + storeless callers keep boxed. Gates: 3613/3613 + fixed point (603540), diff-test byte-identical, mutation-verified (5/7 fail on broken scan), prepare-pr 3x. Awaiting CI + CodeRabbit -> merge.
close_reason: Complete + merged. PR #604 squash-merged as 1226294a. parse_or_fail returns ParsedProgram{stmts,store} (8 sites threaded); quote presence-scan reads the parse-time arena as a FLAT expr-row pass (lower_quotes_via_store + store_has_quote) — first parse-time-store consumer, architecturally better than the boxed walk (no recursion/tree). Provenance-gated: 3 raw-parse sites + unwrapped compile use store; --module_path (sibling merge) + storeless callers keep boxed (documented + spec-guarded presence-equivalence). Audit done (boxed positions strict subset of arena rows; CompConfig equal pre-existing blind spot both sides). Gates: 3613/3613 + fixed point, diff-test byte-identical, mutation-verified, prepare-pr 3x. CodeRabbit: 1 Trivial (guard-spec equivalence assertion) fixed with its own suggestion + confirmed.

title: seed-train-verify CI gate is ~12min/commit — bottleneck is the 590s spec suite (4-vCPU runner, not AVRA_TEST_JOBS)
description:
## Symptom
`seed-train-verify` is the long pole of PR CI into feat/crafting-intepreters: **~700-815s wall (12-13.5 min)**, vs diff-test ~110-175s and bootstrap-window ~85-100s (all three run in parallel per commit). User: "12 mins per commit is not scalable."

## Where the time goes (run 28494657753, representative)
- checkout + setup-llvm + cache-seed restore + fp: **~45s**
- diagnose.sh --seed-train-verify (step 6): **675s**, of which:
  - build bs2 from pin + selfhost fixed-point: **~85s**
  - `bs2 test` full spec suite (3587 tests): **590.1s = 82% of the step**

## Root cause (VERIFIED in code, not guessed)
The 590s is **~450 cold shard COMPILES** (`bs2 _test_shard` of 8 files each: bs2→llc→cc), fanned out by **`AVRA_JOBS`** (main.av:3061 `parse_jobs_env(8)` on the metadata fast-path) — but **`AVRA_JOBS` is unset in CI**, so it defaults to 8-wide while the runner only has **4 vCPU**, so it is CPU-bound at 4 effective cores. Job log shows `[test-cache] miss ... no previous build` on EVERY shard: the per-shard test-compile cache is cold every run (only the seed binary + C objects persist via cache-seed).

**Irreducibility:** the test-compile cache keys on the bs2 toolchain fingerprint (universe_fp: main.av:3011-3022; toolchain_fp: test_runner/mod.av:772-782). Every compiler-source PR — i.e. ~all traffic on this gate — mutates bs2 → the whole cache invalidates by construction. You cannot cache your way out; a compiler change necessarily re-tests everything. **Only more cores / parallelism shrink the wall.**

## DO NOT (flake-gate-weakening — verified traps)
- **Do NOT raise `AVRA_TEST_JOBS`.** It is the WRONG knob: it sets the *in-shard* run-thread interleaving (runner.av:77-79 `test_jobs()`), not compile fan-out. It is contractually pinned to `2` to MATCH seed-train.yml (the "surface order-dependent flakes at the train's interleaving" invariant; cvnu / 4szi.1 / #538-#539). Raising it on the PR gate alone tests a different interleaving than the post-merge train (reopens the hole this gate closes) and can MASK a jobs=2 race. If ever changed, change BOTH workflows together — and that's a correctness investigation, not a speed lever.
- **Do NOT matrix-shard the suite across jobs.** Splitting files across processes destroys cross-file order-dependence coverage (the gate's whole purpose) AND re-pays ~130s setup+build per matrix job. `bs2 test` also has no index-slice primitive (only dir/path scoping; discovery.av:338-348) and files are badly skewed (313/671 under packages/std-avrac).
- **Do NOT persist build/cache cross-run.** ~0% hit on compiler PRs (above) + stale-artifact replay hazard in a trust gate (zp5b/fxfz/pdme footguns).

## DO (the safe levers)
1. **Bigger single GitHub-hosted runner** (more vCPU **with proportional RAM**, e.g. 8-vCPU/32GB or 16-vCPU/64GB — NOT vCPU-only, so a degraded non-fast-path run at ~3GB/shard can't OOM), set **`AVRA_JOBS` explicitly to ~ncore**. Single process keeps the interleaving identical → correctness-neutral. Apply to seed-train.yml too for parity. Amdahl floor: wall = ~130s serial (setup+build+fixedpoint) + suite/N. Realistic: 8-vCPU → ~6-7 min; 16-vCPU → ~4-5 min. Diminishing returns past ~8-16 vCPU because the 130s floor dominates. **BLOCKER: requires larger runners enabled/billable for this repo — a maintainer/billing decision; unverifiable from the tree.**
2. **Compose with q2tr** (share the from-pin bs2 build across the 3 parallel gates) to attack the ~85s serial build phase orthogonally.
3. Already-good (confirmed, no action): the suite runs ONCE per PR — seed-train-verify publishes a `seed-suite-verified/<fp>` status the post-merge train reuses to skip its own suite (seed-train-verify.yml:95-127 → seed-train.yml:60-92 → diagnose.sh:804-807).

## Related
- q2tr (P3): share from-pin bs2 build across gates — compose with lever 1.
- x2hu (P2): memory-aware job dispatch — would make AVRA_JOBS self-tuning on a bigger runner.
- 4apk (P0 epic): COMPILER-FAST.

title: Typed string patterns in match — declarative parsing without a parser
description:
Flagship beauty feature from the string-model design thread. Allow string literals as match patterns with captures that bind to O(1) string slices, and TYPED captures that parse-and-validate inline. Example:

  match req.line {
      "GET {path} HTTP/1.{minor: int}" -> serve(path, minor)
      "{method} {path} HTTP/{_}"        -> reject(method, path)
      _                                  -> bad_request()
  }

Untyped captures ({path}, {method}) bind to string slices (views, no copy). Typed captures ({minor: int}) parse the matched span to the named type and FAIL the arm if it does not parse. Literal segments must match exactly. Also supports the head/tail form "{head}{tail}" (head: char via O(1) decode, tail: string via O(1) slice) for recursive scanning. Intended as the FIRST reach for structured text so most code never pulls in a regex/parser lib.
design:
Performance contract: a pattern compiles to a SINGLE anchored left-to-right scan. Each capture consumes until the next literal segment (non-greedy to the next anchor); NO backtracking, so matching is linear in input length O(n), like a hand-written parser. Typed captures are an inline parse over the captured slice. This linearity is the as-fast-as-Rust guarantee and the reason it is NOT regex (no alternation/quantifier blowup).

Relationship to regex: complementary, not a replacement. These cover fixed-shape text; regex stays for fuzzy/variable patterns (char classes, repetition, alternation, optionals). If regex ships it should be the linear-time kind (RE2 / Thompson NFA) to preserve the perf promise.

Prior art (pieces exist; clean combo is rare): Raku grammars are the closest built-in declarative parser; Scala has regex/string extractors in match (case r"..."); F# active patterns can express it; C sscanf / Python parse lib are the same idea at runtime, outside match. No mainstream language appears to offer format-string-as-pattern with typed captures inside match arms WITH a linear-time guarantee.

Must integrate with the lens/cursor model (captures are slices/cursors) and the always-valid-UTF-8 invariant. Also worth exposing as a boolean test (is) and a Result-returning parse, not just in match.
notes: From the s[i] / string-model design thread; siblings 29f3 (string->u8 + bytes index), bw1y (nullable index), pmo3 (newtype-of-list), plus the lens/cursor string redesign. User flagged as a must-have ("REALLY like... make sure we have this feature allowed"). Captured so it is not lost; not blocking v1 bootstrap.

title: walker/all_children must descend into node-bearing STRUCTS (match arms, struct-lit fields, params) so the arena holds them
description: A1 (forge-crafting-intepreters-a1ew) made arena ingest cross-type via the derive walker's all_children(), but the walker classifies a field whose type is a plain STRUCT (MatchArm, WhenArm, FieldEntry, ParamEntry, CompConfig, Variant, ...) as Scalar — is_self_type is strict == against the four AST ENUM names only. So nodes embedded in those structs (Stmt.Match arm patterns+bodies, struct-literal field exprs, fn param default exprs/types) are NOT ingested into the arena; the arena holds only the walker-reachable ENUM-node tree. Same boundary applies to children()/visit()/map() (pre-existing). RESOLUTION options: (a) extend derive_walker's field classifier to descend into node-bearing struct fields (resolve the struct def via ctx, emit nested traversal); or (b) it is subsumed by ps3t B (parser-builds-arena: every node gets an id at parse time, structs included). Until one lands, 'arena holds the whole tree' is literally 'whole WALKER-REACHABLE tree' (documented in core/arena.av ingest_program). Behind AVRA_L1_INGEST; not blocking. Part of epic ps3t.
close_reason: Resolved via its own listed options: option (a) landed for MatchArm + FieldInit (y5um.3 Stages 1-2, PRs #599/#602 — StructListOfSelf walker coverage, byte-identical); option (b) chosen for the residual (ParamEntry, WhenArm, CompConfig, Variant, remaining containers) per the 2026-07-01 architecture decision — subsumed by y5um.4 (B1 parser-builds-arena), where struct-embedded nodes get ids natively with structure stored. Successor: forge-crafting-intepreters-y5um.4.

title: CI: seed-train skips the redundant full suite when the merged source already passed seed-train-verify
description: Post-merge seed-train re-runs build + fixed-point + FULL SUITE (~6.5 min) that the required seed-train-verify PR gate already ran on the same source (squash merge => same tree, same compiler-source blob-shas => same window_fingerprint). Skip the suite in mode_seed_train when a PASS marker for window_fingerprint(integration_seed, HEAD) exists. CORRECTNESS: must stay safe for the concurrent-merge case (two PRs each green independently, their merge is an untested combination) — the fingerprint check handles it (combined tree has different blob-shas => no marker => run the suite). This is the exact hole seed-train-verify was added to close (4szi.1 / #538/#539), so do NOT skip unconditionally. Needs cross-WORKFLOW PASS-marker propagation: seed-train-verify writes a marker keyed on the fingerprint into actions/cache; seed-train restores + checks. Own PR (distinct cross-workflow mechanism + correctness surface). Still keeps build+fixed-point+hermetic+publish. Depends on 4c3b's seed-binary cache landing first.
notes: REOPENED: the merged cache-based marker handoff is a NO-OP. Verified from CI logs: seed-train run on the rrnq merge (869f92c0) RAN the full suite (3454/3454 in 529.8s) — the skip did NOT fire. Root cause: GitHub cache BRANCH-SCOPING. The PASS marker is saved by seed-train-verify on a pull_request run (producer steps confirmed green: Record + Save marker), but that cache is scoped to the PR; the seed-train push run on the integration branch cannot read a PR-scoped cache. Producer saved, consumer can't read. (The seed-binary cache #577 + llvm deb-cache #578 DID hit in the train — build is fast.) FIX (user chose 'full win'): scope-independent API handoff — seed-train-verify publishes a commit status seed-suite-verified=success with the tested window_fingerprint in its description on the PR head (permissions: statuses: write); seed-train finds HEAD's PR, reads that status, and skips only if state==success AND published fp == HEAD's recomputed fp (intervening base change => mismatch => suite runs). diagnose.sh --seed-verify-fp + the AVRA_SEED_TRAIN_SKIP_SUITE branch stay as-is; fix is workflow-only.
close_reason: GENUINELY FIXED + VERIFIED LIVE via PR #580 (squash a652bfdc). The post-merge seed-train run #28393685241 SKIPPED the suite via the scope-independent commit-status handoff. Log evidence: train id:skip step logged 'seed-suite-verified/9bc81934..a4ac = success on PR head f08c0448 — skipping the suite'; AVRA_SEED_TRAIN_SKIP_SUITE=1; 'seed train: spec suite skipped — PASS marker matches this seed+source fingerprint'; NO 3454/3454; the Build-from-pin/verify/publish step took 42s (vs ~10min running the suite, e.g. 869f92c0). Mechanism: seed-train-verify (read-only) + isolated publish-seed-verify-pass job (job-scoped statuses:write, needs:verify success, same-repo gated, no checkout) publishes seed-suite-verified/<fp>=success on the PR head; seed-train (statuses:read+pull-requests:read) resolves HEAD's PR via commits/{sha}/pulls, reads that head's statuses, skips iff seed-suite-verified/<HEAD-fp>=success. Safe-by-construction (any miss runs the suite; fp re-checked vs HEAD). Replaced the #579 PR-scoped-cache no-op (cache branch-scoping made the marker invisible to the integration-branch train). CodeRabbit's 2 Major findings (isolate statuses:write to a no-checkout job; gate fork PRs) fixed in f08c0448 + confirmed. CI-only; diff-test byte-identical.

title: CI: cache the LLVM 20 toolchain in setup-llvm (kill apt reinstall + jqd0 403 flake)
description: setup-llvm runs apt-get update + install llvm-20/clang-20/lld-20 on every job of every workflow (~1-2 min) and is the source of the jqd0 apt.llvm.org 403 flake. Cache it. LLVM_PREFIX resolves to /usr/lib/llvm-20 (everything llc/include/libLLVM lives there) BUT diagnose.sh resolves the toolchain via /usr/bin/llvm-config-20|llc-20 symlinks apt creates, so a /usr/lib/llvm-20 dir-cache must also recreate those /usr/bin symlinks on a hit. Alt: cache the .deb archives + install offline. ALL-CI blast radius (a broken toolchain reds every workflow) => own PR with its own CI iteration loop, NOT bundled with the content-keyed seed cache (4c3b). Sibling of jqd0.
close_reason: Merged: nmp1 via #578 (squash f0b1d697, LLVM .deb-archive cache), rrnq via #579 (squash 869f92c0, seed-train suite-skip via PASS marker). All CI green; CI-only (no seed cycle). Closes epic 4apk's near-term seed-cycle levers alongside 4c3b (#577).

title: codegen: field access on a generic-struct element of a List via index fails (element type not monomorphized)
description: A field access on a generic-struct value obtained by indexing a List fails codegen: let bs: List<Box<int>> = [mk()]; bs[0].items.length -> internal compiler error 'field access on non-struct value (ty=Box<int>, field=items, obj=(index bs 0))'. The List element type Box<int> stays the un-mangled generic name through the index+field-access path instead of resolving to the monomorphized struct (Box__int), so codegen can't find the struct layout. Reproduces single-module (not collision-related). Direct struct field access and nested struct field (Wrapper<Box<int>>.inner.items) work; only List-element-via-index is broken. Discovered while testing z4xp. Repro: type Box<V> = {items: List<V>}; fn mk() -> Box<int> { Box {items:[1,2,3]} }; fn f() -> int { let bs: List<Box<int>> = [mk()]; bs[0].items.length }.

title: Make coverage-critical walkers exhaustive (drop _ -> default): annotate_stmt + tc_check_type_applied
description: Concrete L5/vndt target with a soundness motivation, not just a lint warning. Two hand-written walkers with a _ -> default wildcard silently swallowed cases and produced real holes during the sh0g/hk70 work: (1) typeck annotate_stmt's '_ -> stmt' default skipped SpecBlock, GivenBlock AND Select — two separate F1002 generic-inference holes on one line; (2) typeck tc_check_type_applied's '_ -> tc' default hides Channel/Closure/Fn/Task (nested-type carriers). Cure: drop the wildcards, name every Stmt / ValueType variant, so the NEXT missing case is a compile error instead of a runtime segfault/ICE. This is the mechanism behind the 'each thorough pass still left a hole' pattern — hand-enumerated coverage can't be trusted; exhaustiveness must be compiler-enforced. Scope before starting (naming all variants ripples; some may need real handling vs explicit no-op); may interact with seed if it changes match shape. Belongs with L5 no-drift; the deeper fix is L4 deriving these walkers from the AST (y9y4) so coverage is automatic.

title: Extend F1004/totality gate to explicit EXPRESSION type arguments (channel<T> ctor elem + turbofish type_args)
description: The F1004 under-applied-generic gate (sh0g) covers every TYPE ANNOTATION position (params, return, let/mut/const, fields, payloads, newtype inner, lambda params, extern, trait sigs) + recursion through containers. It does NOT yet cover explicit type arguments written in EXPRESSIONS: (1) channel ctor elem — `let ch = channel<GenOpt>(1)` builds with a bare-generic element type (ChannelNew.elem is a ValueType, cleanly gateable via tc_check_type_applied at the ChannelNew check); (2) generic-call turbofish — `wrap<GenOpt>(x)` builds with a bare type arg (GenericCall.type_args is List<string> — the stringly-typed surface 5idg restructures; gate it there/after, not by re-parsing strings now). Both are the same under-determined-type class (totality rule ps3t.4.5) via a different surface (explicit expr type args vs annotations); both reach mono with a bare generic and risk the first-match wrong-layout segfault for struct elems (enum elems are uniform {tag,ptr} so lower risk). Repros build clean today. DEPENDS ON 5idg for the turbofish (List<string>) half. Channel-elem half can land independently.

title: Trait default method not inherited by impl — empty impl ICEs with 'undefined method' at codegen (F9999)
description: An impl that relies on a trait DEFAULT method (provides no override) ICEs at codegen instead of inheriting the default body. Minimal repro (no generics involved): trait MakeB { fn make(self) -> int { 42 } } / type Thing = { x: int } / impl MakeB for Thing { } / fn main() { let t = Thing { x: 0 }  let n = t.make() } -> error[F9999]: internal compiler error during codegen: codegen error: undefined method `Thing.make`. The default method body (parsed as a Function in the trait decl per trait_decl/parser.av) is never synthesized into the inheriting impl's method table. Pre-existing; unrelated to the F1004 gate / spec annotation work (no bare generics, no spec; the gate never fires). Spec relevance: the Error trait (spec Axis 12) relies on default methods (message/kind/cause/context/trace defaults), so this blocks idiomatic trait defaults. FOLLOW-ON when fixed: a trait default method BODY is currently in the annotate pass's TraitDecl skip (the same _ -> stmt default that hid the spec/given and select holes), so once inheritance works, a generic construction in a default body will need annotate descent too (mirror annotate_select_arms). Locus: trait impl codegen/inheritance + annotate_stmt TraitDecl.

comments.author: Claude
comments.text: Investigated (repro confirmed: bs2 compile → F9999 'undefined method Thing.make'). Root: trait DEFAULT methods are parsed as Function (with body) in the TraitDecl while REQUIRED ones are ExternFn; collect_method_names_from_stmts only collects ExternFn, so the empty impl passes conformance but no Type__method is ever synthesized → codegen (fn_decl/codegen.av:519) can't resolve the dispatch. Cross-unit metadata path (synth_impl_method_stmts) already fills defaults but only as body-LESS @external_unit stubs (impl lives elsewhere) — not reusable for same-unit. Fix = a resolve-time synthesis (near rewrite_impl_stmt, names.av:1237): for each impl, look up its trait's default Function methods, and for each not overridden, inject a Type__method Function with self retyped to the impl Type. BLOCKER for a clean fix: the default body must be DEEP-CLONED per impl (fresh stmt/expr ids) so per-impl self-typing + the per-id arg_ty_of annotate side-table don't collide across impls of the same trait; no deep-clone helper exists, and building a generic one overlaps the B-final walker/with_children refactor (y5um.8.9.x) currently in flight. Recommend landing after B-final settles (reuse the derive walker's with_children for the clone), or building a deliberate clone_subtree facility. Unclaiming to avoid colliding with the active walker refactor.

title: struct VALUE via variable/expr into a value-scalar slot is not layout-gated
description:
98z0 closed the CTOR-into-scalar holes (enum ctor + struct literal, incl. parenthesized). A struct VALUE that reaches a value-scalar slot through a VARIABLE or non-ctor expression is still uncaught:

  type Box = { val: int }
  fn main() { let s = Box { val: 9 }  let x: int = s }   // compiles clean — wild store

The literal arm in check_expr_expected only sees literals; a variable/if-expr/block whose type is a concrete struct flows through the universal arm, whose shared assign_layout_conflict gate has no struct predicate. It deliberately has none: a bare type-param is .Struct-form, so a broad struct->scalar check would false-positive on type params (the documented 140-artifact minefield behind int_into_pointer_slot).

Fix needs a type-param-SAFE concrete-struct predicate: .Struct with a non-empty nominal AND !vtype_mentions_unresolved(arg_ty), paired with slot_is_concrete_value_scalar. Must be validated against diff-test (the universal arm runs on the compiler's own source, ~140 inference-artifact exprs) to confirm zero false positives before wiring into assign_layout_conflict.

Repro: let s = Box{val:9}; let x: int = s  (and if-expr/block variants). Related: 98z0 (ctor forms, done), 63wu (the layout-conflict gate family).
notes: BLOCKED on w0kt. Attempted the shared-gate struct-VALUE predicate (concrete_struct_into_value_scalar_slot, type-param-guarded via !vtype_mentions_unresolved on the ARG) in PR #557 and REVERTED it: the full suite caught 54 spurious F1000s compiling cli/main.av via the metadata fast-path (main.av:331 self.__parent = cli_new(...) reported @std::cli::Cli not assignable to int). Root cause: the SLOT type resolves to int as an INFERENCE ARTIFACT (real type is a pointer/struct); a real int slot is indistinguishable from an artifact int slot. The type-param guard is on the ARG side, so it does not help — the artifact is on the SLOT side. This is the same w0kt minefield documented for int_into_pointer_slot (typeck returns .Int as a fallback for ~140 unresolved exprs). FIX REQUIRES w0kt first: make inference return .Unknown (not .Int) for unresolved slots, THEN the struct-VALUE gate (and the fn-arg struct-LITERAL case) become safe. Until then, struct VALUES into scalars stay ungated. The ctor-position cases (enum everywhere, struct literal at let/return, parenthesized) ARE safe and shipped in #557.

title: Make Parser save/restore provably complete (ParserState is a hand-synced subset)

(1) ParserState completeness #560 (squash 11260b5d): folded the 4 context-mode flags + quote_depth into ParserState/save_state/restore_state; gensym_seq documented as the one deliberate exclusion (monotonic); unit tests round-trip each field + mutation-checked.
