title: impl parser must capture impl-target type-params onto Stmt.Impl; retire type_decl_tps side-table
description: PR #552 retro-review (S1/S2): parse_impl_declaration discards impl Foo<T> type-params via skip_angle_brackets (3 sites in features/impl_decl/parser.av:13-32). cpvo reconstructs them from a name-keyed resolver side-table (names.av type_decl_tps) — a workaround for parser information loss. Principled fix: capture the impl-target type-params and store on Stmt.Impl (seed-affecting AST field add → make seed-patch-traps + reseed, so post-merge on integration per bootstrap window). Then the resolver reads params off the AST node and the side-table + its qualified/short name-collision fallback + the impl<Q> Foo<Q> rename ceiling all go away. Side-table is the tracked interim.

title: Same-name struct and enum should be a cross-kind DuplicateDecl (F30xx)
description: PR #551 retro-review (S1): the duplicate-decl guard checks cur.structs.idx and cur.enums.idx SEPARATELY (typeck/mod.av:1188 vs :1221), so declaring both a struct Color and an enum Color in one module compiles clean. The type registry then collapses them first-write-wins (type_registry.av:78-81), and the new vtype_eq Struct/Enum branch makes them compare EQUAL. Result: E.V(structColor) into an enum-Color field runs to garbage. This is the actual missing guard underneath the op3w/pyly nominal work. Fix: reject same-short-name decls across kinds within a module as F30xx DuplicateDecl.
close_reason: Cross-kind DuplicateDecl implemented + merged (PR #559, squash 7e70fed3). is_duplicate_type_name checks all nominal kind indexes (struct/shape/enum/newtype); every type-decl arm routes through it; same-name across kinds rejected F3105 whichever order. 11 specs, suite 3341/3341, selfhost+diff-test byte-identical, CodeRabbit clean (addressed newtype-reverse + shape coverage over 2 rounds). Union-alias extension (structurally distinct, not the vtype_eq collapse) tracked separately in 8246 — out of this ticket's struct/enum scope.

title: Remove the 703y span bridge in tc_nominal_payload_mismatch once Stmt/SStmt + Expr/SExpr unify
description: The pyly nominal-payload gate (tc_nominal_payload_mismatch, typeck/mod.av) has a TRANSITIONAL bridge (tc_bridges_span / tc_is_spanned_of) that allows a bare value into a spanned-declared slot and vice versa (Stmt<->SStmt, Expr<->SExpr — a struct whose 'node' field canonically IS the other type). This exists because the compiler's OWN code (the quote machinery's Stmt.Annotated payload, plus ~8 enum-ctor sites) constructs bare-into-spanned during the in-flight 703y span migration; without the bridge the gate F1000s the compiler's own source. ONCE 703y unifies the bare/spanned AST node types (Expr/SExpr, Stmt/SStmt collapse), there is no bare-vs-spanned mismatch to bridge — remove tc_bridges_span/tc_is_spanned_of and let the gate catch any residual nominal mismatch directly. This also completes pyly's ORIGINAL named subclass (bare Stmt into SStmt field), which is currently bridged, not caught. Depends on the 703y AST-span migration.
close_reason: VERIFIED COMPLETE (2026-07-09). The 703y span bridge (tc_bridges_span / tc_is_spanned_of) is GONE — grep for those symbols across packages/std-avrac/src returns only a past-tense comment in pyly_nominal_ctor_gate_test.av ('used to fire'). It was removed by the y5um.8 B-final rep flip, which unified Expr/SExpr + Stmt/SStmt by deleting the spanned-wrapper types and making every Expr/Stmt child a typed arena id (ExprId/StmtId) with spans in id-keyed side-tables — so there is no longer a bare-vs-spanned distinction to bridge (0jj8's stated dependency, the 703y AST-span unification, is satisfied). VERIFICATION: (1) the compiler builds + selfhosts on integration WITHOUT the bridge, so its own source no longer constructs bare-into-spanned (the exact reason the bridge existed) — the concern that removing it would F1000 the compiler's own source no longer holds; (2) pyly_nominal_ctor_gate_test.av passes 6/6, including the regression guard 'an Inner into a { node: Inner } Wrap field is still rejected' — proving tc_nominal_payload_mismatch now catches, unbridged, exactly the wrong-typed-through-a-node-field case the bridge used to allow. No residual work; the outcome this ticket tracks is achieved and tested.

title: Wild store: collection into a value-scalar FN PARAMETER unguarded (blocked by i64-legacy extern params)
description: PR #538 / CodeRabbit. A List/Map argument into a value-scalar parameter slot (take_int(xs) where xs: List<int>, n: int) is a wild store, but the collection_into_value_scalar_slot guard CANNOT be applied at the parameter position (tc_check_newtype_args) as-is: extern C bindings declare 'value: int' as an i64-legacy GENERIC value slot and legitimately pass List/Map values — e.g. extern fn avra_map_set_cstr(map: ptr, key: string, value: int) is called with a List<int> from @std::avrac::coverage::aggregate. Applying the guard mass-false-positived (80 shards). FnTypeMeta has no is_extern flag, so the param check can't distinguish a real int param from an i64-legacy generic slot. Proper fix needs ONE of: (a) add is_extern to FnTypeMeta + thread through fn registration + skip extern params (still risky if internal fns use the i64-legacy pattern); (b) migrate the extern map/runtime interface off 'int'-as-pointer to proper ptr/generic types; (c) fold into the nlzq centralization with extern-awareness. The let / reassign / struct-field / call-result positions ARE guarded (PR #538); only the parameter position is deferred. NOTE in source at tc_check_newtype_args.
notes: DONE in PR #539 (commit 370bc5e4). Threaded is_extern through the fn registry (FnTypeMeta + FnTypeFound + fn_type_reg_register; .ExternFn=true, .Function/newtype-ctor=false, ret-ty rewrite preserves). tc_check_newtype_args now uses the FULL check_assign_layout for normal Avra params (collection->scalar enforced) and check_assign_layout_param ONLY for extern shims. Seed-safe (FnTypeMeta not serialized). Suite 3244/3244, fixed point holds, no selfhost false-positive (the #538-deferral regression is gone). Closing on merge.

title: Metadata codec drops generic struct args (Box<int> round-trips as Box) — cross-package layout-conflict gap
description:
CodeRabbit review finding on PR #538 (63wu arc), but PRE-EXISTING and broader than Map. The metadata binary codec's VT_STRUCT arm (build/metadata.av, BytesWriter.vtype / BytesReader.vtype) writes `.Struct(name, _, _)` — it serializes the struct name + sym id but DROPS the generic type args — and the reader rebuilds `vtype_struct(name, 0)` (no args). So any generic struct in an exported signature round-trips with its args erased: `Box<int>` and `Box<string>` both become bare `Box` across a package boundary.

Surfaced by the Map(K,V) work because map values can now carry generic structs (`Map<string, Box<int>>` round-trips as `Map<string, Box>`), but the defect is general: it affects List<Box<int>>, tuple elements, fn params, etc. — anywhere a generic struct appears in an EXPORTED signature that crosses the metadata boundary. In-process typeck is unaffected (it works on the in-memory ValueType with full args); the gap is cross-package signature sharing.

Impact today is limited: no current @std/compiler exported signature carries a generic struct inside a Map (per the vtype_codec_roundtrip_test note), and the layout-conflict checks run at typeck time pre-metadata. But it is a real correctness hole for cross-package generic-struct layout-conflict detection.

Fix (heavy lift, coordinate with a metadata format bump / legacy tag path so old payloads aren't misread):
  writer VT_STRUCT: self.string(name); self.u64_le(sym_id_for(name)); self.vtype_list(args)
  reader VT_STRUCT: name; id; args = self.vtype_list(); return ValueType.Struct(name, args, 0)
Apply identically to the VT_ENUM/Newtype arms if they also drop args. Deferred from PR #538 to keep that PR scoped to the in-process wild-store fixes.

title: ICE (F9999): block-bodied closure (params) -> RetType { body } crashes codegen
description:
Deep-probe finding (63wu arc). A closure with a BLOCK body crashes codegen with F9999.

Repro:
  fn main() { let f = (x: int) -> int { x }  let _ = f(1) }   // F9999 internal compiler error during codegen
  // also: (x: int) -> Box<string> { Box { val: 9 } } -> F9999 "undefined variable `Box` in function `__lambda_0`"

Contrast: the bare-expr closure form works:
  fn main() { let f = (x: int) -> x  let _ = f(1) }           // OK
  let f = (x) -> Box { val: x }                                // OK (expr body, no block)

So the arrow-plus-block closure form (params) -> RetType { body } either misparses or codegens a lambda whose block body cannot resolve its free identifiers (the "undefined variable in __lambda" symptom). The bare-expr form lowers fine. This blocks block-bodied / explicitly-return-typed closures entirely.

ICE-policy violation (F9999 must be unreachable from user input). Investigate whether (params) -> RetType { block } is intended grammar (CLAUDE.md lists closures as "(x) -> body"). If supported, fix the lambda codegen so the block body's scope/captures resolve. If NOT supported, the parser must reject it with a clean F0001 + help, never let it reach codegen. Separate from the wild-store conflict work but found in the same sweep.
notes: SCOPE (read 2026-06-24): the fix is a parser GRAMMAR DISAMBIGUATION, not a simple missing codegen case. Key contrast: '(x) -> Box { val: x }' is VALID (closure body = struct literal) but '(x: int) -> Box<string> { Box{val:9} }' ICEs — the differentiator is the '<TypeArgs>'. So the parser must disambiguate '-> Name { ... }' (struct-literal body, valid) from '-> RetType { block }' (return-type-annotated block-bodied closure). Two valid interpretations of the same '-> Ident ... {' prefix. Decide intent FIRST (spec Axis 28 lists closures as '(x) -> body' / '(x: int) -> body' — expression bodies; block-bodied closures with explicit ret types are NOT clearly in-spec). If block-bodied closures are intended -> implement parser disambiguation + lambda block-body codegen (the '__lambda_0' undefined-capture symptom = block body's scope/captures not wired) — a real feature. If NOT intended -> parser rejects '(params) -> RetType { block }' with clean F0001+help WITHOUT breaking the valid '-> StructName { fields }' body form (the hard part: telling them apart). Either way F9999-from-user-input is an ICE-policy violation that must die. NOT a session-tail patch — needs a spec decision + careful parser work.

title: ICE (F9999): bare Ok/Err/Some constructor call reaches codegen as undefined function
Wild store: closure-call arguments not typechecked against closure param types
Wild store: FnTyped-vs-FnTyped param/ret layout conflict not detected
Wild store: closure-call arguments not typechecked against closure param types
description:
Deep-probe finding (63wu arc). A closure stored in a local var has its RESULT type checked (let f=(b:string)->b; let x:int=f("a") IS F1000), but its ARGUMENTS are not:
  type Box<T> = { val: T }
  let f = (b: Box<string>) -> b
  f(Box{val:9})   // Box<int> into the closure's Box<string> param — compiles clean, SHOULD be F1000
  let g = (s: string) -> s; g(9)  // int into string param — also slips
The .Call path checks args against registered free-fn params but not against a local closure var's FnTyped/Closure param types. Fix: when the callee resolves to a local of FnTyped(params,ret), run the same generic_args_layout_conflict + int_into_pointer_slot per arg. Depends on the closure binding carrying its param types (FnTyped) — verify and thread if needed.

title: Wild store: FnTyped-vs-FnTyped param/ret layout conflict not detected
notes: SCOPE (investigated 2026-06-24): NOT a clean gate fix — needs a foundational fn-as-value typing change. TWO parts required: (1) generic_args_layout_conflict (typeck/mod.av:1680) needs a .FnTyped branch — mirror the Tuple branch: 'if (a is .FnTyped) && (b is .FnTyped) { return type_list_layout_conflict(tc, vtype_fn_params(a), vtype_fn_params(b)) || nested_layout_conflict(tc, vtype_fn_ret(a), vtype_fn_ret(b)) }' (accessors vtype_fn_params/vtype_fn_ret exist in core/ast.av). This propagates to the fn-call arg gate (tc_check_newtype_args:2453-2457 -> check_assign_layout -> assign_layout_conflict -> generic_args_layout_conflict). BUT part (1) ALONE is dormant: I built+tested it and the repro STILL checks clean. (2) THE REAL BLOCKER: a bare fn-name passed as a value (the arg 'g' in 'apply(g, ...)') types via '.Ident(name) -> type_lookup(tc.types, name)' — the value-binding env, NOT the fn registry tc.fns — so arg_ty is .Unknown and the gate is skipped (vtype_is_unknown). THREE Ident sites: 3528 (infer_arg_for_display — feeds F1003 emission, risky to touch), 3811 (check_expr), 3932 (check_expr_expected). Proper fix: a fn-name-as-value resolves to ValueType.FnTyped(resolved param vtypes from fn_type_get(tc.fns,name).params, ret_ty) for NON-generic fns (tp.length==0; generic fn-values mention unbound T -> skip). FnTypeFound shape at mod.av:174. This is FOUNDATIONAL (broad blast radius: F1003, fn-comparison, fn-assignment, the compiler's own higher-order-fn usage) and needs full suite+selfhost+diff-test — selfhost DOES exercise fn-values so a regression would be caught. NOT a session-tail patch. This is the 3rd typeck ticket (with cpvo, j568) whose 'clean' fix has foundational depth — validates the 'stop hand-patching; do ps3t' guidance.

title: Centralize the layout-conflict check — one gate for 'value meets expected type' (kills per-position drift)
description:
ROOT-CAUSE insight from the 63wu wild-store audit. The layout-conflict (wild-store) check is hand-implemented per (position × expr-kind) across ~15+ sites, and each must REMEMBER to call generic_args_layout_conflict / int_into_pointer_slot. Many didn't — that is the dominant root cause behind 63wu/q6p4/lb81/ibjo/a85d/tokv (NOT wildcards: in each, the handler exists and runs, it just omits the check). This is decentralization drift, distinct from vndt (which only catches literal match _-> swallows; it caught ~1 of these, tc_unify) and distinct from the if-chain sibling 4gid/7ao0 (generic_args_layout_conflict's missing container branches).

THE FIX: route every 'a value meets an expected type' through ONE gate (check_expr_expected is meant to be it) so a position cannot omit the layout check. Concretely: (1) make the bespoke per-position checks (with_check, field_assign_check_expr, tc_check_enum_ctor_args, check_collection_value_arg, check_struct_lit_fields) all funnel their value-vs-declared comparison through a SINGLE shared predicate+reporter; (2) audit that every position that binds a value to a known type calls it; (3) ideally invert control so new positions get it by construction. Even check_expr_expected's own arms can be incomplete (a85d was inside it), so the gate must be uniform across expr-kinds too. This is a SEMANTIC check, so it is NOT covered by ps3t L4 (derived walkers generate traversal, not layout semantics) nor by vndt/L5 (exhaustiveness over matches) — it is its own focused refactor. Highest-leverage item from the audit: collapses ~15 hand-rolled checks to 1 and makes the whole wild-store class drift-proof.
notes: FOLLOW-UP (40c3adbc): a self-review double-check found one preserved-drift shortcut in the Batch-1 conversion — match-tail (tc_check_match_tail_conflict) was routed through check_assign_layout_param (no collection), faithfully preserving a PRE-EXISTING omission: a tail-match arm returning a List/Map into a value-scalar return slot (fn f()->int { match c { _ -> [1] } }) compiled clean (wild store). Fixed: match-tail is a real return slot (not a fn-param extern i64-legacy int / wlll), so it now uses the FULL check_assign_layout (collection→scalar added; int+generic already present). This is exactly the per-position drift nlzq exists to kill — item (e) is now genuinely done, not just behavior-preserved. Safe (collection check is artifact-free, int|bool exemption untouched); suite 3231/3231, fixed point holds. NOTE: a pre-existing complementary double-diagnostic remains at the direct-return collection position (return [1] into int emits both the layout-violation AND the return-type-mismatch message) — two useful complementary messages, NOT introduced by nlzq; left as-is because removing it would scatter the collection check back across positions (the drift nlzq fights).
close_reason: Complete: centralized the wild-store layout-conflict class into two documented shared gates (narrow assign_layout_conflict family for artifact-prone positions; broad nested_layout_conflict for reliable element/value positions). All ~15 positions audited and covered; enum-ctor/struct-field documented as intentionally-stronger. Behaviour-preserving (diff-test byte-identical), full suite 3228/3228, fixed point holds, coverage added. Commits 9a9697b7,757e70f6,de37d10e on claude/amazing-cori-28v9fs.

title: Field assignment (s.field = v) doesn't typecheck the value against the field type — wild store
description: Found during the 'what's left' audit of the 63wu/wild-store conflict-detection arc. field_assign_check_expr (features/struct_decl/mod.av:205) checks obj + value expressions but never compares the value's type against the field's declared type. So BOTH a generic-arg conflict and a bare scalar mismatch slip through as wild stores: type S = { b: Box<string>, name: string }; mut s = S{...}; s.b = Box{val:9} (Box<int> into Box<string> field — OK, should be F1000); s.name = 9 (int into string field — OK, should be F1000). This is the direct-field-assignment twin of with-update (lb81, fixed) — same fix shape: resolve obj's struct name (vtype_struct_name), look up the field's declared type, and run the scalar string-mismatch + generic_args_layout_conflict checks (the single-field version of check_struct_lit_fields). Clean, bounded, high-value (field assignment is a very common construct). NOTE: index-assign xs[0]=v / m["k"]=v does NOT parse (F0001) so it's not a construct; .set covers that path via ibjo.
close_reason: Field assignment now typechecks the value against the field's declared type. field_assign_check_expr resolves the obj's struct name (vtype_struct_name) and routes through check_field_assign_ty → check_one_field_ty (the single-field analog of check_struct_lit_fields, shared with struct-literal field checking), catching both generic-arg layout conflicts (Box<int> into a Box<string> field) and scalar string mismatches (int into a string field) as F1000. Committed b5e1504b; covered by field_assign_conflict_test.av (6 specs, 3 negative + 3 positive). Full suite 3201/3201, selfhost fixed point holds.

title: with-update field values are not type-checked against struct field types (s with { b: Box{val:9} })
description: Expr.With(obj, inits) is lint-scanned and annotated but its field-init values are NOT type-checked against the struct's declared field types, so s with { b: Box{val:9} } on type S = { b: Box<string> } stores a Box<int> in the b slot (wild store) and compiles clean. Likely no field-type check exists at all for with-update (not just the generic-arg case). Fix: in the With typecheck, resolve obj's struct type and check each init value against the corresponding field type (scalar<->ptr + generic_args_layout_conflict), mirroring StructLit field checking. Found during 63wu deep round.
close_reason: Fixed + validated. lb81: with_check now routes through check_struct_lit_fields (field-exists + scalar + generic-arg layout conflict) keyed on the source struct name (commit 3aa1ea1d). ibjo: check_method_call guards push/set/insert/map.set value args via check_collection_value_arg (generic_args_layout_conflict + int_into_pointer_slot), reusing precomputed arg types (commit 72dbd457). Both pushed to claude/amazing-cori-28v9fs. Full suite green + selfhost fixed point byte-identical; targeted probes confirm conflicts caught with no false positives (incl. generic-mut contexts).

title: Generic enum ctor result type drops inferred type-args — Wrap<string> = Wrap.W(Box{val:9}) escapes
description: For a generic enum (enum Wrap<T> { W(v: Box<T>) }), the ctor Wrap.W(Box{val:9}) does not infer T=int into the result type (stays Wrap<?>), so the let-binding conflict check generic_args_layout_conflict(Wrap<?>, Wrap<string>) can't fire and the conflict escapes. Also tc_check_enum_ctor_args skips when the payload type mentions a type param (Box<T> still generic at ctor-check time). Needs enum-ctor result-type inference (bind T from payload args, like fn-arg inference binds type params), then the existing let/return/arg conflict checks catch it. Sibling of E1 (non-generic). Found during 63wu deep round.
notes: Confirmed during the deeper 63wu sweep: the built-in Result/Option ctors are instances of this same gap — .Ok(Box{val:9}) into Result<Box<string>,_> and .Some(Box{val:9}) into Box<string>? both compile clean (SHOULD be F1000). Same mechanism: the generic enum's payload type param is unbound at ctor-check time, so the result type stays Result<?>/Option<? > and the let/return conflict check can't fire. Fixing enum-ctor result-type inference closes the user-defined AND the built-in Result/Option cases together.
close_reason: Fixed + merged via #546 (squash a4c4189d). tc_infer_enum_ctor_type_args infers a generic enum's type-args from the ctor payload, wired into explicit (check_expr), subjectless (check_expr_expected), and .Some-into-T? paths; the existing layout gate then catches the conflict. Covers user enums (Wrap), built-in Result/Option, explicit+subjectless forms, optional T?, and the return position — all emit F1000; valid programs clean. Gate-local (g97x tracks the shared-unifier Struct/Enum arm) so IR is byte-identical (HRN diff-test confirmed twice). Suite 3281/3281, selfhost byte-identical, 13-case spec test.

title: enum-ctor payload arg not checked for generic-arg layout conflict (Wrap.W(Box{val:9}) into W(v: Box<string>))
description: tc_check_enum_ctor_args does a scalar<->ptr representation check on payload args but NOT a generic-arg layout conflict, so a same-representation-class value with conflicting generic args slips into an enum payload slot: enum Wrap { W(v: Box<string>), N }; Wrap.W(Box{val:9}) compiles (Box<int> into a Box<string> payload = wild store). Fix: in tc_check_enum_ctor_args, when the scalar-vs-ptr check passes, also run generic_args_layout_conflict(arg_ty, field_ty). Non-generic enum case is directly fixable (field type is concrete). Found during 63wu deep round.
close_reason: Fixed: tc_check_enum_ctor_args now runs generic_args_layout_conflict(arg_ty, field_ty) when the scalar↔ptr check passes, catching Box<int>-into-Box<string>-payload wild stores. Non-generic enum payloads covered; generic-payload case (Box<T>) is the separate enwi (needs ctor result-type inference). Test enum_ctor_payload_layout_conflict_test.av 5/5; committed; full-suite gate running.

title: Collection mutation methods (List.push / Map.set / .insert) don't typecheck the value arg against the element/value type
description:
Surfaced during 63wu deep review. A wrong-typed value passed to a collection mutation method is a wild store but is NOT caught — the method-call typeck returns the result type without checking the value arg against the receiver's element/value type. General (List AND Map), pre-existing, independent of 63wu's literal-path fix.

Repro (both compile clean, both wild stores):
  type Box<T> = { val: T }
  mut xs: List<Box<string>> = [Box{val:"ok"}]; let _ = xs.push(Box{val:9})   // Box<int> into List<Box<string>>
  mut m: Map<string, Box<string>> = {"a": Box{val:"ok"}}; m.set("b", Box{val:9})  // Box<int> into Map value slot

Fix: check_list_method/check_map_method (features/{list_lit,map_lit}/typeck.av) need the receiver's element/value type threaded in (the receiver type is now Map(.Str,V) / List(elem) post-63wu) and must run generic_args_layout_conflict on the value arg(s) for push/set/insert. Mirrors check_list_lit_with_expected / check_map_lit_with_expected but for the method-call path.
close_reason: Fixed + validated. lb81: with_check now routes through check_struct_lit_fields (field-exists + scalar + generic-arg layout conflict) keyed on the source struct name (commit 3aa1ea1d). ibjo: check_method_call guards push/set/insert/map.set value args via check_collection_value_arg (generic_args_layout_conflict + int_into_pointer_slot), reusing precomputed arg types (commit 72dbd457). Both pushed to claude/amazing-cori-28v9fs. Full suite green + selfhost fixed point byte-identical; targeted probes confirm conflicts caught with no false positives (incl. generic-mut contexts).

title: Layout-conflict + type-arg inference skip several container ValueType variants (Newtype/Channel/Task/Union) — tuple-wrap bypass class
description:
Sibling of vndt, surfaced during 63wu deep review. Two recursion functions enumerate container ValueType variants by hand and silently no-op on the ones they miss, so a layout conflict (a wild store) escapes by wrapping in the unhandled container:

1) typeck generic_args_layout_conflict (if-chain dispatch): had branches for List/Map/Optional + nominal Struct/Enum args, but NOT Tuple (FIXED on claude/amazing-cori-28v9fs — was a TRIVIAL total bypass: let t:(int,string)=(1,9) compiled), and still NOT Newtype/Channel/Task/Union. vtype_type_args only exposes Struct/Enum args, so any other container needs an explicit branch.
2) typeck tc_unify (match with _ -> acc, a literal vndt site): had List/Task/Optional/FnTyped, was missing Map (FIXED) and is still missing Channel. Its mono twin unify_param has Channel but not the symmetric set — keep them in lockstep.

REMAINING: add Newtype/Channel/Task/Union branches to generic_args_layout_conflict (each carries inner type(s) that can hide a conflict) and Channel to tc_unify. Each is a potential wild-store hole like Tuple/Map were. Reuse the type_list_layout_conflict helper added on the 63wu branch. Gate on full suite (shared hot function — watch for false positives; the settled-type guard should prevent them). ROOT-CAUSE framing: this is the if-chain analog of vndt's match-_ removal — these hand-maintained variant dispatches drift whenever a container variant is added. Ideally derive the recursion (y9y4 derive_walker) so it can't drift.
close_reason: Investigated all four container variants; the structural-branch approach applies to none of them, the real remaining item is re-filed: (1) Channel/Task — channel<T>/task are CONSTRUCTOR-ONLY syntax (Expr.ChannelNew), not type-annotation forms, so they cannot reach generic_args_layout_conflict or tc_unify from source (channel<int> as a param type is F0001) — no structural branch needed/reachable; (2) Union — tagged heterogeneous type, not a single-layout wrapper, recursing it would be semantically wrong (each value is tagged), excluded by design; (3) Newtype — structural strip is DEAD (W resolves to .Struct not .Newtype at conflict time), needs nominal registry resolution instead — re-filed as a focused P3 ticket. Tuple (the severe, reachable one) was already fixed in 6dd7a772. tc_unify Channel parity is moot (no channel type annotations). Net: the reachable/applicable container recursions (List/Map/Optional/Tuple) are all done.

title: Efficient string/bytes builder + single-pass join — kill O(n²) iterative-concat traps compiler-wide
description:
Generalizes the snw0 seed-train OOM fix (PR #537 / commit 9bbcd394). That bug was an accidental O(n^2): BytesWriter.finish combined chunks via a left fold of acc.concat(chunk), recopying the whole accumulator each step — 576KB of metadata output cost ~14GB of intermediate buffers and OOM-killed the 16GB CI. PR #537 fixed THAT site (divide-and-conquer concat, O(n log n)).

The underlying pattern is general infrastructure, not metadata-specific:
- A single a.concat(b) / a + b is already O(a+b) (one alloc + one copy) — NOT the problem.
- ITERATIVE concatenation (build a result by repeated concat in a loop/fold) is O(n^2): each step recopies everything accumulated so far (Schlemiel-the-Painter). Applies to BOTH bytes AND string (diagnostics rendering, codegen IR text, .join, any accumulate-in-a-loop).

Scope:
1. Provide an efficient, documented general facility in @std:
   - A bytes/string BUILDER with amortized-doubling append (Vec/StringBuilder semantics): O(n) total, no per-append allocation. (BytesWriter currently allocates one bytes object per .u8/.u32 write — also a target.)
   - An O(n) single-pass join/concat_all(List<bytes|string>): sum lengths -> one allocation -> copy each piece exactly once. Likely warrants a runtime avra_bytes_blit (memcpy) primitive so the combine is one memcpy pass, not per-byte.
2. Audit existing iterative-concat / accumulate-in-a-loop sites across the compiler and route them through the builder/join. Confirm List<string>.join is single-pass (not a fold). Prime suspects: diagnostic/render code, codegen IR-text assembly, metadata.
3. Subsumes: upgrade BytesWriter.finish from the current O(n log N) divide-and-conquer to the single-allocation O(n) optimum once the blit primitive exists (the remaining log factor I flagged on PR #537).

Acceptance: documented O(n) builder + join in @std; BytesWriter is single-allocation/amortized; audit complete with O(n^2) hot-path sites converted; no remaining accumulate-in-a-loop O(n^2) on a hot path. Relates to epic 4apk (COMPILER-FAST).

title: Map literals track no value type — Map<K, Box<string>> = {k: Box{val:9}} conflict undetectable
description: A map-value generic conflict (let m: Map<string, Box<string>> = {"k": Box{val:9}}) is a real wild store — m["k"].val is int but typed string — but is UNDETECTABLE because ValueType.Map is a BARE variant (core/ast.av:448, no fields) and vtype_from_name("Map") -> ValueType.Map drops the args (core/ast.av:576). Nothing in the type system tracks map key/value types, so there's no V to check a map value against. FIX requires making Map carry K/V: change ValueType.Map -> ValueType.Map(key, value), populate it in the parser/resolver for Map<K,V> annotations and infer it for MapLit entries, update every .Map match site, then thread V to map values for the conflict check (like check_list_lit_with_expected does for elements). SEED IMPACT: ValueType is processed by the seed, so adding a field needs make seed-patch-traps + a seed cycle (make update-seed) — which the bootstrap window forbids on a feature branch. Best done on the integration branch as a dedicated change. Distinct from the other 26ql work (all of which was doable without touching core types).
close_reason: Implemented: ValueType.Map now carries (key, value) types (mirrors List(elem)). Parser fills K/V from Map<K,V> annotations; map-literal inference pins the value type in all 3 paths; generic_args_layout_conflict recurses through a matching Map shell; check_expr_expected gains a .MapLit arm checking every value. Threaded K/V through all ValueType.Map sites (vtype_eq/eq_deep, stamp_ids, display/render_full, mono mangle/unify/nonconcrete/from_string, metadata codec encode+decode, quote lower + eval decode, codegen arms). The wild store Map<string,Box<string>>={"k":Box{val:9}} is now F1000; valid maps + matching instantiations still compile. New spec test map_value_layout_conflict_test.av (9 cases). Full suite 3145/3145; selfhost fixed point byte-identical. Committed 39b9ac07, pushed to claude/amazing-cori-28v9fs (no seed.lock bump — feature-branch discipline; merge will auto-trigger the seed train to bake the Map field into v8).

title: Generic fn returning a bare type param from a scalar literal isn't conflict-checked (id(9))
description: let y: string = id<T>(9) miscompiles silently (runtime prints null): tc_infer_type_args does NOT bind T from a literal arg, so with fill-only inference the expected type legitimately fills T=string (gap-fill), and the scalar int->string assignability leniency in check_binding (the !(r.ty is .Int) skip) hides the rest. Two parts: (1) make tc_infer_type_args bind a type param from a literal/value arg's static type so id(9) infers T=int; (2) tighten scalar int->string assignability OR add a guarded layout check on the .Call return (note: builtin string surfaces as Struct("string") which the type-param guard treats as unresolved, so the naive .Call layout_conflict is dead — needs resolve to .Str first). Distinct from the generic-arg OVERRIDE closed in 26ql.
notes: CLOSED via e63c5b59. The documented id(9)->string wild store is rejected in all leaking positions (let/arg/reassign; field+return already did). tc_infer_type_args already bound T=int from the literal (part 1 was a non-issue); the fix was tightening int->string assignability (part 2). Scoped to int->string (clean, unambiguous, 0 FPs, byte-identical diff-test, selfhost+8 suites green, 9 regression tests). Broader scalar->ptr (int->struct/list, needs Optional/Ptr exclusions) split to forge-crafting-intepreters-w0kt. NOTE: my first attempt looked dead due to a STALE bs2 (didn't clear packages/cli/src/build/cache when editing the non-entry typeck/mod.av) — the CLAUDE.md dev-loop gotcha; always full-clear when editing non-entry files.
close_reason: int->string wild store (id(9)) closed in all positions; broader scalar->ptr split to forge-crafting-intepreters-w0kt

title: Generic-arg conflict: map literal values bypass the layout check
description: A wrong generic annotation on a map value (`let m: Map<string, Box<string>> = {"k": Box{val:9}}`) is NOT caught by the generic-arg layout conflict check, because map literals are typed bare `.Map` (MapLit -> ValueType.Map at typeck/mod.av) — they carry NO key/value type at all. Closing this needs map key/value type tracking FIRST, then thread the value type to map-literal values in check_expr_expected (a .MapLit arm), mirroring the .ListLit element check. Broader than the struct-literal positions closed in 26ql. Construction is memory-safe regardless via the mono gap-fill; this is diagnostic-completeness.

title: test-runner metadata fast-path is broken on a cold tree (two bugs) — forces the OOM-prone whole-program fallback
description:
The per-file test runner's metadata fast-path (the 10x speedup: stub @std/* in each shard, link pre-built producer .o's) does not engage on a cold tree, forcing the memory-heavy whole-program fallback. TWO independent bugs:

1. PRE-BUILD REDIRECT FAILS (cold tree). pre_build_workspace_std_packages (main.av ~996) runs each pkg build with '> ${dir}build/prebuild.log'. Packages NOT produced by 'make build' (std-process, std-test) have no build/ dir, so the shell can't open the redirect — the command fails (rc=1, no log) BEFORE bs2 runs. Two such failures => pre-build rc=2 => fast-path disabled. Fix: 'mkdir -p ${dir}build' before the redirect. (Verified: with build/ present both packages lib-build rc=0.)

2. PRODUCER OBJS INCOMPLETE (even when the pre-build succeeds). With build/ dirs present the pre-build succeeds and the fast-path engages, but ~79 shards then fail to LINK: 'undefined symbol: @std::avrac::test_runner::write_fixture' and '__release_@std::avrac::core::Stmt' / '__release_...EmitValue' / '...StmtResult'. nm confirms std-avrac's unit.realobj.o does not define write_fixture at all. So the --lib producer realobj omits the test_runner module AND the cross-package __release_<T> RC shims that consumer shards stub. This is the 08ro symptom class resurfacing. Fix is in lib-mode codegen: the producer objs must define every symbol a metadata-stub shard externs (test_runner module + generated __release_ shims for @std types used across the boundary).

Until BOTH are fixed the fast-path can't be safely enabled; the runner falls back to whole-program shards, whose concurrency is now memory-capped (the sibling OOM fix: jobs=2 when want_meta=false). Repairing this restores the 121s->11s fast path. AVRA_USE_METADATA_LIB=0 forces the (now memory-safe) fallback explicitly.
notes:
INVESTIGATED in depth (claude/amazing-cori-28v9fs). Findings:

BUG 1 (mkdir redirect): REAL. Cold-tree packages (std-process/std-test, not built by 'make build') lack build/, so the pre-build's '> build/prebuild.log' redirect fails before bs2 runs. One-line fix (mkdir -p) verified to work. BUT it's GATED on yczz: with mkdir, the pre-build proceeds to compile std-avrac, which OOMs (~15GB, see yczz), wasting ~280s before falling back. So mkdir is net-negative until the compiler memory footprint is fixed — kept REVERTED for now, re-apply after yczz.

BUG 2 (undefined write_fixture / __release_ symbols): was MY contamination, not a real codegen gap. The clean correct-root build defines write_fixture + 288 __release_ shims (3280 fns). The 'undefined' came from the lib-build cache being keyed on the package SOURCE FINGERPRINT ONLY, not AVRA_LIB_PKG_ROOT: my wrong-root ('@std.avrac' vs '@std::avrac') investigation builds cached a symbol-less .ll that the real run reused. That cache-key gap is a REAL soundness bug (a normal build-then-test with differing roots could poison it too).

SHIPPED: cache-key soundness fix — fp_for_unit now mixes lib_pkg_root into the unit fingerprint (BuildInputs.lib_pkg_root threaded through all 3 construction sites). Verified: a wrong-root then correct-root build now land in DISTINCT cache slots (write_fixture defines: 0 vs 3). selfhost + diff-test pending.

The cold fast-path itself is blocked on yczz (compiler memory ~10x too high). The sibling jobs-cap (60ba291c) already makes the whole-program fallback memory-safe, so the suite is reliable regardless.
close_reason: SUPERSEDED / folded into the existing structure (per review: this duplicated scoped tickets). Disposition of its two bugs: (1) cold-tree pre-build redirect failure — REAL, NEW, fixed in commit e5c54c09 (mkdir the log dir); recorded under snw0. (2) undefined test_runner/__release_ symbols — was TWO things: my own cross-root cache poisoning (fixed c381f9c6, see pdme.1) + the pre-existing producer-library subsetting which is already 08ro. The cold-tree OOM that forces the degraded path is snw0 (lever c done = jobs-cap 60ba291c; levers a/b open). The '15GB compiler bloat' angle (yczz) was a session-pressure misdiagnosis, closed. Nothing unique left in gvi5.

title: Nested generic instance as explicit annotation not monomorphized (Box<Box<int>> param, Maybe<Maybe<int>> return)
description: Now that the >> lexer split (ntcb) lets nested generic type ANNOTATIONS parse, a second gap is exposed: a nested generic instance used as an EXPLICIT param/return annotation (not inferred from a literal) isn't collected/mangled by the monomorphizer. Repro (all PARSE fine post-ntcb, fail at codegen): (1) 'type Box<T>={val:T} fn f(b: Box<Box<int>>)->int{b.val.val}' -> 'field access on non-struct value (ty=)' — the param's nested type resolves to empty; (2) 'enum Maybe<T>{Just(v:T),Nothing} fn f()->Maybe<Maybe<int>>{...}' -> 'unknown enum Maybe__int'. Single-level annotations (Box<int> param) work; only NESTED explicit annotations fail. Root cause: mono collects instances from struct literals / ctor calls / generic calls, but the explicit-annotation path (param/return ValueType) doesn't recurse to collect+mangle the inner instance. Adjacent to wpqd (which fixed the literal-construction path). Fix: collect generic instances appearing in param/return/let type annotations and rewrite those annotation ValueTypes to mangled names, recursing into nested args. Separately, Map<K,V> indexing on an annotated local ('let m: Map<string,int>={...}; m[k]') hits 'indexing on non-string/list value' — likely a distinct Map-codegen gap, may warrant its own ticket.
notes: STRUCT half FIXED (commit f35619c0, branch claude/fyzs-annotation-mono): field access on a generic-struct value typed by a return/let/param annotation now works (single + nested) via (1) codegen emit_field_on_value reclassifying Enum-form mangled names through resolve_codegen_vtype, and (2) mono rewrite_instance_vtype rendering the full type to disambiguate nested instances. This also fixed a pre-existing single-level gap. REMAINING (separate tickets filed): nested generic ENUM match typeck F1000; generic literal inline in a then-block not collected across test-runner units. Keep fyzs open until the enum case lands.
close_reason: Both named repros now work end-to-end (verified): (1) Box<Box<int>> as a param/return/let annotation — fixed in PR #534 (codegen reclassifies Enum-form mangled names to structs + mono disambiguates nested instances via full-render); (2) Maybe<Maybe<int>> return + nested match — fixed in PR #535 (v3a3: typeck same-instantiation payload binding + mono keeps distinct concrete insts). Remaining deeper/edge cases are tracked separately: 3+ levels and a nested ctor written directly as a match subject = ebs1 (typeck expected-type propagation through nested ctors); a generic literal inline in a then-block = w62c (test-runner per-unit collection). Closing the umbrella per its stated scope.

title: Lower test-suite memory cost: degraded-mode shards compile all of @std (~10GiB each)
description: The bundled test runner is fine when the @std metadata fast-path works (shards STUB @std + link a prebuilt producer .o → lightweight). But when the fast-path degrades (08ro fixes now make it degrade CORRECTLY, to whole-program shards), each shard compiles its FULL @std closure — i.e. the entire self-hosted compiler — at ~10GiB anon-rss (confirmed via dmesg: bs2 OOM-killed at 10.9GiB). Parallel whole-program shards then OOM on a ~15GiB box, and a cold 'make build && make test' (make build's ~10GiB peak + cold pre-build + cold shards) can tip even the fast-path into degrading. Net: the full suite can't run cold on a 15GiB box. NOT a compiler-correctness bug; a memory-footprint/resource issue. Levers: (a) make degraded-mode shards NOT pull in all of @std (compile only the test + its actual closure, or always require the producer objects); (b) reduce the compiler's per-compile memory (the whole-program @std compile holding the full AST+IR resident); (c) cap shard parallelism by available RAM when degraded. Standalone lib build is only 137MiB (no emit_metadata blowup — an earlier misdiagnosis). Surfaced over a long debugging session where session-accumulated memory pressure + the fxfz cache-freeze (now fixed) masqueraded as code bugs.
notes:
PROGRESS from the qcvb-branch debugging (claude/amazing-cori-28v9fs):
- LEVER (c) IMPLEMENTED — commit 60ba291c: prepare_test_run now caps whole-program FALLBACK shard concurrency to jobs=2 (vs the default 8) when !lib.want_meta. Measured ~6GB used / ~9GB free at jobs=2 vs the 8-wide OOM. The suite now COMPLETES on a 15GB box (degraded but no OOM crash). AVRA_JOBS still overrides.
- NEW degradation cause found + fixed (commit e5c54c09): the pre-build redirect to ${pkg}build/prebuild.log fails for packages make-build never produces (std-process/std-test have no build/ dir) → pre-build rc!=0 → fast-path disabled on EVERY cold tree, any box. mkdir -p fixes it. This is distinct from the memory issue and was masking it.
- CONFIRMED your 'standalone lib build ~137MiB / session-pressure misdiagnosis' note: I re-walked into exactly that trap (measured '~15GB' under session-accumulated pressure, filed it as yczz, then re-measured clean = build succeeds rc=0). yczz CLOSED as the same ghost. The ~10GiB cost is the DEGRADED SHARD whole-program @std compile (lever b), not the lib build.
- STILL OPEN (this ticket's core): levers (a) degraded shards shouldn't pull ALL of @std, and (b) reduce that whole-program compile's footprint — so a cold 'make build && make test' fits on 15GB with the fast-path ENGAGED (not just degraded-but-safe).

title: Test-runner producer-library link breaks when a non-harness shard imports @std.avrac.test_runner
description: Adding a compile-error test (uses 'use @std.avrac.test_runner.{write_fixture}' + 'extern fn avra_shell_exec') under features/generics/tests/ makes ~76 UNRELATED bundled shards fail to link with 'ld.lld: error: undefined symbol' for core/std symbols (sstmt_at, sstmt_dummy, sexpr_dummy, value_to_stmt_list, features::modules::filter_to_target_unit, __release_@std::lsp::IoError). Deterministic, reproducible from a fully clean 'make clean && make build && make test' (69/69 pass, 76 shards fail). The same file passes in isolation ('bs2 test <file>') and the comptime tests dir (which also uses write_fixture) passes — so it is the shard COMPOSITION/producer-library subsetting: when a shard that doesn't normally include test_runner pulls it in, the AVRA_LIB_OBJS realobj linked into that shard is missing symbols (inconsistent metadata/realobj state). Same family as 927f/jdgo/fxfz. Root-cause fix: ensure every shard links a complete producer-library realobj regardless of which @std modules its test files import (or build the realobj with fast-path stripped, like the seed train does). Surfaced red-teaming the 2px2 PR; worked around there by not adding a test_runner-importing compile-error test in the generics shard.
notes: NOTE from gvi5 debugging: a DISTINCT cause of the same 'undefined symbol' symptom exists and is now fixed — cross-root cache poisoning (commit c381f9c6, see pdme.1): a build under a different/empty AVRA_LIB_PKG_ROOT cached a symbol-less .ll that a correct-root consumer reused. That's separate from THIS ticket's clean-build producer-library SUBSETTING (a shard importing test_runner links a realobj that doesn't define it). With the cache-key fixed + the fast-path forced off, a clean run showed 0 undefined symbols here — but the fast-path couldn't be exercised cleanly on the 15GB box (it degraded for the snw0 memory reason), so this subsetting bug is NOT yet confirmed fixed/closed. Keep open; re-test once snw0 lets the fast-path engage cold.

title: Nested generic struct monomorphization: Box<Box<int>> codegen 'unknown struct Box'
description: A generic struct used as another generic struct's type-arg (Box<Box<int>> via let b = Box { val: Box { val: 9 } }) type-checks under 2px2 (b.val.val substitutes to int) but fails at CODEGEN: 'unknown struct generic_struct_field_substitution_test::Box (emitting fn ...)'. The nested instance isn't monomorphized/registered: codegen sees the bare generic name 'Box' instead of the mangled 'Box__Box__int'/'Box__int'. Pre-existing mono/codegen gap (before 2px2 the nested field access typed leniently as Unknown so it never reached this codegen path); orthogonal to 2px2 field-access substitution. Surfaced while red-teaming the 2px2 PR. Repro: type Box<T> = { val: T }; fn f() -> int { let b = Box { val: Box { val: 9 } }  b.val.val }. Fix in the monomorphizer: when inferring a generic struct's type-args from a struct-typed field init, recurse so the inner instantiation is also collected + emitted.
notes: ROOT CAUSE confirmed (deeper than first thought). The construction inference is FINE: typeck annotates the inner Box{val:9} as Struct("Box",[Int]) (via tc_struct_lit_vtype/2px2), and mono's infer_from_field_inits reads init.value.ty, so the outer correctly infers T=Box<int>. The gap is DOWNSTREAM in mono specialization: when specialize_struct emits the monomorphized outer struct (Box__Box__int), it substitute_vtype's the field 'val: T' to Box<int> = Struct("Box",[Int]) but never MANGLES that nested generic-instance field type to the monomorphized name Box__int. Codegen's resolve_codegen_vtype then looks up the bare "Box" → F9999 'unknown struct Box'. NOT fixable via infer_lit_ty (tried — construction inference uses .ty, not infer_lit_ty; reverted). Real fix: during struct specialization, rewrite generic-instance types appearing in substituted field types to their mangled names (and ensure the inner instantiation Box<int> is collected/emitted), OR have codegen resolve a Struct-with-type_args by its mangled name. Mono-side (option A) is the right place — mirrors how call/ctor sites get mangled. Repro: type Box<T> = { val: T }; fn f() -> int { let b = Box { val: Box { val: 9 } }  b.val.val }.
close_reason: Fixed: nested generic struct monomorphization works for double/triple nesting, distinct deep instantiations (Box<Box<int>> vs Box<Box<string>>), generic-struct fields, and with-expr. Root causes: (1) instance dedup collapsed distinct instantiations via type-arg-blind vtype_eq — added local vtype_eq_with_args in the mono merge check; (2) specialized struct field types kept bare generic names — added rewrite_field_types + .TypeDecl rewrite arm; (3) unify_param could not bind a param reachable only through a generic-struct field, and vtype_mangle_slug diverged from the specialized decl name — cross-matched Enum/Struct decl-vs-instance forms via vtype_type_args and flattened the slug to match mangle_name_ordered with a double-encode guard. Also fixed a non-generic codegen bug underneath: nested struct literals shared the outer's copy_alloc_target stack slot (struct_decl + with_expr now clear it before filling fields). Tests: nested_generic_struct_test.av (6), nested_struct_literal_test.av (4); generics/struct_decl/with_expr/enum/match/null suites all green. Committed 65d89161, branch claude/wpqd-fix. Nested generic type ANNOTATIONS remain blocked by the separate lexer >> limitation (ntcb/6oan).

title: Infer enum-literal type args from constructor payload (EnumCtor analog of StructLit inference)
description: A bare generic enum-ctor literal like `CiEnum.CiSome(5)` is typed as `Enum(name, [], 0)` (empty type args) in both typeck (annotate fast-path + check_expr, ~mod.av:1845/2982) and mono.av infer_lit_ty (:578). So when such a literal is passed to a generic fn where a type param is reachable ONLY through the enum arg, inference fails with F1002 — the unify_param Enum arm (jl8q) has no args to unify against. Fix: infer the enum's type args by matching the constructor payload exprs' types against the variant's declared field types (which reference the enum's type params), populating Enum(name, [resolved...], 0). Mirrors the tuple-literal fix in jl8q and is a sibling of 2px2 (StructLit instance type args). Needs the enum registry (tp + variants) threaded to the inference locus. Workaround until then: a typed binding (`let m: CiEnum<int> = ...`) or turbofish carries the args so unify_param binds correctly. Union- and Newtype-literal type-arg inference are analogous and can ride along.
close_reason: arg_concrete_ty/infer_lit_ty now re-infer a bare generic enum-ctor literal's type args from its payload (reusing resolve_enum_type_args), so a type param reachable only through the enum binds at the call site without a type annotation. Tested in generic_container_inference_test.av (bare CiEnum.CiSome(5)). Full suite 3027/3027 + selfhost byte-identical. NOTE: a no-payload variant with explicit turbofish args (EaMaybe<int>.EaNone) is a separate, narrower case not covered here.

title: codegen: int(newtype) crashes (null deref) instead of unwrapping or erroring
description: Found while building the L1 arena (ps3t.3.2). With 'type ExprId = int', the expression 'int(id)' where id: ExprId compiles but crashes at runtime with 'null pointer dereference (accessed address 0x1)'. Expected: either unwrap to the inner int (like .raw()), or a clean type error (F-code). The .raw() method is the correct unwrap path; int(newtype) should not silently produce crashing code. Repro: type ExprId = int; fn main() { let id = ExprId(1); println(string(int(id))) }.

title: Hermetic spec test for the diff-test (HRN) harness — scratch-repo + stub compilers
description: The diff-test harness (diagnose.sh --diff-test) is verified today by live probes (run manually: PASS on identical compiler source, FAIL/rc1 on a codegen-differing base, corpus skip/compare loop) and by CI (.github/workflows/diff-test.yml on every PR), but has no committed hermetic spec — the same gap, and same cause, as the window gate's jd7y. Two obstacles to a fast committed spec: (1) diagnose.sh binds REPO_DIR to its own location, so a hermetic run needs a scratch-git-repo + REPO_DIR/BOOTSTRAP_DIR parameterization (shared with jd7y); (2) the harness builds two REAL compilers (~minutes) — too slow for the suite — so the test needs a seam to supply two cheap, deliberately-differing 'compilers' (or compare two pre-built IR files), exercising the OUTPUT contract without a full build. Assertions to cover: identical IR -> PASS/rc0; differing IR -> FAIL/rc1 + readable diff; corpus input OLD can't compile -> skipped (not failed); NEW fails an input OLD compiled -> divergence; DIFF_TEST_QUICK=1 skips the corpus. Testability refactor, not a behaviour change.
acceptance_criteria: A committed spec (avra_shell_exec-driven, like seed_train_test.av) exercises the diff-test harness hermetically against a scratch fixture with stubbed/cheap compilers, asserting the PASS/FAIL/skip/quick matrix; runs in the bundled suite in seconds (no real compiler build).

title: Deliberate-SIGABRT crash test containment is batch-composition fragile
description: capture_thread_isolation_test.av's deliberate SIGABRT (designed to be caught, exits 0 in isolation) escapes and corrupts batch-mates when the parallel runner's batch packing shifts. Adding PR #524's standalone seed_self_contained_test.av flipped the suite from 2988/2988 green to '1 spec crashed'; AVRA_TEST_JOBS=1 made it worse (2 sibling failures). Likely a sibling mid avra_shell_exec fork/waitpid when SIGABRT fires. Root-cause fix: make deliberate-abort containment independent of batch packing (run the crash unit solo, or harden the longjmp/sink unwind vs concurrent fork). #524 worked around it by folding the spec into an existing file (file-set matches the green baseline). Family: d4jv (in-process test parallelism) / irh4 (shard packing nondeterminism).
close_reason: Duplicate of forge-crafting-intepreters-4m1e (same crash-containment batch fragility; 4m1e has the fuller writeup).

title: Assembled test shards share one global type namespace — a test-local type can shadow stdlib types for its batch-mates
description: A test file declaring 'enum Result { Ok(value: int), ... }' (multi_payload_enum_test, now renamed) shadowed stdlib Result<T,E> for every file in its assembled shard: batch-mates' '.Ok(b)' payloads typed as int, failing shard compile with 'field access on non-struct value' — and in the reversed file order the contamination broke @std/process instead. Failure is nondeterministic by shard PACKING (adding unrelated test files reshuffles batches and flips it on/off), which is the worst kind of flake. Immediate fix was renaming the test's enum; the structural fix is per-file namespacing (or collision detection with a clear diagnostic) in the test assembler, so a test file's top-level decls cannot leak into batch-mates. Repro recipe preserved: './build/bs2 _test_shard <file_declaring_Result> <any_file_matching_stdlib_Result>'.

title: Scratch-repo harness to spec the bootstrap-window gate-1 decision matrix
description: The window gate's git-graph behavior (off-train pin-change rejection, vendored→pinned migration tolerance via content identity, pre-lock vs lock-era resolution, integration-branch exemption) is verified today by live probes (scratch branches + committed lock bumps, run manually and in CI) but has no committed spec — diagnose.sh binds REPO_DIR to its own location, so a hermetic test needs a scratch-git-repo harness: init a fixture repo under build/cache/_window_harness with a fake integration branch + seed pin, run a REPO_DIR-parameterized gate against it, and assert the full matrix (pass / violation / migration / dirty-pin warn / on-integration skip). Requires threading REPO_DIR/BOOTSTRAP_DIR overrides (env or args) through the gate functions — a testability refactor, not a behavior change.

title: Fixture .bin freshness ignores C link inputs — run_fg reuses binaries built against stale runtime.o/llvm_wrapper.o
description: run_fg's reuse rule is '[ bin -nt fg ] && [ bin -nt BS2 ]' — the C link inputs aren't consulted, and under the test harness AVRA_SKIP_ENSURE_BS2=1 also skips ensure_llvm_wrapper/ensure_runtime, so an llvm_wrapper.c or runtime.c edit never reaches already-built fixture binaries. Found via mutation testing: a deliberately broken extern-redeclare guard in llvm_wrapper.c left extern_guard_tolerance_test green because the fixture .bin (and the link cache keyed on the stale .o) predated the mutation; after manually rebuilding the .o and clearing fixture bins + build/cache/link, the spec failed as designed. Fix direction: include the link-input fingerprint (link_shared_fp) in the fixture-bin freshness rule, and make the harness path refresh the C objects (cheap, hash-keyed) before dispatch. Same staleness family as the known mtime-freshness tickets.

title: Parallel per_file shards OOM-kill bs2 fixture compiles (Linux 16GB/4-core) — flaky bundled spec failures
description:
During a pre-commit per_file suite run, the kernel OOM-killed a bs2 process (total-vm 1.8GB, anon-rss 1.6GB) mid fixture compile; the affected unit (walker_wrapper_single_test, 3x no-metadata fixture compiles — the heaviest class) then failed its assertion on garbage output while passing 3/3 in isolation. dmesg: 'Out of memory: Killed process (bs2)'. The stall detector fired 7x in the same run.

Shape: per_file mode runs multiple shard binaries concurrently, each running units on AVRA_TEST_JOBS (=nproc) threads, each unit shelling 'diagnose.sh --run <fixture>' whose bs2 compile peaks 1-2GB RSS. Worst-case concurrent RSS = shards x jobs x 2GB >> 16GB. Same class as the documented macOS jetsam mass-kill (jdgo/d4jv notes in ensure_bs2), now reproducing on Linux.

Fix direction: cross-process throttle on heavyweight fixture compiles (counting semaphore in build/, honoring an AVRA_FIXTURE_JOBS knob with a memory-aware default), or make the per_file orchestrator budget total concurrent bs2 compiles rather than per-binary threads. Don't paper over with reruns — the failure mode poisons assertions with truncated output.
notes: WIP stashed on claude/gallant-ritchie-ng2sz8 (stash: slot throttle for diagnose.sh + test_runner + spec) — deliberately NOT in PR #521 per owner's scope call; resume after the PR lands.
close_reason: Throttle landed (run_fg slot + --slot-exec wrap for the test runner's direct compiles, AVRA_FIXTURE_JOBS default 2, pid-reaping mkdir semaphore, hermetic 4-case spec). Suite 2988/2988 + fixed point. Reconciled with the post-stash restructures; seed-train workflow note updated.
