title: Pin-don't-vendor: seed.lock + release-artifact hosting (Rust stage0 model)
description:
Pin, don't vendor (Rust/Go stage0 model):

- Replace the checked-in bootstrap/seed/seed.ll with seed.lock: {version, sha256, url} — a few lines of text.
- Host seed artifacts (per release/cycle) on GitHub Releases; make fetches + verifies the hash into build/ (cached; offline fallback = last fetched copy).
- make update-seed gains a publish step (or a release script) producing the artifact + lock bump.
- Repo shrinks ~28MB; clones and merges get fast; seed conflicts become 2-line lock conflicts.

Depends on sdmg.2's seed-train discipline (the lock advances on the train).

Acceptance: fresh clone with no seed.ll builds end-to-end via the lock fetch; merge of two lock bumps resolves by taking the newer.
close_reason: Implemented + both acceptance criteria executed. seed.lock {version,sha256,url} replaces the vendored 27MB seed.ll (now gitignored, fetched + sha256-verified, content-cached, offline-tolerant); seed/v1 published to GitHub Releases (3.2MB gz) via the new --seed-publish / make seed-publish; window gate + --seed-merge + pre-commit lifeline are lock-aware and transition-safe; gate 1 compares pinned CONTENT so the migration commit passes. Acceptance 1: fresh clone with no seed.ll built end-to-end via anonymous lock fetch (sha verified, bs2 self-compiles, runs programs). Acceptance 2: two lock bumps merged as a 5-line text conflict resolved by taking the higher version. Hermetic spec tests/seed_lock_fetch_test.av (4 cases). Commit b3eeec9, pushed.

title: Minimal stage-1 seed kernel + bootstrap-tolerant extern guard (Zig model)
description:
Long-term: shrink the seed and make it tolerant (Zig model).

- Minimal stage-1 kernel: the seed need only compile a restricted-subset compiler (or a minimal stage2) rather than the full self-hosted tree. Restricted subset changes rarely => seed cycles become rare events.
- Seed tolerance (nearer-term, separable): the extern-redeclare guard (llvm_wrapper.c avra_llvm_add_function) should WARN, not abort, when the conflict is between a stage-binary's baked predeclare table and the source's extern decl (benign ABI drift under opaque pointers — proven 2026-06-11); abort stays for source-vs-source conflicts. Generalize seed-patch-traps thinking: a previous-generation seed should survive compiling modestly newer source.

Acceptance (tolerance part): a seed whose decl table predates a signature refactor builds the newer source with warnings; source-level duplicate extern conflicts still abort.
notes: Tolerance half DONE (31b69c7): avra_llvm_add_function warns + adopts the source signature for declaration-vs-declaration drift (RAUW, name takeover), aborts when a body exists, AVRA_STRICT_EXTERN_GUARD=1 restores abort. 5-case spec + real acceptance ride (stale baked table vs refactored avra_rc_collect decl → warning, green -O2 build). Bonus: ensure_seed now fingerprints runtime.c+llvm_wrapper.c into the seed key (stale-seed failures were misattributed to LLVM -O2 bugs). REMAINING: the minimal stage-1 kernel (Zig model) — the long-term half.
close_reason: Tolerance half shipped (31b69c7: declaration-drift warn + RAUW, strict-env escape, 5-case spec, real acceptance ride). Kernel half REJECTED by owner 2026-06-12: the compiler must keep dogfooding the newest language features; the multi-agent problem is solved by the sdmg.2 train + gates + sdmg.3 lock, not by a frozen-subset kernel.

title: diagnose.sh --seed-merge: one-command seed-merge staging automation
description:
Encode the 2026-06-11 staging dance into one command: diagnose.sh --seed-merge [--base ours|theirs]

Automates: choose base seed -> make seed-patch-traps -> build stage1 -> (on stage failure: report which class — parse/extern-guard/runtime-corruption — with next-step hints) -> stage1 compiles merged source -> link bs2 -> self-compile verify -> make update-seed -> fixed point -> summary.

Replaces hours of agent archaeology with a deterministic script + good failure taxonomy. Add a doc section in SEED_MERGES.md (sdmg.1) pointing at it.

Acceptance: on a synthetic two-branch seed divergence (test fixture repo state), --seed-merge produces a green merged seed without manual IR surgery.
close_reason: Implemented (diagnose.sh --seed-merge + --seed-merge-classify), taxonomy spec-tested (7 cases, tests/seed_merge_classify_test.av), SEED_MERGES.md leads with the one-command path. Acceptance executed: synthetic two-branch divergence (two scratch branches, disjoint fn additions, FAST seed cycles, genuine 3-way binary conflict on seed.ll) staged green by --seed-merge in 54s — base=ours, seed regenerated, fixed point holds, zero manual IR surgery. Commit 9c0ddf6, pushed.

title: bs2 build <dir> null-crashes instead of a diagnostic (directory passed as entry file)
description:
`./build/bs2 build packages/std-json` (directory as positional arg) dies with the generic runtime null error:

    error: unexpected runtime error in function `__libc_start_main`
    A null value was used where an object was expected.

Expected: either a clean diagnostic ('entry must be a .av file; to build a package run from its root with --lib') or, better, DWIM: detect a directory arg with an avra.toml and build that package.

run_build_command (cli/main.av): the path arg flows into manifest/entry resolution; some slot stays null on the directory path and gets dereferenced. Found while debugging the pre-build chain (2026-06-11) — the crash misled the investigation for a while because it shadowed the real per-package invocation (cd <dir> && bs2 build --lib), which works.

Per the ZERO RAW ERRORS policy this must surface as a CompileError with help text, not a runtime null trap.

title: bs2's shard/test link path doesn't discover LLVM_PREFIX — hard fails on Linux without env
description:
`bs2 test` / `_test_shard` link with `-L$LLVM_PREFIX/lib -lLLVM` where LLVM_PREFIX defaults to /opt/homebrew/opt/llvm (macOS). On Linux containers without an exported LLVM_PREFIX every shard fails 'unable to find library -lLLVM' (594/594 shards failed before diagnosis, 2026-06-11).

scripts/diagnose.sh already has the discovery logic (_find_llvm20_prefix: llvm-config-$MAJOR on PATH, /usr/lib/llvm-$MAJOR, ...). Port the same fallback chain into the compiled link path (build/link.av default_link_options or the env read site) so `make test` works out of the box on Linux. Keep the env var as the override.

Acceptance: on a Linux box with LLVM at /usr/lib/llvm-20 and NO LLVM_PREFIX exported, `make test` links shards successfully.

title: Atomic cleanup registration: RcCleanupEntry/DeferEntry.Release constructible only via a zero-initializing chokepoint
description:
# Goal

Make 'cleanup-registered implies definitely-initialized' true by construction at a single chokepoint.

## Today

The zm77 fix lives in ctx.bind (codegen/types.av): zero-init via avra_llvm_zero_init_local happens right before pushing RcCleanupEntry + DeferEntry.Release. Nothing stops a future emitter from building an alloca and pushing an RcCleanupEntry / DeferEntry.Release directly, recreating the bug.

## Work

- Make RcCleanupEntry construction private to one registration function that ALWAYS emits the entry-block null store. Registration and initialization become a single atomic operation; no call site can opt out.
- Same for DeferEntry.Release: route through the same chokepoint.
- Audit every existing push to ctx.rc_cleanup / ctx.defers (grep) and convert to the chokepoint.

## Acceptance

- Exactly one function in the codebase can register a slot for RC cleanup, and it emits the zero-init unconditionally.
- grep shows no direct RcCleanupEntry{...} / DeferEntry.Release(...) construction outside it.
- Spec suite + selfhost green.

UPDATE 2026-06-11 (merge 3f8798a9): the universal ptr-alloca zero-init now lives in avra_llvm_build_alloca itself, so EVERY alloca is null until first stored — the safety invariant holds regardless of registration site, and the bind-level zero-init was removed as redundant. This ticket's remaining value is encapsulation hygiene (single registration chokepoint, no stray RcCleanupEntry/DeferEntry.Release construction), not safety. Downgraded P1→P2.
notes: DONE + merged (#605 squash 078b0278). Extracted Ctx.register_rc_cleanup as the SOLE construction site for RcCleanupEntry + DeferEntry.Release; Ctx.bind delegates to it, so the cleanup list and defer stack can never drift apart and no other emitter can push a half-registered cleanup slot (the zm77 shape). Third leg of the zm77 defense-in-depth (rcsf.2 checks IR, rcsf.3 catches at runtime, rcsf.1 makes the registration hole structurally impossible by encapsulation). Pure refactor: byte-identical IR (diff-test selfhost+corpus), full suite 3610/3610, selfhost fixed point holds. Enforced by tests/rc_cleanup_chokepoint_test.av (greps assert each of RcCleanupEntry and any .Release( construction — qualified OR leading-dot, excluding match-arm consumers — appears at exactly one site in codegen/types.av). prepare-pr 3x + CodeRabbit's one finding (qualified-only grep bypassable by leading-dot shorthand) fixed + verified by CodeRabbit. Isolated from ps3t. Avra has no enum-construction visibility control, so grep-based CI enforcement is the pragmatic best available.

title: Phase arenas for the AST — pipeline data out of the RC heap (spec Axis 9)
description:
# Goal

Phase arenas for the AST (spec Axis 9): take compiler pipeline data out of the RC heap entirely.

## Why

zm77's damage was bizarre because the compiler's own long-lived data (the AST) lives in the same RC heap as transient codegen temporaries — one stray release freed a parse tree. The AST has perfect arena lifetime: allocated across parse→mono, read-only during codegen, dropped wholesale at pipeline end.

## Work

- Allocate AST nodes (Expr/Stmt/SExpr/SStmt/Pattern/MatchArm/ValueType where pipeline-owned) from a phase arena, not avra_rc_alloc; they never enter the rc_set.
- A stray release of an arena pointer becomes detectable (combined with rcsf.3's strict mode: heap-range non-RC pointer → abort).
- Drop the arena wholesale after object emission.
- Bonus: removes per-node refcount traffic from the hot compile path; measure compile-time delta.

## Acceptance

- AST allocations no longer appear in the rc_set; suite + selfhost fixed point green.
- Under AVRA_RC_STRICT=1, a synthetic stray release of an AST pointer aborts instead of freeing.
- No compile-time regression (expect improvement).

title: Drop elaboration: definite-init-driven, block-scoped RC cleanup + null-is-uninitialized spec invariant
description:
# Goal

Generate RC cleanup from definite-initialization analysis (drop elaboration), with block-scoped cleanup — the v1.0-grade fix.

## Why

Rust killed this bug class with drop elaboration + drop flags. Avra's entry-block null-init is a degenerate drop flag (null = uninitialized), which works because every RC type is pointer-repr and null is reserved. Formalize and structure it:

## Work

- Spec: add the invariant 'null is the canonical uninitialized state of every RC slot; cleanup of null is a no-op' to the memory model (Axis 9) so future codegen and the production compiler must uphold it.
- Block-scoped cleanup: a loop-body local's release belongs at the loop-body scope exit, not the function epilogue. Makes 'cleanup runs but binding didn't execute' unrepresentable by construction, and preserves defer/errdefer LIFO interleaving within scopes.
- Audit per-iteration release semantics: today a loop-local rebind across N iterations relies on reassignment-release to not leak the first N-1 values — verify, add a leak test (rc live-count before/after a loop).
- Cleanup emission driven by a definite-init dataflow pass rather than declaration order.

## Acceptance

- Spec text lands; cleanup for scoped locals emitted at scope exit; epilogue only handles fn-scope locals + params.
- Leak test proves per-iteration releases happen; suite + selfhost green.
- rcsf.2's verifier still passes (slot invariant preserved under the new scheme).

UPDATE 2026-06-11 (merge 3f8798a9): the merged tree surfaced garbage READS beyond RC cleanup (uninit slots consumed as AST node pointers — layout-sensitive 'unmatched tag' crashes). The universal alloca zero-init is the interim blanket; definite-initialization analysis should ultimately prove init-before-use and let codegen elide the blanket null stores where provably dead.

title: [lexer] nested generic close '>>' lexes as shift — List<List<string>> fails to parse
description: mut batches: List<List<string>> = [] dies with 'expected generic type argument' — the >> closing a nested generic lexes as one shift token. Rust/C++ both split >> in type position. Found planning batched test shards (worked around with a named Batch struct, which read better anyway — but the gap bites any nested generic).
close_reason: Fixed by PR #533 (merged into feat/crafting-intepreters): the lexer's >> right-shift token is split into two > at the generic-close sites (parse_generic_type_args + skip_angle_brackets), so nested generic type annotations parse — List<List<int>>, List<List<string>>, List<List<List<int>>> via >>>, Map<string,List<int>>. The real >> shift operator is unaffected (guarded by tests). Test: parse/tests/nested_generic_close_test.av.

title: [typeck] Task<T,E>: spawn returns untyped .Int; .await unchecked
description: spawn { v } types as .Int regardless of body type (spawn_check in features/spawn_expr/mod.av — the capture_stdout_parallel test comments on it). ValueType.Task(result_ty) exists; wire it through typeck so .await yields the body's type and .cancel() is checked. Spec Axis 18 lists Task<T,E> mirroring Result.

title: [parser] list comprehensions reject range iterables and tuple binders
description: Two forms whose for-statement twins already work fail to parse in comprehensions: [x for i in 0..n] (range iterable) errors with 'expected ] after list' at the .., and [y for (i, x) in xs.enumerate()] rejects the tuple binder ('expected variable name after for'). The comprehension parser should accept any for-statement header. Found while writing the test runner's collector in idiomatic style (d4jv prepare-pr); both sites fell back to for-loops.

title: Generic call on an optional-unwrapped value emits 'add ptr, ptr' (bad IR / llc reject)
description: Passing an optional's unwrapped value into a generic fn and using the result arithmetically emits invalid IR. Repro: 'fn id<T>(x: T) -> T { x }' then 'fn f(x: int?) -> int { id(x!) + 1 }' (force-unwrap) OR 'match x { let v -> id(v) + 1, none -> 0 }' (present-bind) both lower to '%add = add ptr %1, inttoptr (i64 1 to ptr)' and llc rejects with 'invalid operand type for instruction'. The monomorphizer instantiates id as id<ptr> (the unwrapped value is seen as ptr, not its inner int), so the return is ptr and '+ 1' is ptr arithmetic. Plain 'id(41) + 1' works, so the gap is specifically generic inference over an optional-derived value. Orthogonal to xm2g.8 Part B (no test there uses generic-over-unwrapped-optional); surfaced while probing present-bind type precision during prepare-pr. Fix belongs with monomorphizer type inference for optional unwrap (resolve/mono), not the optional-match surface.
close_reason: Fixed: infer_lit_ty now handles force-unwrap Call, binding the type param from id(x!). Merged in #675 (squash 14be83e1). 10 spec fixtures + mutation-verified + diff-test byte-identical.

comments.author: Claude
comments.text: REPRODUCED (2026-07-09). Trigger: a generic call whose result feeds ARITHMETIC — 'fn id<T>(v: T) -> T { v }; let x: int? = 5; let r = id(x!) + 1'. Emitted IR contains '%add = add ptr %2, inttoptr (i64 1 to ptr)' — the generic call result %2 is typed ptr (the generic T repr) instead of the concrete int, so '+ 1' lowers to POINTER arithmetic ('add ptr, …') rather than integer add. It happens to compute the right value at -O0 (the ptr numerically IS 5), so the spec passes, but the IR is ill-typed (llc rejects 'add ptr' under -O2 / opaque-pointer strictness — the ticket's 'llc reject'). NOTE the simple 'let r = id(x!)' (no arithmetic) round-trips fine; the bug needs the result in an arithmetic/int-typed context. ROOT CAUSE hypothesis: at the call site, id(x!)'s result type isn't lowered from the generic T to the inferred concrete int — mono/codegen keeps the boxed/ptr repr for the return. FIX AREA: generics/mono result-type lowering (llvm_type_for_full for the monomorphized return) or the arithmetic operator's operand coercion (unbox/inttoptr-strip when a ptr-typed generic result is a concrete scalar). Subtler than ai3u (it's in the mono↔codegen type-lowering seam, not a coerce site). Candidate next milestone.

title: Tuple literal elements not boxed for an optional position — (5,6) into (int?,int?) segfaults
description:
emit_tuple_inner (features/tuples/codegen.av) stores each element raw with its own type, never coercing to the position's expected type — the analog of the List<T?> bug (uyao). A tuple literal flowing into a tuple type with an optional position is not boxed, so a later unwrap dereferences a raw scalar as a box pointer and SIGSEGVs.

REPRO:
  fn f(p: (int?, int?)) -> int { let (a, b) = p; if let v = a { v } else { -1 } }
  f((5, 6))   // SIGSEGV — 5 stored raw, unwrapped as a box

Same root cause as the landed List fix and the deferred Map case (ks8q): a literal flowing into an optional-typed slot must box its present scalar elements. Tuples are heterogeneous, so there is no none-detection shortcut — this needs expected-type threading at the slot (let / call-arg / return).

PROPER FIX (shared with nztt/ks8q): one GENERAL recursive literal coercion that descends into List/Tuple/Map element types and boxes optionals, replacing the per-construct ad-hoc boxing (adding tuple+map copies would be cumulative duplication). This is the bidirectional-typing / expected-type-flow work that gating (xm2g.5) tightens. Found during xm2g.8 Part B prepare-pr round 4 (combinatorial matrix).
close_reason: MERGED — PR #674 (squash 7845fb1) into feat/crafting-intepreters. Tuple elements are now boxed into optional positions instead of stored raw, fixing the SIGSEGV when a scalar tuple element bound for a T? slot was later unwrapped (t.N! read the raw scalar as a box pointer). General coerce-time fix: emit_optional_coerce is tuple-aware (needs_tuple_rebox + emit_tuple_rebox in optional_repr.av re-box element-wise, recursing for nested tuples), covering let/mut/reassign/struct-field/with/list-elem/global; the two inline coerce sites that bypass it (arg loop in helpers.av, fn-body return in fn_decl) got the same primitive — so ALL positions box uniformly. All CI green (diff-test byte-identical 641313-line selfhost + corpus, window, rc-strict, seed-train-verify, publish-seed-verify-pass). 13 spec fixtures across every position (present/absent controls), mutation-verified (core boxing + arg wiring both load-bearing). No seed cycle.

comments.author: Claude
comments.text:
SCOPE (2026-07-09, in progress on claude/ai3u-tuple-optional-boxing). ROOT CAUSE confirmed: emit_tuple_inner (features/tuples/codegen.av) stores each element RAW, typed by inference (.Tuple([Int,Int])), never seeing the expected (int?,int?) — so a scalar lands in an optional slot and a later t.N! reads it as a box pointer → SIGSEGV. Reproduced via spec (compiled path; note bs2 run uses the broken eval interpreter — useless for this).

POSITIONS (all must be covered per rule 19 — 'tuple literal into an optional position' is general):
- let / mut binding: FIXED (construction-time emit_tuple_expected boxes each elem via emit_optional_coerce, dispatched in let_stmt emit_var_decl mirroring the List<T?> case). let/mut/mixed(int?,string) PASS.
- function ARG position (take((5,6)) into (int?,int?) param): STILL SIGSEGVs — arg coercion is inline needs_optional_box in codegen/helpers.av:111, does NOT call emit_optional_coerce.
- function RETURN position ((7,"hi") from (int?,string)): STILL SIGSEGVs — separate coerce site.
- const: rejected earlier (needs compile-time constant) — not this bug.

DESIGN for the complete fix (the right one): make emit_optional_coerce (codegen/optional_repr.av) TUPLE-AWARE — when coercing a .Tuple value into a .Tuple slot-type whose elements differ in optionality, re-box element-wise (load slot, recursive emit_optional_coerce to the slot elem, store into a fresh tuple buffer). That covers every site already routed through emit_optional_coerce (let, struct field, with-update, list-elem, globals). THEN route the arg site (helpers.av) + the return site through emit_optional_coerce so tuples box there too — centralizing optional coercion (rule 8). Then the let-only construction-time special-case can be reverted (subsumed) OR kept as a literal-path alloc optimization. Multi-site codegen change; byte-identical expected (no compiled type hits this, but VERIFY via diff-test — an intended IR change if the compiler does use tuple-of-optionals). TICKET STAYS OPEN — arg/return positions not yet done.

title: [null] `?`-split (F1202) not enforced inside `match` arm bodies
description: The Phase-2 `?`-split makes `?`-on-optional an error (F1202; `?` is Result-only). That gate is NOT applied inside `match` arm bodies: `match n { _ -> someOptional? }` and `let r = match n { 0 -> x?, _ -> x? }` (x: int?) compile with NO F1202, whereas the same `let v = x?` correctly raises F1202. So `?`-on-optional silently slips through any match arm. Root cause is in match-expr arm-body type-checking (check_match_arms / enter_arm_with_guard) — the arm body is checked in a context that doesn't surface the TryOnOptional diagnostic. Surfaced by a mutation check during prepare-pr (a narrowing test that used a match arm passed even with narrowing disabled, because the arm `?` is ungated either way). Pre-existing; orthogonal to flow narrowing.
acceptance_criteria: `?`-on-optional inside a match arm raises F1202 exactly as it does in a let/return; a spec test asserts F1202 for `match n { _ -> x? }` with x: int?. Green.

title: Map<K, V?> values not boxed into optional repr
description:
A map literal whose value type is a tagged optional (Map<string, int?>) does not box its present scalar values into the optional repr — the parallel of the list-of-tagged-optional boxing bug fixed for List in xm2g.8 Part B. Repro:

    let m: Map<string, int?> = {"a": 1, "b": none}
    let x = m["a"]
    if let v = x { v } else { -1 }   // mis-typed / crashes on unwrap

Fix mirrors the list fix: box present tagged-scalar values into V? at map-literal construction (and at annotated-binding / call-arg slots). Discovered during xm2g.8 Part B prepare-pr.

comments.author: Claude
comments.text: SCOPING (2026-07-09): the map-LITERAL case already round-trips — 'let m: Map<string, int?> = {"a": 5}; m.get("a")!' returns 5 (PASS), so map-literal-into-optional-value boxing is handled (likely via the same expected-type dispatch as List<T?>). The bug must need a DIFFERENT trigger: insertion via .set(key, val) with a bare value, a map comprehension, or a non-literal value flowing into a Map<K,V?> position (the coerce sites that bypass emit_optional_coerce — cf. ai3u's arg/return finding). NOTE: '[]' indexing on Map<K,V?> is F1206-rejected (use .get). Next: reproduce via .set / non-literal insertion to find the unboxed path, then apply the same optional-coerce boxing (ai3u/#674 pattern). Not a clean single-line repro like ai3u.

comments.author: Claude
comments.text: SCOPING CONT'D (2026-07-09): every Map<K,V?> value-boxing path I can construct now ROUND-TRIPS correctly — map literal, .set(bare val), non-literal value, bool? (false distinct from absent), float? (0.0 present), present/absent via .get. So the core 'value not boxed into optional repr' symptom appears RESOLVED (likely by the 63wu wild-store / optional-coerce work). Cannot definitively close (rule 19): the ticket has NO original repro, and a residual unboxed path may exist in a form I haven't hit (map comprehension, Map<K, Map<..>?>, or a specific iteration/entries API). ACTION for a future tick: either recover the original repro, or treat like pyly/0jj8 (verify comprehensively across all map value-insertion APIs, then close with evidence). NOT a clean bug-fix milestone right now — pivoting to hd52.

title: List<T> → List<T?> coercion for non-literal args & collection variance
description:
Passing a non-literal List<T> value into a List<T?> slot does not box its elements. A list LITERAL is now boxed at construction in every context (none-bearing literal, annotated let binding, and call argument — see emit_list_lit / emit_list_lit_expected / fill_arg_array_boxing). But a VARIABLE list still flows raw:

    let raw = [1, 2, 3]   // List<int>
    sp(raw)               // sp(xs: List<int?>) — SEGV on unwrap inside sp

raw holds unboxed ints; the call site only special-cases ListLit args, so no rebox happens. Two valid resolutions (design decision): (a) typeck REJECTS List<int> where List<int?> is expected (lists are invariant — the strict choice), or (b) emit a runtime element-rebox at the coercion boundary (matches the permissive optional coercion used elsewhere). Same applies to let/return slots fed by a variable. Discovered during xm2g.8 Part B prepare-pr; the literal paths (the common case + the original crash) are fixed.
notes: Also covers NESTED list literals: `f([[2, 3]])` into a `List<List<int?>>` param crashes — the outer list's element type (`List<int?>`) isn't threaded into the inner list literal, so the inner `[2,3]` stays raw `List<int>` and unwrap segfaults. The single-level boxing (none-literals, annotated bindings, direct `List<T?>` args) is fixed; the general fix is recursive expected-type threading through nested collection literals (and variable/return positions) — i.e. a deep `List<T>`→`List<T?>` coercion. Repro: `fn f(xss: List<List<int?> >) -> int { mut t=0; for xs in xss { for x in xs { if let v = x { t = t+v } } }; t }` then `f([[2,3]])` (note: `>>` needs a space — separate pre-existing lexer gap).

title: [null] flow narrowing not applied to return-position `?` (re-checked un-narrowed)
description: In a guarded scope, `if x != none { let v = x?; return v }` narrows correctly (no F1202), but `if x != none { return x? }` re-flags F1202. The return-type-check pass (tc_check_explicit_returns / implicit-return) re-walks return values to verify they match the declared return type, and that re-walk does not carry the flow-narrowed type environment — so a narrowed `x` reverts to `T?` and `x?` trips the `?`-on-optional gate. Pre-existing (predates the perf pass); surfaced by a combinatorial narrowing test. Fix: thread the narrowed env into return-value re-checking, or check return values once in the narrowed main pass. Likely subsumed by the bind-fresh rework (xm2g.8). Workaround: bind to a `let` first.
acceptance_criteria: `if x != none { return x? }` no longer F1202; return-value type-checking sees the same flow-narrowed env as the main check; covered by a test. Green.

title: [tooling] ICE breadcrumb has no output test — add a deterministic ICE trigger
description: The ICE localization cursor (avra_ice_phase/push_fn/pop_fn/at + the F9999 crash-handler in runtime.c) is exercised implicitly by every compile in the suite (a stack imbalance or state corruption would fail selfhost), but the crash-HANDLER output itself is untested — testing it needs the compiler to actually segfault, which no current input does. Add a deterministic trigger (e.g. a test-only intrinsic that null-derefs under a guard env var) and a spec test asserting the F9999 block contains phase + fn-trail + span. Low risk (output formatting of a bug-only path), filed during prepare-pr on the nullability/ICE PR.
acceptance_criteria: a deterministic ICE trigger exists (test-gated, not in normal builds); a spec test asserts the crash handler prints F9999 with phase, function trail, and file:line:col. Green.

title: [null] Fence raw `ptr`/FFI null at the unsafe boundary — keep --debug-null there
description: `none` for pointer-backed optionals IS the null pointer (0), so a raw `ptr` of 0 and a `Str?`/struct?/enum? `none` share bits and conflate at the FFI / LLVM-C-API boundary. Quarantine raw nullable pointers behind an explicit unsafe/bare-level boundary (spec Axis 2 levels) so the app/systems subset stays statically null-clean. Dynamic null checking (--debug-null / avra_null_arg_*) then becomes the PRINCIPLED tool AT that boundary (like Rust's `unsafe`), not a workaround sprinkled through safe code. Lower priority than the narrowing-soundness fix (xm2g.8).
acceptance_criteria: raw nullable `ptr` confined to an explicit unsafe/FFI surface; safe-level code cannot silently mix `ptr`==0 with a typed `none`; --debug-null documented as the FFI-boundary tool. Green.

title: comptime decoder value_to_match_arm silently drops a guard on decode failure
description: In features/eval/mod.av value_to_match_arm, the 'guard' arm does `match value_to_expr_node(g_val) { .Ok(g) -> guard_opt = sexpr_dummy(g); .Err(_) -> {} }`. A decode FAILURE silently becomes 'no guard', turning a guarded match arm into an unguarded one (a semantic change) instead of propagating the error. Pattern/body arms are safe (a null pattern/body is caught by the missing-pattern/body checks that return .Err), but guard is legitimately optional so its decode error is swallowed. Pre-existing: the base (MatchArm? return) had identical behavior; the Phase-2 Result migration preserved it faithfully (not introduced by that PR). FIX: distinguish 'guard absent' (Expr.None sentinel, already handled) from 'guard present but undecodable' — the latter should return .Err so the expander reports it rather than silently dropping the guard. Found during prepare-pr Phase 1 of the nullability PR.

title: [null] Phase 6: diagnostics contract — null-safety as the showcase
description: Define + centralize the diagnostics contract in diagnostics/: every Diagnostic has stable F-code, precise span (start+end), message, help remedy, optional structured suggested_edit{span,replacement}. Add structured output mode (avra check --diagnostics=json). avra explain F1xxx worked example + canonical fix per null F-code. Root-cause-only reporting (suppress cascades) for null errors. Make every null F-code meet the contract; these are the reference other features copy. ZERO RAW ERRORS (CompileError::render only). Doc §4 Phase 6.
acceptance_criteria: diagnostics contract implemented + centralized; --diagnostics=json emits structured records (code, span start+end, message, help, optional suggested_edit); avra explain covers every null F-code; each null F-code test asserts remedy text present; cascades suppressed for null errors. build/test/selfhost green.

title: [null] Phase 5: finalize ? (Result-only), remove 'null' alias, update spec Axis 10
description: Remove the 'null' alias (none only; migrate remaining occurrences). Finalize ? as Result-only per spec 10.5/12.x minus the Option-propagation clause. Update spec docs/2026_04_18_FULL_SPEC.md Axis 10 to reflect: none keyword, ?-split (no ?-means-absent), dual representation note, flow-narrowing-as-sugar. Doc §4 Phase 5.
acceptance_criteria: 'null' alias removed (grep clean); ? finalized Result-only; spec Axis 10 updated to match. build/test/selfhost green.

title: [null] Phase 3: flow narrowing (sugar, never load-bearing)
description: Typeck narrows T? -> T after 'if x != none', 'if x == none { return/break/continue }', and match arms binding the present case. Additive ONLY: narrowing must never suppress an error gating would raise; it only avoids requiring an explicit unwrap where presence is proven. Doc §4 Phase 3. | SOUNDNESS AUDIT (2026-06-08): the shipped retype-the-variable model (spec 10.4 option a, TypeScript/Kotlin) is UNSOUND under reassignment — `mut x: int?; if x != none { x = g(); x? }` is wrongly accepted (proven repro, no F1202). This caps safety below Rust/Zig and violates this ticket's own 'additive only — never suppress an error gating would raise' invariant. Spec 10.4 is now decided as bind-fresh (Rust/Zig). The sound model is split into xm2g.8, which BLOCKS gating (xm2g.5). This ticket stays OPEN until narrowing is sound (bind-fresh / effectively-final).
acceptance_criteria: narrowing tests pass; the SAME access outside the guard is still an error (proves narrowing is non-load-bearing). build/test/selfhost green. | ADDED (soundness): reassigning the narrowed variable to a maybe-absent value inside the guard MUST drop the narrowing (a subsequent unguarded use is an error) — narrowing never survives a reassignment.

title: [null] Phase 4: flip to gating — non-null by default (the grind)
description: Typeck enforces non-null-by-default (doc §3): none/T? cannot go where non-optional T is required (field access/method/arithmetic/non-optional arg/return) without unwrap/narrowing -> F1200; 'let x: int = none' -> F1201; ?-return-type coupling -> F1204. T? auto-widens from T. Emit all F-codes with remedies. Iterate: fix every surfaced violation across compiler+stdlib until selfhost byte-identical green WITH enforcement on. Do NOT weaken a rule to pass (CLAUDE.md 1-4,16). Doc §4 Phase 4. | SOUNDNESS: gating MUST derive non-nullness from bind-fresh narrowing (xm2g.8) and may NEVER trust a flow-narrowed mutable variable across a reassignment or aliased mutation. Without this it inherits the xm2g.4 hole and ships a 'compiles-but-segfaults' bug. Depends on xm2g.8.
acceptance_criteria: non-null-by-default fully enforced; let x:int=none is F1201; un-handled T? use is F1200; both with remedies; every existing violation fixed; selfhost byte-identical green with enforcement ON. No rule weakened.

comments.author: Claude
comments.text: Canonical gating example to enforce: BARE member access on an optional (no `?.`) is currently accepted and crashes on none. Repro: `type P = { n: int }` then `let p: P? = none` / `p.n` -> runtime 'null pointer dereference (accessed address 0x0)'. On a PRESENT optional `p.n` silently auto-unwraps (returns the field), so it compiles and 'works' until the value is none — exactly the hole T? exists to close. When gating lands, bare `.field`/`.method` on a `T?` must be a typeck error pointing to `?.` or an unwrap (`p!.n`, `if let`). Same shape as the F1204/F1205 operator rejects already landed, but pervasive (member access is everywhere), so it belongs in the gating grind, not a quick reject. Found during xm2g.8 prepare-pr round-after-round mining.

title: [null] Phase 2: real value-type Option codegen + ?./?? typing + ?-split (errors-only)
description: Make int?/bool?/float? distinguish none from Some(0)/false/0.0 (the core bug fix). Type ?. and ?? against the representation (?. -> U?; ?? -> non-optional T). Split ?: ? on a T? becomes a compile error (F1202) with remedy; ? on Result unchanged. Audit compiler+stdlib for ?-on-optional and migrate to ??/?./match BEFORE enabling the error. Doc §4 Phase 2.
acceptance_criteria: value-type optionals distinguish none from zero/false (tests); ?. and ?? typed correctly; ? on a T? is F1202 (test asserts code); no ?-on-optional remains in compiler/stdlib. build/test/selfhost green; seed if needed.
close_reason: Phase 2 complete: value-type optionals distinguish none from zero/false; ?.->U? and ?? typed correctly; ?-split enforced — ? on a T? is F1202 (DiagCode.TryOnOptional) with remedy, ? on Result unchanged (assertion test 2/2); NO ?-on-optional remains in compiler/stdlib/tests (parser fully migrated to Result + comptime/eval + 3 test files migrated). build/test green 2714/2714 (0 failed); selfhost bs2==bs3 byte-identical (521690-line IR) WITH F1202 gating active; seed.ll = verified fixed-point IR. Landed on slice/xm2g.3 @ 02561e6f (incl. prepare-pr cleanup).

title: y9y4.9 follow-up: dogfood remaining homogeneous ValueType walkers (rewrite_vtype, stamp_ids_vtype, count/collect id-zero)
description:
More hand-rolled homogeneous ValueType walkers (not blocked by y9y4.18) that should ride the derived methods, found during PR #10's deeper review:

  - resolve.rewrite_vtype (names.av) — ValueType->ValueType; structural arms (List/Fn/FnTyped/Closure/Union/Task/Tuple) can collapse to '_ -> vt.map(...)'. CARE: nominal arms are guarded ('if name != ""'); an empty-name Enum/Newtype currently hits '_ -> vt' (no recurse) but would recurse under '_ -> .map'. Verify empty-name nominal can't reach here, or handle explicitly, before collapsing.
  - core.stamp_ids_vtype (ast.av) — same hybrid shape (nominal arms stamp ids + recurse; structural arms recurse). Same guard caveat.
  - core.count_id_zero_in_vtype / collect_id_zero_names_vtype (ast.av) — FOLDs; candidates for the derived .fold once .fold's visit order is confirmed (self+children, no double-count).

Each needs the same per-variant equivalence verification PR #10 did for tc_subst_vtype (a map(identity)/fold property check). Parent y9y4.9 stays open.

title: type alias in a type-pattern binding ICEs (match v { MyStr(s) -> s.length } where type MyStr = string)
codegen ICE: generic fn returning typeparam inside Tuple/Union (fn f<T>(x:T)->(T,int)) — undefined variable T
close_reason: Fixed: tc_subst_vtype now recurses into Tuple/Newtype via the derived ValueType.map (was falling through to '_ -> ty'). Generic fns returning a type-param inside a Tuple or Union now substitute it correctly — pair<T>(x)->(T,int) and first_or<T>(x)->T|int both work; full suite 2680/2680 + byte-identical selfhost. Covered by generic_tuple_union_return_test.

title: [infra/test] test_runner LLVM_PREFIX/LLC fallback — fixture runs assume macOS Homebrew paths
description: cached_fixture_compile_and_run (test_runner/mod.av:469) defaults LLVM_PREFIX to /opt/homebrew/opt/llvm with no llvm-config fallback (diagnose.sh has the fallback; test_runner duplicates the logic without it). On Linux this breaks direct fixture links (-L<missing>/lib -lLLVM). Also: container ships only versioned libLLVM.so.N (no bare libLLVM.so symlink), and diagnose.sh picks $LLVM_PREFIX/bin/llc (llc-18) which cannot parse bs2's LLVM-19+ 'getelementptr inbounds nuw' output — needs llc-20. Fix: mirror diagnose.sh's llvm-config fallback in test_runner, prefer a >=19 llc, and document/auto-create the libLLVM.so symlink (or set LLC/LLVM_PREFIX in a SessionStart hook). Workaround this session: export LLVM_PREFIX=$(llvm-config --prefix) LLC=/usr/lib/llvm-20/bin/llc and ln -s libLLVM.so.1 libLLVM.so.
close_reason: Not a bug — misdiagnosed. The toolchain gaps (LLVM_PREFIX, llc version, libLLVM.so) are resolved by running scripts/bootstrap.sh, which pins LLVM 20 and prints/persists the required env (export LLVM_PREFIX=/usr/lib/llvm-20; export LLC=/usr/lib/llvm-20/bin/llc). The llvm-20 prefix already ships a bare libLLVM.so, and test_runner reads LLVM_PREFIX from env (set by bootstrap.sh), so its macOS-path default never bites in a bootstrapped env. The real gap this session was operator error: I did not run scripts/bootstrap.sh before building/testing.

title: Inline closure stored in fn-typed struct field returns null when called
description: type C = { run: fn(int)->int }; C { run: (x:int) -> {...} }.run(41) returns null. Named-fn refs (C{run: some_fn}) work (uap_fn_field_test), but inline closure literals stored in a fn-typed field don't execute — likely closure {fn_ptr,env} vs bare fn-pointer representation mismatch in the UAP indirect-call path. Discovered during vez6.11 design exploration.

title: [test-runner] bundled-mode flakies (i7gw companion) — characterize and fix so pre-commit can drop --per_file
description:
## Problem

bs2 test bundled mode runs the suite ~3x faster than --per_file (7s vs 22s warm). Pre-commit uses --per_file because bundled has known flakies, per main.av:2828-2832: '2257/2257 passes; bundled mode has known flakies (see bd forge-crafting-intepreters-i7gw)'.

Empirically I ran bundled this session and got 2606/2606 passing — but a single sample doesn't characterize flakes. Need to characterize, then fix.

## Symptoms / investigation needed

1. Run bundled mode 20+ times. Record which tests fail intermittently.
2. For each flaky test, identify the bug class: shared global state? Test ordering dependency? Threading race? Memory pressure?
3. Fix.

## Why this matters

Pre-commit's test step is 22s on --per_file. Dropping to 7s bundled saves ~15s per commit. Compounds across the team / CI / claude-code iterations.

## Acceptance

- bundled mode passes 100x consecutive runs.
- Pre-commit hook switches to bundled (remove --per_file flag).
- Pre-commit warm test step drops from ~22s to ~7s.

## Companion

forge-crafting-intepreters-i7gw is about parallelizing the bundled compile. This is about characterizing existing flakies. Two distinct slices of the same epic.
notes:
INVESTIGATION RESULT (2026-06-01 session): Bundled-mode cold and warm performance both make the "pre-commit switch" goal infeasible at i7gw's current state.

Measured (post-cbg3/zp5b/6w6v on commit 15e6b4a3):
- Cold (`make clean` + first bundled run): >25 min, single bs2 PID at 79% CPU, didn't complete in observed window (process was running, log only contained "[test-cache] miss aefe73700622").
- Warm (subsequent run, repeatedly attempted): single bs2 process at 79% CPU, did NOT complete in 600s timeout. Only emitted "[test-cache] miss" line and went silent.
- Per-file (--per_file, baseline): cold 541s parallel, warm 23.5s parallel.

Comparison: bundled is single-process serial compile of one ~2631-test program. Cold is 3-4× slower than per-file. Warm is >25× slower than per-file. Closing flake characterization without data because bundled never completed an iteration to characterize.

CONCLUSION: 20l2 is BLOCKED on i7gw (parallelize bundled compile). The "switch pre-commit to bundled" speed claim assumed an i7gw-parallelized bundled path. The current serial bundled mode is so much slower than parallel per-file that switching would be a regression, not a perf win.

Suggested action: defer 20l2 until i7gw lands. Re-characterize bundled flakes AFTER i7gw — at that point bundled wall time should be competitive with per-file, and the original 22s→7s claim can be re-validated. Leaving open with this characterization.

title: [test-perf] migrate expand_introduces_validation_test off hand-rolled bs2 compile shell-out
description:
## Problem

expand_introduces_validation_test.av runs ~734ms warm — the slowest single shard in the test suite. It shells out to bs2 compile + cc link + run a fixture that exercises ResolvedDecls.introduces validation. The warning emitted at compile time IS recorded in the diagnostic bag (see expand_macro.av:686-694), so check_source can observe it — BUT the test source imports @std.avrac.features.comptime / @std.avrac.core / @std.avrac.diagnostics AST types that check_source can't resolve under its no-file-modules constraint.

## Fix options

1. Route through cached_fixture_check_no_metadata or cached_fixture_run. Cold = same as today (~14s + link + run), warm = ~10ms from cache. Net: 734ms wall drops to ~10ms across the suite. Caveat: still relies on stale-cache-poisoning protection (zp5b).
2. Extend check_source/typecheck_source with optional file-based-module-loading. Big-ticket fix that unblocks several other migrations.

(1) ships now; (2) is a broader project.

## Acceptance

- Test wall drops to <50ms warm.
- Both invariants still observable: phantom-name warning surfaces AND _real_emitted() executes (runtime check).
notes:
Investigated but blocked.

The test asserts on BOTH the bs2 compile-time warning AND the runtime println output. The cached helpers (cached_fixture_run / cached_fixture_run_no_metadata) route through diagnose.sh's --run mode, which captures bs2 compile stderr only on FAILURE — on success it goes to BUILD_DIR/last_run.log and is discarded before the binary runs. Verified empirically: a cached_fixture_run_no_metadata invocation against the existing fixture returned only the runtime 'println(7)' output. The phantom-name warning was nowhere in the captured string.

The original hand-rolled run_capture (manual bs2 compile + llc + cc + run, capturing stderr at every stage) is correct for this test's needs. Migrating it requires either:

(a) Enhance diagnose.sh --run to preserve bs2 compile stderr on success — this is the right systemic fix and would benefit other tests with compile-time-warning assertions. But diagnose.sh is in the test marker hash, so any change to it invalidates every shard binary cache entry → full ~400s cold suite run on that commit.

(b) Add cached_fixture_compile_and_run_with_stderr as a new test_runner helper that does the manual dance, with content-keyed caching.

Either way, the 6w6v migration is a downstream consequence of (a) or (b) landing first. Closing with this note and the hand-rolled test left in place — it's accurate, just slow (~734ms warm, ~14s cold per fp invalidation).
close_reason: Closed by 15e6b4a3 → cached_fixture_compile_and_run helper lands the option-(b) approach. Test wall: 734ms → 16ms warm. Concatenated compile+run output preserves both phantom-name warning + runtime println(7) assertions.

title: [pre-commit] cache marker misses scripts/diagnose.sh + seed/seed.ll + Makefile inputs
description:
## Problem

Commit 82e286e9 added a test-suite cache marker keyed on bs2 + every .av under packages/tests + runtime.c + llvm_wrapper.c. Three inputs are NOT in the hash, and changing them could cause the cache to serve stale-success:

- scripts/diagnose.sh — used by fixtures via diagnose.sh --run / --build. A change can affect fixture output without invalidating the marker.
- seed/seed.ll — if user stages a seed change without rebuilding bs2, tests get skipped despite a relevant input change.
- bootstrap/Makefile — currently tests invoke bs2 directly so this is fine TODAY, but adding a build step to the test target would break.

## Fix

Add scripts/diagnose.sh and seed/seed.ll to the TEST_INPUT_HASH computation in bootstrap/scripts/pre-commit. Bootstrap Makefile too if we want full coverage of test-invocation paths.

## Acceptance

- Hash includes the three inputs.
- Changing any of them invalidates the marker on next commit.
- ~50ms hash cost stays the same (these are small files).
notes: Landed in bea71a60. Hash now includes scripts/diagnose.sh, seed/seed.ll, bootstrap/Makefile. Cost: 100ms → 200ms (seed.ll dominates). Pre-commit cached-path total still under a second. Pre-commit on this change: 22s test + push. No perf regression.

title: [test-perf, codegen] Refactor AVRA_T6_PROBE env-gated eprintln to a callable residuals fn
description:
## Problem

t6c_stamp_test.av runs `bs2 compile` with AVRA_T6_PROBE=1 / AVRA_T6_PROBE_DETAIL=1 and greps stderr for a 'residual id=0 name[i]:' line. 14.1s per spec — and the only reason it's a subprocess test is that the probe is process-global eprintln state.

## Root cause

The probe-detail output is computed inside the typeck (or codegen?) and emitted to stderr via env-gated eprintln. The actual residual-list computation is a pure function on (stmts, type_reg) — but it isn't exposed; it lives inline next to the printer.

## Fix

Extract the probe computation as a pure callable:

    fn tc_id0_residuals(stmts: List<SStmt>, type_reg: TypeRegistry) -> List<string>

The env-gated eprintln becomes a 3-line wrapper that calls this fn and prints each name. The spec test calls the pure fn directly via in-process AST construction (parse a fixture source → run resolve → call the residual fn). No env vars, no subprocess, no stderr grep.

## Acceptance

- New `tc_id0_residuals` (or sibling name) is a callable, tested in-process.
- AVRA_T6_PROBE printers continue to work — they go through the new fn.
- t6c_stamp_test runs in <100ms instead of 14.1s.
- The fixture source used by the test stays identical so the regression coverage is the same.

## Files

title: [codegen] cycle analysis misses Tuple/Union element types — silent rc leak
description:
## Symptom

`type Node = { pairs: List<(Node, int)> }` cycles through Tuple but `analyze_cycles` returns Node as non-cyclic. The emitted `__release_Node` omits `avra_rc_suspect`, leaving the cycle live in memory.

## Root cause

`packages/std-avrac/src/codegen/cycles.av:64` (`type_reaches_target`) handles Struct, Enum, List, Newtype, then falls to `_ -> false`. The wildcard swallows .Tuple, .Union, and other container shapes that contain reachable element types.

## Repro

```
type Node = { pairs: List<(Node, int)> }
fn main() -> int { 0 }
```
`bs2 build /tmp/cycle.av --emit-ll` → resulting `__release_Node` has no `avra_rc_suspect` call. Compare to the control `type Inner = { kids: List<Inner> }` — which DOES get the call.

## Why this stayed open in this session

Spent ~45 minutes trying to land the fix; the seed-baked IR for `type_reaches_target` (266 lines) does NOT change when the source's match arms change, AND a brand-new top-level fn added to cycles.av (`PROBE_MARKER`) is silently DROPPED from the seed-compiled main.av.ll. Reproduced after `rm -rf build/cache packages/cli/src/main.av.ll`, sidecar nuke, and `make build`. Looks like a deeper seed compilation infrastructure issue specific to cycles.av (or to per-function caching) — separate from the actual fix.

## Fix

Add explicit `.Tuple(elements) -> ...` and `.Union(types) -> ...` arms that recurse via a shared `elements_reach_target` helper. Either solve the seed-compilation issue first or land it inline.

## Test

`packages/std-avrac/src/codegen/tests/cycle_through_tuple_test.av` (sketch written this session, deleted on revert): compile a Node-through-Tuple struct, grep `__release_Node` body for `avra_rc_suspect`.

title: [seed/comptime] Hot-reload @comptime fns — bs2 reads macro source directly, no seed cycle
description:
Structural fix for the @comptime dev cycle. Today every edit to a @comptime macro definition (derive_walker, derive_marshal, quote_*) OR the macro evaluator (comptime/eval.av) requires a full seed cycle (~2-3 min via 'make update-seed') because the seed COMPILES the user source — and the seed's macro IR is what runs at compile time. Until the seed is updated, bs2 keeps emitting the old macro expansion even though the source on disk is new.

## Proposed shape

Add a build mode where bs2 reads @comptime fn source DIRECTLY from packages/std-avrac/src/ and interprets it (via the existing @comptime evaluator infrastructure), rather than executing the IR baked into the seed. Enabled via env (e.g. AVRA_LIVE_COMPTIME=1) or a build mode (e.g. 'make build-live'). Editing derive_walker source and running bs2 picks up the new macro output without ANY seed update.

## Acceptance

- Editing a @comptime fn body and rerunning 'make build-live' (or equivalent) reflects the new macro output in under 30s — the ticket's original target.
- The live mode produces byte-identical IR to the seeded mode, modulo macro output (i.e. the only difference is that the macro ran on the live source).
- 'make build' (default) stays seeded — the live mode is for development, the seeded mode is for reproducibility + bootstrap chain integrity.
- Live mode skipped by pre-commit + selfhost so the bootstrap chain still requires the seed cycle for committed code.

## Notes

The right long-term shape. Bigger lift than the make-target consolidation (so07.7.13). Doesn't block the consolidation — they compose: with live mode active, 'update-seed' becomes a rare bootstrap-discipline command rather than an inner-loop pain point.

Filed during so07.7.13 review — the macro-cycle target proposal would have been a 7th seed-related tool; this is the structural alternative that retires the toolchain accretion entirely.
notes:
INVESTIGATION FINDING: the @comptime interpreter is already live — derive_walker is interpreted from source at every compile, not from baked IR.

The actual blocker for 'edit macro, see new behavior in <30s' is the **compile cache key**. Reproduced experimentally:
- Added eprintln to derive_walker source.
- Direct: rm -rf packages/cli/src/build packages/cli/src/main.av.ll && build/seed compile main.av → 4 LIVE-PROBE hits.
- Cached: build/seed compile main.av (cache warm) → 0 hits. Cache returns stale main.av.ll without re-running the @comptime expansion.

The cache key sees main.av's content + bs2 hash + profile, but the dep graph propagation that would invalidate main.av's slot when @std/avrac/features/walker/derive.av changes is exactly what pdme.1 tracks.

Closing as subsumed by pdme.1 (Transitive package fingerprint propagation in cache key) under the uzs9 umbrella. When pdme.1 lands, edits to any @comptime fn under @std/* will invalidate the dependent main.av/test .ll cache slots, and the existing live-interpreter path will surface the new macro output on the next build — exactly what so07.7.21 was asking for, but as a side-effect of correctness work rather than a separate live-mode toggle.

No code change for so07.7.21 itself. CLAUDE.md's macro-cycle commentary should drop the '4-step dance' framing once pdme.1 lands; for now the cycle is still needed because the cache hides the change.

title: [mono] Pull bidirectional generic-call inference from typeck instead of re-deriving
description:
## Problem

so07.7.15 added bidirectional generic-call inference at the typeck layer — `tc_subst_generic_ret_with_expected` consults the caller's expected return type when arg types alone don't pin a type parameter. That fixed the typeck-side F1000.

But the monomorphizer runs as a separate pass after typeck. It collects generic instantiations from call sites and instantiates each. When it encounters `unwrap_node_list(xs)` in a fn returning `List<Stmt>`, it re-runs its own type-arg inference (per features/generics/mono.av) which only looks at arg types. With `xs: List<SStmt>` providing W=SStmt but no arg carrying T, mono fires F1002 'cannot infer type parameter T'.

Concrete repro from so07.7.2 attempt:

```
fn unwrap_node_list<W, T>(xs: List<W>) -> List<T> {
    mut out: List<T> = []
    for x in xs { out.push(x.node) }
    out
}

export fn unwrap_sstmt_list(xs: List<SStmt>) -> List<Stmt> {
    unwrap_node_list(xs)   // F1002 at mono time: cannot infer T
}
```

## Fix

Mono should pull type-arg bindings from the typeck-resolved call's expected return type, not re-derive from scratch. Two paths:

**A. Typeck stamps the instantiation.** At the call site, after `tc_subst_generic_ret_with_expected`, also resolve all type-args and stamp them onto the Expr.Call node (a new field on Call, or a side-channel registry). Mono reads the stamped bindings directly.

**B. Mono extends its own inference.** Pass the call-site expected return type into mono's instantiation logic (currently in features/generics/mono.av's `record_call_inst` / `unify_param`). Mirror what so07.7.15 did at the typeck layer.

(A) is the architectural fit — typeck already has the resolved info; mono just needs to consume it.

## Acceptance

- The collapsed `unwrap_sstmt_list(xs) { unwrap_node_list(xs) }` form (so07.7.2) compiles cleanly through typeck AND mono.
- F1002 doesn't fire for any call where typeck's bidirectional inference succeeded.
- 2553+ specs still pass.

## Notes

Filed as a follow-up to so07.7.15. so07.7.2 stays open, now blocked on this ticket.
notes: Landed in 87e2e553. Both mono passes (collect + rewrite) now expected-aware via infer_from_params_with_expected. Unblocked W2 (so07.7.2).

title: [typeck] Generic call inference: consult expected return type, not just arg types
description:
## Problem

Generic call inference (typeck/mod.av's `tc_infer_type_args` / `tc_subst_generic_ret`) only pulls type-args from positional argument types. It doesn't consult the caller's *expected return type*.

Concrete: a generic `fn f<T>(xs: List<int>) -> List<T> { ... }` called from a context expecting `List<Stmt>` should pin `T = Stmt`. Today: T stays Unknown.

so07.7.2 (collapse unwrap_sstmt_list + unwrap_sexpr_list) hit this. Tried:

```
export fn unwrap_sstmt_list(xs: List<SStmt>) -> List<Stmt> {
    unwrap_node_list(xs)
}

fn unwrap_node_list<W, T>(xs: List<W>) -> List<T> { ... }
```

The inner call pins W = SStmt from the arg, but T stays Unknown because no argument carries T. Result: F1000 'function returns List, body produces List'.

## Fix

Extend `tc_subst_generic_ret` to accept an `expected: ValueType?` parameter. When the call site has a known expected type (let-binding RHS with annotation, fn-body return position, fn-call-arg against a typed param, etc.), thread it down. Use it as an additional constraint on the type-args: unify `expected` against `rec.ret_ty` and harvest bindings.

Same shape as so07.4 (T4) did for list literals: thread the expected type, use it to disambiguate.

## Surface affected

- typeck/mod.av: `tc_subst_generic_ret`, `tc_check_fn_call_with`, `tc_infer_type_args`
- Callers of those that have an expected_ty (call sites in check_binding, check_match_expr_arms via check_expr_expected, etc.)

## Acceptance

- `let xs: List<Stmt> = unwrap_node_list(sstmts)` — T pinned to Stmt from let annotation.
- so07.7.2 can collapse the two unwrap_X_list helpers to a single generic call.
- 2553+ specs still pass; bs2/bs3 fixed point holds.

## Notes

Filed as a T6 sub-issue because the broader "nominal identity should be context-aware" theme T6 carries.
notes: Landed in 95d42b42. typeck side complete. mono-side parallel fix needed for so07.7.2 collapse — filed as so07.7.16.

title: [test_runner] 'bs2 test <file>' should scope to <file>; output truncation hides results
description:
## Problem

Two related issues in the spec test CLI:

**1. `./build/bs2 test <file.av>` runs the WHOLE test suite, not just `<file>`.** The filename arg is treated as a discovery starting point (or ignored entirely — TBD), not a scope filter. Running a single test file means waiting for ~2500 specs to run, or using `FILTER=<substr>` to narrow.

**2. Test output is truncated.** When the suite passes, the final `tests passed in Xs` line shows but the per-spec PASS/FAIL is cut after ~10-15 lines on the harness side. This hides per-test results I need to debug. Particularly bad for new specs that are buried in the output.

## Fix

**Issue 1**: respect `<file>` arg as a scope filter. `bs2 test <file>` runs ONLY the specs in that file. Adding a separate `bs2 test --all` for the full-suite invocation.

**Issue 2**: investigate where the truncation happens. If it's harness-level (claude-code tool wrappers), file a different ticket; if it's bs2's own output management (a "too much output, cutting" heuristic), make the truncation user-controllable.

## Acceptance

- `bs2 test <file>` runs ONLY that file's specs (verify by spec count).
- A spec that PASSES in a single-file run produces PASS output visible to the user.
- Doc the CLI shape in the test_runner README / WHY.md.

## Notes

Productivity blocker — debugging individual specs requires hacks. Both issues hit during the y9y4.11 session.
notes: Landed in eeeacc1d. `bs2 test <path>` now scopes to that file via 3-strategy match (exact / suffix / basename). Output-truncation issue is harness-level (separate concern); typed up but not actionable from bs2.

title: [test_runner] Fixture cache invalidation: hash macro source files into toolchain_fp
description:
## Problem

`test_runner/mod.av::read_or_compute_toolchain_fp` hashes only `build/bs2`, `build/runtime.o`, `build/llvm_wrapper.o` to invalidate the fixture stdout cache. It assumes any source change shows up in those binaries.

In practice, derive_walker source changes that update the macro IR baked into bs2 DO propagate (bs2 is rebuilt → new hash → cache invalidated). BUT changes to handwritten helpers consumed by the macro (e.g. `unwrap_sstmt_list` in core/ast.av) may produce the same bs2 if the static IR sections happen to match, leaving the cache stale.

Hit during y9y4.11: had to manually `rm -rf build/cache/fixture_stdout/` repeatedly. Even when I was sure my code changed.

## Fix

Hash relevant source files into the toolchain_fp in addition to the binaries:
- `bootstrap/packages/std-avrac/src/features/walker/derive.av`
- `bootstrap/packages/std-avrac/src/features/comptime/eval.av`
- `bootstrap/packages/std-avrac/src/core/ast.av`
- Generally, every file whose contents can affect macro evaluation or AST shape.

Or simpler: drop the file-level filter and hash ALL `.av` source in std-avrac. Cheap (these are tiny) and bulletproof.

## Acceptance

- Modify any .av source under packages/std-avrac/src/ → next fixture test rerun is a cache MISS.
- Modify only a test file → cached fixture stdout still hits (test changes don't invalidate the toolchain).
- Spec test exercises the invalidation.

## Notes

Encountered during the y9y4.11 debug session as the immediate productivity blocker.
notes: Landed in 1cd23a1f. toolchain_fp now hashes std-avrac .av source via shasum-of-shasums; sidecar freshness uses find -newer -print -quit for O(1) check. Eliminates the rm -rf build/cache/fixture_stdout/ workaround.

title: [typeck] Remove assignable_with_unknowns Unknown-as-wildcard once T4 fully threaded
description:
## Problem

`assignable_with_unknowns` in `core/ast.av` treats `Unknown` as a wildcard inside container shapes (List, Tuple, Task, Closure, FnTyped, Newtype, Enum, Struct). The reason: pre-T4, empty list literals typed as `List<Unknown>`, and arms like `let xs: List<int> = []` only typechecked because the wildcard let the inferred type unify with the declared.

After T4 (29c6bf4c) the typed-context positions thread `expected` down, so empty literals start with the right element type. The wildcard is now defense-in-depth, not load-bearing — but only for positions T4 covers. Other positions (fn call args, fn return positions, etc.) still rely on it.

## Fix

Phase 1: audit every site that produces `List<Unknown>` post-T4. Likely:
- `[ret]` in arm body when ret's binding type is Unknown (T5 partially fixes this for Self-recursive, but generic params + non-Self fields stay Unknown)
- `[]` outside threaded `expected` positions (the few not yet threaded)
- Builtin returns like `[].map(...)` where the lambda return is unresolved

Phase 2: thread `expected` through the remaining positions so the literal never lands as `List<Unknown>`.

Phase 3: delete the Unknown-as-wildcard logic from `assignable_with_unknowns`. Container shapes only match when their inner types do, no wildcard. Run the suite — anything that breaks is a site Phase 2 missed.

## Acceptance

- `assignable_with_unknowns` no longer special-cases `.Unknown` inside `.List` / `.Tuple` / etc.
- `vtype_assignable` reduces to `vtype_eq || narrowed_assignable_to || union_contains`.
- All 2552+ specs still pass.

## Notes

Subset of T6's broader goal of "nominal identity should be exact." Wildcard tolerance is the workaround we built when identity wasn't reliable.
notes: ROOT CAUSE was the metadata serializer's lossy display: fmt_stmt rendered `List<U>` as bare `List`. After switching fmt to vtype_render_full (1a03ceec), the wildcard is gone and 2551/2551 pass. Wildcard tests retired; test fixtures got explicit annotations. Nested-container Unknowns in Tuple/Task/Closure/FnTyped/Newtype still tolerate Unknown internally — separate cleanup if desired.

title: [derive_walker] Annotation-based wrapper-list discovery (replace hardcoded SStmt/SExpr table)
description:
## Problem

derive_walker's wrapper-list classifier holds a hardcoded table:

```
wrapper_inner_type:    SStmt -> Stmt, SExpr -> Expr
wrapper_unwrap_helper: SStmt -> unwrap_sstmt_list, SExpr -> unwrap_sexpr_list
```

Adding a new span-wrapper (MatchArm.body, FieldInit.value, future wrappers) requires editing the macro. CLAUDE.md rule 16 forbids exactly this kind of brittle heuristic: "No string-matching to detect behavior. Use annotations, type system checks, or structural analysis."

## Fix

Annotation-based discovery. Wrapper structs declare:

```
@walker_wrapper(field: "node")
export type SStmt = { node: Stmt, line: int, col: int, ... }
```

derive_walker reads the annotation off any struct it encounters as `List<X>` element type, learns `field` is the projection to the wrapped Self, and emits an unwrap appropriately. Generalises to nested projections too (`MatchArm` with `body.node`).

## Acceptance

- `@walker_wrapper` annotation parsed + retained through resolve.
- derive_walker reads it via the macro's introspection of field.resolved struct decls.
- No hardcoded wrapper names in derive_walker source.
- Adding a new wrapper = adding the annotation, no macro edit.

## Notes

Filed under T6 because once nominal identity is handle-based (T6), the macro can do `is_struct_decl_with_annotation` cleanly via TypeId lookup instead of name string matching against the wrapper table.
notes: Landed in 06053a2c. Root cause: SStmt/SExpr hardcoded table was a workaround for missing ctx-based introspection. Three blocking bugs fixed along the way: (1) vtype_eq strict-string nominal compare (added nominal_names_match for bare-vs-FQN tolerance — smaller T6 step), (2) check_expr's GenericCall arm dropped explicit type-args (added check_generic_call), (3) unwrap_node_list was private (exported). Observable test: walker_wrapper_discovery_test defines a novel MyWrap/MyTree pair the macro has never seen, asserts children() returns 3.

title: [testing/foundations] T8: Shape-matrix property test for derive_walker (and reusable runner for other @expand macros)
description:
## Problem

derive_walker's bug surface is the cross-product of:

- Variant count: {1, 2, 3+}
- Per-variant field-kind composition: (n_scalar, n_direct_self, n_list_self) drawn from {0, 1, many}^3

Today the test suite covers one shape (Pattern's: all scalar OR list-of-self, no mixed-binding variants). The bug in /tmp/derive_walker_repro4.av (single variant `Mix(ret: Shape, params: List<Shape>)`) only surfaced because I happened to try that exact shape. Other shapes likely have latent bugs:

- All-scalar variant with 5+ fields — does pattern_for synthesize 5 underscored binders correctly?
- Variant with 2 direct-self fields + 1 list-self — does block_expr_for_children build `list_concat([a, b], xs)` correctly?
- Variant with 3 list-self fields — does the fold reduce correctly?
- Empty enum — does build_children_fn produce a degenerate match?
- Single-variant enum — exhaustiveness check?

Manual reasoning won't cover this. A property test will.

## Fix

Write `features/walker/tests/derive_walker_shape_matrix_test.av`:

1. A `shape_corpus()` generator yielding ~30 enum source strings covering:
   - 1, 2, 3 variants
   - per-variant kinds in {(s=0,d=0,l=0), (s=1,d=0,l=0), (s=0,d=1,l=0), (s=0,d=0,l=1), (s=1,d=1,l=0), (s=1,d=0,l=1), (s=0,d=1,l=1), (s=1,d=1,l=1), (s=0,d=2,l=0), (s=0,d=0,l=2), (s=0,d=2,l=2)}
2. For each shape:
   - Write the synthesized enum source to a fixture (use the existing write_fixture helper from test_runner)
   - Compile with `avra_shell_exec("./build/bs2 check <fixture>")`
   - Assert exit code 0 + no F1000 / F1003 / F3000 / F9999 in stderr
3. On failure, the test name encodes the shape (e.g. "shape: 2 variants, [s=1,d=1,l=0]+[s=0,d=0,l=1]") so the report is actionable.

Layer it generic: extract a `shape_generator_test_runner` helper so other macros (derive_marshal, future @expand authors) can register their own corpora.

## Acceptance

- ≥30 shapes in the corpus
- All pass once T4 + T5 + T6 land
- Regression introduced in derive_walker (revert a recent feat commit) makes the relevant shape FAIL with a clear name
- Optional Phase 2: random shape generation seeded from a PRNG (true fuzzing layered on top of the deterministic corpus)

## Depends on

- T3 (macro-output validation) — so the shape test failures have useful diagnostics
- T4, T5, T6 — the underlying bugs need to be fixed before the test makes sense (otherwise it's a permanent red signal)

## Blocks

- y9y4.10 (Phase 6 final verification) — that ticket should incorporate the shape matrix as its primary acceptance criterion

## Impact

Catches every shape-combination regression at the right layer (the macro itself). Prevents the situation where a fix for one shape breaks another silently. Generalizes to other macros once the runner is extracted.
notes: T8 shape-matrix property test landed (commit 5d0461cc). 30 derive_walker shapes (1/2/3-variant × {0,1,2}^3 (s,d,l) combos + edge cases). Bundled into 1 'bs2 check' call (~14s vs 30×14=420s per-shape) — failures still pinpoint shape via F-code source line because enum names encode their shape. Workaround for 9p1d still active via AVRA_USE_METADATA strip; 9p1d-lazy fix in flight.

title: [comptime/foundations] T7: Stmt/Expr as first-class runtime Values — eliminate quote/encode/decode roundtrip
description:
## Problem

@comptime functions return `Value` (the runtime currency). The @expand pipeline that takes a macro's output and splices it into the parent scope therefore needs to convert Value -> Stmt and Value -> Expr. Today this involves a 5-hop roundtrip:

1. Macro body constructs Stmt.Let(name, vt, init) — a typed AST value at compile-time logic level
2. features/quote_expr/lower.av::construct_stmt encodes it as an Expr.EnumCtor(...) tree — source-code-shaped
3. eval evaluates that Expr to produce a Value (enum kind, payload = list of Values)
4. features/comptime/eval.av::enum_value_to_stmt decodes the Value back into a Stmt
5. resolve + typeck walk the decoded Stmt

Each hop can lose information. Recent encounters:

- 64fe2c84: construct_stmt's Let/Mut/Const dropped the resolved_vt slot (encoded as ValueType.Unknown). Fixed.
- y9y4.12: enum_value_to_stmt didn't cover NoOp / Break / Continue / If / While / For / ForIn / Defer / Errdefer / Parallel / TraitDecl variants. Fixed.
- This session: enum_value_to_expr didn't cover Assign. Fixed in 3181e429.
- Open: enum_value_to_value_type doesn't preserve TypeId (sets id=0) — drives y9y4.17.

Every macro author pays the same tax. Every new Stmt/Expr variant must be added to BOTH the encoder AND the decoder. Drift between the two is silent — the decoder either returns null (macro splice fails with no clear message) or constructs a degraded variant.

## Fix

Make Stmt and Expr first-class runtime values. Extend the eval loop's Value union:

```
.Stmt(s: Stmt)
.Expr(e: Expr)
```

(Or `.AstNode(kind: AstKind, payload: ptr)` with an internal AstKind enum — TBD which is cleaner; both work.)

Then:

1. @comptime fns can directly write `return Stmt.Let(name, vt, init)` — the eval loop boxes the Stmt into a Value.Stmt at fn-return time.
2. value_to_stmt becomes `match v { .Stmt(s) -> s, _ -> null }` — no decoding.
3. construct_stmt, enum_value_to_stmt, and the entire features/quote_expr/lower.av encoder + features/comptime/eval.av decoder collapse into the eval-loop boundary.
4. AST nodes carry their resolve+typeck state through the Value layer without re-derivation.

### Migration plan

Phase A: introduce Value.Stmt / Value.Expr variants. Both old (encoded) and new (direct) paths work. value_to_stmt accepts both — direct unboxing or via decode.

Phase B: migrate features/walker/derive.av (and other @expand macros) to return Stmt/Expr directly.

Phase C: deprecate construct_stmt / enum_value_to_stmt; emit warnings for any remaining call sites.

Phase D: delete the encoder + decoder once no callers remain. Estimated -500 LoC across quote_expr/lower.av + comptime/eval.av.

## Acceptance

- Value union extended; eval loop boxes Stmt/Expr return values
- features/walker/derive.av returns Stmt directly; no construct_stmt in the path
- features/comptime/expand_macro.av splice path handles direct-Stmt Values
- All existing macro tests pass (vez6.6.4: value_to_stmt decodes... etc — those should still work via the deprecation path)
- bs2/bs3 fixed point holds
- After Phase D: grep for `construct_stmt(` / `enum_value_to_stmt(` returns nothing

## Depends on

- T6 (interned TypeId) — Stmt's type slots need stable identity to roundtrip through Value boxing without re-resolving

## Blocks

- (none directly, but enables Phase D cleanup that touches every @expand macro)

## Impact

Eliminates the largest macro-pipeline bug surface. ~500 LoC of mirror-the-encoder-or-things-break logic deleted. Future Stmt/Expr variant additions don't need encoder+decoder edits — just the variant.

Largest lift in this epic but also the highest cleanup payoff.
notes: PLAN RECONCILE (2026-06-15): native-boxing (box_ast_value) is the L2 INTERIM; the ORC JIT (ps3t.5) is the end-state that deletes interpreter+Value+roundtrip (doc Layer 2). #1-5 done. #6 (delete construct_stmt/enum_value_to_stmt) now tracked by L4 @codec (ps3t.6) + jw6v (quote rework).

title: [generics/foundations] T5: Generic call inference unifies across all argument positions
description:
## Problem

Generic function call inference fails when arguments have heterogeneous concrete-vs-Unknown types.

Concrete repro (/tmp/derive_walker_repro4.av):

```
@expand(derive_walker)
enum Shape {
    Leaf,
    Mix(ret: Shape, params: List<Shape>),
}
```

derive_walker's block_expr_for_children emits the Mix arm as:

```
list_concat([ret], params)
```

where:
- `list_concat<T>(a: List<T>, b: List<T>) -> List<T>`
- `[ret]` has type `List<Unknown>` (pre-T4, list literal element type bottom-up only)
- `params` has type `List<Shape>` (from variant decl)

Expected: inference pins T = Shape, returns List<Shape>.
Actual: T stays Unknown, return type is List<Unknown>, fails to unify with sibling `__derive_walker_empty` (List<Shape>) — F1000.

The structural issue: generic call inference doesn't unify across argument positions. The "first arg wins" rule (or whatever the current rule is) loses information when one arg is more-specific.

## Fix

In features/generics/mono.av (or the call-checking site in typeck/mod.av — TBD which is the right layer):

1. When resolving a generic call `f<T>(a: A, b: B)`, walk all argument positions to collect type-variable constraints.
2. For each generic param T, take the join (or lub) of all positions that mention T.
3. If position 1 says T=Unknown and position 2 says T=Shape, the lub is T=Shape (Shape is more specific than Unknown).
4. Substitute and re-check.

Edge cases:
- Argument types disagree concretely (T=Int from pos 1, T=Str from pos 2) → error at the CALL site with a clear "can't infer T: position 1 says Int, position 2 says Str"
- All positions say T=Unknown → result is T=Unknown (current behavior, fall through to call-site context which T4's bidirectional inference handles)

## Acceptance

- `list_concat([], [some_shape])` returns List<Shape> typed
- /tmp/derive_walker_repro4.av (or T8 shape-matrix equivalent) compiles cleanly
- derive_walker's block_expr_for_children emits an arm that typeck'd unifies with sibling List<Self> arms
- A new test exercises generic call inference with one Unknown arg + one concrete arg

## Depends on

- T4 (bidirectional list-literal inference) — `[]` and `[x]` need to be typeable so inference can pull T from them when an adjacent arg is concrete

## Blocks

- y9y4.6, y9y4.7, y9y4.8 (the apply tickets — fixes the mixed-shape variants in ValueType/Stmt/Expr)
- y9y4.11 (wrapper-list shapes List<SExpr> etc — likely hits the same issue)

## Impact

Closes the direct cause of derive_walker's mixed-shape variant bug. Generic functions become safe to call from macro-emitted code without pre-pinning every type arg.
notes: Landed in eb711c32. Self-recursive bindings (.Self, .List<Self>) carry their proper type into the arm body; non-Self fields stay Unknown until T6. Spec test exercises shape_children mixed-binding variant, wrap_depth single Self field, tagged_item_count scalar+list-of-Self. derive_walker mixed-shape repro (/tmp/derive_walker_repro4.av) now passes — Shape__children typecheck'd cleanly. 2532/2532 specs pass; bs2/bs3 fixed point holds; bs2 self-check passes (4e0a). The remaining qualification-mismatch surface (non-Self fields, F1003 in Result<T,E> contexts) stays scoped to T6.

Post-resolve, list-of-self arms use field type Enum("@std::avrac::core::ValueType", [], N). vtype_eq Enum case: id=0 falls through to name comparison; bare != qualified. assignable_with_unknowns has no Enum case so falls through to false.
