title: [codegen/typeck] emit_method_call fires F1000 'arms have different types: fn vs int' when dispatching unknown method on enum
description:
When user code calls `obj.method(args)` where the method is not defined on obj's type, the typeck doesn't report 'undefined method' — instead it surfaces an F1000 inside std-avrac's own emit_method_call function:

```
error[F1000]: match expression arms have different types: `fn` vs `int` (in function `@std::avrac::features::fn_decl::emit_method_call`)
```

## Repro

```avra
use @std.avrac.features.walker.{derive_walker}
@expand(derive_walker)
enum Tree { Leaf(value: int), Node(left: Tree, right: Tree) }
fn id(t: Tree) -> Tree { t }
fn main() {
    let t = Tree.Leaf(1)
    let r = t.map(id)  // .map is not defined on Tree
    println("done")
}
```

`env -u AVRA_USE_METADATA -u AVRA_LIB_OBJS bash scripts/diagnose.sh --run /tmp/that_file.av` → F1000

## Why this matters

This obscures every 'undefined method' diagnostic behind an unrelated typeck error inside std-avrac. While investigating y9y4.2 (Slice B map), the error misled debugging — looked like derive_walker's map emission was wrong when in fact map() was never emitted.

## Likely root cause

`emit_method_call` in features/fn_decl/codegen.av has a match (line 456: `let tid = match r.ty { .Struct(_, id) -> id, .Enum(_, _, id) -> id, _ -> 0 }`) plus the method-lookup fall-through. Something in that path triggers F1000 when the method isn't found, instead of returning err_emit('undefined method ...').

## Acceptance

- Calling `obj.nonexistent_method(args)` on a struct or enum surfaces F-coded 'undefined method' (or similar) rather than F1000 about emit_method_call's internals.
- y9y4.2 (Slice B map) debugging is unblocked.

title: [derive_walker] Slice C prereq: extend @comptime Stmt/Expr decoders for ForIn / For / nested method-call shapes
description:
Adding visit() to derive_walker requires the macro to emit Stmt.ForIn (`for c in self.children() { c.visit(f) }`). The @comptime decoder in features/comptime/eval.av doesn't recognise Stmt.ForIn or Stmt.For — value_to_stmt returns null, value_to_stmt_list cascades to null, value_to_resolved_decls returns null, and the @expand caller surfaces F4006.

Even with ForIn/For decoders added (attempted: see eval.av:518-547 staging), the surrounding Function decoder fails silently — no DBG fires in any decoder, suggesting an upstream gap (param-type decoder doesn't handle FnTyped? body StructLit shape mismatch? decoder fallthrough hits something other than the variant arms).

## Scope

- Decode Stmt.For / Stmt.ForIn (3-4 payload positions, last is a nested Stmt body).
- Audit Stmt + Expr decoders against the full `construct_*` encoder coverage in lower.av — every variant the encoder writes must have a roundtrip decoder.
- Add a developer-mode tracer that prints the first variant the decoder rejects, so future decoder-coverage gaps surface immediately.

## Acceptance

- A @comptime macro emitting `fn foo(self) { for c in self.children() { c.bar() } }` roundtrips through invoke_macro and lands as a valid Function decl.
- Slice C (visit/fold/find/any in y9y4.3) unblocks.

## Why this matters

Slice A's children() worked because it only needs Function + Match + ListLit + Call + Ident — all already decoded. Slice B (map) and Slice C (visit/fold/find/any) both emit for-loops + method-calls + lambdas, so the decoder gap is the gate.
close_reason: Decoders added for For/ForIn/If/While/Defer/Errdefer/NoOp/Break/Continue/Parallel/TraitDecl in features/comptime/eval.av. Spec test decoder_stmt_coverage_test.av exercises Function → body → ForIn → Block → Call recursive path end-to-end. Commit 60442e47. 2515/2515 passing. Unblocks y9y4.2 (Slice B) + y9y4.3 (Slice C).

title: [expand] @expand(derive_walker) on a core/ast.av enum hits recursion limit (16)
description:
Adding `@expand(derive_walker)` directly to a core enum (e.g. Pattern in core/ast.av) compiles std-avrac successfully, but at consumer compile-time the @expand fixpoint loop hits its 16-iter limit.

## Repro

1. Edit packages/std-avrac/src/core/ast.av: add `use features.walker.{derive_walker}` and `@expand(derive_walker)` on `export enum Pattern`.
2. make build → succeeds (std-avrac compiles itself fine).
3. Consumer fixture that imports @std.avrac.core.{Pattern} and calls Pattern.children() → F4000 @expand recursion limit exceeded.

## Suspect causes (investigation pending)

- Macro emission may inadvertently produce a stmt that still triggers any_expand_annotation in iter N+1. derive_walker emits [target.stmt (bare EnumDecl), children_fn]. Neither should carry @expand — but the fixpoint clearly thinks otherwise.
- Possibly the rewrite_uses pass that runs between iterations re-applies the @expand annotation when processing the from_macro-tagged enum (annotation is on the original source's Annotated wrapper; might be reachable via tree lookup somehow).
- Or the resolver's idempotent qualification of QualifiedIdent in annotation args produces a slightly different stmt each iter, so the equality check that should detect fixed point fails.

## Acceptance

- @expand(derive_walker) on Pattern, ValueType, Stmt, Expr in core/ast.av all compile, selfhost, and downstream consumers can call .children() on each.
- Fixpoint terminates in 1-2 iterations for these decls (not 16).

## Workaround until fixed

Apply derive_walker inside a test fixture (works fine for arbitrary user enums) but NOT to the bootstrap's own core/ast.av enums. y9y4.5-y9y4.8 (apply to Pattern/ValueType/Stmt/Expr) are blocked on this.
close_reason:
Root caused: any_expand_annotation in features/comptime/expand_macro.av didn't recurse into Module bodies. When a package (e.g. std-avrac) carried @expand on a nested decl (e.g. core/ast.av's Pattern), consumers' fixpoint loop saw has_exp=false at iter 0 — walker never invoked, derived method never synthesised, F9999 'undefined method X.children' at codegen. The earlier-reported '16-iter recursion limit' was a different manifestation (probably stale build cache).

Fix: any_expand_annotation now recurses via peel_annotations + .Module(_, body). Pattern @expand fires through Module wrappers, fixpoint terminates in 2 iters.

Verified end-to-end: @expand(derive_walker) on Pattern in core/ast.av compiles, selfhosts, downstream consumers can call Pattern.children() on Or/NestedVariant/Wildcard/etc. Spec test packages/std-avrac/src/features/walker/tests/walker_pattern_test.av PASS. Full suite 2513/2514 (parallel_stmt is preexisting flake; passes in isolation).

title: [derive_walker] Wrapper-list shapes (List<SExpr>, List<SStmt>, List<MatchArm>, List<FieldInit>) — unwrap .node/.value/.body
description:
Real bootstrap AST variants nest their children via wrapper types:

- Stmt.Block(body: List<SStmt>) — SStmt wraps Stmt with span
- Expr.Call(callee: Expr, args: List<SExpr>) — SExpr wraps Expr
- Expr.StructLit(_, inits: List<FieldInit>) — FieldInit has key + value (SExpr)
- Expr.MatchExpr(subject: Expr, arms: List<MatchArm>) — MatchArm has pattern + guard + body

For Stmt walker:
- Recognise List<SStmt> as a list of Stmt children (each wrapped in SStmt)
- children() emits `for s in body { out.push(s.node) }` (or equivalent)

For Expr walker:
- Same for List<SExpr>, List<FieldInit>, List<MatchArm>
- Per-wrapper unwrap path: SStmt → .node, SExpr → .node, FieldInit → .value.node, MatchArm → .body.node

## Design questions

- Hardcoded per-wrapper unwrap paths (simple, works today) vs annotation-based wrapper discovery (`@walker_wrapper(field: "node")` on SStmt; needs metadata flow).
- For Slice A children(), the macro needs only the unwrap pattern. For Slice C visit/fold, the same wrappers come in. Settling the design once unblocks both.

## Acceptance

- @expand(derive_walker) on Stmt compiles, children() correctly flattens Block.body to its inner Stmt elements.
- @expand(derive_walker) on Expr compiles, children() correctly handles Call.args + MatchExpr.arms + StructLit.inits.
- Spec tests for each wrapper shape.

## Depends on

- forge-crafting-intepreters-y9y4.1 (Slice A children — closed)
notes: Landed in 2e8f714f. The classifier now strips '::' qualification before the wrapper-table lookup, and name_matches accepts the suffix relation symmetrically. Stmt.Block + Expr.Call wrapper-list shapes are unwrapped via unwrap_sstmt_list / unwrap_sexpr_list. 2552/2552 specs pass.

title: [metadata] @comptime fn annotation + body not preserved across metadata mode — breaks @expand from metadata-loaded packages
description:
When std-avrac is loaded via AVRA_USE_METADATA=1, `@comptime` annotations on exported fns are stripped and their bodies are reduced to empty stubs. The @expand pass then can't find the macro fn in the @comptime registry (F4002 'no @comptime fn named X in scope') AND would have no body to evaluate even if it could.

## Repro

```
$ env AVRA_USE_METADATA=1 bash scripts/diagnose.sh --run /tmp/avra_walker_basic_test.av
F4002: @expand(@std::avrac::features::walker::derive_walker) — no @comptime fn named ...
```

Without AVRA_USE_METADATA: works fine.

## Impact

Every `@expand(macro_fn)` site in test fixtures that depend on a std-avrac-provided macro fails when the test runner uses metadata mode (which it does by default for ~38x speedup). Without the fix:
- Tests for derive_walker (y9y4.*) can't run via the normal test_shard pipeline.
- All future @comptime-macro features that ship via std-avrac will silently break for downstream consumers using metadata.

## Root cause

`packages/std-avrac/src/build/metadata.av` FnDeclEntry has no `is_comptime` field. Even if it did, `synth_fn_decl` emits the fn with an empty body (`@external_unit` stub) — `@comptime` fns must keep their full body to be invokable at compile time on the consumer side.

## Fix

1. Add `is_comptime: bool` to FnDeclEntry. Serialize/deserialize.
2. metadata_extract.av: detect `@comptime` annotation on the source fn, set the flag.
3. P5 generic-body path already preserves bodies for generic fns; extend the gate from `is_generic` to `is_generic || is_comptime` so @comptime fns also get their bodies into the metadata.
4. metadata_synthesize.av: when reconstructing, wrap the synthesised Stmt.Function in `@comptime` annotation when the flag is set.

## Acceptance

- `env AVRA_USE_METADATA=1 bash scripts/diagnose.sh --run /tmp/avra_walker_basic_test.av` runs and produces `leaf=0 node=2`.
- bs2 selfhost still passes.
- Existing metadata-using tests stay green.

## Workaround until fixed

walker_basic_test + walker_list_self_test bypass metadata mode by running their fixture under `env -u AVRA_USE_METADATA -u AVRA_LIB_OBJS`. Documented escape hatch — see comment in main.av:2515.
notes: 9p1d lazy parse fix landed (commit 3aba48df, pushed). Root cause: FnDeclEntry had no is_comptime flag and body-ship gate was generic-only; @comptime fns lost their bodies on metadata roundtrip and consumers hit F4002. Naive eager-parse regressed every metadata-loaded consumer to 5+ min / 1.5 GB RSS. Fix: runtime.c global g_lazy_comptime + Avra externs; FnDeclEntry.is_comptime threading; synth emits empty-body @comptime+@external_unit wrapped Stmt.Function and stashes source; comptime_lookup_lazy rehydrates from stash on first lookup; comptime_drain_lazy populates all helpers before macro eval (eval Call path has no lazy hook). Observable test: comptime_body_metadata_roundtrip_test.av exercises type_short_name folding from metadata-loaded std-avrac. Perf: std-cli compile in ~13s vs 5+min on eager-parse. pry2 (typeck tuple+imported-struct false positive) still open.

title: [tooling] `bs2 fix` auto-expansion: rewrite `_ -> body` into explicit per-variant arms
description:
Migration tool for the REMOVE WILDCARDS rollout. `bs2 fix --rule=no-wildcard` walks every `match expr { ..., _ -> body }` over a declared enum, and rewrites to N arms (one per variant not already matched), each with the same body.

## Sketch

```avra
// Before
match s {
    .Let(_, _, _) -> handle_let()
    _ -> default()    // hides Mut, Const, If, While, Function, …
}

// After bs2 fix --rule=no-wildcard
match s {
    .Let(_, _, _) -> handle_let()
    .Mut(_, _, _) -> default()
    .Const(_, _, _) -> default()
    .If(_, _, _) -> default()
    // …(every other variant, one arm)
}
```

The user then reviews — usually deciding which variants genuinely want the default and which need a real impl.

## Why

Manual migration of 2700+ sites would burn months. Auto-expand makes the migration mechanical.

## Acceptance

- `bs2 fix --rule=no-wildcard <file>` rewrites the file in place.
- Each rewritten arm has correct ParamEntry shape (matches variant payload arity).
- `bs2 fix --dry-run` shows diff.
- Spec test: round-trip a small file through the tool, verify identical runtime behaviour before/after expansion.

## Depends on

- Generic AST visitor (currently y9y4.9 will deliver, or 93k3 stand-in).
- Knowledge of enum variant set per type — already in TypeRegistry post-resolve.
acceptance_criteria: `bs2 fix` auto-expansion: rewrite `_ -> body` into explicit per-variant arms — delivered; build + spec suite green; selfhost byte-identical fixed point holds.

title: [lang/spec] Forbid `_ ->` in declared-enum match — promote F9001 to error for closed sums
description:
Promote F9001 from warning to error when the matched type is a declared `enum` (not a `union` or a primitive). Spec axis 8.7 currently says wildcards on declared enums warn if hiding >2 variants — change to 'forbid entirely'.

## Why

Per session 'REMOVE WILDCARDS': every wildcard arm on a declared enum is a latent silent-drop bug for any future variant.

## Design questions

- Escape hatch? Initial direction: **no**. If the user genuinely wants a fallthrough, write `_ -> compile_error("unhandled")` or list every variant.
- What about exhaustive matches that already enumerate every variant + add `_ ->` defensively (no missing variant — the wildcard is dead)? → Just remove the dead arm.
- What about generated code from macros? → derive_walker generates per-variant arms by construction; nothing to break.

## Acceptance

- F9001 fires as a hard error when match-subject type is `ValueType.Enum(...)`.
- F9001 stays as today (warning, threshold 3) for `ValueType.Union(...)` and primitives.
- Spec axis 8.7 updated in docs/2026_04_18_FULL_SPEC.md.
- Diagnostic guides the user: list missing variants by name + suggest `bs2 fix`.

## Depends on

- vndt-sibling: `bs2 fix` auto-expansion (so users have a migration path).
- y9y4 (derive_walker rollout — gets the hardest walker sites cleaned up first).
acceptance_criteria: Forbid `_ ->` in declared-enum match — promote F9001 to error for closed sums — delivered; build + spec suite green; selfhost byte-identical fixed point holds.

title: [comptime/eval] Auto-register pure @std.avrac.core fns so @comptime macros can call them
description:
When a @comptime macro calls a pure helper from @std.avrac.core (method_mangled_name, variant_payload_name, type_join, etc.), the eval crashes with 'can only call functions (callee=@std::avrac::core::method_mangled_name kind=type_marker)'.

## Root cause

The comptime registry only auto-registers fns explicitly marked @comptime. Pure helpers in @std.avrac.core are runtime fns; the eval has no entry for them. Current workaround in derive_walker is inlining the helper as a string template literal — every macro author has to repeat this.

## The fix

Auto-register every pure (no side effects, no globals) fn from @std.avrac.core into the comptime registry at startup. Heuristic: if the fn body uses only pure exprs (no eprintln, no avra_shell_exec, no extern fn calls), register it.

Alternatively: gate on an annotation @pure that the @std.avrac.core authors apply.

## Evidence in code

bootstrap/packages/std-avrac/src/features/eval/mod.av lines 991-1004 — the existing comment about this:

> // vez6.6.4: special-case the AST-construction wrappers from
> // @std::avrac::core. lower_quotes emits sexpr_dummy / sstmt_dummy
> // …
> // Auto-registering every pure @std::avrac::core fn would be cleaner but requires the
> // typechecker to distinguish pure from impure helpers — tracked
> // as the second half of vez6.6.4 (auto-register).

This ticket finishes the second half.

## Acceptance

- @comptime macro can call method_mangled_name(x, y) and get the actual string back.
- derive_walker can drop the inlined '${enum_name}__children' template literal in favour of the helper.
- No regression in existing comptime / @expand tests.

## Related

- vez6.6.4 (where this was originally split out).
- y9y4 epic (derive_walker) — multiple macros benefit.

title: [derive_walker] Wrapper-list shapes: List<SExpr>, List<FieldInit>, List<Variant>
description:
Today the macro recognises a child when `field.resolved` is an Enum/Struct matching the parent's name. Real AST variants nest children via wrapper types:

- Stmt.Block(body: List<SStmt>) — SStmt wraps Stmt with a span.
- Expr.StructLit(name: string, inits: List<FieldInit>) — FieldInit wraps Expr with a key.
- Expr.MatchExpr(subject: Expr, arms: List<MatchArm>) — MatchArm carries Pattern + guard + body.

The macro needs to:
1. Recognise List<SStmt> as 'list of Stmt-with-wrapper'; produce `for s in body { out.push(s.node) }` to flatten.
2. Same for SExpr / FieldInit / MatchArm — config the unwrap shape per wrapper type.
3. children() should return the flattened List<Self>, not the wrapper.

## Why

Without this, every variant carrying a List<SStmt> body is missed → children() returns wrong subset → fold/visit/find skip half the tree.

## Acceptance

- Macro recognises List<SExpr/SStmt/FieldInit/MatchArm> as child carriers.
- children() flattens correctly. Spec test: Block(body: [Let, If]) → children() returns [Let, If].

## Depends on

- y9y4.1 (Slice A).
close_reason:
Direct List<Self> field handling complete (e.g. Pattern.NestedVariant's sub_patterns: List<Pattern>). Macro now classifies fields as scalar / direct-Self / direct-List<Self> and emits appropriate body shapes: bare ListLit for direct-only, Ident for single-list, or repeated list_concat for the mixed direct+list case. Spec test packages/std-avrac/src/features/walker/tests/walker_list_self_test.av PASS through the full test runner.

Wrapper-list shapes (List<SExpr> with SExpr.node unwrap, List<FieldInit> with .value, List<MatchArm> with .body, etc.) are a distinct concern — re-filed as a follow-up ticket since the bootstrap AST enums Pattern + ValueType + Stmt + Expr can each be derived without wrapper unwrapping for most variants. Expr.Call (callee: Expr + args: List<SExpr>) is the canonical wrapper-list mixed case; tracked separately.

Bug found + fixed during this slice: list-of-LocalBinding mutation leak in resolve/names.av (bind_params_ctx + bind_pattern_ctx pushed into the shared underlying list, causing cross-fn name leaks). Switched to list_push_copy. 2513/2513 tests now pass. See 6if1.

title: [derive_walker] Slice C.visit: Type__visit(self, f) depth-first pre-order traversal
description:
Layer template-style helpers on top of children():

- fold(self, init, f: (acc, Self) -> acc) -> acc — left-fold over self + descendants.
- visit(self, f: (Self) -> ()) — depth-first traversal for side effects.
- find(self, pred: (Self) -> bool) -> Self? — first descendant matching pred.
- any(self, pred: (Self) -> bool) -> bool — short-circuit existence check.

## Sketch

```avra
fn Stmt__visit(self: Stmt, f: (Stmt) -> ()) {
    f(self)
    for c in self.children() { c.visit(f) }
}
```

These don't need per-variant arms — they're library code on top of children() / map(). Generated once per type for the user-facing dot-syntax.

## Why

- find()/any() simplify checks like 'does this fn body return?' from 30-line recursions to one call.
- visit() replaces every diagnostic-collection walker.

## Acceptance

- All four methods generated for each enum that gets @expand(derive_walker).
- Spec test: fold sums child counts. visit collects all idents. find returns the first qualifying node.

## Depends on

- y9y4.1 (Slice A) — needs children() to exist.
close_reason: Type__visit(self, f) lands. Depth-first pre-order via children(). Pattern + Tree pick it up via @expand(derive_walker) — verified end-to-end on both. Spec test walker_visit_test.av PASS. Slice C originally bundled fold/visit/find/any — visit was the simplest (no generics, no return, no nullable). The others split into y9y4.13 (fold, generic accumulator), y9y4.14 (find, nullable return), y9y4.15 (any, short-circuit bool). Commit 4871689c. 2516/2516 passing.

title: [derive_walker] Slice B: map(self, f) -> Self per-variant transform
notes: Landed in 0ebd047d. Type__map emitted alongside children/visit/any/find. Per-variant reconstruction: f(field) for DirectSelf, list_map(field, f) for ListOfSelf, scalar/wrapper-list pass through. Observable test: map(double_leaf) over MTree{Leaf,Node} doubles each leaf's value (3+4 -> 14 via sum check). title: metadata fast-path mysteriously drops F9050 warning inside bs2 test shard env (not in standalone bs2 compile)
description:
Repro:
- Standalone shell:
    AVRA_USE_METADATA=1 AVRA_LIB_OBJS=<paths> ./build/bs2 compile <fixture-with-@expand-introducer>.av
  → F9050 warning visible in stderr, grep -c '_phantom_never_decl' returns 2.

- Inside a bs2 test shard binary calling the same compile via avra_shell_exec:
    ./build/bs2 compile <fixture>.av 2>&1
  with the shard's inherited env (AVRA_USE_METADATA=1, AVRA_LIB_OBJS=<paths>, AVRA_STD_LISTING_FILE, AVRA_STD_UNIVERSE_FP, AVRA_SKIP_ENSURE_BS2=1):
  → F9050 warning NOT visible.
  → Test 'phantom name in introduces surfaces a stderr warning' (expand_introduces_validation_test.av) fails.

Workaround in place: the test fixture wraps the compile with 'env -u AVRA_USE_METADATA -u AVRA_LIB_OBJS' so the @expand pipeline runs the non-metadata path, where F9050 reliably surfaces. This is a real workaround masking an underlying inconsistency.

Investigation done:
- AVRA_USE_METADATA only gates module-resolve fast-path in features/modules/resolver.av — it does NOT directly gate the @expand pipeline or the F9050 emit site (features/comptime/expand_macro.av invoke_macro).
- The per-F-code warning render cap (commit 2a698503) was confirmed NOT to be the cause — F9050 has its own F-code, can't be buried by F9001 wildcards under per-code cap=3.
- Standalone bs2 compile with the same env vars set manually DOES surface F9050.
- The shard binary must be doing something else differently — possibly stale cached test binary, or the SHARD'S OWN bs2 invocation goes through a different code path I haven't located, or the test binary itself was compiled with a stale render_list.

Acceptance criteria:
- 'bs2 compile' produces F9050 identically whether AVRA_USE_METADATA is set or not.
- expand_introduces_validation_test.av no longer needs the 'env -u' wrapper to pass.

Not blocking: the warning DOES surface for users invoking 'bs2 compile' directly (the user-facing path). Only the in-process test runner sees this inconsistency.
close_reason: Diagnosis was wrong. Investigation via XXX trace prints confirmed F9050 IS emitted correctly by 'bs2 compile' with AVRA_USE_METADATA=1 — the test's 'compile' string contained '_phantom_never_decl' and 'F9050' both. The real failure was downstream: with AVRA_USE_METADATA=1 the .ll has EXTERN refs to std-avrac fns, but the test fixture's hand-rolled cc invocation only linked build/runtime.o + build/llvm_wrapper.o, missing the AVRA_LIB_OBJS std-* .o files. cc silently produced no binary (just an LLVM triple warning) and the test's run step caught 'No such file or directory'. The F9050 assertion passed; the contains('7') assertion failed because the binary literally never ran. Real fix in commit eae3e2e2: lib_objs_cc_args() helper reads AVRA_LIB_OBJS at runtime and splices the .o paths into the cc command, matching what build/compile.av does in the orchestrator's own link path. Workaround removed. No metadata-fast-path bug exists at the @expand pipeline level.

title: expand_introduces_validation_test: F9050 visible in compile stderr but test framework sees it as missing
description:
After uegu (commit 6279939d) and the warn_count<10 cap removal (this commit), the F9050 ExpandIntroducesPhantom warning IS emitted to bs2 compile stderr (verified manually: 'bs2 compile /tmp/fixture.av 2>&1 | grep _phantom_never_decl' returns 5 matches showing 'warning[F9050]: @expand(introducer) — ResolvedDecls.introduces lists `_phantom_never_decl`...').

The test fixture (packages/std-avrac/src/features/comptime/tests/expand_introduces_validation_test.av) uses avra_shell_exec to run bs2 compile + cc link + binary run, then asserts out.contains('_phantom_never_decl') && out.contains('7'). Manual replication produces both — phantom warning appears 5 times in compile stderr, binary outputs 7.

In bs2 test --per_file mode the assertion returns false; the test fails consistently across runs.

Investigation pending: avra_shell_exec uses popen(cmd, 'r') which captures stdout only; the test relies on '2>&1' redirection to fold stderr into stdout. Either the redirection isn't reaching popen via the test runner's subprocess, or the test runner's working dir / env differs from the manual repro.

Workaround: none needed for users — the warning surfaces correctly via 'bs2 compile' / 'bs2 check'. Only the in-process test assertion is affected.

Acceptance:
- expand_introduces_validation_test passes under bs2 test --per_file
- F9050 warning visible in shell-execed compile output as it is in manual runs

Discovered: 2026-05-28 during uegu DRY pass + render warning-cap fix.
close_reason:
Root cause: bs2 test --per_file sets AVRA_USE_METADATA=1 + AVRA_LIB_OBJS pointing at pre-built std-avrac .o. With metadata fast-path active, bs2 compile uses the cached unit.realobj.o (which DOES contain the F9050 code) but goes through a different pipeline (the metadata path) that skips the full @expand bag accumulation, so F9050 never lands in stderr. A plain interactive bs2 compile (no env vars) emits F9050 correctly.

Fix: the fixture now wraps the compile call with 'env -u AVRA_USE_METADATA -u AVRA_LIB_OBJS' — same idiom already used by deps_sidecar_test and metadata_fast_path_size_test per packages/cli/src/main.av:2365-2368. Forces the fixture through the full resolve_and_expand_program pipeline so F9050 surfaces. The 'avra build/check/compile' user-facing commands are unaffected because they don't set those env vars.

Filed bug for follow-up: the metadata fast-path silently drops F9050 (and presumably any other in-pass diagnostics added after the metadata snapshot was taken). The right long-term fix is for the metadata path to merge the @expand bag, but that's a deeper plumbing question — bd 2zxg should be filed separately if/when the @expand-via-metadata path becomes hot.

title: quote-surface gaps: arm kind, type-position splice, iteration splice
description:
Step 2 of the @expand pipeline handoff doc lists four quote-surface probes. All four fail today, but unblocking them requires extending the tree-walk evaluator (features/eval/mod.av), not just the quote parser/lower.

Probe 1: `quote arm { ~pat -> ~body }` — no `arm` kind in parse_quote_kind. Adding it needs a new arm-shaped Quote dispatch path and a construct_match_arm encoder.

Probe 2: splicing a List<MatchArm> into a match body — depends on probe 1, plus the splice lowering needs to recognise arm-list position in match-arm positions.

Probe 3: `fn helper(x: ~name_arg) -> ~name_arg` — type-position splice. parse_type_atom rejects `~` because it expects a Tk.Identifier / Tk.KwDyn / Tk.KwFn / Tk.LeftParen / Tk.LeftBracket first.

  error: @expand(build) — macro evaluation failed: no eval_stmt handler

Defer the four probe fixes to a follow-up session after the pipeline-order fix lands, when there is more headroom and the eval interpreter has been audited for tree-walk gaps.

title: @expand macros cannot introduce top-level decls (pipeline order)
description:
Phase 1 audit finding (2026-05-25).

A @expand macro that returns Stmt.Function (or any decl-introducing Stmt) succeeds at the macro layer but its output never reaches codegen as a usable declaration. Empirical proof:

  @comptime
  fn build_fn() -> Stmt {
      let empty_body: List<SStmt> = []
      let empty_params: List<ParamEntry> = []
      let empty_tp: List<TypeParamEntry> = []
      Stmt.Function("_gen", empty_tp, empty_params, ValueType.Unknown, empty_body)
  }
  @expand(build_fn)
  fn placeholder() {}
  fn main() { _gen() }   // resolve error: undefined variable _gen

After compilation, '_gen' appears only as a string literal in the IR (the fn name from the encoded payload). No 'define i64 @_gen()' block is emitted.

Root cause: pipeline ordering in cli/main.av:

  parse -> modules -> expand_components -> derive_marshal -> resolve_names
        -> expand_macros -> run_comptime -> typecheck -> codegen

resolve_names runs BEFORE expand_macros. So when expand_macros emits a new top-level decl, the resolver/symbol-registry has already finished its pass and the decl is invisible to downstream stages.

Why expand_macros runs there: it needs run_comptime's eval runtime to be primed, and that runtime requires resolved names for the macro body to call helper fns.

Three architectural options:

1. Re-run resolve_names after expand_macros. Easy to describe, cascades through typeck/mono/codegen — those passes assume a single resolution pass. Each would need an incremental re-resolution path.

2. Move expand_macros BEFORE resolve_names. Breaks any macro body that calls helper fns via imports (the body needs resolved names to invoke them at @comptime).

3. Split expand_macros into two phases: a pre-resolve phase that emits decls (no body eval), a post-resolve phase that runs macro bodies (already present). Decls go through the normal resolver in between.

Option 3 is probably cleanest but is still a multi-day refactor.

Pre-resolve compiler-internal passes (marshal-style) are unaffected — they run at the right pipeline position with full programmatic AST access. That's the established pattern for compiler-internal derives. This ticket is specifically about user-level @expand macros.

Related work landed in same session:
- 98e32334 — @expand multi-stmt return support (a real improvement, independent of this issue)
notes:
Detailed handoff doc landed: docs/2026_05_25_EXPAND_PIPELINE_HANDOFF.md

The doc contains: empirical probe, root-cause analysis, three architectural options (Option C recommended), step-by-step implementation plan, test plan, verification criteria, what NOT to touch, glossary for context-fresh agent.

Next agent reads that doc, lands Option C, then a follow-up agent picks up derive_walker on the @expand path.

--- 2026-05-26 — Step 4 MVP landed (c11c4749) ---

Done:
- resolve_names split into resolve_names_pre_expand + validate_scopes_after_expand
- cli/main.av resolve_and_expand wrapper interleaves expand_macros between the halves
- 3 regression tests: expand_decl_introducing_test (fn), _type, _enum
- All 4 pipeline call sites (check, fmt, test, build) use the new flow
- Selfhost fixed point holds; 2471 tests pass

Verified: macros emitting fn, type, enum decls via quote stmt all
compile and execute correctly. Original bug ("undefined variable _gen")
is resolved.

Out of scope (left for follow-up sessions, per handoff doc):
- Programmatic Stmt.Function(...) construction (eval gap — separate)
- expand_introduces_impl, expand_multi_decl, expand_nested tests
- Full Option C with from_macro SStmt tag + collect/eval split
- ResolverCtx infrastructure (handoff doc step 5)
- Quote-surface probes (handoff doc step 2)

Staying open per CLAUDE.md rule 19 until handoff doc work is complete.

title: closures capturing mutable outer vars hold dangling stack pointer
mono fails on list_push_copy<T> for new types added after cc88ea78
description: The seed monomorphizer cannot synthesize list_push_copy specializations for types introduced after commit cc88ea78. Workaround in place: non-generic _push_<T> helpers in hygiene/typeck/list_ops (see d0c8f5af and edf876ed). Also drove the inline snapshot-then-append workaround now centralized in codegen/types.av as push_loop_frame / push_defer_entry. Once the seed mono is fixed and the seed cycled forward, delete those non-generic helpers and the push_loop_frame / push_defer_entry exports, switching everything back to the generic list_push_copy<T>.
notes:
Deep investigation 2026-05-25: the mono bug is real but not trivially fixable.

The path:
1. Source has `use list_ops.{list_push_copy}` (unqualified import).
2. Resolver rewrites all uses to `QualifiedIdent("@std::avrac::list_ops::list_push_copy")`.
3. mono.av:826 collect_generics records generic fn decls keyed on bare name (e.g. "list_push_copy").
4. mono.av:964 collect_inst_expr looks up the call's qualified name in regs.fns — never finds it.
5. mono.av:1667 rewrite_expr same lookup, same miss. Call stays unmangled.
6. codegen emits `call @std::avrac::list_ops::list_push_copy` — fn doesn't exist (only spec'd `@list_push_copy__T` would). `err_emit('undefined function ...')`.

Why list_map etc. still work: those are also QualifiedIdent post-resolve and ALSO miss the lookup. But typeck or somewhere else must be normalizing them — the IR shows `@list_map__T` specs do exist. Need to trace why list_map differs from list_push_copy.

Hypothesis (not verified): some prior pass normalizes the call to bare-Ident form for SOME generics but not all. Or some other code path adds qualified-name aliases to the registry. Investigation needs: instrument collect_generics + collect_inst_expr to log every name seen, run on a minimal repro, compare list_map vs list_push_copy.

Also discovered: per-package build cache (packages/*/build/cache/*/metadata.bin) hides source edits. `make build` after editing lib source can succeed using stale IR. Must delete metadata.bin or use a stronger invalidation to test mono changes.
