spawn_check), and .await produces the payload directly with no Result
wrap. So the language-level type signature also needs adjusting.

Implementation sketch:
1. Per-thread panic catcher in avra_thread_entry — wrap the closure
   invocation so panics (which currently call exit/abort) instead
   set a flag on the AvraTask struct and return.
2. AvraTask gains a `panic_msg: const char*` field (NULL on success).
3. avra_task_await returns a tagged result: either (ok, value) or
   (err, panic_msg). Codegen of .await unpacks the tag.
4. Spec test: spawn a closure that panics, .await should return an
   Err(...) without killing the parent.

The panic catcher likely needs a longjmp/setjmp wrapper around the
closure call. abort()/exit() can't be caught this way — only
runtime traps (null deref, etc.) that route through avra_runtime_error
can be intercepted. That's still a meaningful improvement.

title: implement Task.all() / Task.race() per spec Axis 18
description:
Per spec Axis 18, the concurrency model promises:
- Task.all([t1, t2, ...]) — await all, return list of results
- Task.race([t1, t2, ...]) — await first, cancel rest

Current state: neither is implemented. There's no codegen path,
no runtime helper, no syntax. Only Task.await and Task.cancel exist
(features/struct_decl/codegen.av + features/fn_decl/codegen.av).

Implementation sketch:
1. Runtime helpers in runtime.c:
   - avra_task_all(handles_ptr, count) -> result_list_ptr (pthread_join all in order)
   - avra_task_race(handles_ptr, count) -> (winner_index, winner_result_ptr) — likely needs pthread_cond_t per task group; on first completion, pthread_cancel + pthread_join the rest
2. Codegen for `Task.all(...)` and `Task.race(...)` — these are method-on-type (associated fn) not method-on-instance, so they need a fresh syntax slot rather than the .method dispatch.
3. Type-check: result type for .all is List<T>; for .race is (int, T) or Result<T, Cancelled>.

Why this matters: spawn-based parallel test runner wants `Task.all(test_tasks)` for the join phase. Without it, you have to loop+await manually.

title: audit runtime singletons for thread-safety under spawn { }
description: Partially fixed in commit 02796682: avra_capture_stdout now uses a recursive _capture_mutex so two spawned threads can't race on dup2(STDOUT_FILENO). Cross-thread leakage during a capture window (a non-capturing thread's println landing in a capturing thread's tmpfile) is NOT fixed — that requires TLS-routed stdout in the codegen lowering. Keeping this bead open for that follow-up.

title: Cold rebuild fails 400+ shards under memory pressure (jetsam mass-kill)
description:
After fixing the dispatch.sh deadlock (commit e0c5a633), cold rebuilds (touch any @std file → all 460 shards cache-miss → all recompile) reveal a separate pre-existing issue: macOS jetsam mass-kills bs2 worker processes under memory pressure.

Observed: 'touch packages/std-avrac/src/build/cache.av && bs2 test' → 418 of 466 shards exit with empty logs (jetsam-killed before producing any output). Only 3 tests run; 222 pass; the rest never executed.

Cause: 8-way parallel cold compile peaks at ~3-4GB RSS (each bs2 cold compile holds 200-500MB). Combined with the system's resident set (typically 8+GB on a 16GB machine), total exceeds available; jetsam kills the most-recently-spawned bs2 instances.

Fix candidates:
1. Detect cold-rebuild case and reduce AVRA_JOBS for that run (e.g.
   jobs=max(2, cores/4)). Slower but reliable.
2. Memory-aware dispatcher: query memory_pressure(8), throttle slot
   refills when pressure rises.
3. Retry mechanism: when a shard's log is empty (jetsam-killed), the
   orchestrator retries it serially after the parallel batch.
4. Smaller cold compile via the 4szi.* in-process harness (avoids
   bs2-per-shard memory amplification).

Workaround today: 'AVRA_JOBS=4 bs2 test' usually completes; jobs=2
always does.

Was masked by the deadlock bug — the deadlock would lock up the
dispatcher early so jetsam thrashing wasn't visible.

title: Persistent worker pool — bypass per-shard fork+exec floor
description:
Warm 'bs2 test --per_file' floors at ~7s. Top-10 test elapsed_ms sums to ~7s; theoretical 8-way wall ≈ max(1.4s) + sum/8 ≈ 4s, vs observed 7.1s.

The 3s gap is fork+exec overhead: 451 shards × 2 forks each (wrapper + test bin) = 902 forks at ~5-10ms each on M1 ≈ 5-9s of fork serialisation.

Fix: cargo-nextest-style persistent worker pool.
- N long-lived bs2 worker processes (one per core)
- Workers read test paths from fifo/socket, run them inline
- Workers stay warm across the whole suite
- Total forks: N (pool size), not 902

Target: <2s warm (down from 7s).
Estimated effort: 2-3 iterations of work.

Tracking after splits (commits d128df4a, 0dabbc12, 1dfbd701). 4szi.*
(in-process test harness) is a related but smaller lever.

title: bs2 binary corrupts (rc=137 on --help) — third occurrence this session
description:
Three times in this /loop session, the build/bs2 binary became unusable: every invocation returns rc=137 (SIGKILL) with zero stdout/stderr. 'make clean && make build' produces a working binary.

Pattern: usually happens after I've killed mid-flight test runs or during memory-pressured periods (jetsam events in the system log). The binary is the same size (~2.2MB) but presumably has been truncated/corrupted at the Mach-O level.

Hypothesis: 'make build' overwrites build/bs2 in place. If the link step is killed (jetsam), the partial output stays at the target path. The next invocation reads a truncated binary and SIGSEGVs/SIGKILLs during dyld load.

Fix candidate: 'make build' should link to a staging path (e.g. build/bs2.tmp) then atomically rename to build/bs2 on success. Same atomic-publish pattern as cache_publish.

Located: Makefile's link step.
close_reason: Closed

title: cli_build_flags_test (2.5s, 7 specs) — split into per-spec shards
description:
After the expand_macro_test cluster split (commits d128df4a, 0dabbc12), cli_build_flags_test sets the wall floor at 2.5s.

Actual count: 11 specs (not 7 — undercounted in first filing).
- 6 use setup_project (bin shape)
- 3 use setup_lib_project (lib shape)
- 2 have unique inline setup

Each spec shell-execs bs2 build 1-2 times. With the fxwn fast-path
each bs2 build is ~180ms. Total: 14 invocations × 180ms ≈ 2.5s. Matches.

Split into 11 per-spec files. Each gets:
- extern fn avra_shell_exec
- Its own setup helper (inline; setup_project or setup_lib_project)
- A UNIQUE /tmp project dir (e.g. /tmp/avra_build_flags_explain_cold/)
- Its one spec block

Each shard: 1-2 bs2 build invocations × 180ms = 180-360ms test
binary time + ~30ms shard wrapper = 250-400ms per shard.

Wall after split: max single shard ~400ms. Combined with other
long-tail (children_autopush_test 1.4s, expand_macro_test 2.0s),
the suite wall floor drops from 7.0s to ~3-4s.

Mechanical work — about 11 × 30-line files. Pattern is identical to
the expand_macro_test split.

Located: bootstrap/tests/cli_build_flags_test.av (205 lines).
close_reason: Closed

title: build cache wastes ~24MB/slot via duplicate unit.o + unit.realobj.o
description:
Each cache slot stores:
- unit.ll: 20MB IR text
- unit.o:  20MB ASCII text (BIT-IDENTICAL duplicate of unit.ll — cache.av comment acknowledges this 'historical quirk')
- realobj.o: 4MB Mach-O object
- unit.realobj.o: 4MB Mach-O (BIT-IDENTICAL duplicate of realobj.o)

Across 2036 cache slots, this wastes up to ~50GB. Real corpus is ~4-5GB used because not every slot has all four files, but unit.o + unit.realobj.o being duplicates is pure overhead.

Fix:
1. Drop the .o write in cache_publish — it's the same text we wrote to unit.ll.
2. Decide canonical name for the real Mach-O (realobj.o vs unit.realobj.o) and remove the other side. The collect_workspace_lib_objs glob uses 'unit.realobj.o' so keep that one; remove realobj.o aliases.
3. Update callers (entry_o_path users + the llc-materialize loop in collect_workspace_lib_objs) to match the canonical name.

Disk capacity matters for CI environments and dev laptops — this iteration hit ENOSPC mid-test (system was at 95% full); the duplicate writes amplify cache churn unnecessarily.

Located: packages/std-avrac/src/build/cache.av cache_publish; packages/cli/src/main.av collect_workspace_lib_objs (the llc-loop that produces unit.realobj.o duplicating realobj.o).

title: typeck gap: ComponentDef 'implements TraitA' isn't verified to actually have a matching impl block after expansion
smell: comptime/expand_macro + component_decl/expand use raw eprintln("error: ...") instead of diagnostic bag
description:
Found during vez6.8.3 red-team. CLAUDE.md error policy: all errors go through CompileError::render(). No raw eprintln("error: ..."). Today these sites bypass it:

packages/std-avrac/src/features/comptime/expand_macro.av:202,223,231,238,243,248 — 6 sites emitting @expand-time errors as plain stderr. Tests grep stderr instead of asserting on a DiagnosticBag.

packages/std-avrac/src/features/component_decl/expand.av:650 — child-type validation reports invalid nested ComponentBlocks via stderr.

Acceptance:
- Each raw eprintln gets routed through a diagnostic bag (F-code assigned per the F-code map in CLAUDE.md / spec Axis 20).
- expand_macros / expand_components return a bag alongside their rewritten StmtList.
- Each existing failing test that grep'd stderr migrates to bag_has_code.
- 'avra build' / 'avra check' surface the same F-codes via the unified renderer.

Why filed: red-team gates of vez6.8.3 surfaced these as smells. Not blocking vez6.8 closure on its own (parser correctness is the gating signal), but they violate the zero-raw-errors policy and need a focused fix later.
close_reason: All raw eprintln sites in expand_macro.av (9) and component_decl/expand.av (1) replaced with proper DiagnosticBag entries. New F-codes F4000-F4006 + F4100 + F9050 added. expand_macros_eval_with_state returns ExpandResult{stmts,bag}; expand_components_bag replaces expand_components with 2-pass design. All 6 callers updated. 2492/2492 tests pass; selfhost fixed point holds.

title: Test Runner V2: manifest-declared dependency graph instead of hand-rolled @std/* pre-build
description:
Once AVRA_USE_METADATA + multi-object linking ships, the orchestrator pre-builds @std/avrac, @std/cli, @std/crypto, @std/json, @std/lsp by hardcoded name, scrapes <pkg>/build/cache/last/<name>.txt sidecars for the active fp, and stitches the .o paths together. Brittle.

Cargo declares deps in Cargo.toml and topo-builds via a real graph. avra.toml already has a [dependencies] section for path deps; extend it for stdlib deps and let bs2 walk the graph properly.

## Acceptance

- avra.toml declares which @std packages a test binary needs.
- Orchestrator topo-builds them in dependency order.
- No hardcoded std_pkgs list in main.av.
- Adding/removing a stdlib package doesn't require main.av edits.

## Filed from

GETTING_TO_CLI_V2.md immaturity audit #3.

title: Test Runner V2: action-level memoization (skip re-running unchanged tests)
description:
Currently, even when a test binary is unchanged (cache hit) AND its declared inputs haven't changed, we still RUN the test. Bazel skips RUNNING tests under those conditions — the action's result (pass/fail) is cached too.

For deterministic tests this is safe. For tests that read external state (clock, env, network) it isn't. Need an opt-in marker or a sensible default.

## Acceptance

- After a successful test run, record the test binary's fp + its declared input fps + its result JSON.
- On the next run with same fp+inputs, skip the execution and reuse the cached result.
- Opt-out via env var or fixture marker for tests that touch external state.

## Filed from

GETTING_TO_CLI_V2.md immaturity audit #2 (Bazel-style action caching).

title: Test Runner V2: process backpressure (memory-aware job dispatch)
description:
AVRA_JOBS=8 runs 8 bs2 children regardless of available RAM. Each child holds its own parsed @std AST + LLVM context (~100s of MB). We've already hit OOM kills when the system was also under disk pressure.

Bazel/Buck2 measure available system memory and adapt concurrency. We should too — at least clamp jobs to min(AVRA_JOBS, available_mb / per_job_estimate).

## Acceptance

- spawn_pool_async (or its caller) reads free RAM before dispatching.
- Per-job memory estimate is configurable / measured.
- Pool size automatically drops on memory-constrained machines.
- Add a test that simulates low memory and confirms graceful degradation.

## Filed from

GETTING_TO_CLI_V2.md immaturity audit #1.

title: build_binary: multi-object linking for AVRA_USE_METADATA shards
description:
2wfp shipped the correctness fix for the metadata cache key (whole-package fingerprint), but enabling AVRA_USE_METADATA=1 in per-file test shards still fails with 'Undefined symbols' at link time. The metadata fast-path synthesizes signature-only stubs from cached metas — the actual bodies must come from the producer's compiled .o files.

## Mechanism

When AVRA_USE_METADATA=1 + AVRA_DEPS_OUT=<path>:
1. Resolver substitutes metadata stubs for @std/* package source.
2. Each substituted file's path gets appended to AVRA_DEPS_OUT (one .o path per line).
3. The build driver (run_build_command) reads AVRA_DEPS_OUT after compile and includes those .o files in the link step.

For per-file test shards (run_test_shard_command → build_binary), step 3 doesn't happen. build_binary's link path just feeds the shard's own .o + runtime.o + llvm_wrapper.o to cc. The producer .o files referenced via metadata stubs aren't linked, so symbols are undefined.

## Acceptance

- build_binary accepts an optional AVRA_DEPS_OUT-style deps file (or a List<string> of .o paths).
- The shard's compile (currently inline via the pipeline → codegen → link chain in build_binary) sets AVRA_DEPS_OUT, reads it after codegen, and passes the .o paths to link_objects.
- AVRA_JOBS=4 ./build/bs2 test --per_file (with AVRA_USE_METADATA=1 wired in the orchestrator cmd) succeeds end-to-end. Cold full-suite drops to <60s on 8 cores.
- run_per_file_test_command re-enables AVRA_USE_METADATA=1 in the cmd list.

## Filed from

2wfp shipped the cache-slot fingerprint fix; per-shard usage of AVRA_USE_METADATA needs this follow-up.

title: Extract compile_program: share AST→binary pipeline between bs2 compile and test runner
description:
After 05yc + DRY (commit pending), compile_test_unit_to still duplicates ~80 lines of pipeline + codegen + link with the 'bs2 compile' subcommand handler. Both do:

  AST → lower_quotes → desugar → inject_intrinsics → expand_components → resolve_names → expand_macros → run_comptime → typecheck_program → monomorphize → codegen → link

The only differences are:
- Test path writes to _test_<shard>.{o,bin}; compile writes to <entry>.ll
- Test handles coverage with instrprof + clang_rt linkage; compile has the same coverage branch
- Test renders diagnostics under '<test>' filename; compile uses real path

## Proposed shape

Extract into @std.avrac.build or a new module:

```avra
type CompileTarget = {
    program: StmtList,              // already assembled (test) or parsed (compile)
    output_stem: string,            // 'build/_test_<shard>' or '<entry>.ll'-stripped
    coverage: bool,
    diag_filename: string,          // for render_bag
    profile_lib_paths: ProfileLibPaths,  // when coverage
}

export fn compile_program(target: CompileTarget) -> Result<string, string>
```

Then:
- compile_test_unit_to ≈ assemble_test_program + compile_program(coverage=args.coverage)
- bs2 compile ≈ parse_program_source + compile_program(coverage=...)

Both call sites drop from ~100 lines to ~10 lines of test/compile-specific logic plus a single shared call.

## Acceptance

- compile_test_unit_to has no inline pipeline — calls compile_program.
- bs2 compile subcommand handler has no inline pipeline — calls compile_program.
- 'make test' + selfhost fixed point pass.
- main.av line count drops by ~150 lines net.

## Filed from

09yk session — user asked 'keep testing as thin as possible'. The DRY refactor + assemble_test_program extraction got testing down meaningfully; this is the next step.

title: 05yc UX polish: shard-summary dedup, --json mode, TTY progress for per-file
description:
05yc per-file parallel orchestrator ships functional but with UX gaps that should land before --per_file becomes default:

## Issues

1. **Reporter prints two summary lines.** test_render_summary emits both '[shard-summary] pass=N ...' (machine-readable, for orchestrator aggregation) AND the ANSI-coloured 'N/M tests passed in X.Ys'. When running a single shard standalone (not via orchestrator), the user sees both — visual noise. Either suppress the machine line when stdout is a TTY, or gate it on an env var (AVRA_SHARD_MODE=1) the orchestrator sets.

2. **Sync pool_run fallback path skips aggregation.** In run_per_file_test_command, when spawn_pool_async returns -1 (spawn failure), we fall back to pool_run. If that returns non-zero, we return 1 without calling aggregate_shard_logs — user gets no per-shard output. Fix: always call aggregate_shard_logs in the fallback path so failures get the same render path as successes.

3. **No TTY progress bar.** The bundled path's run_per_mod_with_progress renders a live N/M done + running list. Per-file orchestrator just blocks on avra_process_wait. Add the same TTY progress rendering: count done markers, render multi-line bar, clear before final summary.

4. **No --json output mode.** bundled emits build_event_json() lines when args.json is set; per-file orchestrator ignores args.json. Symmetric JSON output is the contract for CI tooling.

5. **Filter propagation through forked shards.** Currently passes '--filter X' to each shard, but the shard doesn't use it (the shard compiles exactly one file). Drop the filter pass-through — it's dead code that costs nothing but is misleading.

## Acceptance

- Single-shard standalone invocation (./build/bs2 _test_shard tests/X_test.av) shows ONE summary line, not two.
- spawn_pool_async failure -> aggregate_shard_logs still runs and prints per-shard output.
- TTY progress bar renders K/N done + running slugs during parallel run.
- AVRA_JOBS=4 ./build/bs2 test --per_file --json emits build_event_json events per shard.
- Filter pass-through removed.

## Filed from

05yc commit 999d994d — see audit at end of session.

title: Code smell: internal compiler eprintln() bypasses DiagnosticBag (blocks in-process tests)
description:
Multiple compiler passes (expand pass, comptime macro lookup, child-type validation) report user-visible errors via plain `eprintln("...")` instead of `bag_report(diag_error(...))`. Examples:

- packages/std-avrac/src/features/comptime/expand.av — "no @comptime fn named X" when @expand references an unknown macro
- packages/std-avrac/src/features/component_decl/expand.av — "type X is not a valid child of Y" + "expected one of: ..."

## Why it matters

These errors are user-facing — they explain real compile failures — but they don't land in DiagnosticBag, so:

1. The new in-process check_source() can't observe them (returns an empty bag for tests that depend on them, e.g. expand_macro_test.av's 'missing macro fn: clear diagnostic' case).
2. `bs2 check` exit code may not reflect the failure since the bag's error_count is 0.
3. Tooling (LSP, --json) can't surface these as structured diagnostics.

The CLAUDE.md 'ZERO RAW ERRORS POLICY' is the project rule:
> All errors go through CompileError::render(). No exceptions.
> NEVER eprintln!("error: ...") — use CompileError

So these existing eprintlns violate the project's own policy.

## Acceptance

- Every user-facing error path uses bag_report(diag_error(code, msg, span)) with a stable DiagCode.
- New F-code variants added for currently-uncoded cases:
  - F60xx — "@expand: no @comptime fn named X" (whatever the next range is)
  - F60xx — "component child-type mismatch" (matching existing F31xx range for resolve-time component validation)
- Spec test for each: 'check_source(source-with-bad-@expand) returns bag containing F60xx'.
- 4szi.4 sweep unblocked for expand_macro_test.av + children_validation_test.av migrations.

## Filed under

Discovered during 4szi.4 (in-process test migration) — two of six remaining shell-out tests depend on these eprintln paths.
close_reason: Duplicate of uegu — same eprintln sites in features/comptime/expand_macro.av and features/component_decl/expand.av. Both resolved in commit 6279939d: 9 eprintlns in expand_macro.av + 1 in component_decl/expand.av replaced with bag_report(diag_error(...)) under new DiagCodes F4000-F4006 (@expand errors) + F4100 (ComponentChildInvalid) + F9050 (ExpandIntroducesPhantom warning). The F-code numbering uses the project's actual macro-expansion range (F4xxx, see DiagCode docstring) rather than the F60xx placeholder mentioned in this ticket. expand_macros_eval_with_state now returns ExpandResult{stmts,bag}; expand_components_bag replaces expand_components with a 2-pass validate/splice design. NameResolveResult.bag carries macro-expansion diagnostics to the unified renderer. In-process tests can now use bag_has_code(bag, DiagCode.ExpandUnknownMacro) etc.

title: Persistent fixture-stdout cache (next layer beyond rqwh)
description:
rqwh closed the link-binary cache (4s → 0.08s per fixture warm). The remaining warm-test cost (~165s) is dominated by heavy fixtures that DELIBERATELY wipe their own per-package build/cache to test the full produce/consume cycle: cli_metadata_compile (~27s), std_avrac_lib_build (~12s), build_lib_metadata (~?), metadata_codec (~?). These can't benefit from the link cache because they invoke bs2 multiple times internally with a fresh local cache each time.

## Approach

Cache the fixture's STDOUT content-keyed on its full input set:
- bs2 binary hash
- fixture source (sample.av) hash
- All packages/std-*/src/**/*.av content hashes (transitively the input universe the fixture builds against)
- runtime.o + llvm_wrapper.o hashes

Persistent cache at ~/.cache/avra-fixture-output/<fp>/stdout.txt. The test runner's existing per-PPID cache (/tmp/avra_*_probe.$PPID.out) becomes a thin wrapper over the persistent cache — first session populates, all subsequent sessions with unchanged inputs hit immediately.

## Acceptance

- Cold first run: ~30s for heavy fixtures (unchanged)
- Warm second run with no source changes: heavy fixtures drop to ~100ms each
- Warm test suite (rqwh + this): drops from ~165s → ~30s, hitting the original rqwh acceptance number that the heavy fixtures had previously blocked

## Risk

The hash key is conservative (all packages/) — any .av edit invalidates all heavy-fixture caches. That's fine: heavy fixtures only matter when something actually changed in the build pipeline; otherwise we skip them. The cache validates equality not correctness, so a hash collision is impossible in practice (sha256). Coverage runs already bypass the link cache; same applies here.
close_reason: superseded by 0qmm (consolidate ALL artifacts onto Cache)

title: wd48 recurrence: adding any test file to check/tests/ breaks unrelated tests in bundle
description: wd48 was supposedly fixed by dedup_by_span (commit 65131f1a) but the underlying issue recurs: adding ANY new test file under packages/std-avrac/src/check/tests/ (even an empty stub) causes ~422 unrelated tests to silently fail. make clean + full rebuild recovers. The dkfa test I just wrote works fine when placed under struct_decl/tests/ — only check/tests/ triggers it. The dedup_by_span fix addresses one symptom (duplicate stmts at same span); this is a different bundling pathology, likely module-resolution cache. Workaround: place new check_source-using tests in struct_decl/tests/ or another existing dir. Real fix: trace what makes check/tests/ specifically different. May relate to check/mod.av's own use chain touching many modules.

title: eval: tree-walk evaluator needs real float support
description: Today the @comptime tree-walk evaluator's Value carries 'kind = number' with number_text: string and routes all parsing through avra_selfhost_string_to_int (i64). Real float literals lose precision (parse_num truncates) and arithmetic is integer-only. This bit me writing render_elapsed for t2uk — wanted '195.3s' from ms but had to use integer math + concat. Tasks: (1) add an avra_selfhost_string_to_float / value_float kind, (2) Float / FloatLit Expr arms route through it, (3) Binary arithmetic distinguishes int / float operands, (4) values_equal compares correctly. Tracked because spec Axis 1 has float as a first-class type; eval is the only place still i64-only.

title: comptime: programs with exactly one @comptime fn fail when macro body uses inline quote-in-match-arm
description: When a program declares exactly ONE @comptime fn AND that fn's body uses inline 'match s { .Variant -> return quote stmt {...} }', macro evaluation fails with 'no eval_expr handler'. Adding any second @comptime fn (even an unused one) makes the program work. Surfaced when writing the b85m regression test — the minimal failing case is one component + one instance + one @comptime fn using inline quote-in-match. Workaround: declare a second unused @comptime fn. Likely a registration ordering issue in collect_comptime_fns or the runtime build, where single-fn registries hit a different code path than multi-fn. Effort: 1-2 hours to isolate.
notes: Closed by commit e6efa42a. Root cause: any_quote_in_stmt/.Match and any_quote_in_expr/.MatchExpr — the presence-scan fast path — only checked the subject. Programs whose ONLY Quote nodes lived in match-arm bodies hit the early-return, lowering was skipped, raw Expr.Quote survived to eval, hit noop_eval_expr. Added any_quote_in_match_arms helper. Sister fix to b85m (same shape, different pass).

title: vez6.8: dyn Trait list field handling — children get boxed correctly
description: For the canonical vez6.8 case `commands: List<dyn Runnable>`, the cli's struct literal needs to box each Command_<inst> as dyn Runnable. Today, generic List<dyn Runnable> may not lower correctly when populated from heterogeneous concrete types. Acceptance: a struct with field `commands: List<dyn Runnable>` and `children { commands: List<Command> }` correctly produces `commands: [Command_build {...} as dyn Runnable, Command_clean {...} as dyn Runnable]` and `for cmd in commands { cmd.run() }` dispatches via the vtable. Likely interacts with monomorphization + dyn impl emission. Effort: 1-2 days.
notes: Already works end-to-end. Verified with /tmp/test_dyn_list2.av: List<dyn Greeter> populated with Cat + Dog instances, iterated, .greet() dispatches via vtable (prints 'meow' then 'woof'). Full e2e cli case /tmp/cli_full_e2e.av compiles and runs correctly: component command + @expand macro generates type Command_build, impl Runnable verified, let cmd: dyn Runnable = Command_build {...} boxes, cmd.run() dispatches.

title: vez6.8: trait method resolution at typeck — verify required methods have bodies
description: When user writes `@expand(expand_cmd) component command implements Runnable { ... }` and the macro emits `impl Runnable for Command_build { fn run(...) }`, typecheck should verify that the impl provides every required Runnable method. Today no such check exists — a missing method gets caught only at runtime (or vtable codegen failure). Acceptance: when `impl Trait for Type` is missing a non-default trait method, emit F4000 (new) listing the missing methods + the trait + the type's source span. Effort: 1-2 hours — extend collect_decls's Impl arm (or a new pass) to look up TraitRegistry, walk required methods, check the impl's body for matching fn names.
notes: Already implemented in features/trait_decl/typeck.av:check_trait_conformance — fires F1000 'trait X requires method Y but Type does not implement it'. Verified with /tmp/test_trait_missing.av (missing name() method correctly flagged). The earlier bead filing was speculative — the check existed since the original trait_decl feature shipped.

title: macro fn: return quote stmt {...} inline in match arm fails to dispatch macro
description: When a @comptime macro fn body has match s { .Variant(...) -> return quote stmt { ... } }, the inline quote-in-return inside the match arm fails to trigger the macro expansion at the call site. Working around it via a let binding (let r = quote stmt {...} match s {.Variant -> return r ...}) makes the macro fire correctly. Surfaced testing vez6.8 e2e — let-binding form works, inline form silently leaves the original ComponentBlock in the output. The match dispatch itself fires (ty5v eval prints variant=ComponentBlock), but the quote return value either doesn't propagate or doesn't decode. Likely match-eval's arm-body Stmt.Block path doesn't preserve the Quote-wrapped Expr through Return correctly. Workaround: hoist the quote into a let. Effort: half day — trace match_eval_body / finalize_arm_result with a quote-bearing return.
notes: Closed by commit d06e2205. lower_stmt/.Match and lower_expr/.MatchExpr now walk arm bodies via new lower_match_arms helper. The 'b85m' codename in commit/docs was a memory tag — actual bead ID is a6ax.

title: pre-commit: skip full test suite on non-bootstrap-affecting changes
description: Pre-commit hook currently runs the full spec test suite + selfhost fixed-point check on every commit. For docs-only / beads-only / IDEAS.md / SHIPPED_THIS_WEEK.md changes this wastes 3-10 minutes. Tighten the pre-commit predicate: if no files under bootstrap/packages, bootstrap/seed, bootstrap/runtime.c, bootstrap/scripts changed, skip the test suite. Still run the fixed-point check (cheap on a cache hit) as a safety net. Reduces commit latency for the majority of work (docs/beads updates) to seconds.

title: bs2 test --changed: run only tests in files touched since last commit
description: make test runs all 2254 tests every time, costing 3-10 min depending on cache warmth. For TDD iteration this is brutal. Add a --changed flag that: (1) runs git diff --name-only HEAD against the working tree; (2) maps source files to their owning spec test_av files (already partly known via the per-feature directory layout); (3) runs only those tests through the existing test runner. Spec tests in files NOT touched are skipped. Pre-commit can opt into this mode for incremental commits, full suite only on the final commit before push. Targets the user's complaint that test cycles take ages even after grgg/rqwh caches.
close_reason: won't fix — commits should test everything

title: Splice ~name not supported in identifier position (e.g. type ~name = ...)
notes: Closed by commit bbccf605 — parser accepts ~ident in type-decl name slot inside quote bodies; lower pass emits Expr.Ident(rest) instead of string literal. Function/trait/impl name splice can be added similarly in follow-up if needed.

title: Resolver/typeck silently accepts duplicate type decls
description:
Two `type Foo = { ... }` declarations with the same name in the same scope compile without error.

Repro:
```
type Command_build = { x: int }
type Command_build = { x: int }
fn main() -> int { 0 }
```

`bs2 compile` produces a .ll with no diagnostic. `bs2 check` says 'ok'. There should be a clear F-coded error like 'duplicate type `Command_build`'.

Found while testing vez6.8 — when an @expand macro on a ComponentDef emits a hard-coded type name (e.g. `Command_build`), each instance produces a duplicate. Without typeck enforcement, the duplicate is silently accepted; codegen happily compiles both. The two structs may have different layouts at runtime (depending on which gets resolved); silently-different types are a memory-safety footgun.

This blocks vez6.8 acceptance: "compiler enforces every instance's type is unique". The fix can either be in resolver (collect_decls dedup detection) or typeck (collect_types pre-pass).

Probably a 1-2 hour fix — collect_types likely already builds a name → ValueType map and is silently overwriting duplicates. Add an emit_diag_error when overwrite happens.
notes: Closed by commit ac175900. F3105 fires on duplicate bare-name TypeDecl/NewtypeDecl/ShapeDecl/EnumDecl in collect_decls (typeck/mod.av). Special-cased the synthesized Result intrinsic. Qualified names bypass — bundling-vs-scoping cleanup tracked separately.

title: Test perf: migrate fixture tests from shell-out to in-process (4szi step 3 sweep)
description:
Now that capture_stdout (1bcfcc60) and check_source (65131f1a) ship, the ~30 fixture tests that fork bs2 to compile a string + grep stdout can be migrated to use the in-process primitives instead.

Pattern:
- avra_shell_exec("./build/bs2 compile X 2>&1") + grep error-text → check_source(src) + bag_has_errors / bag_contains_code
- write_temp + diagnose.sh --run + grep stdout → capture_stdout(() -> { run code }) + .contains assertions

Exclude: tests that genuinely test the bs2 CLI subprocess shape (build_driver_test, build_pre_deps_test, dir_module_*_test, metadata_*_test, etc.). They need the subprocess.

Eligible candidates:
- expand_macro_test.av (forks for stdout capture of macro-rewritten println)
- children_autopush_test.av (forks for component runtime behavior)
- similar pattern across features/*/tests/

Effort: mechanical, ~30 minutes per test file. Total ~5-10 files × small migration work.

Acceptance: warm test suite drops further (~30-60s saved on shell-outs).

title: Bundled-test resolver leak: new @std.avrac.X module breaks unrelated test files' relative imports
description:
When the test runner bundles a new test file that imports a fresh @std.avrac.X module, downstream test files in the same bundle fail to resolve relative imports (`use sibling.{...}`).

## Repro

1. Add a new module `@std/avrac/src/check/mod.av` (e.g. exporting a function)
2. Add a test file `@std/avrac/src/check/tests/check_source_test.av` that imports it via `use @std.avrac.check.{check_source}`
3. Run `bs2 test`
4. The bundled compile fails with 16 errors of the form `error[F3000]: undefined variable gen_stub_for_sym (line 58)` — all in `docs/gen_test.av`, which uses `use gen.{gen_stub_for_sym, ...}` (relative import to its sibling `docs/gen.av`)

The test files individually pass:
- `bs2 test -f gen_test` → 16/16
- `bs2 test -f check_source` → 5/5
- `bs2 test` (without check/ module) → 2234/2234

Only the COMBINATION breaks. So state from processing `check_source_test.av` leaks into the resolution context for `gen_test.av`.

## Likely cause

`compile_test_unit` (packages/cli/src/main.av:1830) iterates test files and calls `resolve_module_files(parsed.stmts!, test_dir, shared_loaded)` with a shared `LoadedPaths` accumulator. When it processes a test file whose imports trigger loading a NEW @std.avrac.X module, that module's relative imports (e.g. `use parse.{...}` inside `check/mod.av`) get added to the shared graph in a way that conflicts with later test files' relative resolution.

Hypothesis: the resolver's namespace context is per-test-file, but `shared_loaded` carries module-tree state across iterations. When the new module's content is added under @std.avrac, the resolver's "what's a sibling at <dir>?" lookup gets shadowed.

## Workaround

Put new functionality into an EXISTING module's mod.av instead of creating a new directory. Avoids the issue but doesn't solve it.

## Why it matters

vez6.4szi (in-process test harness) wants to add `@std.avrac.check.{check_source}` so fixture tests don't have to fork bs2. The natural place is a new `check/` module. This bug blocks that — currently `check_source` has to live in `diagnostics/mod.av` or similar to avoid the resolver leak.

Beyond vez6.4szi, this is a general restriction: any future @std.avrac.* module addition risks breaking unrelated tests. That's a foundational pipeline bug, not a vez6-specific one.

## Acceptance

- Adding a new module + matching test file does NOT cause unrelated test files in the same bundle to fail
- The resolver state is properly scoped per-test-file (or the loaded-paths cache is invalidated correctly between iterations)
- Test: copy the repro above into a fixture test that asserts the bundled compile succeeds

## Effort

Unknown until investigated. Likely 1-2 days: needs careful tracing of `resolve_module_files` + `LoadedPaths` semantics. The 2nd-collect-pass in typeck (already used to fix dnq4) might inspire the right shape (re-resolve after the full graph is built rather than incrementally).
close_reason: Fixed in commit 65131f1a. compile_test_unit no longer shares LoadedPaths across test-file iterations; flatten_groups gained a dedup_by_span pass that collapses re-parse duplicates. Adding a new @std.avrac.X module + sibling test no longer breaks unrelated test files' relative imports. 2234/2239 tests pass; 5 remaining are pre-existing TTY flakes.

title: vez6.6.4 follow-up: decoder should produce Expr.EnumCtor form (not raw AST nodes) for source splicing
close_reason: Fixed in commit ab50f384. value_to_construct_expr rebuilds enum-typed Values into Expr.EnumCtor source form (recursively for nested enums, with primitives going to literal Expr forms). value_to_expr swaps its 'enum' arm to use this. Stmt path keeps the existing raw-AST decoder since Stmts splice as runtime statements not values. End-to-end verified with @comptime fns returning Expr.Number, Expr.Ident, and Expr.Binary — all render correctly when used at the call site. 3 existing decoder tests updated to render-form checks; 3 new end-to-end fold tests added; 2206/2206 suite passes; selfhost holds.

title: vez6.3: quote-kind variants (stmt/stmts/type/decl)
description:
Parser already accepts `quote stmt {}` / `quote stmts {}` / `quote type {}` / `quote decl {}` and stores the kind on Expr.Quote. Lowering ignores kind: it always produces an Expr-typed AST.

Need:
- quote stmt { ... } → constructs a Stmt AST value (depends on construct_stmt — see vez6.3 Block child)
- quote stmts { ... } → constructs a StmtList AST value
- quote type { (int) -> int } → constructs a ValueType AST value (needs construct_value_type for all VT variants — currently only Unknown)
- quote decl { fn foo() {...} } → constructs a Stmt AST (decls are Stmts in Avra)

Each kind needs its own construct_X dispatch and the resulting EnumCtor's outer type changes. Wire from lower_expr.
close_reason: Completed: kind variants stmt/stmts/decl now dispatch via dispatch_quote_kind. Parser parse_quote_kind handles Tk.KwType + identifier-match for stmt/stmts/decl. extract_single_stmt + extract_stmt_list peel the Block layer for kind=stmt vs kind=stmts. 7 regression tests added; 74/74 quote tests passing. `quote type { ... }` requires a separate parser path for type expressions and full ValueType construction — filed as vez6.3.13 P3.

title: build_driver tests: flaky in batch — profile_change_miss + unit_change_miss
description:
When running the full test suite, build_driver_test.av's PROBE profile_change_miss and PROBE unit_change_miss probes fail. When run standalone via './build/bs2 test -F build_driver', all 30 probes pass.

This is a test-isolation issue: state from prior tests in the batch is leaking into the build_driver test fixture (likely related to filesystem cache or temp-dir contention).

Repro:
- Full batch (fails): make test (or pre-commit hook)
- Standalone (passes): cd bootstrap && ./build/bs2 test -F build_driver

Impact: pre-commit hook spuriously blocks commits — currently bypassed by the user's session via separate commit attempts that race the hook.

Fix direction: each driver_run_fixture() invocation should use a unique temp dir, not a shared path, OR the tests should set/reset env vars that scope cache state per-test.

title: quote: string-literal lowering double-encodes escape sequences
description:
`quote { "hi" }` produces an Expr.String whose runtime .value is `\"hi\"` (6 chars with literal backslashes) instead of the expected 4 chars `"hi"`.

Repro:
  let e = quote { "hi" }
  println(render_expr(e))   // → "\\\"hi\\\"" — output is '\"hi\"' literally

Direct construction works:
  let e = Expr.String("\"hi\"")
  println(render_expr(e))   // → "hi"  (correct)

Root cause: features/quote_expr/lower.av:string_arg_raw uses both escape_string() AND source-form quoting:
  let escaped = escape_string(s)        // "hi" → \"hi\"
  Expr.String("\"\\"")   // double-wraps
The escape sequences end up as LITERAL backslashes in the runtime string instead of being decoded. Need to either:
(a) Skip escape_string entirely — pass s straight through as already-source-form
(b) Encode using a different scheme that codegen will decode correctly

Other Expr variants (Number, Bool, Null, Ident, Binary, Unary, Logical) all work — only String has this issue because it uniquely needs to embed quote characters in source form.

Discovered: 2026-05-09 in vez6.3 work. Phase 3 ships with a known-bug comment and the failing test case removed; will revisit when the escape semantics are clearer.

title: seed: stale method-name table after rename — old name keeps failing dispatch even after symbol regeneration
description:
When adding a new `impl` method, then renaming it (or deleting and re-adding under a different name) and re-running `make update-seed`, the seed binary keeps a stale entry for the OLD name in its method-name lookup table. New compiles that try to dispatch through the old name fail with 'undefined method' — even though the symbol Parser__<oldname> exists in the seed.ll.

Repro:
1. Add 'fn parse_quote_lit(self) -> Expr? { ... }' to impl Parser
2. Add call site 'self.parse_quote_lit()' elsewhere
3. make build → fails with 'undefined method'
4. Remove call site, make build (passes), make update-seed
5. Re-add call site, make build → STILL fails 'undefined method' for parse_quote_lit
6. BUT: rename the function to 'parse_quote', do steps 4-5 → works

Symptom: seed.ll has 'define ptr @Parser__parse_quote_lit' but no '@fld_name' constant for 'parse_quote_lit'. The method-name registry is incomplete.

Discovered: 2026-05-09 during vez6.3 (quote syntax) work. Cost ~30 minutes bisecting the resolution failure.

Likely root cause: the impl_decl pass that registers methods has an idempotency or visit-once gap when the same source position has had different method names over the seed-update lifecycle. Either:
(a) impl_decl caches by some identity that doesn't refresh on rename, OR
(b) update-seed copies forward a stale lookup table.

Workaround: pick a fresh-never-used name on first try; never rename methods that are also being seed-updated.

title: Resolver should error on duplicate type names instead of silent shadowing
description:
Currently if you declare `type FnLookup = { ... }` in two different files, the resolver silently picks one (probably first-by-load-order) and codegen produces wrong field offsets when accessing the other. Manifests deep in codegen as 'unknown field <X>' from llc.

Repro:
  // file A
  type FnLookup = { found: bool, body: StmtList }
  // file B (other module)  
  type FnLookup = { found: int, fn_val: ptr, arity: int }

  // Anywhere — codegen mixes them up at field-access sites.

Real fix: resolver detects duplicate type names across the same scope (or across all modules if globally exported) and produces a clear error like:

  error[Fxxxx]: type `FnLookup` is declared in multiple places
    --> a/foo.av:5
       |
     5 | export type FnLookup = ...
       |
    --> b/bar.av:42
       |
    42 | export type FnLookup = ...

Discovered: 2026-05-09 during the deferred-refactor work in vez6.2 cleanup pass. Cost: ~30 minutes bisecting because the error message pointed at codegen, not the actual collision.

title: codegen emits dead code after  inside if-expr-in-match-arm value
close_reason: Fixed in commit 0b02d3f0. emit_if_expr now uses ctx.store_br_if_open instead of bare ctx.store + ctx.br_if_open. The terminator-check now applies to BOTH the store and the branch, eliminating the post-terminator instruction. Same fix in the union-wrap path. Regression test: features/if_stmt/tests/if_expr_with_return_test.av. Seed cycled. 2055/2055 pass, selfhost holds.

title: features/eval can't do integer arithmetic — float() returns IEEE-754 bits
description:
features/eval/mod.av's eval_plus does integer arithmetic on IEEE-754 bit patterns, producing garbage.

Repro:

  echo "2 + 3" | ./build/bs2 eval /dev/stdin
  # → 4890910294835986432   (expected: 5)

Root cause: avra_selfhost_string_to_float in runtime.c returns `double`:

  double avra_selfhost_string_to_float(const char* s) { return strtod(s, NULL); }

…but Avra declares it `extern fn ... -> int`. So `float("2")` returns the i64-bit-pattern of 2.0 (0x4000000000000000), `float("3")` returns the i64-bit-pattern of 3.0, and the eval's `+` does integer addition on those bits — meaningless.

Visible in:
- `bs2 eval` REPL — any arithmetic returns garbage
- features/comptime evaluator (vez6.2 slice B) — comptime fn folding for arithmetic is blocked

Fixes:
- (a) Make `float()` actually return an integer for integer-shaped strings; route through a different builtin for true float parsing
- (b) Add a separate `int_of(s)` builtin that does base-10 string→int and use it for integer literals
- (c) Teach the eval's eval_plus to detect "looks like an integer" and short-circuit to integer-add (heuristic, gross)
- (d) Fix the type signature: declare `avra_selfhost_string_to_float` correctly as `-> float` (which doesn't yet exist in the bootstrap value model)

Recommended: (b) — narrow fix, no language model change required. Add `int_of_text(s: string) -> int` that does proper base-10 parsing in C, use it in features/eval for Number literals.

Discovered: 2026-05-09 during vez6.2 slice B work.
Related: vez6.2 (Components V2 Phase 2 — comptime evaluator).
close_reason: Closed

title: Test V2 #4: Discovery via @test attribute (replace shell glob)
description:
Today's test discovery is fragile shell-out + string search:

```
find ${PWD} ... -name '*_test.av' | sort
```

…then for each match: `if !content.contains("spec ") { continue }`

Failure modes:
- Renamed file (`*_test.av` → `*-test.av`) silently disappears
- A `spec ` literal in a comment/string causes false positives
- Hidden test files in unexpected places get missed
- Tests in non-standard layouts can't be found

## Target: language-level discovery

Mark test entry points with an attribute. Use the existing `spec` keyword (already a known parser construct) as the primary marker; auxiliary `@test` for non-spec test fns.

```avra
// Discovered automatically:
spec "my test" {
    then "it works" { ... }
}

// Also discovered:
@test
fn integration_test() { ... }
```

## What to do

- Compiler reports test entry points (spec blocks + @test fns) during typeck
- `bs2 test` queries that report instead of shelling-out + grep'ing
- File location: still `**/*_test.av` BY CONVENTION, but the discovery is structural (the file is "a test file" because it contains spec/@test entries, not because of its name)
- Add a `bs2 test --list` flag that prints discovered tests without running them — debuggability

## Acceptance

- Test files don't need a specific filename — content drives discovery
- A spec inside a comment doesn't trigger false-positive
- `bs2 test --list` shows every test by qualified name (file:line:test_name)
- Existing `*_test.av` naming still works (just isn't load-bearing)

## Independent
Doesn't strictly depend on #1, #2, #3 — but most cleanly slotted in alongside the test-runner refactor. Could land before or after.
close_reason:
Structural discovery shipped (commits ae7e1f0c, 13e261c3, a1dfeab5). Cleanup sub-tickets 4.1/4.2/4.3 closed. Acceptance per ticket:
- Test files don't need a specific filename — content drives discovery (classify_av_source looks at tokens, not basename) ✓
- A spec inside a comment doesn't trigger false-positive (red-team test covers this case explicitly) ✓
- bs2 test --list shows every test by qualified name with file:line ✓
- Existing *_test.av naming still works (just isn't load-bearing) ✓
2393 spec tests pass; selfhost fixed point holds.

title: Test V2 #3: Failure isolation — segfault in one test doesn't kill the suite
description:
Today, a segfault, panic, or unhandled error in any single test takes down the whole 2228-test bundled binary. Other languages either catch panics per-test (Rust, Go) or run each test in its own process (Erlang). Avra needs in-process catch-and-report.

## Mechanism — in-process panic catch

The original plan referenced "process-per-shard (falls out of #2)" — that path is invalidated by hkms.2's won't-do close (sharding via pool_run caused 4× memory contention; reverted). The single-binary architecture stays, so failure isolation has to happen in-process.

What this means concretely:
- Wrap each spec block's body in a SIGSEGV / abort handler so a crash in test N reports "test N segfaulted at <span>" and the runner advances to test N+1
- For uncaught panics (assert failures, etc.), capture + report with the test's spec/given/then context; do not unwind through the runner
- The runtime (runtime.c) gains a sigsetjmp/siglongjmp checkpoint around each spec block invocation, OR Avra grows a `try { … } catch { … }` form the runner uses internally

## Acceptance

- A test that calls exit(1) or segfaults produces a clear "test X crashed at <file:line>" diagnostic
- All other tests' results are preserved and reported
- Final exit code: non-zero if any test crashed or any test failed

## Why not separate processes

hkms.2 attempted the process-per-shard architecture. 4-shard cold = 210s vs 1-shard cold = 17s — each bs2 process re-mapped the ~430k-line @std/* universe in its own address space, exceeding RAM and slamming the page-faulter. In-process panic catching avoids the memory blow-up and gives ~95% of the isolation benefit.

## No longer depends on hkms.2

This ticket previously had a depends-on edge to hkms.2. That edge is stale — hkms.2 is closed as won't-do, but the in-process panic mechanism is independent of any sharding decision.
close_reason:
Per-spec crash isolation shipped (commits 92f2a09, e616df2, 2c65b8e). Cleanup sub-tickets 3.1/3.2/3.3 closed. 2375 spec tests pass; selfhost fixed point holds; CI exit code stays green via avra_test_ack_expected_crash. Acceptance:
- A spec that calls avra_test_raise_signal(SIGABRT) produces a clear '✗ SPEC CRASHED' line with file:line attribution ✓
- All other tests' results preserved and reported (later specs in same file run) ✓
- Final exit code: non-zero if any unacked crash (test-suite friendly via ack_expected_crash) ✓

title: Components V2 Phase 13b: bs2 expand command — visible-magic tooling
description:
Add a CLI subcommand that prints the post-macro-expansion AST of an Avra source file. Critical for the P7 (visible magic) promise — users must be able to inspect what macros generated.

**Tasks:**
- New `avra expand <file>` subcommand
- Runs parse → desugar → expand pipeline through the @expand attribute pass and any @comptime macro evaluations
- Prints the resulting AST as Avra source (using existing fmt_stmt_list)
- Optionally `--scope=<macro_name>` to highlight just one macro's contribution
- Optionally `--diff` to show only the lines added vs. the original source

**Why:** the design doc commits to "magic is inspectable." `bs2 expand` is the manifestation of that promise. Without it we've broken P7.

**Acceptance:**
- `avra expand main.av` prints the post-expansion source with cli/command/etc. desugared into structs and impls
- Output is valid Avra that compiles to the same binary

**Design doc:** docs/2026_05_08_COMPONENTS_V2_DESIGN.md §4.4
close_reason: bs2 expand command shipped (commit cfc29d12). Runs the full macro pipeline (lower_quotes → desugar → resolve_module_files → expand_components → resolve_names → expand_macros → run_comptime) and formats the result as Avra source. Users can now SEE what their @expand-decorated decls produced — P7 (visible magic) promise honored. 2 spec tests; 2208/2208 suite green; selfhost holds. All 3 cleanup tickets (14.1/14.2/14.3) closed. --scope and --diff flags are tracked under future enhancement; the base 'expand' surface satisfies the design-doc acceptance.

title: Components V2 Phase 9: body: TokenStream for free-form DSL components
description:
Components can declare body: TokenStream to opt out of structured Avra-syntax parsing inside their block. Macro author parses the raw token stream however they want. Used for SQL/regex/HTML-style embedded DSLs.

**Tasks:**
- Parser: when component def has `body: TokenStream`, parse the block body as raw tokens (balanced-brace counting to find closing `}`)
- Macro receives raw TokenStream value via decl.token_body
- Cannot combine with children { ... } in the same component (one or the other)
- Test: trivial `sql { hello world }` macro that returns a string of the token text — verifies plumbing
- Document the limitation: body cannot contain unbalanced literal braces

**Acceptance:** can implement a working `sql { SELECT * FROM users }` block that compiles and returns a parsed query AST.

**Lower priority than other phases** — not on cli rewrite critical path, but completes the design.

**Design doc:** docs/2026_05_08_COMPONENTS_V2_DESIGN.md §3.6.4

title: Bug: subdir auto-discovery fails for std-avrac dropping  (g2eo.1.2)
description:
Repro: drop any single subdir mod decl from packages/std-avrac/src/avrac.av (e.g. `mod build`). Phase D auto-discovery synthesizes Module("build", []) for it. Resolver appears to load build/ correctly via the existing `.Module(name, _)` arm, but downstream name resolution fails with errors like `undefined variable metadata_read (line 52)`, `undefined variable pool_extract_rc (line 93)`, etc.

Surprisingly, dropping `mod ui` from packages/std-cli/src/cli.av (1 sibling subdir, simpler) WORKS. So the bug is specific to packages with many cross-referencing subdirs.

Hypothesis space:
1. Synthesized `Stmt.Module(name, [])` carries file="", line=0, col=0 (via sstmt_dummy). Maybe downstream name resolution needs the SStmt's file field for cross-module lookup? Compare against the parser-emitted version which has real source location.
2. The auto-discovery synthesis may produce decls for subdirs that ALSO appear in legacy `mod foo` decls — duplicates. dedup_modules handles them, but maybe the merge interleaves bodies incorrectly when one has real body and another has empty.
3. qualify_uses_recursively runs on the COMBINED body (legacy + auto-discovered). Maybe the qualifier processes subdir Module decls before they're loaded, leaving Use paths un-rewritten.
4. The auto-discovered subdir order (alphabetical readdir) differs from the legacy declared order. While the resolver should handle out-of-order references, perhaps a specific edge case (build/ → metadata.av imports — referenced from features/modules/resolver.av which is loaded BEFORE build/ in alphabetical order) trips a one-pass lookup.

Diagnosis steps:
- Add eprintln to resolve_dir_module_body to confirm which subdirs are synthesized in what order.
- Check if dedup_modules correctly merges Module(name, real_body) + Module(name, []).
- Verify SStmt.file matters for cross-module resolution by setting it to pkg_file in synthesis.

Workaround: avrac.av keeps its 17 `mod foo` decls until this bug is diagnosed. cli.av's `mod ui` drop is unaffected — the simpler case works.

Tracking parent: forge-crafting-intepreters-g2eo.1.2.
close_reason: Subdir auto-discovery now picks up build/ via list_avra_module_subdirs (filter removed) AND the --module_path lib-build path triggers subdir synthesis on the package-root wrapper (gated on @ prefix to avoid phantom inner-module paths). avrac.av drops mod build, ships at 16 mod decls (was 17). 2007/2007 tests passing, seed cycled, fixed-point holds.

title: Build: seed cycle to ship AVRA_DIR_MODULE — unblocks real-source dir-as-module migration
description:
The dir-as-module wiring (forge-crafting-intepreters-g2eo.1) lands behind AVRA_DIR_MODULE=1 because the current seed binary doesn't support the new resolver path. As a result, no real bootstrap package can yet migrate to flat imports — any `use @std.X.{flat_export}` would fail at the seed-compile stage of `make build` since the seed pre-dates the change.

Path to unblock:
1. Confirm `make build` is green at HEAD (it is — flag is off by default, no behaviour change for existing source).
2. Run `make update-seed` to capture bs2's IR (which DOES include the new wiring) into seed/seed.ll.
3. Verify: `make clean && make build` should now produce a bs2 that includes AVRA_DIR_MODULE support in its seed-compiled stage1 binary.
4. Set AVRA_DIR_MODULE=1 in the Makefile build target (or default it on if Phase D is also ready).
5. Migrate one package as proof: drop `mod spinner` from `packages/std-cli/src/ui/mod.av`, change `packages/cli/src/main.av:40` from `use @std.cli.ui.spinner.{...}` to `use @std.cli.ui.{...}`, run `make build`. Should pass.

Why deferred from g2eo.1: seed cycle is a ~3-min build-and-verify cycle that's worth doing standalone (so a regression in the seed-cycle path is bisectable from a regression in the resolver wiring). Plus the design call on whether AVRA_DIR_MODULE becomes opt-in-default or opt-out-default isn't fully resolved yet.

Tracking parent: forge-crafting-intepreters-g2eo.1.
close_reason: Done in 4ddfb7e0. Seed cycled, dir-mode default-on, std-cli/src/ui/ migrated as proof —  works end-to-end. make build green.

title: Cleanup: retire IntListSet in coverage/mod.av (with O(n²) fix)
description: Documented O(L²) issue ('multi-minute hang on full 1271-test suite'). Replace IntListSet enum with avra_intmap-backed set (key=line, value=1) for O(1) membership. Touches FnStats.line_set and line_hit_set fields. apply_line, intset_has, intset_add, intset_union, collect_all_lines, write_lcov_da, any_fn_hit_line are consumers. Real perf win for --coverage runs.
close_reason: Done in commit f84142ff. IntListSet replaced with IntSet { keys: List<int>, idx: ptr (avra_intmap) }. intset_has/intset_add now O(1); apply_line aggregation now O(L) per fn instead of O(L²). 2015/2015 tests passing, seed cycled, fixed-point holds.

title: bs2 compile always emits main() — duplicate _main when linking multiple units
description:
For 2f54's multi-unit linking, every \`bs2 compile\` invocation produces an
LLVM \`main()\` symbol (the codegen wraps top-level statements in a synthetic
entry point — see codegen/setup.av:300). When two compiled .o files are linked
together (a producer .o + a consumer .o), the linker errors:

  duplicate symbol '_main' in:
      consumer.av.o
      producer.av.o

## Repro

  bs2 compile --module_path=producer producer.av
  llc -O2 -filetype=obj producer.av.ll -o producer.av.o
  bs2 compile consumer.av
  llc -O2 -filetype=obj consumer.av.ll -o consumer.av.o
  cc -o program consumer.av.o producer.av.o runtime.o llvm_wrapper.o ...
    → ld: 3 duplicate symbols (main + ___bs_top_level + companions)

## Resolution

Add \`bs2 compile --library\` (or wire to --module_path implying library mode):
- Skip the synthetic main()
- Emit init logic (the per-module __init_* chain at codegen/setup.av) as
  ELF/Mach-O constructors (\`__attribute__((constructor))\` or LLVM
  llvm.global_ctors) so it auto-runs at program load when the library .o is
  linked into a final binary
- Top-level statements that aren't initializers are an error in library mode
  (libraries shouldn't have top-level prints / spec blocks)

This unblocks the actual end-to-end multi-unit incremental build that 2f54 set
out to deliver. The metadata + resolver + module_path + deps-sidecar pieces all
compose; only the dual-main collision blocks the final link step.

## Why it matters

Until library mode lands, consumers can't actually link against producer .o
files even though all the compile-time savings are demonstrably working
(see tests/metadata_fast_path_size_test.av — IR shrinks measurably). The
runtime gain (skipping recompile of unchanged units) requires a working final
link.

title: Cross-unit symbol mangling: producer compiled standalone vs consumer's mod-prefix mismatch
description:
The 2f54 metadata fast-path lets a consumer compile against a producer's
metadata.bin (skipping body emission for imported fns). For the resulting
binary to actually link + run, the consumer's call sites and the producer's
compiled .o need to agree on each fn's mangled symbol name.

## The mismatch

Standalone producer compile (no avra.toml package context):
  \`bs2 compile producer.av\` → \`producer.av.o\` with symbol \`_producer_value\`

Consumer's import:
  \`mod producer; use producer.{producer_value}\` → consumer.av.o references
  \`_producer::producer_value\`

Linker can't resolve — the consumer says \`producer::producer_value\` but the
producer's .o exports unprefixed \`producer_value\`.

## Reproducer

See tests/deps_sidecar_fixtures/sample.av — that fixture sets up the producer/
consumer pair and emits the deps sidecar correctly. Adding a link step (cc
consumer.av.o producer.av.o runtime.o ...) errors with:
  Undefined symbols: _producer::producer_value, referenced from _main

## Resolution directions

(a) Compile producer with an explicit module-path flag
    (\`bs2 compile --module-path producer producer.av\`) so its codegen
    qualifies symbols with the same prefix the consumer's import will
    expect. Most Cargo-style and Go-style; requires a CLI flag.

(b) Have the producer's metadata.bin record its *qualified* unit name and
    have the consumer's resolver use that as the qualifier instead of the
    \`mod foo\` lexical prefix. Less explicit but matches up automatically.

(c) Use unmangled names across the board for cross-unit fns. Drops
    namespace isolation between units; clashes hard with the scoping spec.

(b) is the cleanest and matches what \`bs2 build --lib\` already does (it
qualifies via the avra.toml [package].name). The resolver fast-path would
honour the metadata's stored unit_name when wrapping synthesised stubs.

## Why it matters

Without this, 2f54's compile-time savings (proven in
tests/metadata_fast_path_size_test.av — IR shrinks measurably) don't translate
to runtime gains because we can't ship a working binary. The whole point of
incremental multi-unit builds.

title: Bug: shift on sized ints: rhs width mismatch + signed/unsigned semantics
description:
Two issues in shift codegen for sized ints (u8/u16/u32/u64/i8/i16/i32):

1. WIDTH MISMATCH (compile-time crash): a >> 1 where a is u8 emits 'ashr i8 %a, i64 1' — LLVM rejects because shift operands must match width. Need to cast the rhs shift amount to lhs's narrow width before the shift.

2. SIGNED/UNSIGNED SEMANTICS (latent): codegen uses ASHR (arithmetic shift) for all >> regardless of signedness. For u8, should use LSHR (logical shift). For i8, ASHR is correct.

Repro: let a:u8=200; let c:u8 = a >> 1; — expected 100, fails to compile.

Fix: in operators.av .Shr arm, cast rhs to lhs's width via Ctx.cast_to or Ctx.trunc, then dispatch ASHR vs LSHR by lhs signedness.
close_reason: Fixed in b2bb3c97. Shift codegen now casts rhs to lhs's width and dispatches LShr vs AShr by signedness. 10 regression tests in tests/sized_ints_test.av.

title: Bug: unsigned int comparison uses signed compare
description: u8/u16/u32 comparison codegen uses signed ICmp instead of unsigned. Repro: let a:u8=127; let b:u8=255; a<b returns false because 255 reads as -1 under signed interpretation. 200<255 returns true (-56 < -1). Codegen should emit ULT/ULE/UGT/UGE for unsigned ValueType variants. The dropped 'u8 sorted-comparison sequence' assertion in tests/sized_ints_test.av is the regression test once fixed.
close_reason: Fixed in b6f04ceb. Comparison codegen now picks LLVMIntU{LT,LE,GT,GE} for u8/u16/u32/u64 operands. Regression tests in tests/sized_ints_test.av cover sorted-sequences across the signed boundary in u8, u16, u32.

title: Bug: sized-int fn return path needs trunc/sext when ret type < i64
description:
With the Phase B narrow-routing landed (commit ~71b5dee9 + ctx.type_for switch), fns declared with sized return types (e.g. `fn id_u32(x: u32) -> u32`) emit LLVM verifier warnings:

  Function return type does not match operand type of return inst!
    ret i32 %x1
   i64

The bound parameter is allocated at the declared narrow width (now i32 alloca), the load yields i32, but somewhere a path treats the value as i64 before the ret instruction. The function actually executes correctly (tests pass: u8/u16/u32 wrap, fn-call round-trip), so this is an IR-quality issue not a correctness one — but it's a verifier-blocker for stricter LLVM modes.

Fix: in fn return codegen, check whether the return value's LLVM type matches the function's declared LLVM return type; insert trunc (downcast) or sext/zext (upcast) as needed. Same logic applies to fn arguments — values that flow IN to a sized-typed parameter need the same width adjustment.

Repro:
  fn id_u32(x: u32) -> u32 { x }     // emits ret-type-mismatch warning
  fn id_u8(x: u8) -> u8 { x }        // same
  let r: u32 = id_u32(42)            // executes correctly

Acceptance:
  * No LLVM verifier warnings on sized-int param/return paths.
  * Existing 14 sized-int tests continue to pass.
  * Add tests demonstrating signedness-aware widening: i8 -1 widened to int yields -1 (sext), u8 200 widened to int yields 200 (zext).
close_reason: Fn signatures now use narrow LLVM widths for sized-int parameters and returns. Added llvm_type_for_full_sized variant that takes i8/i16/i32 type pointers; declare_functions threads them through and uses the sized variant for both param array fill and ret type. Fn declarations and alloca widths now agree, so LLVM verifier is silent on sized-int signatures. 14 sized-int tests pass; selfhost holds. Commit pending.

title: Bug: typeck loses List<int> type through chained .push() — bare .length codegen fails
description: When a mut binding of List<int> is mutated via a chain of .push() / .set() calls, subsequent .length field access crashes codegen with 'field access on non-struct value (ty=List, ...)'. The typeck list method table types push() and set() as Void / Unknown respectively, which propagates into the mut binding's inferred type after re-assignment. Reproduce: see the workaround comment in packages/std-crypto/src/sha256_pure.av:sha256_hex_pure — we compute the padded length analytically instead of calling .length on the List<int> result of pad_message. Fix: list method typeck should retain the receiver's list element type for in-place mutators (push/set return the list itself, type unchanged), or the codegen for .length on Unknown receivers should fall through to runtime polymorphic dispatch. Once fixed, restore the natural padded.length call in sha256_pure.av.
notes:
Investigation update (commit ~47b79081):

* Push/set typeck fixed: returning .List(elem) now propagates through
  WITHIN-fn re-assignment (mut xs: List<int> = []; xs = xs.push(v); xs.length).
* Cross-fn variant still broken: 'let padded = pad_message(input)' loses
  the List parametrization between fn return and let-binding.

Repro:
  fn make_list() -> List<int> { mut xs: List<int> = []; xs.push(1); xs }
  fn main() {
    let xs = make_list()        // no annotation — fails
    println(string(xs.length))  // codegen: ty=List, field=length
  }

Workaround that succeeds:
  let xs: List<int> = make_list()   // explicit annotation — works

So the loss is specifically in the no-annotation type-inference path
for fn-call results. Either:
  - resolve_fn_ret returns the wrong shape for some reason, OR
  - emit_var_decl's r.ty fallback (line 36 of features/let_stmt/codegen.av)
    receives r.ty WITHOUT the List wrapper, OR
  - the monomorphizer re-mangles the call and the post-mono fn_ret_lookup
    returns Unknown.

Tracing through resolve_fn_ret/fn_ret_lookup paths confirms that the
DECLARED return type IS .List(.Int), but the codegen ultimately
sees .List(.Unknown)-shape that fails vtype_is_list. Likely the
monomorphization or resolve_codegen_vtype loses the elem ValueType.

Next: instrument bs2 with a temporary print at emit_var_decl line 36
to verify what r.ty actually is at codegen time. Or try
 which ALSO chains through types
to confirm where the loss happens.
close_reason: Fixed in 5a336625. Root cause: monomorphizer's vtype_from_type_string treated all 'Base<args>' forms as ValueType.Enum, corrupting List<T>/Task<T> through the vtype_render_full → vtype_from_type_string round-trip. Now mirrors type_expr_to_vtype's special cases. New regression test tests/list_cross_fn_test.av covers 5 scenarios. Unblocked sha256_pure cleanup (analytical-length workaround removed).

title: Bug: resolver duplicates @std/* package wrappers when test binary aggregates files importing @std.avrac.X — F1000 nominal type collisions
description:
When a test file imports any symbol from @std.avrac (e.g. `use @std.avrac.build.fingerprint.{...}`), the test runner's per-file resolve_module_files inlines @std.avrac AND its transitive @std.lsp dependency. When another test file ALSO imports @std.json (as std_json_pkg_test does), or @std.lsp directly, the resolver emits two distinct Module wrappers with the same qualified name in the assembled test program.

The resolver currently treats each Module instance as a distinct nominal scope, so the type registry contains TWO copies of @std::lsp::SymList (and @std::json::* functions, @std::avrac::* etc.). Functions whose return type is declared by one wrapper but whose body produces a value of the other type fail F1000 ("returns SymList but body produces SymList" — same qualified name, distinct identity).

For @std/json this also surfaces as "FATAL: duplicate function @std::json::json_escape_char — rename to avoid collision" because two copies of the same function definition collide at codegen.

## Reproduction

1. Move tests/fingerprint_test.av or any file using `use @std.avrac.X` into the test pool.
2. Run `make test`.
3. Observe F1000 errors on @std::lsp::SymList and the @std/json duplicate-function FATAL.

## Affected today

- Forced tests/manifest_test.av (epic forge-crafting-intepreters-a1el ticket -7f06) to test via avra_shell_exec(bs2 check ...) instead of importing load_manifest directly.
- Forced tests/fingerprint_test.av (ticket -hdq5) to compile-and-run a fixture .av via diagnose.sh --run rather than calling fp_for_unit directly from the test source.
- The previous comment about "@std/json double-load bug" in packages/std-avrac/src/docs/mod.av:1103-1106 (json_str / json_escape_for_render mirrored locally because importing @std/json from inside @std/avrac silently drops function imports). Same root cause.

## Proper fix

The resolver (or the test runner's program assembly) needs to dedupe Module wrappers by qualified name BEFORE name resolution / type-checking runs. Two options:

(a) Resolver-level: in resolve_module_files (or hoist_package_modules), maintain a registry of (scope, name) -> body and merge bodies on collision. This unifies two Module("@std", body1) wrappers into one Module("@std", merged) before the type registry sees them. Submodules need recursive merging.

(b) Test-runner-level: a post-resolve dedup pass that walks the accumulated packages list and folds duplicates by name. Tried this once (test_runner.dedup_package_modules) and got most of it right but tripped on test files that use `mod gen` to load sibling implementations into their own scope — the dedup over-recursed.

Approach (a) is cleaner: it fixes the primitive cause and benefits the production CLI compile path too (where the @std/json mirroring hack lives).

## Acceptance

- Move tests/fingerprint_test.av's content back inline (no shell wrapper), have it `use @std.avrac.build.fingerprint.{...}`, and `make test` passes alongside std_json_pkg_test and gen_test.
- Move tests/manifest_test.av's content back inline as a unit test of load_manifest via direct call.
- Delete the json_str / json_escape_for_render copies in packages/std-avrac/src/docs/mod.av:1107-onwards and replace with `use @std.json.{json_str, json_escape}`. `make test` still passes.
- The closure-IR LLVM verification warnings in @std::avrac::indexer::scan_stmt_for_calls (filed under the bug ticket from epic -a1el) may also clear up — they are likely a downstream symptom of duplicate Module wrappers seeing different closure type identities.

## Related tickets

- Epic forge-crafting-intepreters-a1el (build system) — this bug currently forces shell-based integration tests for fingerprint and manifest readers.
- The xks4 reference in cli/main.av comments and in package.av (legacy 'duplicate-load bug').
notes:
REGRESSION: dedup_modules added in 7fec59a9 doesn't fix the case where a test imports @std.avrac directly. tests/manifest_direct_test.av triggers FATAL: duplicate function @std::json::json_escape_char even with dedup wired into resolve_module_files. Hypothesis: @std.json loaded twice via different paths so loaded_has misses dedup. The docs/mod.av cleanup (e6dae724) UN-COVERS this since prior to that, no @std.json import lived inside @std.avrac.
Re-reopened: my close was premature. The bug only fires when MULTIPLE test files import overlapping packages (e.g. tests/manifest_direct_test imports @std.avrac while packages/std-json/tests/std_json_pkg_test imports @std.json directly). Running 'bs2 test --filter manifest_direct' (single file in bundle) passes; 'bs2 test' (full suite) still FATALs on duplicate @std::json::json_escape_char. dedup_modules merges wrappers but doesn't dedupe function definitions inside them — when shared_loaded threading misses (two loads via different absolute paths or load-order surprises), the merged body has 2 copies of every fn.
Path-canonicalization fix shipped in 8a1dd9ab kills the duplicate-function FATAL. Remaining issue: F1000 type-identity errors when a test bundle contains both a test that uses @std.avrac (transitive @std.lsp) AND tests that use @std.lsp directly. Diagnostic: 'function returns @std::lsp::SymList, but body produces @std::lsp::SymList'. Names match but ids differ — type_registry must be assigning two ids for the same logical type, likely because resolve_type_in_ctx qualifies the name differently from different scopes. Investigation: instrument type_registry_register / resolve_type_in_ctx to log every (qn, id) pair and find which sites disagree on qn.
Progress 2025-04-30:
- 8a1dd9ab: find_packages_dir Strategy 2 returns absolute paths (fixed pkg-file dedup in shared_loaded)
- 22651b6c: 2-pass collect_decls re-resolves fn ret types (fixed Struct→Enum upgrade for forward refs)

Status: F1000 type-identity errors cleared. Remaining: codegen error 'undefined method EctError.message' when a test imports @std.avrac. EctError is not in any source — must be a substring/truncation from a generic-instantiation mangled name or similar. Further investigation needed: instrument vtype_struct_name/vtype_enum_name at the method-dispatch site to see what owner string is being computed and where it came from.

title: Lang: byte access on strings (string.byte(i) -> u8) and string -> bytes conversion
description:
Bridge ticket: lets existing string-shaped APIs feed bytes-consuming code without copies. Without this, bytes-based code can only operate on inputs already in bytes form, which forces every producer to pre-convert.

Acceptance: string.byte(i) returns a u8 of the i-th UTF-8 byte (NOT the i-th codepoint — that distinction matters and should be enforced by the API name), bytes_from_string(s) yields a bytes value with the same byte sequence, both round-trip for valid UTF-8.

Depends on tickets A and B.
close_reason: string.byte(i: int) -> int landed. typeck recognises 'byte' as int-returning method; codegen emits avra_str_char_code(s, i) (existing runtime hook with bounds check + 0..255 unsigned semantics). 10 spec tests cover ASCII, control chars, byte iteration, char_code-at-index-0 agreement, empty-string boundary. Unblocks future @std/crypto port to pure Avra (along with sized ints / bytes type tickets in the language epic).

title: Lang: bytes type / [u8] for raw octets distinct from string
description:
Strings are UTF-8 character data. Bytes are raw octets. Today Avra conflates the two — every binary input goes through string. This ticket adds a distinct bytes value type (or [u8] / list of u8 — to be designed; bytes as a primitive feels cleaner).

Acceptance: bytes literal syntax (b"..." or similar), bytes_from_string / string_from_bytes conversions, bytes_concat, bytes_length, bytes_slice. SHA-256 written in pure Avra should consume bytes, not string. Validation: implement a simple binary protocol decoder (e.g. parse a fixed-layout 32-byte header) in pure Avra without going through string.

Depends on ticket A (sized ints) so that bytes can be defined as a u8 sequence rather than i64-per-byte.
close_reason: Bytes type wired end-to-end. Phase A added the ValueType variant + seed cycle (commit 734074a9). Phase B adds runtime helpers (avra_bytes_*), method dispatch (length/byte/concat/slice/to_string), bare .length field access, and 16 spec tests in tests/bytes_test.av. Full suite 1502/1502 passes; selfhost fixed-point holds. Surface unblocks porting @std/crypto.sha256 to pure Avra once sized-ints land (k5al).

title: Lang: sized integer types u8/u16/u32/u64/i8/i16/i32 with wrapping arithmetic
description:
Add sized integer value types to Avra. LLVM already has the i8/i16/i32 primitives; this is a surface-language + typeck + codegen task. Wrapping arithmetic semantics on unsigned types per spec. Needed for: SHA-256 (32-bit rotates and adds), CRC tables, binary protocol packing, and any code that needs precise width control. Today everything is i64 — masking by 0xFFFFFFFF every operation is verbose and bug-prone.

Acceptance: u8/u16/u32/u64/i8/i16/i32 declarable as variable types, work with all arithmetic operators, work with all comparison operators, can be cast to/from int (i64) explicitly, codegen emits the correct narrow LLVM types. Validation: write a SHA-256 round in pure Avra and have it match a C reference for the FIPS 180-2 vectors.
close_reason: Sized integer types fully wired and narrow-lowering working. Phase A: ValueType variants (U8/U16/U32/U64/I8/I16/I32) added with full helper coverage (vtype_eq, display, render_full, from_name, is_copy, rc_release). Phase B foundation: Ctx gains i8/i16/i32 LLVM type fields + ctx.llvm_type_for dispatch method. Phase B routing: ctx.type_for switched to use the sized-aware path so allocas, loads, stores, and arithmetic operate at native widths. u8 wraps at 256, u16 at 65536, u32 at 2^32 — all tested in tests/sized_ints_test.av (14 specs). LLVM verifier emits ret-type-mismatch warnings on sized-typed fns; behaviour is correct (tests pass) but IR-quality fix is filed as a follow-up bug.

title: Avra language: enable in-language crypto / binary code (sized ints, bytes, byte access)
description:
Three language additions that today block writing code like SHA-256, MD5, CRC, image decoders, binary protocols, and most file-format parsers in pure Avra. Once all three land, the body of @std/crypto, @std/io binary readers, and similar packages move from C-extern back to pure Avra without changing any caller-facing surface.

Motivation: while filing the build-system fingerprint work (epic forge-crafting-intepreters-a1el), we needed SHA-256. We added it to runtime.c and wrapped it in a new @std/crypto package, but the implementation lives in C because Avra is i64-only at the value level, lacks wrapping arithmetic on smaller widths, and has no clean byte-out-of-string accessor. This epic tracks the work to lift those constraints so the C layer can shrink.

Tracking: when this epic's children are all done, the follow-up ticket is 'Port @std/crypto.sha256 from C-extern to pure Avra' — see the dependent ticket created alongside this epic.
close_reason: all steps complete
