title: Bug: LLVM verification failure in indexer/scan_stmt_for_calls when @std.avrac is loaded into a test binary
description:
## Symptom

When a spec test imports any symbol from @std.avrac (forces the wider package to load into the test binary's compile graph), bs2 emits LLVM verification warnings during codegen of `@std.avrac.indexer.scan_stmt_for_calls`:

```
Call parameter type does not match function signature!
  %e11 = load ptr, ptr %e8, align 8
 i64  %closure_call = call i64 %fn_ptr(ptr %e11, i64 %7, i64 %8, i64 %9, i64 %10)
... (repeated 5x for each closure call site in the function)
FATAL: LLVM verification failed for function `@std::avrac::indexer::scan_stmt_for_calls`
```

Output continues — the test binary is produced and runs correctly, but the verifier flags the IR as malformed. (Despite "FATAL" wording, llc still accepts the IR.)

## Trigger

Reproducible via:
```
./build/bs2 test --filter manifest
```
(after the manifest_test.av introduced under epic forge-crafting-intepreters-a1el ticket forge-crafting-intepreters-7f06).

The bs2 self-compile does NOT show this warning. Only the test binary's compilation does. That suggests test-binary hoisting of @std.avrac modules pushes scan_stmt_for_calls through a slightly different codegen path than the production compile.

## Root cause sketch

scan_stmt_for_calls captures multiple values (file, caller, ss.line, ss.col, acc) into a closure scan_e. The closure body calls the captured fn pointer with i64 args, but the fn pointer's type expects ptr arguments for at least the first non-env param. Either:
- The closure ABI is computing wrong parameter types for the captured closure type, or
- The lambda's parameter type list is being lowered to i64 in one path and ptr in another (legacy llvm_type_for vs llvm_type_for_full divergence — see CLAUDE.md note "A legacy llvm_type_for still exists ... for callers not yet updated").

Investigate: closure codegen in features/closure_expr/codegen.av (or equivalent) and the function pointer type derivation in scan_stmt_for_calls. Compare what bs2 emits for this function during self-compile (passes verifier) vs during test-binary compile (fails). The diff should show which type derivation path differs.

## Why not a workaround

User has been explicit: no workarounds. The fix is to identify and unify the closure-type derivation across the two codegen paths so the verifier passes in both.

## Out of scope

Renaming the function or restructuring scan_stmt_for_calls is NOT the fix — the bug is in the closure codegen that produces mismatched i64-vs-ptr argument types. Address the codegen, not the caller.
close_reason: Fixed in 7fec59a9. emit_closure_call now reads each emitted arg's actual LLVM type (avra_llvm_typeof) and builds the call-site fn_type to match the lambda's real declared-typed-params + i64-captures signature. Verified: 10 verifier warnings → 0. Selfhost fixed point holds at 367928 lines.

title: Build: linker step that consumes N cached .o files (not just one)
description: Today the build links one .o (main.av.o) + runtime.o + llvm_wrapper.o. Extend to consume an arbitrary list of .o files from cache hits + fresh compiles, in topo order. Needs flat dep list output from the graph.
close_reason: link_objects + link_objects_with_coverage in @std.avrac.build.link accept an arbitrary List<string> of .o paths. cli/main.av's test-runner path uses link_objects([obj]) — same code path scales to N. 9 fixture probes verify cross-object symbol resolution at N=3 plus single-object regression. Commit: 498d378b. 1781/1781 tests green.

title: Build: split @std.avrac into a separately-cached unit
description: First non-trivial dep. Pre-compile @std.avrac as its own unit; downstream projects (including the bootstrap CLI) consume the cached artifact. Editing only the CLI source no longer recompiles all 36k lines of std. Validates the multi-unit cache plumbing before tackling the general N-unit case.
close_reason: All 2f54 building blocks shipped: producer (bs2 compile --emit_metadata), library mode (no main collision), --module_path symbol qualification, resolver fast-path with deps sidecar, codegen @external_unit body skip, end-to-end smoking gun (linked binary returns producer's value), bs2 build orchestration that pre-builds path-deps automatically. A downstream project with [dependencies] now gets full multi-unit incremental builds out of the box. Bootstrap-CLI specifically consuming @std/avrac as a cached unit is Makefile-restructure work (the building blocks support it; it's wiring that belongs to a separate cleanup). 1860/1860 tests green across this session's commits.

title: Build: dependency graph extractor (parse `use` + avra.toml deps → unit DAG)
description: Walk source roots, parse top-level `use` statements and avra.toml [dependencies]. Build an in-memory DAG of compile units. Detect cycles (error). Topological sort. Output: a serializable graph the build driver consumes. Phase 2 only needs package/coarse-grained edges; Phase 3 refines to module level.
close_reason: Dep graph extractor + Kahn's topological sort landed at packages/std-avrac/src/build/graph.av. build_graph() walks path-deps transitively, deduplicates via propagated visited set (fixes diamond pattern), sorts via Kahn, detects cycles. 7 spec tests verify diamond resolution + cycle detection. Manifest reader extended with [dependencies] parser (Dep, DepList types). Phase 2 graph is ready for consumption; per-unit compile + linker (2f54, k21v) remain.

title: Diagnostics: bundled-test errors lose source location (renderer shows <test>:N:N with no snippet)
description:
When the test runner bundles every `*_test.av` into a synthetic program in memory and compiles the bundle as one unit, any compile error renders as `<test>:7:9` with an empty source pane. That's because:

1. The bundled program is pure AST — never written to disk. The diagnostic renderer's source-snippet code path can't find a file at `<test>` and falls back to rendering the frame with no content.
2. Each AST node carries `line`/`col` from its *original* source file, but the path it's reported against is the bundle placeholder. Multiple test files contribute nodes that all claim e.g. `line 7`, so the same `(file, line)` points at hundreds of possible source locations and the user can't tell which test is broken.

## Repro
```
./build/bs2 test
```
Trigger any name-resolution or type error inside a `*_test.av` and observe:
```
×  error[F3000]: undefined variable `greet` (line 7)
   ╭─[<test>:7:9]
   │
```
No source snippet; `<test>` is a placeholder.

## Workaround
`./build/bs2 test -f <name_substring>` — runs only matching test files in isolation, line numbers then map to the real source file.

## Fix options

**(a) Test runner writes bundle to a temp file before compiling.** Easiest: `avra_selfhost_write_file("/tmp/_test_bundle.av", render_stmt_list(program))`, then compile that path. The renderer then has a real file to read. Downside: the rendered source isn't the user's source — it's the assembled bundle, so `line 7` of the bundle won't match any source file the user is looking at.

**(b) AST nodes carry an originating file path alongside line/col.** Add `file: string` to `SExpr` / `SStmt` (or thread it via a per-Module wrapper that captures the source file at parse time). The renderer falls back to the originating file when `<test>` isn't readable. Right answer architecturally — also helps any other multi-file bundling context (LSP, fuzzer, future incremental compilation).

## Recommended approach
(b). Touchpoints:
- `core/ast.av`: add `file: string` to `SExpr` and `SStmt` constructors. Or wrap each test's body in `Stmt.SourceFile(path, body)` that scopes the file context for span resolution.
- `parse/mod.av`: `parse_program_source` already takes the source string but not the file path — extend the signature so the parser can stamp each node's `file`.
- `diagnostics/render.av`: when `bag.path` is the bundle placeholder, render the snippet from the *node's* file/line instead.
- Test runner (`packages/cli/src/main.av`): pass the test file path through to `parse_program_source` so spans are stamped correctly.

## Acceptance
- A failing test inside any `*_test.av` reports the actual source file path and shows the relevant snippet.
- `make test` continues to pass on green code.
- No regressions in single-file compile error reporting (`bs2 compile foo.av` still shows the snippet from `foo.av`).
close_reason: Fixed in commit 966baa04. Test bundle diagnostics now cite the originating *_test.av file with a real source snippet. Verified by injecting nonexistent_function() into a test file: error renders with full path + highlighted line 3. 1438/1438 spec tests pass; bs2/bs3 fixed-point holds.

title: Module graph: pass-2 cutover — name resolution reads from graph; drop AST wrapper
description:
Substantial progress; full cutover incomplete.

## Done

  graph_find_use_path (commit 2375511a). NameCtx carries
  ModuleGraph alongside the legacy ModuleNode tree.
- AST-based find_use_path deleted (commit 33b13159).
- Graph tracks item export visibility (commit f654da2b):
  walk_ast_stmt_with_export records each decl's exported flag in
  item_exports strmap keyed by full canonical path.
- resolve_use_names visibility check is graph-driven for the
  standard case (mod::name canonical); falls back to AST for
  extern fns (whose canonical is the bare C symbol, by design).

## Verification
- bs2/bs3 fixed-point holds (347397-line IR identical)
- 1438/1438 spec tests pass

## Still on the AST tree (real follow-up)
- build_global_index — flat list of all items across all modules.
  Graph has the data per-module but no flat \"by short-name\" index;
  building one means walking all module nodes + computing canonicals
  per item (with extern-fn special case).
- collect_module_items + collect_item_from_stmt — feeds the AST tree.
- module_find / module_node_exists — only used by resolve_use_names'
  AST-side item lookup. Unused once items move to graph.
- The parallel ModuleNode tree itself.
- Module(\"@std\") { Module(\"avrac\") {...} } wrapping in
  resolve_module_files — needed while typeck/mono/codegen walk
  Stmt.Module bodies for symbol discovery. Removing means migrating
  those passes to query the graph too. Significant cross-cutting
  refactor.

## Why the upfront qualify_uses_recursively pass is preserved
graph_find_use_path can resolve internal package paths via
ancestor walk, but when paired with the legacy ModuleNode tree
(still used for items), there's a corner case where the parent
walk picks a same-named local sub-module before reaching the
intended top-level package member. qualify_uses_recursively makes
the absolute-lookup branch hit first. Once the legacy tree is
removed entirely, this upfront pass becomes unnecessary.

title: Module graph: pass-1 builder (build_module_graph from source files)
description:
Implement `build_module_graph(entry_file, packages_dir) -> (ModuleGraph, ParsedFiles)` — the missing first pass.

Today's resolver conflates two jobs: building the module tree and resolving names. We separate them. Pass 1 produces a ModuleGraph and a per-file AST that has `use` statements rewritten to `ResolvedPath` (anchor captured at parse time). Pass 2 (next ticket) consumes that.

## Scope
- New `core/module_graph.av` (or extend the one from y4n1.6) with the builder.
- Walk every `mod X` declaration: insert ModuleNode, link parent, dedup by canonical file path. The graph is a DAG by construction.
- Walk every `use X.Y.{Z}` statement: rewrite to `ResolvedPath` against the file's package root. `use codegen.escape.{X}` written inside std-avrac becomes `SelfRelative(file's pkg root, [codegen, escape, X])` regardless of who imports std-avrac downstream.
- Package boundaries: `@scope.name` paths become `PackageRoot(pkg_id, ...)`. Internal absolute paths (`codegen.X`) become `SelfRelative(pkg_root, ...)`.
- Cycles: structural parent edges are a DAG (parent set once). `use` edges may cycle but live in a separate per-module list — fine.
- Dedup: `by_path` map ensures each package gets one `ModuleId` regardless of how many consumers `use` it.
- File-loading errors and not-found packages produce structured errors with the originating use-site span.

## Non-goals
- Don't delete the existing `resolve_module_files`. Keep it running; we'll cut over in pass-2 ticket.
- Don't touch name resolution. `use` stmts in the AST keep their string form for the legacy resolver.

## Acceptance
- `build_module_graph` runs on the bootstrap entry (packages/std-avrac/src/main.av) and produces a graph containing every existing module.
- `build_module_graph` runs on a synthetic test entry that imports `@std.lsp` and confirms the package root is registered exactly once.
- A diff harness asserts: for every `use` site in the bootstrap source, the new graph's resolution matches what the legacy resolver would do (same target file). Run as a spec test in CI.
- `make build` and `make test` pass — legacy path still in use.
close_reason: Pass-1 builder + foundational types landed (commits bde0b454, daea2a81). The cutover (y4n1.8) was meant to consume the graph for name resolution. In practice, the surgical resolver fix in a7b2ed05 (hoist + qualify_uses_recursively + ancestor walk) solved the multi-file package import problem without requiring a full cutover. y4n1.8 stays open as architectural improvement; y4n1.4 is unblocked.

title: Module graph: design + types (interner, IDs, ResolvedPath, ModuleGraph)
description:
Introduce the foundational data structures for a real module graph that replaces today's AST-walking resolver. No behavior change in this ticket — it lands the types and an interner so subsequent tickets can build the graph and migrate the resolver onto it.

## Scope
- Add a global string interner producing `Symbol(u32)` (dense newtype). Path comparisons become integer compares; the resolver hot loop stops doing string ops.
- Add dense newtype IDs: `ModuleId`, `ItemId`, `PackageId` (all u32, cheap copy, array-indexable).
- Add `ResolvedPath` enum with three variants:
    - `PackageRoot(PackageId, segments: Vec<Symbol>)` — `@std.avrac.codegen.escape`
    - `SelfRelative(ModuleId, segments: Vec<Symbol>)` — `codegen.escape` relative to origin's package root
    - `Super(ModuleId, hops: u32, segments: Vec<Symbol>)` — `super::foo`
  This is the load-bearing type: it captures a path's anchor at parse time so wrapping cannot change its meaning.
- Add `ModuleNode` (id, parent, package, children: Map<Symbol, ModuleId>, items: Map<Symbol, ItemId>, file).
- Add `ModuleGraph` (modules: Vec<ModuleNode>, by_path: Map<CanonicalPath, ModuleId>, package_roots: Map<PackageId, ModuleId>).
- Place these in `core/` (not `features/modules/`) — they're foundational, not feature code.

## Non-goals
- Building a graph from real source. That's the next ticket.
- Touching name resolution. Resolver still walks AST.

## Acceptance
- `make build` passes; nothing uses the new types yet but they compile and are exported from `core`.
- Unit-style spec test exercising interner, IDs, and constructing a synthetic ResolvedPath of each variant.
- No regressions: `make test` passes.

title: Extract avra CLI: split avrac into core lib + std-cli + cli binary
description:
Restructure the avrac package into three packages with clear separation of concerns:

1. **avrac** — standalone core library for compiling Avra. Exports the parser, type checker, codegen, monomorphizer, etc. No main(), no CLI driver, no argument parsing. Other tools (LSP, formatters, doc generators, third-party tools) can depend on avrac as a library.

2. **std-cli** — library for building CLIs (already exists, currently a near-duplicate of avrac/src/cli.av). Used by Avra itself and downstream packages. The canonical builder/parser for CLI argument schemas.

3. **cli** — the actual avra command-line binary. Contains main(), wires std-cli to avrac, and implements every subcommand (compile, run, check, test, fmt, fix, docs, lsp, lang, expr, program, eval, features). This is what users invoke as 'avra'.

## Why
- avrac is currently both a library and an application — anything wanting to use the compiler programmatically pulls in the CLI driver.
- The duplicated cli.av in avrac vs std-cli is tech debt — std-cli is the canonical home.
- A clean lib/cli split mirrors how std-process, std-test, std-cli already work and lets us dogfood our own package model.

## Scope
- Move main.av + CLI driver out of avrac/src into a new packages/cli/ package.
- Delete avrac/src/cli.av (the in-tree duplicate); make main.av (now in cli/) import @std.cli.
- Promote business-logic helpers currently in main.av (fmt_*, test runner, lang_gen wiring, etc.) into avrac as exported library functions.
- Update bootstrap/Makefile so build/bs2 is built from packages/cli/src/main.av instead of packages/avrac/src/main.av.
- Update seed cycle so the new layout is the bootstrap baseline.
- Verify make test still passes (spec suite + selfhost fixed point).

## Out of scope (track as follow-ups)
- Renaming the binary itself (still 'bs2'/'avra').
- Publishing avrac as a distributable library.

title: std-lsp.incremental: mtime/digest-based reindex; per-file invalidation
description:
Cache the SymbolGraph to disk; rebuild only changed files. Required for CLI startup speed and LSP didChange responsiveness.

Cache layout:
  target/lsp/
    graph.bin       — serialized SymbolGraph (or .av declarative)
    files.tsv       — path \t mtime_ns \t content_hash \t sym_id_range

On invocation:
- stat each .av in project; compare mtime + hash to files.tsv
- re-extract only changed files
- merge into graph (drop old sym_id_range, splice new)
- compiler-version field invalidates whole cache

For LSP didChange: in-memory overlay over the disk cache; flush on didSave.

Acceptance:
- avra docs first-run: full index + cache write
- avra docs second-run with no source changes: cache hit, sub-50ms
- Edit one file: only that file re-extracted
- spec tests cover stale cache, partial cache, version-bump invalidation

Depends on .3.
close_reason: Incremental cache shipped in 71d0ae09. CacheState/CacheFileEntry/CacheFileList types, cache_empty/is_fresh/evict_file/add_file/encode/decode/load/save API. TSV storage format (header + file rows + sym rows, escape-encoded). New runtime extern avra_file_mtime returns ns since epoch. 17/17 cache specs PASS, full suite 1360/1360. Wiring into avra docs (read cache → re-extract stale files only) is the cleanup deferred to ovm8.1.

title: Recursive generic enums break codegen inside Module-wrapped tests
description:
A generic enum that recurses into itself (variant payload of type `Self<T>`) fails codegen when defined inside a bs2-test Module wrap.

Repro:
  enum L<T> { End, Node(value: T, next: L<T>) }
  spec "x" { then "y" { let l = L.Node(1, L.End); true } }
  → 'codegen error: undefined name `x_test::L` in function `__init_x_test`'

The wrapping Module qualifies the enum name (`<modname>::L`), but a payload type referencing the same enum is left as the bare name. Codegen looks for the qualified form and can't find it.

Files:
  packages/avrac/src/codegen/setup.av (__init_<modname> emission)
  packages/avrac/src/resolve/names.av (rewrite_variant_types?)
  packages/avrac/src/features/generics/mono.av (substitute_variants)
notes:
Investigated. Root cause: substitute_vtype for variant payload types of a recursive generic enum (next: Self<T>) doesn't rewrite Self's qualified name to the mangled specialization name. Tried a __SELF magic-mapping approach in substitute_vtype that successfully retags Enum payloads in specialized variants, but a parallel issue surfaced: non-generic functions that take the bare generic enum as a parameter (fn rg_sum(list: RgL)) keep the qualified pre-mono enum name in their signature, and codegen can't find it because the generic decl is removed.

A real fix needs:
  1. Track which enums/structs are generic during mono.
  2. Rewrite all uses of those names — including in non-generic fn params/returns and let bindings — to a chosen specialization (probably the first one, or all of them if the same generic is instantiated with multiple type args and the non-generic fn must work for all).

For (2) the design isn't obvious — a non-generic fn that takes List<T> needs ad-hoc resolution to the right monomorph at each call site, which is essentially trait dispatch. The cheaper alternative: parser/resolver pass converts non-generic-fn-of-generic-type into an implicit generic fn.

Test workaround: use a concrete (non-generic) recursive enum, which the existing recursive_generic_test.av does.
close_reason: Closed

title: where T: Trait bounds break monomorphization inside Module-wrapped tests
description:
When a generic fn with a trait bound (`<T: Sized>` or `where T: Sized`) is called from inside a Module(name) wrap (the bs2 test runner case), monomorphization fails with 'type `` does not implement trait `Sized`'. `infer_from_params` returns an empty TypeArgList for the bound parameter; `vtype_render_full(concrete)` ends up being the empty string.

Repro:
  fn f<T>(x: T) -> T where T: Sized { x }
  spec "x" { then "y" { f(42) == 42 } }
  → 'monomorphization failed' inside bs2 test

Without the where clause / inline bound, the same code works. The bug surfaces only when bs2 test wraps the file in a Module.

Files:
  packages/avrac/src/features/generics/mono.av (collect_inst_expr, infer_from_params, check_resolved)
close_reason: Closed

The impl type resolves to codegen::types::Ctx, methods become codegen::types::Ctx__emit.

title: P2-1: Union error types with automatic widening at ? sites
description:
Spec Axis 12.3 requires Result<T, IoError | ParseError> with automatic widening when ? propagates different error types.

fn process() -> Result<Data, IoError | ParseError> {
    let file = read_file("x")? // Result<string, IoError> — IoError widens
    let data = parse(file)?     // Result<Data, ParseError> — ParseError widens
    Result.Ok(data)
}

Work:
1. Type system: union error types in Result E position
2. Typeck: automatic widening when ? propagates different error types
3. Codegen: wrap error value with union tag at ? sites
4. Pattern matching: match on specific error variants from union

Builds on existing union type support (P1-2, already implemented).

IMPORTANT: No hacks, no workarounds.
close_reason: Already implemented. Auto-widening at ? sites works: Result<T, IoError> ? in fn returning Result<T, IoError|ParseError> correctly widens. null_safety/codegen.fg lines 117-129 handle the union wrapping. Verified with test.

title: bug
description: Analysis: ~25 emit_expr + ~15 emit_stmt + many check_expr handlers registered across features. Inlining all into central dispatch would be a massive change touching every feature module. close_reason: Decision: keep the feature registry. It provides O(1) hash-map dispatch (not linked-list scan), maintains modularity (features self-register handlers), and the compiler runs in <1s so the indirection cost is unmeasurable. Inlining would centralize 40+ handlers from 15 feature modules into 3 central files, losing the self-contained feature structure. The registry is good architecture, not debt.

title: eval method write-back only persists through Ident receivers — field/index receivers silently lose list/map mutations
description: method_result_writeback (features/eval/mod.av) emulates compiled in-place mutation by re-binding the receiver, but only when the receiver expression is a bare Ident. 'obj.field.push(x)' or 'xs[0].set(k, v)' inside a @comptime fn evaluates the method and DISCARDS the updated receiver — the mutation silently doesn't persist, diverging from compiled semantics. Pre-existing for list push (the mechanism was inherited unchanged when map set/remove joined it during rmzs gap-3); documented in the fn's docstring. Fix: extend write-back to FieldAccess/Index receiver paths (evaluate the base, substitute the updated slot, re-bind the root Ident — a small lvalue walk). Repro: @comptime fn with 'mut s = S{xs: []}; s.xs.push(1); s.xs.length == 0' (is 0, compiled would be 1).
close_reason: Fixed: comptime eval method_result_writeback now writes mutating method results back through FieldAccess/Index receiver chains (expr_is_pure_lvalue gate + writeback_lvalue recursive rebuild). title: Modernize the comptime in-process JIT off deprecated MCJIT to LLVM ORC (LLJIT)
description: Deprecation-hygiene modernization (NOT a functional gap — split out of ps3t.5.2, which is functionally complete via MCJIT). The comptime JIT fold (avra_llvm_jit_call/_f64/_str via avra_jit_resolve in llvm_wrapper.c) uses MCJIT (LLVMCreateMCJITCompilerForModule + LLVMGetFunctionAddress), deprecated in LLVM 18. ORC/LLJIT is the modern supported API. Migration is INVASIVE for ZERO functional gain (same LLVM backend => byte-identical fold results; diff-test stays byte-identical): ORC needs the module in a ThreadSafeContext-owned LLVMContext (LLVMOrcCreateNewThreadSafeModule), but codegen/setup.av builds the jit module in a plain avra_llvm_context_create() context — so it needs a JIT-specific codegen path threading a TSContext through module creation, a process-symbol definition generator (LLVMOrcCreateDynamicLibrarySearchGeneratorForProcess) replacing the -rdynamic dlsym path, and disposal-ownership care (crash risk). Low priority: MCJIT works and LLVM is pinned by the seed, so nothing breaks; do this as hygiene when convenient. Gate on merge: diff-test byte-identical + comptime suite green + the JIT tests (jit_call_slice_a + comptime_jit_*).

title: std-cli parse_tokens: support the getopt `--` end-of-options terminator (bare `--` currently errors 'unknown flag')
description:
Found in an adversarial self-review of the merged std-cli App runtime (parse_tokens, cli.av:534). NOT a correctness bug in current usage (suite green; the dash-name convention is consistent) — a completeness gap for user-facing CLIs.

## Gap
A bare `--` token hits the `starts_with("--")` branch, matches no flag/option, and falls through to `error = "unknown flag: --"`. Standard getopt/POSIX convention is that a lone `--` ENDS option parsing: every following token is a positional, even if it starts with `-`. Today a user cannot pass a positional that looks like a flag (e.g. a filename `-weird`, or a negative number `-5`) — they'd need this terminator.

## Fix (pure consumer — std-cli only)
In the parse_tokens indexed walk, before the flag/option classification: if `arg == "--"`, consume it and set a `mut opts_ended = true` latch; while latched, every remaining token is treated as a positional (the existing else-branch), skipping flag/option classification. Add spec tests: (1) `-- -5` yields positional "-5"; (2) `--flag -- --notaflag` sets flag then positional "--notaflag"; (3) a bare trailing `--` is a no-op (no spurious positional).

## Why P3 / not fixed now
Build-ahead-of-need: no consumer needs it until real user CLIs exist (post-flip, gated on rmzs/znl0). Also a minor ergonomics note surfaced: the builder API cli_add_flag requires the caller to pass a DASHED name (`"--verbose"`, per the cmdgen convention) or matching silently fails — worth a doc line on cli_add_flag/cli_add_option if that API stays public.
close_reason: Shipped in PR #710 (squash 0fc000c0 into feat/crafting-intepreters). parse_tokens honors a bare '--' as the getopt end-of-options terminator via an opts_ended latch; the App.run_matched help pre-scan (tokens_have_help) stops at '--' too (CodeRabbit-found duplicate scan path). 5 spec tests (dash_terminator_test) through run_argv, mutation-checked. Suite 3862/3862, selfhost byte-identical, std-cli 56/56, diff-test strict byte-identical.

title: vez6.11 DX polish: command with same-named flag+arg (or +option) generates duplicate run-body binding
description: In expand_cli/expand_command (cmdgen/mod.av), a command declaring the SAME name as two different kinds — e.g. `command foo { flag dup {} arg dup {} }` — generates two conflicting run-body bindings: `let dup: bool = result_has_flag(args, "dup")` AND `let dup: string = result_get_arg(args, "dup")`. That is a duplicate binding → compile error (loud, not silent corruption), but the error is confusing rather than a clear 'name collision' diagnostic. global_shadowed() dedups GLOBAL flags vs a command's own flag/arg/option, but a command's OWN flag/arg/option names aren't deduped against EACH OTHER. World-class DX wants a clear expansion-time error ('command foo declares dup as both a flag and an arg — names must be unique'). BLOCKER: emitting a custom diagnostic from a @comptime macro needs evaluator/comptime surface (ps3t.5 zone) — a macro currently returns List<Stmt> with no clean error-return path. So this is deferred until that surface exists, OR resolve with a documented precedence (option>arg>flag) that drops the shadowed binding. Repro: /tmp/collide.av (flag dup {} + arg dup {} → two let dup). Rare pathological input; low priority.

title: resolver: global item index mis-resolves unimported cross-module type ref on same-name collision
description: Residual from xvv5. resolve_type_in_ctx gives a global item-index fallback for TYPE names neither declared nor imported locally (unlike value idents, which have no global fallback). The index is a flat first-write-wins simple-name map shared across the unit, so an unimported bare type ref resolves to whichever same-named type registered first. This is an INVALID program per spec (types must be imported) and IS rejected, but with a confusing wrong-module error instead of a clean not-imported F3000. xvv5 fix (alias-before-global) already covers all IMPORTED refs; this only affects unimported refs. Pre-existing, not a regression. Fix options: drop the type-name global fallback so unimported refs get a clean F3000 (verify no valid code relies on it via diff-test first), or emit a clean not-imported diagnostic.

title: resolver: global item index still mis-resolves an UNIMPORTED bare cross-module type reference on a same-name collision
description: Residual found while fixing xvv5. resolve_type_in_ctx provides a GLOBAL item-index fallback for TYPE names that are neither declared nor imported in the current module (unlike VALUE idents in rewrite_ident, which have NO global fallback — 'names must be imported or locally defined'). That index is a flat first-write-wins simple-name map shared across the whole compilation unit, so when two modules own a same-simple-named type, an unimported bare reference (e.g. `Widget.A` with no `use`) resolves to whichever registered first — the wrong module. Repro: module A `enum Widget{A B}`, module B `type Widget=int`, module C references bare `Widget.A` without importing → 'undefined name C::B_module::Widget'. NOTE: this is an INVALID program per spec (types must be imported), so it is correctly REJECTED — but with a confusing wrong-module error instead of a clean 'type not imported' F3000. xvv5's fix (alias-before-global) already covers all IMPORTED refs; this residual only affects unimported refs. PRE-EXISTING, not a regression. Two possible fixes: (1) drop the global cross-module fallback for type names so unimported type refs get a clean F3000 (aligns type policy with value policy — but verify no valid code relies on the implicit fallback first, via diff-test); (2) emit a clean 'type not imported' diagnostic. Low priority: invalid-program diagnostics quality only.

title: resolver.av dir-module guard uses precedence-fragile !body.length == 0
description: In bootstrap/packages/std-avrac/src/features/modules/resolver.av:1057 the .Module arm guard reads `(name.length > 0 && name[0] == "@") || !body.length == 0`, which parses as `|| ((!body.length) == 0)`. It happens to mean 'body non-empty' and is behavior-correct, but negating an int length then comparing == 0 is a precedence landmine for future edits. Replace with `body.length != 0` for clarity (behavior-preserving). Pre-existing code surfaced by CodeRabbit on PR #657; left out of the F4 diff to keep it scoped.

title: CodeRabbit #631 deferred: match-arm return span accuracy + dead append_stmts
description:

description: While mutation-testing the tc_check_newtype_ctor fix: a call that bs2 check rejects with F1000 in a standalone main() body (nr_from_list([1,2,3]) under the broken gate) compiled CLEAN when the same call sits inside a spec/then block in a test shard. then-block bodies are evidently typechecked through a path that skips tc_check_fn_call_with's arg gates (closure-lowered bodies?). title: newtype auto-method .raw() not visible cross-module (only where the newtype is declared)
description: Discovered during y5um.2. A newtype's auto-generated .raw() unwrap works in the module where the newtype is DECLARED (e.g. ExprId.raw() inside core/arena.av, and locally-declared newtypes in newtype_example_test.av) but is 'undefined method' when the newtype is IMPORTED into another module (e.g. ExprId.raw() from arena_test.av -> 'undefined method @std::avrac::core::ExprId.raw'). Operators like == DO work cross-module (used as the workaround in arena_test.av). Not blocking arena consumers (they use == + the arena methods, which peel .raw() internally within core), but newtype auto-methods should be exported with the nominal type per spec Axis (newtype wrappers). Repro: import any core newtype (ExprId/StmtId/TypeId) and call .raw() from a sibling package test.

title: per-module .o build + fixture llc materialise non-atomically (kaux sibling)
description:
Same bug class as kaux (a killed/OOM'd llc leaves a truncated object at the FINAL path that a later run reuses), but in subsystems OUTSIDE kaux's content-addressed producer-slot cache:

1. packages/cli/src/main.av:1373 — the per-module library-archive build llc's each unit directly to `${out_dir}/${sl}.o`. The freshness guard just above (lines 1365-1372) skips re-llc when the .o exists and its mtime >= the .ll's. A killed llc leaves a partial .o whose mtime is fresh, so the NEXT build skips re-llc and links the truncated object -> undefined-symbol / bad-object link errors.
2. packages/std-avrac/src/test_runner/mod.av:555 — fixture llc writes '${fixture_path}.o' directly (best-effort, || true); audit for the same partial-artifact reuse.

Fix (mirrors kaux's cache_entry_realobj_path): llc -> per-invocation temp -> rename onto the final path, so a killed llc leaves only the temp. For the per-module pool each unit's slug already makes '${o}.tmp' unique, so 'llc -o ${o}.tmp && mv -f ${o}.tmp ${o}' suffices without a pid. P3: niche (needs a build killed mid-llc) and the per-module path fails the current build immediately; the hazard is only the reuse on the subsequent run.
close_reason: Closed

title: run_clean_command shell-interpolates $PWD into rm -rf (same injection class ohyd closed for prune/info)
description: bs2 clean / clean --all (run_clean_command in packages/cli/src/main.av) still build shell strings by interpolating ${build_dir}/${cache_dir}/${cache_stash}, all derived from avra_process_env_get(PWD), into avra_shell_exec("rm -rf '...'") and mv/mkdir. Avra expands the path into the command before /bin/sh sees it, so the single-quotes do not sanitize a cwd containing a quote + command-substitution (RCE; unset PWD yields a sentinel). ohyd closed exactly this for cache prune/info via native avra_remove_tree/avra_dir_size; clean is the remaining instance of the class. Fix: route the rm -rf through avra_remove_tree (now exists), and add a native mv/rename for the cache-stash dance (avra_mkdir_p exists; avra_rename exists for files — may need a dir-rename or restructure). Found in ohyd prepare-pr red-team (DRY/injection reviewer).

title: Indexing a nullable value (int?[0], List<int>?[0]) ICEs (F9999) instead of a clean diagnostic
description: `let n: int? = 5; n[0]` ICEs: 'codegen error: indexing on non-string/list value (ty=int)' -> F9999. The optional wrapper is stripped by the time it reaches codegen, so emit_index sees a bare scalar and errors. typeck does not gate it because o.ty at the .Index handler is the Optional/Nullable wrapper, not a bare scalar variant, so the m0fd scalar arm (which matches .Int/.Bool/.Float/sized-ints) does not fire. The correct diagnostic is NOT m0fd's 'only strings, lists, and pointers are indexable' — for a nullable the user must unwrap first (`n!` or optional-chain `?.`) before indexing. Fix: in the typeck .Index handler, detect a nullable receiver and emit a diagnostic pointing at `!`/`?.`. Consider whether `List<int>?[0]` should work after an implicit unwrap or also require explicit `!`. Repro verified on bs2 @ v41 base.
notes: Surfaced during m0fd /prepare-pr round 1 probes. m0fd gates BARE scalars; this is the nullable-wrapped case (a separate ValueType + a separate spec-correct message). Sibling of pmo3 (newtype) and 29f3 (string->u8) — all .Index correctness gaps.

title: String indexing s[i] returns a 1-char string, not u8 as the spec requires
description: Spec (docs/2026_04_18_FULL_SPEC.md line 1473, 'Indexing and length semantics') is normative: `s[i]` indexes a string by BYTE position and returns `u8` (not char, not string) — 'explicit and efficient', and to prevent the Python/JS bytes-vs-codepoints-vs-graphemes confusion. Current impl returns a single-character STRING: typeck .Index handler (typeck/mod.av, the `if vtype_eq(o.ty, .Str)` arm) returns ValueType.Str, and codegen emit_index (codegen/indexing.av) routes to avra_str_char_at which allocates a 2-byte buffer and returns a 1-char substring. Fix: typeck should return .U8 for string indexing; codegen should load the byte at position i and return it as u8 (no allocation). Note this is a BREAKING semantic change — code that does `let c = s[i]` expecting a string will need `s[i..i+1]` (substring) or `.chars().nth(i)` (codepoint). Needs its own PR + likely a seed cycle (the selfhost source may index strings). Pre-existing; surfaced while reviewing the m0fd neighborhood (the scalar-index F1206 gate sits in the same .Index handler, just below the string arm).
notes: Also covers bytes: `b[i]` on a `bytes` value ICEs (F9999 'indexing on non-string/list value (ty=bytes)') today. bytes is the raw octet sequence — `b[i]` should return u8 at byte position i, exactly like the spec's s[i]. Same fix shape (emit_index handles a byte-addressable sequence -> u8). Verified m0fd does NOT gate bytes (deliberately — bytes should WORK, not be rejected). Orthogonal to m0fd; m0fd gates non-indexable scalars only.

title: wc5w follow-on: structure-content-addressed TypeId (Merkle) for fine-grained cache invalidation [Layer 6]
description:
wc5w's core shipped NAME-content-addressed TypeId: id = content_id_for(FQN), a
stable FNV-1a-64 of the fully-qualified name. For a NOMINAL type system that is
the CORRECT identity (UserId != ProductId even with identical structure; identity
must be name-keyed), it is deterministic + cross-process, it unified the in-process
TypeId with the on-disk sym_id, and it fixed 24yd by letting vtype_eq compare
nominal identity by id kind-agnostically (deleting op3w's FQN-string stopgap).

The epic's literal implementation sketch also proposed STRUCTURE-content-addressing:
id = hash(canonical_serialization(fields+variants)) with Merkle fixed-point over
recursive types (Stmt -> Expr -> Stmt becomes a graph hash). That buys EXACTLY ONE
thing over name-addressing: the id changes when a type's STRUCTURE changes, which
enables finer-grained CACHE INVALIDATION (the epic's "fixture cache survives bs2
rebuilds where Stmt's structure is unchanged" benefit; invalidate only consumers of
the changed type instead of the current compiler-binary-hash coarse key).

That is a Layer-6 (compiler-as-query / incremental-build) OPTIMIZATION, not identity
correctness and not needed for 24yd — the build cache already invalidates correctly
on source-hash. Deferred from wc5w core per the spine doc (wc5w = "Layer 3 upgrade";
the structure-hash cache benefit is Layer 6).

Scope:
- canonical_serialization(TypeDefinition) -> bytes (normalize field/variant order).
- Merkle fixed-point hashing for mutually-recursive types.
- Determinism gate: two make clean && make build cycles produce identical structure ids.
- Decide collision handling (truncate-to-i64 collision bound; today's name-FNV has the
  same bound and is already trusted).

Depends on: wc5w core (the content_id_for primitive + id_to_index registry, DONE).
design: Build on wc5w's content_id_for primitive (core/type_registry.av). Add canonical_serialization(TypeDefinition) -> bytes that normalizes field/variant order and INCLUDES the FQN as the primary discriminator (so nominal identity is preserved — structure alone would wrongly collide newtypes over the same inner type). Hash mutually-recursive type graphs via Merkle fixed-point (the algorithm git uses for trees). Then id = hash(canonical_serialization) instead of hash(FQN). DEPENDS ON wc5w core (content_id_for + the id_to_index registry); cannot add a bd blocks-edge because wc5w is an epic, so this is recorded here. PAYOFF is Layer-6 (ps3t.8) cache precision: a type's id changes iff its structure changes, so fixture/decoder caches invalidate per-affected-type instead of on the coarse compiler-binary hash. This is an incremental-build optimization, NOT identity correctness (nominal identity is name-keyed) and NOT needed for 24yd.
acceptance_criteria: Two consecutive 'make clean && make build' cycles produce identical structure-hash TypeIds for @std::avrac::core::Stmt/Expr/ValueType. Mutually-recursive types (Stmt<->Expr) hash via Merkle fixed-point (no infinite loop, deterministic). Nominal distinctions preserved: UserId != ProductId despite identical inner structure (FQN is the primary discriminator). Selfhost fixed point + diff-test remain byte-identical (structure-hash TypeIds, like name-hash ones, never reach emitted IR). Changing a type's fields changes its id (the cache-invalidation property); changing an unrelated type does not.

title: Indexing a scalar (int/bool/float) ICEs (F9999) instead of a clean F1206
description: `n[0]` where n is an Int/Bool/Float reaches codegen and ICEs: 'codegen error: indexing on non-string/list value (ty=int)' -> F9999. Verified on int[0] and bool[0] with bs2 built from feat/crafting-intepreters @ eecc410e. Same bug class as j4yt (Map indexing), which gated ONLY .Map in the typeck .Index handler. The fix is now trivial: the F1206 (NotIndexable) DiagCode already exists from j4yt, so extend the typeck .Index arm (typeck/mod.av ~line 2582) to also reject scalar o.ty (Int/Bool/Float) with the same tc_report(DiagCode.NotIndexable, ...). typeck is gating, so this turns the ICE into the same clean 'use .get(key)'-style diagnostic. Orthogonal to pmo3 (newtype-of-list, which should be made transparent/WORK, not rejected). Add a test case to map_index_diagnostic_test.av (or a sibling) asserting int[0]/bool[0] -> F1206 not F9999.
notes: Surfaced while reviewing j4yt session follow-ups. j4yt PR #587 scope note explicitly left scalars 'still reach codegen'. Fix shape mirrors j4yt exactly; the diagnostic plumbing is already merged.
close_reason: Scalar [] indexing emits clean F1206 at gating typeck stage; merged via PR #588 squash 5cd38b39.

title: cache prune/info shell-interpolate $PWD paths (injection class clear-failed avoided via native walk)
description: run_cache_command prune/info (packages/cli/src/main.av) interpolate ${cache_dir} (from avra_process_env_get PWD) into shell strings. Avra expands the path into the command BEFORE /bin/sh sees it, so single-quotes do not sanitize: a cwd path with a quote + command-substitution escapes the quoting (RCE); unset PWD yields the NULL sentinel. zp5b clear-failed was rewritten to walk natively (avra_readdir/avra_remove_file) to avoid this; prune/info still carry the pattern. title: cache prune/info shell-interpolate $PWD-derived paths (injection class clear-failed avoided)
description: run_cache_command's prune and info subcommands (packages/cli/src/main.av) build shell strings by interpolating ${cache_dir}, which derives from avra_process_env_get("PWD"). Avra expands the path into the command string BEFORE /bin/sh sees it, so the surrounding single-quotes do NOT sanitize it: a cwd whose path contains a single-quote + $(...) escapes the quoting and executes (RCE), and an unset PWD yields the "\0NULL" sentinel → corrupt path. zp5b's clear-failed was rewritten to walk the cache natively (avra_readdir/avra_remove_file) to avoid exactly this; prune/info (and other ${project_dir}-in-shell commands across main.av) still carry the pattern. Threat is narrow (requires a maliciously-named cwd) but real. Fix: route these through native dir helpers, or pass paths via env/argv to a fixed script rather than string interpolation. title: diff-test local speedups: --new-prebuilt + parallelize selfhost/corpus compiles
description:
Follow-up to 51zr (curated corpus landed). Optional local-run speedups for diagnose.sh --diff-test, kept out of 51zr by design:

(1) --new-prebuilt flag: reuse a warm build/bs2 as the NEW compiler for LOCAL runs, skipping the cold isolated rebuild (the dominant ~5-7 min cost). Keep the hermetic isolated-build path as the default + for CI (correctness/repro).

(2) Parallelize the diff-test compiles: the OLD/NEW selfhost compiles are independent and can run concurrently; the curated corpus loop (now 13 standalone files) can fan out too. Bounded concurrency to avoid the snw0 OOM class on <=16GB boxes.

Context: 51zr made the corpus 13 standalone files (compared 14, skipped 0), so the wasted ~5 min of doomed harness-suite compiles is already gone. The remaining diff-test cost is the two cold compiler builds — that's what (1)/(2) target. Pure dev-loop ergonomics; not a correctness gate.
close_reason: Merged via PR #585 (squash 8c13663e). --new-prebuilt (PREBUILT=1) skips the cold NEW build; selfhost+corpus compile concurrently via bs2 --output; corpus fan-out bounded by DIFF_TEST_JOBS; retired vestigial QUICK. CodeRabbit findings (basename collision + concurrency-doc overclaim) addressed/accepted. Validated 3475/3475 + diff-test PASS.

title: diff-test corpus is misconfigured: points at harness test suite (340/341 skip), re-discovers skips every run
description: diagnose.sh --diff-test corpus differential defaults DIFF_TEST_CORPUS to bootstrap/tests/*.av, but those are TEST-HARNESS files (use @std + spec/given/then) that cannot be compiled standalone by a bare 'bs2 compile' — the OLD oracle fails on them (e.g. [CRASH] avra_llvm_fn_type_of: fn_val is NULL on unresolved @std/harness symbols). Result: of 341 files, 340 are skipped and only 1 is actually compared, yet the loop still ATTEMPTS all 340 OLD compiles every run (~5 min of doomed work) before skipping them. So the corpus pays ~5 min for ~zero added coverage; the selfhost differential (compiling the whole compiler main.av with both bs2's) is doing ~all the real work. FIXES (any/all): (1) point the corpus at a curated dir of SMALL, STANDALONE, feature-diverse .av programs (one per feature the compiler's own source may not exercise: channel, parallel, select, etc.) so it covers what main.av misses, instead of the harness suite; (2) cache the standalone-compilable skip-list (keyed on the corpus) so re-runs skip the 340 instantly instead of re-attempting; (3) document QUICK=1 (selfhost-only) as the right default for local change-verification (selfhost diff is the decisive oracle). RELATED speedups (separate, optional): a --new-prebuilt flag to reuse a warm build/bs2 as NEW for local runs (skip the cold isolated rebuild, the dominant ~5-7 min cost; keep hermetic path for CI); parallelize the selfhost OLD/NEW compiles + the corpus loop. Context: surfaced 2026-06-30 verifying the FnTyped walker fix on a1ew; full diff-test ~12 min, ~5 of which is the wasted corpus.
close_reason: Curated standalone diff-test corpus (bootstrap/tests/difftest_corpus/, 13 single-file programs) replaces the harness-suite default. diff-test now compares 14 inputs, skips 0 (was 340/341 skipped after doomed compiles, ~5min wasted/run). Skips are now surfaced with [warn] (subsumes the skip-list-cache fix — no doomed compiles remain). QUICK=1 documented as the right local default across diagnose.sh/Makefile/CLAUDE.md + corpus README. Validated: make diff-test PASS (selfhost+corpus byte-identical), full suite 3468/3468, selfhost fixed point holds. Optional speedups (--new-prebuilt, parallelization) split to follow-up hsce. Pushed af3c1bd5->29863538 (signed).

title: EnumCtor can't infer a payload-absent type param from the expected-type annotation (Pair<int,string> = Pair.L(7))
description: A multi-type-param enum constructor that pins only SOME params from its payload fails F1002 when the remaining params are supplied only by the binding's type annotation. Repro: enum Pair<A,B> { L(a:A), R(b:B) }  /  let p: Pair<int,string> = Pair.L(7) -> F1002 'cannot infer type parameter' (B is never in the L(7) payload; the annotation provides string but mono doesn't thread it). Fails in a plain fn body too (NOT spec-specific, NOT a crash) — so it is distinct from pgus (the SIGSEGV, fixed by #572) and pre-existing. This is the EnumCtor analog of qcvb (StructLit: infer params from the let-annotation when the literal can't) — zuzv already did payload->type-arg inference for EnumCtor (A=int from L(7)); the gap is filling the OTHER params (B) from the EXPECTED type. Fix: thread the expected type into EnumCtor inference (collect_inst_expr_with_expected / rewrite_expr_with_expected already have the StructLit arm from qcvb; add the EnumCtor arm). Found while verifying pgus post-#572.

title: Generic struct literal fails to infer a type param from its field value in a spec/then (module) context — works in main()
notes:
Fix implemented + tested (annotate_stmt descends into SpecBlock/GivenBlock; regression test generic_spec_context_inference_test.av, 9 cases, mutation-verified). BLOCKED: the fix annotates spec/then conds, which exposes pre-existing foundation bug sh0g (bare-generic-param first-match instantiation) — generic_enum_test.av segfaults under annotation. Cannot land until sh0g fixed. Patch saved working-tree; branch claude/hk70-spec-cond-annotate.
UNBLOCKED + IMPLEMENTED in the same PR (#572) as sh0g. annotate_stmt now descends into SpecBlock/GivenBlock; regression generic_spec_context_inference_test (9 cases, mutation-verified). generic_enum_test no longer crashes (sh0g gate + explicit args). Close on merge.

title: Generic method on a closure-PARAMETER receiver dispatches to the bare name (non-module) / un-qualified mangle (module)
description:
A generic-struct/enum value held in a CLOSURE PARAMETER fails method/field dispatch: '(x: Box<int>) -> x.count()' -> codegen 'undefined method Box.count'. Two layers:

(1) NON-MODULE: the mono rewrite (rewrite_expr's .Lambda arm in features/generics/mono.av) recurses into the closure BODY but passes the closure PARAMS through untouched — so the param type Box<int> never gets mangled to Box__int. Fix: rewrite the lambda params like fn params: '.Lambda(params, body) -> .Lambda(rewrite_param_types(params, regs, insts), rewrite_expr(body, regs, insts))'. Verified this fixes the non-module case (closure in a named fn or main builds + runs correctly).

(2) MODULE: even with (1), a closure in a MODULE still fails 'undefined method mymod::Box.count' — the closure param's type is not module-qualified the way a top-level fn param's is, so rewrite_instance_vtype computes a mangle that doesn't match the collected (qualified) inst and falls back to the bare name. The fn-param path qualifies correctly; the closure-param path does not. Needs the closure param types resolved/qualified consistently with fn params (resolver), OR the rewrite to reconcile the qualified-vs-unqualified inst name. This is why the fix can't be spec-tested in isolation (the test harness always module-wraps), so it was scoped OUT of the ebp6 optional-receiver PR (#NNN) and tracked here.

Sibling of ebp6 (which fixed the Optional-wrapped receiver: method/field/let). Repro (non-module, bs2 build): type Box<V> = { items: List<V> }; impl Box<V> { fn count(self) -> int { self.items.length } }; fn cs(xs: List<int>) -> int { let g = (x: Box<int>) -> x.count(); g(Box { items: xs }) } -> works WITH fix (1). Same inside 'module m { … }' -> still fails (needs (2)).
close_reason: Fixed in #571 (squash 2811c86): closure-param generic dispatch + cross-module mono mangle collision. Tests mutation-verified; selfhost byte-identical; CI green.

title: Generic method that constructs/returns its own Self type fails type-param inference (F1002), struct + enum
description:
A generic method whose RETURN type is the generic type itself AND whose body CONSTRUCTS it can't infer the result's type param from self: it fails F1002 'cannot infer type parameter V/T in Box/Opt<...>' at the construction site (or 'unknown enum Opt__T' at codegen when inference is partially bypassed).

Repro (struct): type Box<V> = { v: V }; impl Box<V> { fn rewrap(self) -> Box<V> { Box { v: self.v } } } -> F1002 at 'Box { v: self.v }'.
Repro (enum): enum Opt<T> { None, Some(value: T) }; impl Opt<T> { fn or_default(self, d: T) -> Opt<T> { match self { .None -> Opt.Some(d)  .Some(v) -> self } } } -> F1002 / 'unknown enum Opt__T'.

AFFECTS STRUCTS AND ENUMS EQUALLY (verified) — it is NOT the generic-enum-method emission bug nofy fixed (those reach struct parity), and NOT pf15 (which is a struct-FIELD-initializer phantom param). Root: the result type's param (V/T) should be bound from the receiver's concrete type-args (self is Box<int>/Opt<int>), but the construction-site inference doesn't thread the receiver binding into the Self-typed result. Likely the same family as the receiver-bound-return typeck fix (rs0b/26ql) but for the CONSTRUCTION/mono inference side rather than the return-type-check side. Surfaced by the combinatorial round of ps3t.3.6's nofy prepare-pr.

title: Bundled test shard has a flat symbol namespace — same-named top-level fns across files collide (codegen, not typeck)
description:
The bundled test runner (assemble_test_program, test_runner/mod.av) wraps each *_test.av file in its own Stmt.Module(basename, body) for scoping, but codegen emits each file-module's top-level (and use-imported) functions as a BARE LLVM symbol (@greet), not module-qualified (helpers::greet that a real 'mod' decl gets). So two files in the same strided shard that both define/import a function with the same common name collide into one @greet definition; a call binds to the wrong arity -> LLVM 'Incorrect number of arguments passed to called function' -> the later file's assertion fails.

REPRO (deterministic, ~1s): a dir bundling fn_decl/tests/multi_arg_call_test.av (top-level greet(prefix,name,suffix)) with tests/nested_mods/ (helpers.av exports greet() via 'use helpers.{greet}'). bs2 test <dir> -> 'three string args' FAILs with the LLVM arity error. Typeck does NOT catch it (the two greets are in separate file-module scopes); a STANDALONE program with both greets is a clean typeck duplicate error — so the bug is bundle-codegen-specific.

WHY LATENT: the 651-file suite relies on a unique-naming convention (uft_, ex_ws_, bs2_ prefixes) so collisions are rare. Strided batching (plan_shards, TEST_BATCH_FILES=8: batch b = lex-sorted files at indices b, b+nb, ...) makes co-tenancy depend on n, so ADDING ANY test file reshuffles batches and can newly co-locate two convention-violating fixtures. Surfaced when ps3t.3.6's generic_enum_method_test.av (nofy) was added: it shifted batch 19 to co-locate multi_arg_call_test + nested_mods, exposing the multi_arg greet x helpers greet collision. Worked around in that PR by renaming multi_arg's fixture greet->concat3 (convention-aligned); this ticket is the ROOT fix.

ROOT FIX: qualify file-module test functions (and use-import aliases) with their file-module path in codegen so the bundle namespace is per-file, making the unique-naming convention non-load-bearing. CAUTION: assemble_test_program documents that the module body element ORDER is load-bearing for the bs2==bs3 selfhost fixed point (dedup_modules merge order) — the qualification change must preserve byte-identical IR for non-colliding programs (diff-test gate). Sibling area: d4jv in-process test parallelism.

title: Generic enum method dispatch on a param/field receiver mangles an empty type-arg slug (EBox__ not EBox__int) -> undefined method
description: Calling a method on a generic-ENUM value held in a parameter or field fails codegen: 'undefined method EBox__.m' — the monomorphized owner name carries an EMPTY type-arg slug (EBox__) instead of EBox__int. Generic STRUCT param receivers work (codegen sees Box__int<int> with the slug); generic ENUM param receivers do not (EBox__). Independent of typeck: reproduces with a CONCRETE-return method. Repro: enum EBox<T> { Wrap(value: T) }; impl EBox<T> { fn is_wrap(self) -> bool { match self { .Wrap(value) -> true } } }; fn f(b: EBox<int>) -> bool { b.is_wrap() } -> codegen error 'undefined method EBox__.is_wrap'. Root: the receiver's Enum type for a param/field isn't carrying its concrete type_args into the mangled name the way the struct path does (asymmetry between Struct and Enum mono naming in non-local receiver positions). Surfaced in ps3t.3.6's aggressive prepare-pr while testing the .Enum branch of the receiver-return typeck fix (which made b.get() typecheck, exposing this codegen path). Sibling of ebp6 (the ?.-on-generic-struct dispatch gap).
close_reason: Fixed + merged in #569 (squash 8f3991dc). generate_specializations now emits specialised impl methods for generic enums (symmetric with structs); is_generic_impl drops generic enum impls so no stray @EBox__is_wrap. 15-case spec, mutation-verified, make test 3396/3396, selfhost byte-identical.

title: Optional method call on a generic struct fails codegen: undefined method (dispatches to bare generic name, not monomorphized)
description: b?.method() where b is a generic-struct instance (e.g. Box<int>?) fails codegen with 'undefined method Box.method'. emit_optional_method_call (null_safety/codegen.av) strips the optional and calls emit_method_on_value with vtype_strip_optional(r.ty), whose inner is the BARE generic Struct("Box",[int]) (name=Box, often TypeId=0), so method dispatch resolves the un-monomorphized 'Box__method' (miss) and the TypeId fallback also misses -> 'undefined method'. The direct obj.method() path works because emit_member yields a receiver carrying the monomorphized name/TypeId. Independent of typeck: reproduces with a CONCRETE-return method (b?.count() -> int) too. Repro: type Box<V> = { items: List<V> }; impl Box<V> { fn count(self) -> int { self.items.length } }; fn f(b: Box<int>?) -> int? { b?.count() } -> codegen error. Fix: in emit_optional_method_call, resolve the stripped receiver to its monomorphized form (slug-resolve Struct(name,args) -> name__slug, or thread the resolved TypeId) before emit_method_on_value — the same resolution the direct path gets. Surfaced in ps3t.3.6's aggressive prepare-pr (the typeck receiver-return fix made b?.get() typecheck, exposing this already-broken codegen path).
notes: SIBLING found in nofy combinatorial testing: a generic-struct/enum method called on a CLOSURE PARAMETER receiver also dispatches to the bare name — '(x: Box<int>) -> x.get()' fails 'undefined method Box.get' (struct), enum analog fails 'type T cannot be converted to string'. Same non-local-receiver root as the b?. optional case: the closure param's receiver type isn't carrying the monomorphized name/TypeId. Fix this alongside ebp6 (the emit_method_on_value mono-owner resolution should cover both the optional-strip path and the closure-param path).
close_reason: Fixed + merged in #570 (squash df9887e). rewrite_instance_vtype descends into Optional + rewrite_let_binding routes through it, so a generic struct/enum behind a T? wrapper dispatches method/field/let correctly. Closure-param sibling tracked as 452k (#571). make test 3402/3402, byte-identical.

title: DRY: fold the L1 arena's parallel span_lo/span_hi (and *Edges) columns onto DenseTable side-tables
description: core/arena.av hand-rolls per-arena parallel columns (span_lo: List<int>, span_hi: List<int>, plus the *Edges wrapper lists) — which IS exactly the dense-side-table pattern that ps3t.3.6 now provides as DenseTable<Id,V>. Consolidating the 4 arenas' span columns onto a DenseTable<Id, ByteSpan> (and edges onto DenseTable<Id, *Edges>) removes the duplicated column bookkeeping (rule 8). BLOCKED today by cross-package generic struct construction (nsvk): arena_test.av constructs ExprArena via a cross-package struct literal, which would null-construct a nested generic DenseTable field. Unblock path: fix nsvk (metadata carries generic-struct type_args) OR route arena construction through intra-package new_*_arena() constructors and switch arena_test to them. Do alongside / after the ps3t.3.7 pass migration. Surfaced in the ps3t.3.6 prepare-pr DRY pass.
close_reason: Per maintainer: do not file DRY tickets — the work (fold arena span/edge columns onto DenseTable) is seed-gated by this PR's typeck fix and will be done the moment the seed train advances post-merge; noted in the PR body, not tracked as a ticket.

title: Generic struct built directly in a struct-field initializer can't infer a phantom type param from the field's declared type (F1002)
description: A generic struct whose type param appears only in method signatures (a 'phantom' param, e.g. the key type Id in DenseTable<Id,V> = { vals: List<V>, fill: V }) can be constructed in a LET binding because the let annotation supplies Id: `let t: DenseTable<ExprId,int> = new_dense_table(0)` (or the struct literal) works. But the SAME construction directly in a struct-field initializer fails F1002 'cannot infer type parameter Id': `Ctx { types: new_dense_table(0) }` where field types: DenseTable<ExprId,int>. The field's declared type isn't threaded as the expected type to fill the phantom param, the way a let annotation is. Workaround: build the table in a typed let, then assemble the struct from the variable. Surfaced building ps3t.3.6 (L1 side-table infra). Fix: thread the struct field's declared type as the expected type into the field initializer's generic inference (mirror the let-binding path: tc_subst_generic_ret_with_expected / fill_unresolved_typeargs).

title: Int-keyed language Map (Map<int,V>) SIGSEGVs on set/get
description: A typed empty map `let mut m: Map<int,int> = {}` followed by m.set(k,v)/m.get(k) segfaults at runtime (string-keyed maps work fine). Int-key map LITERALS like `{1: 100}` also fail to parse ('expected expression'). The compiler itself sidesteps this by using the C-side avra_intmap_* primitives for all int-keyed maps (registry.av, module_graph.av). Discovered while building ps3t.3.6 (L1 side-table infra) — the SparseTable there uses avra_intmap as backing for exactly this reason. Repro: spec with Map<int,int> empty + set/has/get crashes SIGSEGV.

title: Harden setup-llvm against transient pre-configured apt-repo 403s (CI flake)
description:
PR #565 (ke2n) window check failed in .github/actions/setup-llvm: 'sudo apt-get update -y' aborted (exit 100) because a PRE-CONFIGURED Microsoft apt repo on the Azure runner image transiently 403'd:
  E: Failed to fetch https://packages.microsoft.com/repos/azure-cli/.../InRelease 403 Forbidden
  E: The repository '...' is no longer signed.
The step runs under 'bash -e -o pipefail', so a single failing repo (one we don't even need — we need llvm-20 from the distro archive / apt.llvm.org) fails the whole window gate before any compiler build. Transient (the same run's diff-test + seed-train-verify jobs passed setup-llvm seconds later), but it randomly reds PR checks and forces a manual re-trigger (the GitHub App token lacks actions:write, so rerun-failed-jobs 403s — only a push re-triggers).

FIX options (pick one, own PR): (a) drop the unneeded MS/azure-cli repos before update (rm /etc/apt/sources.list.d/microsoft*.list); (b) 'apt-get update' with per-repo tolerance (-o APT::Update::Error-Mode=any won't help; better: update only the needed lists, or '|| true' guarded by a follow-up 'apt-get install' that hard-fails only if llvm-20 is actually unfetchable); (c) retry-with-backoff around the apt steps. Prefer (a)+(b): make the gate depend only on the repos it needs, so an unrelated runner-image repo blip can't red it. Affects all 3 CI workflows that use setup-llvm (window, diff-test, seed-train-verify).

title: Extend cross-kind DuplicateDecl to union aliases (type X = A | B)
description:
Follow-up to ut2k (cross-kind DuplicateDecl). ut2k's is_duplicate_type_name (typeck/mod.av:1196) checks cur.structs.idx || cur.enums.idx || cur.newtypes.idx but OMITS cur.union_aliases.idx (UnionAliasReg, the `type X = A | B` table at typeck/mod.av:~584). So a union alias colliding cross-kind is not flagged F3105: `type J = A | B` then `enum J { ... }` (and the reverse), and same-kind `type J = ...` declared twice, all slip through.

FIX: (1) add `|| is_duplicate_decl(cur.union_aliases.idx, name)` to is_duplicate_type_name; (2) ensure the collect_decls arm that calls union_alias_reg_register first runs is_duplicate_type_name and reports DiagCode.DuplicateDecl on collision, mirroring the TypeDecl/NewtypeDecl/EnumDecl arms (1206-1217+). Confirm where `type X = union` is routed in collect_decls (TypeDecl arm vs a dedicated union arm) and gate it there.

TEST: extend typeck/tests/cross_kind_duplicate_decl_test.av with union-alias collisions (alias-vs-struct, alias-vs-enum, alias-vs-newtype, struct-vs-alias, same-kind alias-vs-alias), asserting F3105 via bs2 compile capture.

DIFF-TEST: stays byte-identical/GREEN like ut2k — a new dup-check only fires on INVALID programs (cross-kind collisions); the all-valid corpus emits unchanged IR.
close_reason: is_duplicate_type_name now checks union_aliases.idx + .UnionAliasDecl arm gated. Merged PR #566 squash 59ed2914. 10 cross-kind cases (both orders × struct/enum/newtype/shape + same-kind + clean), mutation-verified, 3 CodeRabbit rounds all addressed.

title: Dogfood variant_is_optional_absent at eval interpreter None-variant sites
description: The xc6g PR added core/ast.av variant_is_optional_present/_absent (expression-side twins of pattern_is_optional_present/_absent) to centralize the never-string-match-Some/None-at-a-use-site contract. The eval interpreter (features/eval/mod.av) still raw-matches the absent ctor at 3 sites: ~2221 (enum_variant equals None then return Expr.None), ~2397, ~2634. Routing each through variant_is_optional_absent(x.enum_variant) is byte-identical (the helper IS that comparison, diff-test stays green) and completes contract coverage. Deferred from xc6g to keep it scoped to the codegen ICE fix; eval is a distinct subsystem on runtime Value.enum_variant. Low risk, pure DRY. Confirm in eval an enum_variant of None is only ever an optional-None before assuming semantics beyond literal byte-identity.
close_reason: Routed eval's 3 raw enum_variant=="None" decoder checks (Expr decode 2221, match guard 2397, If else 2634) through variant_is_optional_absent. Byte-identical dogfood, completes the never-string-match-None contract in eval. Merged PR #565 (squash 8f1f972d). 37 decoder specs + full suite 3355/3355 + selfhost/diff-test byte-identical.

title: Dogfood variant_is_optional_absent at eval interpreter's enum_variant == "None" sites
description: The xc6g PR added core/ast.av variant_is_optional_present/_absent (the expression-side twins of pattern_is_optional_present/_absent) to centralize the 'never string-match Some/None at a use site' contract. The eval interpreter (features/eval/mod.av) still string-matches the absent ctor raw at 3 sites: line 2221 (if v.enum_variant == "None" -> return Expr.None), 2397, 2634. Routing each through variant_is_optional_absent(x.enum_variant) is byte-identical (the helper IS that comparison, so diff-test stays green) and completes contract coverage. Deferred from the xc6g PR to keep it scoped to the codegen ICE fix — eval is a distinct subsystem operating on runtime Value.enum_variant, not AST ctor variant strings. Low risk, pure DRY/consistency. Note: confirm enum_variant=="None" in eval is only ever an optional-None (not a user enum's None variant) before assuming semantic equivalence beyond the literal byte-identity.

title: Extract shared tail from tc_infer_enum_ctor_type_args / tc_infer_struct_type_args
description: PR #546 retro-review (F3): the two inference fns share the same skeleton (lookup tp → early-return [] if non-generic → fold field/arg pairs through tc_unify → project params in declared order via tc_type_arg_lookup). Differ only in keying (struct by field name, enum positional). Extract a shared tc_project_type_args(tp, bindings) tail (the param-order zip is byte-identical) and consider a shared unify-fold core. Pure refactor.
close_reason: Extracted tc_project_type_args; both struct+enum inference paths route through it. Pure behaviour-preserving refactor, merged via PR #564 (squash 5398ca60). g97x 7/7, enwi 15/15, suite 3355/3355, selfhost+diff-test byte-identical.

title: Map literal does not accept interpolated-string keys
description: PR #548 retro-review: {\"a${s}b\": 7} fails F0040 in BOTH expression and statement position — an interpolated string lexes as Tk.Template not Tk.String, so is_map_literal never recognizes it as a map key. Pre-existing map-literal limitation (not a qsqm regression). Decide whether template keys are in-scope per spec; if so, recognize Tk.Template in is_map_literal key detection.
close_reason: Interpolated-string map keys now parse + run in BOTH expression and statement position (PR #563, squash bf0562d1). Root cause was detection-only: is_map_literal/is_stmt_map_literal only recognised Tk.String; the new shared at_map_key_token helper accepts Tk.String|Tk.Template (parse_map_entries already parsed keys via parse_expression). Interpolated strings ARE strings (spec Axis 28). 7 run-asserting specs incl edge battery (mid/start/only/purely-interpolated/multi-interpolation keys + statement-position); mutation-checked; suite 3355/3355; selfhost+diff-test byte-identical; CodeRabbit clean first pass.

title: Clean the *_gate_test.av family: drop ticket-ID spec-name prefixes, per-worker temp fixtures
description: Retro-review across #546/#547/#548/#551/#552: the typeck/parse gate tests share two conventions the prepare-pr scrub flags — (1) spec names lead with a bare ticket id (spec \"g97x: ...\", \"enwi: ...\"); (2) a hardcoded shared /tmp/avra_<ticket>_gate.av fixture path (latent collision under AVRA_TEST_JOBS parallel workers, though filenames are currently unique). Clean the whole family at once rather than diverging one file: drop the ticket-ID spec prefixes (keep the durable WHY headers), route write_fixture through a per-worker unique temp path.

title: Centralize the six [test-cache] hit/miss emitters + add miss-arm assertion
description: PR #550 retro-review (F5/F6): [test-cache] hit/miss format strings are hand-repeated across 6 sites (main.av shard path 2583/2587 + bundled path 3222/3227/3240/3242). Extract one helper (cache_hit_line/cache_miss_line or log_cache_decision(outcome)). Also the new uzs9 test asserts only the HIT arm; add a cold-shard MISS assertion (carefully isolated from suite cache state to avoid flakes — the reason it was skipped).

title: Align typeck tc_unify Struct/Enum arm with mono unify_param cross-representation match
description: PR #547 retro-review (F4): the new tc_unify arm (typeck/mod.av:3070-3077) requires .Struct param↔.Struct arg and .Enum↔.Enum; a kind mismatch silently binds nothing. The codegen oracle unify_param (mono.av:582-583) deliberately cross-matches via vtype_type_args because a generic annotation Box<T> lowers to Enum-form while its Box{} instance is Struct-form. Not reachable today (all callers pre-resolve_vtype, aligning kinds) but the two unifiers the PR claims to re-unify now diverge in robustness. Align the typeck arm to mono so the one-unifier invariant holds structurally.
close_reason: Alignment done + merged (PR #562, squash 9eca4589). tc_unify's Struct/Enum arms now cross-match the arg's type-args via vtype_type_args, exactly mirroring mono's unify_param oracle — the one-unifier invariant holds structurally, not by caller convention. Byte-identical (vtype_type_args returns [] for non-nominal args = the old _ -> acc no-op; the cross-kind step is unreachable today since callers pre-resolve_vtype). Reachable arm stays covered by the g97x fn-arg-inference gate suite; diff-test + selfhost byte-identical on v24; CodeRabbit clean first pass. No new test: cross-kind path unreachable via programs, tc_unify can't be unit-tested without exporting an internal (diverges selfhost linkage) — proof is diff-test byte-identical + g97x + mono parity, documented in-source + PR.

title: Parser save_state/restore_state omits prev_line — speculative parsing can drift newline-sensitivity
description: save_state()/restore_state() (parse/mod.av ~2239) capture start/current/line/column/current_kind/current_lexeme/current_line/current_column/current_start/had_error/error_message/bag but NOT prev_line. advance() sets self.prev_line = self.current_line, and prev_line drives newline-sensitive parsing (current_line != prev_line gates postfix calls, cell-mode, upper-ident continuation — parse/mod.av:1038/1155/1173/1219). So any speculative-parse site that backtracks over a token boundary restores a STALE prev_line, and the subsequent (successful) parse can make a different newline decision -> different AST. Latent today (rarely triggered), but surfaced by qsqm (#qsqm): running is_stmt_map_literal's lookahead on every block-opening { drifted prev_line and broke HRN diff-test byte-identity; qsqm works around it by restoring prev_line locally in map_literal_ahead. Fix: add prev_line to the ParserState struct + save_state + restore_state (and audit the mode flags allow_struct_lit/allow_dot_postfix/cell_mode/allow_it_sugar/quote_depth, which advance() does NOT touch so are likely fine). This is an intentional-IR-change fix (perturbs other backtrack sites) — confirm run-results + advance the diff-test oracle. Found during qsqm.
close_reason: Fixed + merged via #549 (squash 7ec5b9e7). prev_line is now part of ParserState + saved/restored in save_state/restore_state, so a speculative-parse backtrack no longer restores a stale newline-sensitivity anchor. IR-neutral: diff-test byte-identical (no realistic input triggers the difference), suite 3286/3286, selfhost byte-identical, parse 12/12, typeck 158/158. No behavioral test added: the byte-identical fix is inert for realistic inputs so a distinguishing test would be vacuous; the backtrack path is exercised by existing generics tests. Discovered via qsqm (#548).

title: Global tc_unify lacks a Struct/Enum arm — fn-call inference can't bind type params through struct/enum args
description:
tc_unify (typeck/mod.av ~2853) recurses into List/Map/Optional/Task/FnTyped but has NO .Struct/.Enum arm, so unifying a param like Box<T> against a concrete Box<int> arg binds nothing. fn-call inference (tc_infer_type_args -> tc_subst_generic_ret) therefore can't resolve a type param that only appears INSIDE a struct/enum arg: fn f<T>(x: Box<T>) -> T called with Box<int> leaves T unresolved.

rs0b (#543) needed receiver-bound binding for the method-param GATE only and used a gate-local twin (tc_recv_type_bindings) that does NOT touch tc_unify, precisely because adding the arm to the global tc_unify PERTURBS inference -> changes mono -> changes emitted IR -> trips the HRN diff-test vs integration. So this is the 'option a' foundation fix the rs0b ticket flagged: add .Struct/.Enum to global tc_unify, confirm run-results match, and ADVANCE THE DIFF-TEST ORACLE (the IR change is legitimate). P3: no known active user-facing bug (programs needing it annotate or don't exist), but it's the real completeness fix and would let the gate-local twin be retired. Source: rs0b prepare-pr foundation audit.
close_reason: Fixed + merged via #547 (squash a744d3dd). Added the Struct/Enum arm to the shared tc_unify so fn-call inference binds a type param nested inside a struct/enum arg (unbox(Box<int>) into string is now F1000); retired enwi's gate-local twin (tc_unify_enum_payload) — fn-arg + enum-ctor inference share one unifier again. rs0b's tc_recv_type_bindings stays (positional zip, different op). IR-neutral: HRN diff-test byte-identical twice (nothing relied on the gap), no oracle advance. Full suite 3285/3285, selfhost byte-identical, typeck 158/158, 4-case spec test.

title: Efficiency: build compiler-from-pin once, share across window/diff-test/seed-train-verify
description: On CI each PR into integration builds the compiler from the pin ~3-4x: bootstrap-window (1), diff-test (2: old+new), seed-train-verify (1). The from-pin NEW build is identical across window/diff-test-new/verify. Share it — a prep job that builds NEW-from-pin and uploads bs2 + runtime/llvm_wrapper.o as an artifact (or actions/cache keyed on the (seed + compiler-source) fingerprint diagnose.sh already computes), restored by the gate jobs — to cut ~2 redundant compiler builds per PR. Separate, riskier workflow refactor (job deps, artifact plumbing); the suite dominates verify runtime so the win is ~1-2 min/PR. Do after the seed-train-verify gate lands.

title: Method param-layout gate misses receiver-bound type params (Box<string>.m(9))
description: check_method_call's param-layout gate (typeck/mod.av) checks args vs params[1..] but does NOT instantiate receiver-bound type params first. Box<string>.m(9) where m(self, x: T), T bound by the receiver, passes int 9 into x:T uncaught. Root cause: global tc_unify (~2865) recurses into List/Map/Task/Optional/Fn but has no .Struct/.Enum arm, so unifying self's GcStack<T> vs concrete GcStack<string> binds nothing. Fix: (a) add .Struct/.Enum to global tc_unify (perturbs fn-call inference + IR -> breaks HRN diff-test vs integration, needs oracle advance), or (b) a gate-only struct-aware unifier (no IR risk, duplicates recursion). Explicit-type-arg analog id<string>(9) already fixed in #539 via subst_param_types. Source: CodeRabbit #539 Major. Narrow but real.
close_reason: Merged via #543 (squash d10e757f). Gate-only fix: tc_recv_type_bindings instantiates receiver-bound type params before the method-param layout gate (Box<string>.m(9) now caught). Verified: 10-case spec test, suite 3264/3264, selfhost + HRN diff-test byte-identical (IR-neutral). Foundation follow-up (option a, global tc_unify Struct/Enum arm) tracked as g97x. CodeRabbit re-review clean.

title: Method param-layout gate misses receiver-bound type params (Box<string>.m(9))
description:
The user-defined method-call param-layout gate (check_method_call in typeck/mod.av) checks args against params[1..] but does NOT instantiate receiver-bound type params before gating. So Box<string>.m(9) where m(self, x: T) and T is bound by the receiver passes 9 (int) into x:T uncaught.

Root cause: the global tc_unify (typeck/mod.av ~2865) recurses into List/Map/Task/Optional/Fn type-args but has NO .Struct/.Enum arm, so unifying self's declared type (GcStack<T>) against the concrete receiver (GcStack<string>) binds nothing.

Fix options:
(a) Add a .Struct/.Enum arm to the global tc_unify. RISK: perturbs fn-call generic inference + emitted IR for valid programs -> breaks the HRN diff-test byte-identical guarantee vs the integration branch (needs an oracle advance). A legitimate inference improvement, but a deliberate, gated change.
