(b) A gate-only struct-aware unifier used solely to instantiate params for the layout gate (never for inferred types) -> no IR risk, but duplicates tc_unify's recursion.

Sibling already fixed: the EXPLICIT-type-arg analog id<string>(9) is closed in #539 via subst_param_types (explicit bindings are directly available; no unification needed). This ticket is the receiver/method analog.

Source: CodeRabbit review on PR #539 (Major). Reachable but narrow (generic method taking the impl type param, called with a layout-mismatched literal).

title: check_expr_expected arms should catch ONLY generic-arg conflicts (kill the return collection→scalar double-diagnostic)
description:
Surfaced during nlzq prepare-pr (Phase 10). At a RETURN of a collection into a value-scalar slot (fn f() -> int { return [1] } / return xs), TWO diagnostics fire: the check_expr_expected arm's collection→scalar check (.ListLit reject_collection_into_value_scalar / the _ and .Call arms' check_assign_layout_no_int) AND the return path's vtype_assignable mismatch. They are complementary (layout-violation + return-type-mismatch) and both correct, but the int case emits only ONE (the arms omit int via _no_int, leaving it to the positional int-block/vtype_assignable) — so collection is inconsistent with int.

PRE-EXISTING (a85d/#538 put collection→scalar at the shared expected-type arms); nlzq preserved it byte-identically. NOT a correctness hole (the wild store IS caught, just twice at return).

CLEAN FIX (out of nlzq scope — behaviour change, multi-position): make the check_expr_expected arms catch ONLY the generic-arg conflict (generic_args_layout_conflict — the one thing vtype_eq/vtype_assignable structurally cannot see), and move collection→scalar to the POSITIONAL checks: add a collection block to check_binding (mirroring its existing int-block), rely on vtype_assignable at return, and the full gate at match-tail (already done in 40c3adbc). Then the arms' role becomes crisp ('catch what assignability can't'), binding/return/match each emit exactly one diagnostic, and int+collection are consistent. Verify list-element / map-value literal positions (which use nested_layout_conflict, not the arms) are unaffected; re-gate full make test. Low priority: it's verbose-but-correct, not a bug.

title: List/Map first-element type inference doesn't skip leading none (infers void? not int?)
description: CodeRabbit review on PR #538 (pre-existing for lists). tc_first_elem_ty pins the element type from elements[0]; a leading none makes [none, 1] infer List<void?> instead of List<int?>. tc_first_map_value_ty (added in this PR) mirrors the same first-value behavior and also misses later none values. The compile is clean (the program is valid), but the annotated SExpr.ty can disagree with the actual nullable container layout. Fix: iterate to the first NON-none element/value for the base type, then optionalize if any none is present (a map_lit_value_optionalize analog of list_lit_optionalize). Low priority / pre-existing: it's an inference-accuracy issue, not a wild store; deferred from #538 to keep that PR scoped to the layout-conflict gates.

title: Defensive: validate map-literal keys are string in check_map_values_against (macro-generated AST path)
description: CodeRabbit review on PR #538. Source-level non-string map keys are already rejected (a non-string key literal like {9: "x"} produces F0040). The residual concern is a macro/quote-transformed AST that synthesizes a MapLit with a non-string key, bypassing the source-level guard — map codegen pointer-casts keys (ctx.to_ptr), so a non-string key would be a wrong-representation hazard. check_map_values_against currently iterates only odd (value) indices. Defensive hardening: validate even (key) indices are string-typed too. NOTE: must avoid false positives on Unknown-typed keys (inference gaps) and string-compatible keys — a naive 'types[i] is .Str' would wrongly reject those, so guard with the settled/unresolved checks the value path uses. Low priority: no verified reachable trigger today (source keys are covered); this is belt-and-suspenders for the macro path.

title: map.set result should preserve receiver's value type, not the argument type
description:
CodeRabbit review finding on PR #538 (63wu arc). In map_lit/codegen.av, emit_map_set returns ok_emit(map, .Map(.Str, val_r.ty)) — it types the result of `m.set(k, v)` from the ARGUMENT's value type rather than the receiver map's declared value type. Since map.set mutates an existing map, the chain result should preserve the receiver's static value type, not adopt the argument's (which can be less precise, e.g. Unknown).

Fix (CodeRabbit "heavy lift"): thread the receiver map's ValueType into emit_map_method_call / emit_map_set and return .Map(.Str, receiver_value_ty).

Practical impact is currently nil for valid programs: the ibjo collection-mutation check (check_collection_value_arg) already rejects a set value whose layout conflicts with the map's value type, so for well-typed code val_r.ty matches the receiver's value type. This is a precision/consistency refactor, deferred from PR #538 to keep that PR scoped to the wild-store conflict fixes. Low priority.

title: generic_args_layout_conflict misses newtype-wrapped nested value conflicts (needs nominal registry resolution, not structural strip)
description: Spun out of 4gid. A newtype used as a NESTED value carries an uncaught inner conflict: type W = Box<string>; let m: Map<string, W> = {"k": Box{val:9}} compiles clean (Box<int> value vs W's inner Box<string> = wild store). generic_args_layout_conflict is purely structural and W resolves to .Struct("W") (NOT .Newtype) at conflict-check time, so a structural Newtype-strip branch is DEAD (verified during 63wu deep round — added then reverted). Proper fix: resolve nominal names via the type registry (the fn has tc available) to detect a newtype and compare its declared inner layout. Narrow case (newtype-of-generic-struct as a nested generic-arg/container value); the direct binding case is already gated by the newtype nominal check.

title: A collection/map literal is silently assignable into a scalar slot (let x: int = [1,2] / {"k":1})
description: Surfaced during 63wu deep review. A list/map literal (a heap ptr) assigned to a scalar (e.g. int) annotation compiles clean — the ptr is stored in the int slot. General (List AND Map), pre-existing. Inverse direction of ry1a (which catches scalar->ptr); this is collection-ptr->scalar. Not a classic deref wild store (the int isn't dereferenced) but a type-safety violation that should be F1000. Repro: let x: int = [1,2] => OK (should be F1000); let x: int = {"k":1} => OK. Likely belongs with the broader scalar<->ptr assignability tightening (w0kt) once the everything-is-i64 FFI boundary is migrated.
close_reason: Fixed + validated (commit 2cdacd98, pushed). check_expr_expected's .ListLit/.MapLit arms now reject a value-scalar expected type — a list/map literal (a pointer) into an int/float/bool slot was the inverse of the ry1a scalar→ptr hole. Narrow by construction (only value scalars gated; non-scalar pointer slots are nominal mismatches handled elsewhere) so no false-positive surface. Full suite green + selfhost fixed point byte-identical; 8/8 dedicated test + probes confirm valid List/Map bindings, unannotated literals, nested lists unaffected.

title: Bare {…} map literal at block-statement start parses as a block (F0040), not a map
description: Found during 63wu prepare-pr. A function body whose sole expression is a bare map literal — fn f() -> Map<string,V> { {"k": v} } — fails to parse: the outer { opens the fn body, then the inner { is read as a nested block, and the map entry 'k: v' yields F0040 'expected expression'. Workaround: use 'return {…}' or bind to a let first (both parse + typecheck fine, incl. the 63wu value-conflict check). This is a pre-existing parser/disambiguation ergonomics gap (bare {…} block-vs-map ambiguity at statement position), independent of 63wu. Fix: in expression-statement / implicit-return position where a Map is expected, prefer the map-literal parse, or require an explicit cue. Repro: fn f() -> Map<string, int> { {"k": 1} } => F0040; fn f() -> Map<string, int> { return {"k": 1} } => OK.
close_reason: Fixed + merged via #548 (squash a3f0a7b9). parse_statement gates its block branch on a STATE-FREE raw-source peek (is_stmt_map_literal): a bare map at statement/implicit-return position (fn f() -> Map { {k:v} }) now parses as a map; real blocks and {} stay blocks. State-free on purpose — a save_state-based lookahead drifts because the backtracking infra omits prev_line (surfaced+filed as cpi6); the diff-test caught 3 layers of state-drift before the pure-peek fix landed byte-identical. Suite 3286/3286, selfhost + diff-test byte-identical. Spec test asserts the bare map's runtime value.

title: Generalize scalar->pointer assignability tightening beyond int->string (int->struct/list/map)
description: ry1a closed the int->string wild store in let/arg/reassign. The same wild-store class for OTHER pointer-layout targets still leaks: let f: Foo = 9 (int->struct), let xs: List<int> = 9 (int->list), map/enum. Generalizing the predicate from (declared is .Str) to vtype_is_ptr_layout(declared) is the natural fix BUT is delicate and needs exclusions to avoid false positives: (a) .Optional — let x: int? = 9 is valid (wraps Some(9)); (b) .Ptr — int<->ptr is intentional in FFI/runtime code; (c) trait auto-boxing; possibly more. Each exclusion is an FP source, so do it incrementally with a full selfhost+suite gate per step. Lower priority than int->string (struct/list-typed slots fed a bare int are rarer than string).
notes:
REFINED root cause: the ~140 FPs are the everything-is-i64 FFI BOUNDARY, not an
inference fallback. 130 extern fns are declared to return int but actually return
pointers (avra_map_get_cstr, avra_map_new_cstr, list/alloc helpers, ...). Code
legitimately reinterprets: assign a C int result to a real annotated pointer type
(e.g. a List<int> annotation over avra_map_get_cstr's int return). The int->ptr
generalization cannot distinguish this from a real wild store (int literal into a
List slot) because BOTH are .Int into a ptr-layout type. So w0kt is gated on
migrating the extern FFI bindings to proper ptr return types, then ptr->List is
allowed via the .Ptr exclusion while int->List is flagged. That is a large,
separate everything-is-i64 FFI cleanup (130 externs + runtime.c). int->string
stayed clean because string slots are not fed C int results.

title: mono expected-type completeness: const collect/rewrite asymmetry + nested-struct-in-field threading
Nested generic enum ctor written directly as a match subject infers bare type
description: A nested generic enum constructed INLINE as a match subject loses the inner type-arg, so the payload binding can't be matched. Repro: 'enum Maybe<T>{Just(v:T),Nothing} fn read()->int{match Maybe.Just(Maybe.Just(3)){.Just(i)->match i{.Just(n)->n,.Nothing->0},.Nothing->0}}' -> codegen 'unknown enum Maybe' (bare). Typeck infers the inner ctor Maybe.Just(3) as bare Maybe (no return-type/expected context to pin T=int), so the outer subject is Maybe<Maybe> and the payload i binds to bare Maybe. The cross-function form (construct in a fn returning Maybe<Maybe<int>>, match in another) WORKS (fixed in v3a3) because the return type pins the inner. Root: typeck nested-enum-ctor literal inference without expected type. Distinct from v3a3 (payload binding + mono inst collection, fixed). Workaround: construct via a return-typed fn.
notes: Also covers DEEPER nesting in return position: 'fn mk()->Maybe<Maybe<Maybe<int>>>{Maybe.Just(Maybe.Just(Maybe.Just(7)))}' then a 3-level match fails 'unknown enum Maybe__Maybe__int' (the MIDDLE instance). Root is the same: typeck doesn't propagate the expected type THROUGH nested enum ctors, so inner/middle ctors infer bare types and the middle instance is never collected. Double-nesting (v3a3, now fixed) works because its two needed instances are covered without the middle (outer via return-type scoping, inner via the leaf literal). Fix: propagate expected type into enum-ctor payload args during typeck (check_expr EnumCtor with expected Maybe<X> → check the payload arg with expected X). Surfaced via v3a3's prepare-pr red-team.

title: impl on concrete generic instance (impl Box<int>) doesn't substitute T in method bodies
description: An impl block targeting a CONCRETE generic instance leaves the type param unsubstituted in method bodies. Repro: 'type Box<T>={val:T} impl Box<int>{fn get(self)->int{self.val}} fn f()->Box<int>{Box{val:6}} fn g()->int{f().get()}' -> F1000 'function Box__get returns int, but body produces T'. The method's self.val should be int (T=int from the impl target Box<int>), but typeck/mono treats self.val as the unsubstituted T. Generic impls written as 'impl<T> Box<T>' work; only impls bound to a concrete instance (impl Box<int>) fail. Pre-existing (typeck/impl-specialization), surfaced via the fyzs PR's combinatorial red-team. Distinct from fyzs (field access on annotation-typed values, fixed) and 1gs2 (chained List[i].field typeck). Workaround: use 'impl<T> Box<T>' or a free fn.

title: Generic struct literal inline in a then-block not monomorphized across test-runner units
description: A nested generic struct LITERAL constructed directly inside a spec then-block isn't collected/specialized, so a param/field type referencing it resolves empty. Repro: 'type Box<T>={val:T} fn f(b:Box<Box<int>>)->int{b.val.val} spec "x"{then "a"{f(Box{val:Box{val:4}})==4}}' -> codegen 'field access on non-struct value (ty=)'. The SAME code with the literal/call moved into a regular fn (then-block calls the scalar fn) works (fyzs fix). Single-level inline-in-then works; only NESTED inline-in-then fails. Root: the test-runner compiles then-blocks as @deferred_init units; the nested instance collected in the then-unit isn't shared with the unit where f's param type is rewritten. Sibling of fyzs. Use regular fns to construct nested generics in tests until fixed.

title: Nested generic enum match: arm-type mismatch F1000 on Maybe<Maybe<int>>
description: Matching a nested generic ENUM hits a typeck arm-type error. Repro: 'enum Maybe<T>{Just(v:T),Nothing} fn mk()->Maybe<Maybe<int>>{Maybe.Just(Maybe.Just(3))} fn read()->int{match mk(){.Just(i)->match i{.Just(n)->n,.Nothing->0},.Nothing->0}}' -> F1000 'match expression arms have different types: Maybe<Maybe<int>> vs int'. The outer .Just(i) binds i as Maybe<int> but the inner match over i is mis-typed, so the outer arms are seen as Maybe<Maybe<int>> vs int. Single-level enum match (Maybe<int>) works. Sibling of fyzs (which fixed the generic STRUCT annotation field-access half via codegen reclassify + mono disambiguation); this is the generic ENUM half and is a TYPECK issue (nested generic enum payload binding in match), not codegen. Surfaced while working fyzs.
close_reason: Fixed by PR #535 (merged 3b7f3dc). Nested generic enum match (Maybe<Maybe<int>>) now works: (1) typeck pattern_binding_type requires the same INSTANTIATION (not just same nominal) for the self-recursive shortcut, so the payload binds at the right depth; (2) mono scope_insts_for_ret keeps fully-concrete distinct insts (the inner Maybe__int) instead of blanket-removing all same-base, and drops non-concrete placeholders. DRY: vtype_eq_deep promoted to core (with container recursion). Tests: nested_generic_enum_match_test.av (5 incl. distinct string, inner Nothing, enum-in-enum, generic-struct payload). diff-test byte-identical. Remaining deeper cases (3+ levels, inline-ctor-as-subject) tracked as ebs1; then-block inline as w62c.

title: Metadata codec drops generic-struct type_args (asymmetric with Enum) — cross-module field substitution won't fire
description: After 2px2 gave ValueType.Struct a type_args slot, the metadata codec (build/metadata.av) still serializes Struct as name+sym_id only, while Enum serializes name+sym_id+vtype_list(args). So a generic struct instance's type_args are lost across a module boundary: a Box<int> imported via metadata decodes as Box with empty args, and field-access substitution (tc_specialize_field_ty) no-ops (empty args), so b.val types as the unsubstituted T cross-module. Within a compilation unit 2px2 works (typeck sees construction + access together); this is the cross-module tail. NOT a regression — pre-2px2 Struct carried no args at all. Fix: mirror the Enum arms in metadata.av's VT_STRUCT encode/decode (write/read vtype_list(args) after sym_id); the sample.av round-trip fixture stays green (empty args round-trip equal). Needs full suite + selfhost since it changes the metadata binary format. Surfaced red-teaming the 2px2 prepare-pr.

title: unify_param doesn't unify type params nested in Tuple/Optional/Map/Union/Enum-args
description: features/generics/mono.av unify_param structurally unifies through List/Task/Channel/Fn/FnTyped/Closure, but not Tuple, Optional (T?), Map, Union, or Enum type-args. So a type param reachable only through one of those containers does not bind — in either fn-argument inference OR generic-struct construction inference (which now reuses unify_param, qcvb). E.g. a field (A, B) or T? won't bind its params from the init. Extend unify_param with the missing container arms (mirroring the List arm), pairwise for the multi-child ones. Affects the shared unify_param, so add fn-arg + struct-construction tests for each container. Surfaced during prepare-pr on PR #529.
acceptance_criteria: A type param nested in Tuple/Optional/Map/Union/Enum-args binds from the init/argument in both fn-arg and struct-construction inference; tests per container; selfhost green.
notes: unify_param extended to recurse through Tuple/Optional/Union/Enum-args/Newtype (mirroring the List arm). Tuple/Optional bind end-to-end from literals (required also fixing the typeck annotate fast-path that typed tuple literals as empty Tuple([])). Enum arm verified via a typed-binding arg (generic_container_inference_test.av). Map is nullary (no type args) so vacuously covered. The remaining bare-enum-LITERAL inference (CiEnum.Some(5) without a type annotation) is a distinct sibling gap filed as zuzv — populating the literal's type args from its payload, like StructLit/2px2 — NOT part of unify_param. Tests: generic_container_inference_test.av (6 specs). Full suite 3026/3026 + selfhost byte-identical.
close_reason: unify_param now unifies type params through all containers (Tuple/Optional/Union/Enum-args/Newtype); Tuple/Optional/Enum covered by generic_container_inference_test.av; full suite + selfhost green. Bare-enum-literal type-arg inference split to zuzv (distinct sibling of StructLit/2px2 inference, not unify_param).

title: Preserve original annotations through generic fn/method specialization
description: Both specialize_fn and specialize_method in features/generics/mono.av replace a generic decl's annotations with only @mono_spec when emitting a specialization, dropping originals like @inline. Consistent between the two today, but a latent gap: an @inline (or other behavior-bearing annotation) on a generic fn/method is lost in its specializations. Fix in ONE place if the machinery is shared, or both, so specializations carry original annotations + @mono_spec. No current consumer (no annotated generic methods/fns rely on this yet); surfaced by CodeRabbit on PR #528 (mkwc).
acceptance_criteria: A generic fn/method with a behavior-bearing annotation keeps it (alongside @mono_spec) in each specialization; covered by a spec; selfhost green.

title: DRY: extract a shared 'build compiler from a git ref' core (window gate + diff-test)
description: diagnose.sh has two composers of the same isolated-build sequence — materialize_treeish_seed -> window_copy_tree -> window_c_objects -> window_stage_binary -> hermetic_compile_env compile -> llc_link_bin: mode_check_bootstrap_window (the window gate) and dt_build_compiler (the diff-test harness). The heavy lifting already lives in shared window_* primitives, so the overlap is only the ~6-line composition, and the two differ in surrounding concerns (the window gate interleaves the seed-train gate, fingerprint-cache-with-lock, dirty-tree warning, and a smoke test). A shared build_compiler_from_ref(ref, out)->bs2 core would remove the residual duplication, but extracting it touches a CI-load-bearing gate, so it was deferred out of the diff-test PR to avoid destabilizing the window gate. Do it as its own change with the window gate re-verified.
acceptance_criteria: A single helper builds a compiler from a git ref into a dir (returning its bs2), used by BOTH mode_check_bootstrap_window and dt_build_compiler; window gate + diff-test both still pass; no behaviour change.

title: Remove the L0 tracer-bullet scaffolding (bootstrap/scratch/tracer_bullet.av)
description:
The L0 tracer bullet (bootstrap/scratch/tracer_bullet.av, from ps3t.1.1) is intentionally THROWAWAY scaffolding — a thin end-to-end slice that validated the L1-L6 architecture (per-type arena, content fingerprints, grammar-DSL parser, red-green memoized query, fingerprint-keyed codegen cache) and produced the GO verdict. It is NOT wired into the real pipeline. Once the real layers supersede it, the scaffolding should be deleted so it does not linger as dead code.

Do NOT remove it yet: it stays useful as a re-runnable reference/gate until the real query+incremental engine exists. This ticket is blocked on L6 (ps3t.8); when that lands, delete the tracer.

KEEP the decision record: docs/2026_06_15_L0_TRACER_BULLET_GONOGO.md is a point-in-time gate record and stays.
acceptance_criteria: ps3t.8 (L6) complete; bootstrap/scratch/tracer_bullet.av deleted (and bootstrap/scratch/.gitignore removed if scratch/ is now empty); docs/2026_06_15_L0_TRACER_BULLET_GONOGO.md RETAINED; no dangling references to the tracer remain (grep clean).

title: [codegen] Own mid-level IR (MIR) between AST and LLVM — DEFERRED
description: Option (b) from #6 (IR/codegen). DEFERRED — sequenced after the foundation. Today codegen is AST->LLVM direct. Introduce an own MIR (Rust-MIR / Swift-SIL style) between AST and LLVM: AST -> MIR -> LLVM -> machine code. Buys: (1) the right home for language-level analysis/opt (Drop/errdefer insertion, escape analysis, monomorphization, flow checks) — awkward on the AST, impossible on LLVM IR; (2) a STABLE + compact content-addressable cache/serialization unit (vs LLVM IR's verbosity + cross-version churn); (3) backend independence (pluggable MIR->backend: WASM/Cranelift/interpreter); (4) cleaner incremental codegen. Near-term path is option (a): per-function LLVM-bitcode caching with an ABSTRACT cache unit so MIR slots in later without re-plumbing. Spine doc: docs/2026_06_14_AST_SOURCE_OF_TRUTH_EPIC.md (Layer 6 / IR). Re-parent under the umbrella (ps3t) during ticket cleanup.
acceptance_criteria: An own MIR sits AST->MIR->LLVM; MIR is content-addressed + the per-fn codegen cache unit + a home for language-level passes; backend boundary clean. DEFERRED until optimization/LLVM-stability demands it.

title: Metadata name codec breaks on identifiers containing/leading '__' (split("__") ambiguity)
description: metadata_extract.av:572 splits mangled names on '__' to recover path segments. An exported fn whose own name starts with (or contains) a double underscore — e.g. 'export fn __probe() -> int' in @std.avrac.pathutil — round-trips wrong: consumers resolve the import but codegen reports 'undefined function @std::avrac::pathutil::__probe'. Found while building the sdmg.5 seed-merge E2E (probe fns named __sm_probe_a). Fix: unambiguous mangling (length-prefixed segments or a separator that cannot appear in identifiers), plus a spec test with dunder-named exports.

title: [errors] duplicate-function FATAL is a raw eprintln (zero-raw-errors violation)
description: setup.av:~1417 'FATAL: duplicate function `name` — rename to avoid collision' is an eprintln + hard stop, predating the diagnostics framework. Route through CompileError with a proper F-code, source locations for BOTH definitions (the F3105 conflicting-extern diagnostic from d4jv is the template — same class, proper rendering). Found red-teaming user fn names that shadow libc/runtime symbols.

title: [test-runner] cost-aware batch striping (replace size-proxy with measured shard times)
description: Batched shards stripe over the size-sorted file list (TEST_BATCH_FILES=8) — source size is a weak proxy for cost; the cold critical path is whichever batch drew the heaviest fixture-compiling tests. Persist per-file elapsed_ms from shard results (the @marshal TestResults sidecar already carries elapsed) and stripe by measured cost; revisit K with that data. Numbers at K=8 today: cold 471->334s, warm 39->19s on the full suite.

title: [coverage] atomic instrprof counters — un-pin coverage from jobs=1
description: instrprof counters are not atomic, so the coverage path pins AVRA_TEST_JOBS=1 for exact counts (run_test_coverage_path). Atomic counters (or per-thread counter pages merged at exit) would let coverage runs use the parallel runner. Until then the pin is documented and load-bearing.

title: [channels] formalize element ownership: retain-on-send refcount convention
description: send retains ptr-backed elements (receiver's scope owns the +1 traveling through the channel). Conservative escape analysis means a sender-constructed struct sent away may carry one extra refcount in some shapes; values queued at process exit are reclaimed by teardown. Formalize the transfer convention when the RC ownership model gets borrow rules (spec Axis 9).

title: [docs] green-thread claims vs pthread reality in spawn/parallel grammar
description: spawn_expr and parallel_stmt grammar.md claim green threads / fibers; the runtime is pthread-per-spawn (avra_spawn). Either land the fiber scheduler (spec Axis 18 v1.0 language) or fix the docs — today they misinform anyone designing against cooperative scheduling assumptions.

title: [codegen] Void -> LLVM void migration (drop the i64-for-void decl convention)
description: llvm_type_for_full lowers .Void to i64; setup.av's runtime decl table documents and follows the convention (callers discard a junk register). The honest lowering is LLVM void — a signature-level change across every fn emit site. The convergent-declaration abort (d4jv) made the convention explicit and enforced; this ticket removes it.

title: [channels] select on closed channels: arm semantics
description: v1 select semantics: closed+drained channels never fire their arm; all-closed-and-drained traps with 'select: all channels closed and drained'. Go-style 'closed arm fires with null' needs select to integrate the recv() -> T? shape per arm — a typed-arm design decision (spec Axis 18). The trap is correct-but-blunt for v1; revisit with real consumer patterns.

title: Result catch { none } into a T? binding rejects: catch body unified against the bare Ok type, not the annotated T?
description: let v: int? = risky() catch { none } where risky() -> Result<int, str> fails typeck with F1000 "catch body type void does not match expected type int". The catch unifies its body against the bare Ok type (int), ignoring the let annotation (int?), so none (a valid int?) is rejected and the Ok int is not widened to int?. Expected: the whole `expr catch { body }` takes the outer expected type (int?), the Ok branch auto-wraps int -> int?, and none is accepted -> a clean Result<int,E>-to-int? conversion. REPRO: fn risky(b: bool) -> Result<int, str> { if b { .Ok(5) } else { .Err("no") } }  then  fn main() -> int { let v: int? = risky(true) catch { none }  0 }. FIX SHAPE: thread the expected type into emit/check of catch so the Ok branch and the catch body unify against it (like if-expr branches do). TEST: a then-block asserting the program above compiles and v is present/none correctly. Found during xm2g.8 prepare-pr coercion-point sweep; catch×optional interaction.

title: Interpolation in a spec/then description string: parse error whose recovery OOM-kills the compiler on larger files
Indexing a newtype-of-list is not transparent: xs[0] on a 'type Ints = List<int>' value ICEs
description: Indexing a newtype whose underlying type is a list fails: 'type Ints = List<int>' then 'let xs: Ints = [1,2,3]; xs[0]' (directly, or after unwrapping an Ints? optional) reaches codegen 'indexing on non-string/list value (ty=Ints)'. The index operator does not see through the newtype to its List<int> base. Pre-existing and orthogonal to nullability — surfaced while probing optional-of-newtype (List<int>? works directly; only the newtype wrapper breaks) during xm2g.8 Part B prepare-pr round 3. Fix: in index codegen, strip newtype to its underlying type before the list/string dispatch (vtype_strip_newtype or equivalent), mirroring how field access / method calls resolve newtype transparency.

title: dyn-Trait optional: method call on unwrapped value ICEs (undefined method)
Optional match exhaustiveness: missing none arm should be a compile error
description: A match over T? that omits the absent case (no `none` arm and no `_` wildcard) — e.g. `match x { let v -> v }` — is accepted by typeck and only traps at RUNTIME (avra_match_unreachable) when the subject is none. Per spec Axis 8 (exhaustive matching, compiler-enforced), this should be a compile-time error like a non-exhaustive enum match. Add an exhaustiveness check for optional-typed match subjects (present arm + none/wildcard required) in features/match_expr/typeck.av (tc_check_exhaustive already handles enums/unions — extend to Optional). Belongs with the gating work (xm2g.5). Found during xm2g.8 Part B prepare-pr (round 3).
close_reason: tc_check_exhaustive now handles Optional: a T? match must cover present (let v) + absent (none), or a _ wildcard; a missing case is a compile error (F9001) like a non-exhaustive enum match. Tests in match_present_test.av (present-only, none-only → F9001; present+none, wildcard → ok). Full suite 2802/2802, fixed point holds.

title: [null] `if let` / `let-else` on a NON-optional subject silently mis-branches
description: The bind-fresh `if let v = x` / `let v = x else` desugar lowers the presence test to `x != none` / `x == none`. When `x` is NON-optional, that comparison is meaningless and can be WRONG: `if let v = 0 { A } else { B }` takes B because `0 != none` is false in the raw repr (0 == none). `if let` should require an OPTIONAL subject (type error, like Swift/Rust), but the parser desugars before typeck so it can't check. Proper fix: a typeck lint that flags `x ==/!= none` (and the if-let/let-else desugar) when `x` is not `T?` — F-code in the F1200 range, remedy: use a plain `let`. Also covers general misuse of `== none` on a non-optional. Low priority (misuse, rare) but silent-wrong, so worth a diagnostic. Surfaced during prepare-pr of the if-let desugar (xm2g.8 Part B).
acceptance_criteria: `if let v = <non-optional>` and `<non-optional> == none` raise a diagnostic with a remedy; optional subjects unaffected; tests cover the int-zero case. Green.

title: Centralize the List<T?> element-boxing loop (3-way dup) without perturbing module order
description:
The list-of-optional boxing loop is duplicated 3 ways: emit_list_lit's none-path (features/list_lit), emit_list_lit_expected (features/list_lit, used by let_stmt), and the inline loop in fill_arg_array_boxing (codegen/helpers). Centralizing is desirable but FRAGILE: putting the shared helper (emit_optional_list_lit) in codegen/optional_repr.av — which calls ctx.emit — regressed walker_map_wrapper_list_test (wrong output, not a crash). optional_repr.av is a foundational codegen primitive imported early/widely; adding a ctx.emit-dispatching fn there perturbs module/compilation order (the same hazard its own WHY comment documents for the codegen->feature edge). 

Repro: move the box-loop into optional_repr.av as emit_optional_list_lit and route emit_list_lit/let_stmt/fill_arg_array_boxing through it; walker_map_wrapper_list_test goes 4/4 -> 0/4 (the .map() over List<MyWrap> produces stale/wrong values). Reverting to the decentralized version restores 4/4.

Correct approach to try: host the shared helper in a HIGHER codegen module that already calls ctx.emit + imports features (e.g. codegen/helpers.av), NOT in optional_repr.av; have features/list_lit + let_stmt import it from there (feature->codegen, no cycle). Verify walker_map + full gate stay green. Filed during xm2g.8 Part B prepare-pr round 2.

comments.author: Claude
comments.text: Tried the ticket's suggested fix (host emit_optional_list_lit + a box-values kernel in codegen/helpers.av, route emit_list_lit none-path / let_stmt / fill_arg_array_boxing through it). It STILL regresses the derive_walker map suite: walker_map_wrapper_list_test, walker_map_any_fidelity_test, walker_map_test all go green->0 (wrong .map() output, not a crash), same symptom as the optional_repr.av attempt. So the perturbation is NOT specific to optional_repr.av — adding ANY new exported codegen fn that calls ctx.emit and is imported by features/list_lit + let_stmt shifts compilation/monomorphization order enough to miscompile derive_walker's generated map. The real blocker is the order-dependent codegen/mono (a determinism bug), not the helper's location. Reverted the consolidation; the 3-way dup stays (documented inline). hynr needs the module-order determinism fix first — leaving OPEN. Verified during xm2g.8 Part B prepare-pr (super-aggressive pass).

title: match-on-optional: inner-value structural patterns (widen or typeck-reject)
description: Optional match (xm2g.8 Part B) supports present-bind (`let v`), absence (`none`), wildcard, literal patterns, and guards. Structural patterns over the INNER value (inner-enum variants like `.Red`, nested patterns, type patterns) currently reach codegen and raise a clear err_match_ty (loud, not silent) directing the user to unwrap first (`if let v = x { match v { … } }`). Two improvements: (1) move that rejection into typeck with a proper F-code (F12xx) so it fails earlier and consistently, OR (2) widen to support inner-value matching by delegating the present branch to the normal enum/value match machinery over the unwrapped value. Also: the optional-match codegen returns Result<_, string> raw errors (consistent with the existing union-match path in the same file) — route through CompileError/F-codes when typeck gates this. Filed during xm2g.8 Part B prepare-pr.

title: or-pattern of type-patterns ICEs instead of clean error (match v { int(n) or string(s) -> .. })
comptime values_equal: enum/list/struct compare equal by kind only (==' is degenerate)
description:
features/eval/mod.av values_equal() compares by kind, with a catch-all '_ -> true' for every non-scalar kind:

    fn values_equal(left, right) -> bool {
        if left.kind != right.kind { return false }
        match left.kind {
            "number" -> parse_num(l) == parse_num(r)
            "string" -> l.text == r.text
            "bool"   -> l.bool_value == r.bool_value
            _ -> true   // enum / stmt / expr / value_type / list / struct
        }
    }

So in a @comptime fn, '==' between two values of kind enum/list/struct/stmt/expr/value_type returns true whenever the KINDS match, regardless of variant or payload. e.g. two different enum variants compare equal; two different lists compare equal;  is always true for any Expr x.

Pre-existing (not introduced by so07.8 boxing; boxing actually refined it slightly — comparing a boxed Stmt to a boxed Expr now correctly returns false on the kind check). Surfaced during so07.8 prepare-pr Phase 1b.

Fix: structural comparison per kind —
- enum/stmt/expr/value_type: compare enum_type + enum_variant + recursively enum_payload (or the native payload once boxed).
- list: same length + element-wise values_equal.
- struct: same struct_type + field-wise values_equal.

Note: structural AST equality is exactly the soundness the s80z @codec roundtrip (decode(encode(x))==x) needs, so coordinate with s80z. Add a comptime test exercising '==' on enum/list values.

Repro: a @comptime fn returning '(Expr.Number("1") == Expr.Number("2"))' folds to true.

title: Retire quote-stmt encoder: delete construct_stmt + enum_value_to_stmt (so07.8 Phase D tail)
description:
Split out of so07.8 acceptance #6: `grep construct_stmt( / enum_value_to_stmt(` returning nothing.

so07.8 delivered the eval-boundary collapse (boxing + O(1) unwrap + the consumer-side decoder relocated to the boundary). The LITERAL #6 grep cannot be satisfied without retiring the `quote stmt` / `quote stmts` language feature:

- `construct_stmt` (quote_expr/lower.av) is the lowering for `quote stmt`/`quote stmts`. Zero production callers, but ~30 tests across features/comptime/tests + features/quote_expr/tests exercise it (every `return quote stmt { ... }` fixture, splice tests, quote_basic_test). It also backs stmt_to_value (1-/2-arg macro decl boxing).
- `enum_value_to_stmt` is its inverse at the eval boundary (box_ast_value + value_to_stmt fallback). The two are an encoder/decoder pair.

To complete Phase D the language must drop the `quote stmt` surface (macros build native AST directly, as derive_walker already does) OR re-architect quote-stmt lowering to emit a native-AST literal Expr that eval boxes — including a deferred-splice mechanism (today construct_stmt inlines ~ident splices so they evaluate at expansion time; a naive native literal would break splicing).

Scope:
1. Decide product direction on `quote stmt`/`quote stmts` (keep with encoder, or retire).
2. If retiring: migrate the ~30 quote-stmt tests to native AST construction, delete construct_stmt + the quote-stmt lowering, and collapse enum_value_to_stmt into the eval boundary so both greps return nothing.
3. stmt_to_value gets a direct Stmt->Value encoder (no Expr roundtrip).

Depends on so07.8 (landed).
close_reason: Duplicate of s80z (B7 @codec derive), which already owns this and depends on so07.8.

title: Generic type annotation immediately followed by '=' mis-lexes '>=' (e.g. let x:List<R>=...)
description:
A generic type annotation with no space before the assignment '=' fails to parse: the lexer reads the closing '>' plus '=' as a single Tk.GreaterEqual token, so generic-arg parsing never sees the closing '>'.

Repro (all fail with F0001 'expected generic type argument' at the '>'):
  let x:List<R>=[]
  let x:List<Row>=table<Row>{ ... }
  let xs:Map<string,int>={}

Workaround: put a space before '=' (`let x: List<R> = []`).

Root cause: maximal-munch lexing of '>=' doesn't account for a preceding open generic. Options: (a) in the type-annotation/generic-args parser, split a GreaterEqual into '>' + '=' when a generic '<' is open (re-lex / token surgery), or (b) track generic-open depth in the lexer and emit '>' separately. (a) is more localized.

Surfaced during c080 red-team. General parser bug, not table-specific (`List<R>=[]` fails identically).

title: Undefined struct type in a struct literal is an F9999 codegen ICE, not a clean error
description:
A struct literal naming an undefined type — e.g. `Nope { x: 1 }` or `table<Nope> { ... }` — reaches codegen and aborts with F9999 "internal compiler error during codegen: undefined struct type `Nope`" instead of a clean resolution/typecheck error.

The typecheck struct-literal validator (features/struct_decl/typeck.av check_struct_lit_fields) skips field/type validation when struct_type_lookup returns empty, because an empty lookup also covers legitimate cases: generic type params (surface as Struct(name)), forward refs, and cross-module not-yet-resolved structs. So it can't simply error on 'not in registry'.

Fix: give typeck a way to distinguish an undefined nominal type from an in-scope generic param (the resolver already knows the full set of declared type names + the generic params in scope). Then a struct literal whose name is neither a known type nor an in-scope generic param is a clean error (suggest F3xxx resolution or F1xxx typeck) with the type name, instead of an ICE.

Surfaced during c080 (typed table literals) red-team. Not table-specific — affects all struct literals.

title: [test-runner] preserve bs2 compile stderr in diagnose.sh --run to unblock 6w6v migration
description:
Today diagnose.sh's run_fg() runs `bs2 compile` and redirects its stdout+stderr to BUILD_DIR/last_run.log. The log is only cat'ed to stderr on failure; on success it's silently discarded before the binary runs.

That makes cached_fixture_run / cached_fixture_run_no_metadata return only the runtime output. Tests that need to assert on a compile-time warning (the @expand introduces-vs-decls divergence is one example, blocking ticket 6w6v) can't use the cached helpers — they're stuck with hand-rolled compile+llc+cc+run pipelines that don't benefit from content-keyed caching.

Fix options:
1. In run_fg, also tee the compile log to stdout (so 2>&1 capture by callers picks it up). Risk: clobbers expected stdout for tests that don't expect it.
2. Add a separate diagnose.sh mode --run-with-compile-stderr that captures both. Cleaner.
3. Add a new test_runner helper cached_fixture_compile_and_run that does the dance directly, bypassing diagnose.sh.

(2) is probably cleanest. (3) is the smallest delta but adds a parallel pipeline.

Acceptance: at least one test currently using a hand-rolled pipeline (expand_introduces_validation_test.av) migrated through the new mechanism with cached warm reruns.

title: [naming] packages/std-avrac/src/build/ collides with build-output naming — rename
description:
The directory packages/std-avrac/src/build/ holds source files implementing the build SUBSYSTEM (cache.av, metadata.av, fingerprint.av, pool.av, driver.av). Sibling directories packages/std-avrac/build/ and bootstrap/build/ hold actual build OUTPUTS.

This naming collision is a foot-gun: any find / rm / nuke pattern targeting build OUTPUT (e.g. `find packages -path '*build/meta*' -delete` to drop stale metadata.bin entries) silently matches the SOURCE path packages/std-avrac/src/build/metadata*.av and deletes source files. Lost this session to exactly that mistake (had to git checkout to restore 4 source files).

Fix: rename packages/std-avrac/src/build/ to packages/std-avrac/src/build_system/ (or similar). Update all use statements: `use build.X` -> `use build_system.X`. Probably ~50-100 sites across the codebase.

Acceptance:
- src/build/ renamed, all imports updated
- selfhost holds
- common-noun find patterns ('*build*' or '*cache*') can no longer match source paths

title: [pre-commit] background test process is orphaned on Ctrl-C / early exit
description:
## Problem

Commit 97d01f48 backgrounds the test suite. If the user kills the hook with Ctrl-C (SIGINT), the background bs2 test process may survive its parent, continuing to consume CPU until natural completion (~22s warm).

Same applies if the foreground fp check exits via 'die' before the script reaches the 'wait TEST_PID' line — though the current script structure runs wait unconditionally before any exit, so that path is fine. SIGINT is the main risk.

## Fix

Add a trap on SIGINT / SIGTERM / EXIT that kills the background test PID. Bash idiom:

    cleanup() { [ -n "$TEST_PID" ] && kill "$TEST_PID" 2>/dev/null; }
    trap cleanup EXIT INT TERM

## Acceptance

- Ctrl-C in the hook kills the bg test process within ~100ms.
- No orphan bs2 processes after hook exit.
notes: Landed in eae80956. Single trap on EXIT/INT/TERM kills TEST_PID if alive (SIGTERM + 0.2s grace + SIGKILL backstop). TEST_PID initialized empty so trap is well-defined on every exit path.

title: [cli] discover_one_file short-circuit: audit CLI flag combinations
description:
## Problem

Commit caccd598 added the discover_one_file short-circuit: when path_filter is an existing literal file, classify just that file. I audited edge cases (no specs, top-level main, directory, non-existent path) but did NOT systematically audit every CLI flag combination.

Specifically:
- bs2 test --filter X path/to/file.av — short-circuit returns [file]; filter_discovered then narrows by basename. If file's basename doesn't contain X, accepted=[]; message is 'No spec test files matched filter' (good) — but is that the SAME message the pre-short-circuit code would have produced? Need to verify.
- bs2 test --coverage path/to/file.av — coverage path runs through compute_test_build_inputs (bundled cache key includes coverage flag). Does the short-circuit interact correctly with the coverage code path?
- bs2 test --list <path> + --filter — interaction.

## Fix

Manually walk every (path_filter ✕ filter ✕ coverage ✕ list-only) combination and verify output matches pre-short-circuit behavior. Add specs to discovery_filter_test.av for the path_filter + filter interaction at the unit level.

## Acceptance

- Every flag combination produces identical user-visible output as pre-short-circuit.
- Unit specs added for the interaction.
notes: Landed in 3b7a6c09. 5 new specs over synthetic inputs covering filter_by_path + filter_discovered composition.

title: [pre-commit] test-marker race: input hash captured before tests run, written after — window for missed invalidation
description:
## Problem

Commit 82e286e9's pre-commit cache marker computes TEST_INPUT_HASH at hook start, runs the suite (10-30s), then on success writes the hash to .tests_verified. If the user modifies a .av file BETWEEN the hash capture and the marker write, the marker records the pre-edit hash. A future commit of the edited file then skips tests despite a relevant input change.

Tiny window, real risk on rapid-edit workflows (e.g. claude-code).

## Fix

Recompute TEST_INPUT_HASH immediately before writing the marker. If the recomputed hash differs from the captured one (someone edited mid-suite), refuse to write — the input has drifted and the test result is no longer trustworthy.

## Acceptance

- Marker only written when pre-suite and post-suite input hashes match.
- Window for missed invalidation closes.
notes: Landed in 6d51e63d. Hash recomputed at marker-write time; if it drifted from the captured-at-start hash, the marker is NOT written. Mid-suite edits force the next commit to re-run tests. Cost: one extra shasum (~200ms) on the marker-write path. Cache-hit path 0.47s (proven warm).

title: [test-coverage] pry2_return_local_binding_test lost the package-import path when migrated to check_source
description:
## Problem

Commit feadaac9 migrated pry2_return_local_binding_test.av to in-process check_source. The original source imported @std.avrac.diagnostics.{Span, MacroFnOrigin} — exercising the package-import + let-binding interaction. The migration inlined Span / MacroFnOrigin as local struct decls because check_source skips file-based module loading.

The bug it guards against (tc_check_stmt_returns missing .Let/.Mut/.Const arms) is package-agnostic, so the inline version still catches that. But the test no longer exercises the integration of imported package types with the return-check pass.

## Fix options

1. Keep the inline version AND add a separate fixture-cache-routed test that uses the import. Two tests, two coverage paths.
2. Extend check_source / typecheck_source with an optional 'file-based modules' mode for tests that need stdlib resolution.

(1) is faster. (2) is the right systemic answer.

## Acceptance

- Coverage of (package-import + let-binding + return-check) is restored.
- Total test wall doesn't regress meaningfully (the integration test stays cached so warm reruns are ~10ms).
notes: Landed in 98eb1f75. Second spec exercises @std.avrac.diagnostics imports via cached_fixture_check_no_metadata. Coverage restored. Wall: warm 0.4s shard.

title: [walker/tests] Replace brittle magic-number counts with structural assertions
description:
## Problem

Walker spec tests assert specific child counts:

```
out.contains("block=3")   // Stmt.Block with 3 stmts
out.contains("call=3")    // Expr.Call with 1 callee + 2 args = 3
out.contains("nested=2")  // Pattern.NestedVariant with 2 sub_patterns
```

These break the moment we add another field to the variant (e.g. a span field, a flag) or change derive_walker's behavior in a subtle way (e.g. how it folds direct + list children). The number "3" carries no semantic meaning.

## Fix

Switch to structural assertions:

```
let children = block.children()
children.length == inner.length  // exactly the inner stmts, no more
children[0] is Stmt.NoOp
```

For mixed shapes (Call: 1 direct + N list):
```
let children = call.children()
children.length == 1 + args.length
children[0] is Expr.Ident  // the callee
```

Each assertion encodes WHY the count is what it is. Adding a field that's correctly classified as scalar (kind=0) doesn't break the test.

## Acceptance

- walker_pattern_test.av / walker_valuetype_test.av / walker_stmt_expr_test.av use derived counts (input.length, 1 + args.length, etc.) instead of magic numbers.
- Tests still pass.
- Adding an unrelated scalar field to a tested variant doesn't break the test.

## Notes

Caught while reviewing y9y4.11 work. The block=3 / call=3 assertions are correct for the current shape but brittle.
notes: Landed in 780becd2. 3 walker test files refactored.

title: [comptime/eval] Audit + add missing string methods (last_index_of, starts_with, ...)
description:
## Problem

The @comptime evaluator rejects `.last_index_of(...)` with "field access on non-struct value (kind=string, field=last_index_of)". Other string methods may be similarly absent — the eval surface lags the runtime's.

Hit while implementing y9y4.11's `short_name`. Workaround: manual left-to-right substring scan tracking the last `::` position.

## Fix

1. Audit core string operations that the runtime supports: `contains`, `substring`, `length`, `replace`, `split`, `to_upper`, `to_lower`, `index_of`, `last_index_of`, `starts_with`, `ends_with`, indexing.
2. Cross-reference against `features/eval/mod.av` to find which are missing from the evaluator.
3. Add each missing method to the eval dispatch table for kind="string".
4. Spec tests in features/comptime/tests/ exercising each at @comptime time.

## Acceptance

- Audit produced as a checklist.
- Every runtime string method is callable from @comptime.
- Spec tests cover the previously-missing methods.

## Notes

Continuation of W9 (string indexing). Same underlying root cause — eval surface needs to track runtime surface.
notes: Landed in 7f559304. starts_with / ends_with / index_of / trim / to_upper / to_lower / replace added. split + repeat deferred.

title: [comptime/eval] Support string indexing s[i] in @comptime evaluator
description:
## Problem

The @comptime evaluator rejects string indexing `s[i]` with "eval error: index on non-list value (kind=string)". Runtime supports it but eval doesn't lower the index op for the `string` kind.

Hit while implementing y9y4.11's `short_name` — wanted `if name[i] == ':' && name[i-1] == ':' { ... }`. Had to switch to substring scan with `name.substring(i, i+2) == "::"` which is awkward and slower.

## Fix

In `features/eval/mod.av`'s index expression handler, add a string-kind branch: return a single-char string (or int code point — match the runtime's behavior).

## Acceptance

- @comptime fn that does `name[i]` on a string evaluates without error.
- Result matches runtime semantics (probably a 1-char string per Avra convention).
- Spec test in features/comptime/tests/ exercises string indexing in an @comptime fn.

## Notes

Independent of T6 — pure evaluator surface gap. Filed here per the audit grouping.
notes: Landed in 7f559304. Index expr eval handles string kind, returning single-char string via substring(i, i+1). Validated via derive_walker's short_name back-scan.

title: [comptime/eval] Add eprintln + print + eprint intrinsics to call_builtin
description:
## Problem

The @comptime evaluator (`features/eval/mod.av::call_builtin`) supports `println` and `string` only. `eprintln` is undefined. derive_walker debugging hit F4005 "undefined variable `eprintln`" repeatedly.

This forces println-based tracing, which writes to stdout and contaminates fixture-test cached output.

## Fix

Add `eprintln` to call_builtin alongside `println`. Same shape, different stream:

```
if name == "eprintln" {
    if args.length == 0 { eprintln("") } else { eprintln(render_value(args[0])) }
    return ok_result(runtime, value_null())
}
```

Also consider `print` / `eprint` (no newline) for completeness.

## Acceptance

- @comptime fn calling `eprintln(...)` evaluates without F4005.
- Output goes to stderr, doesn't pollute fixture stdout caches.
- A spec test in features/comptime/tests/ exercises an @comptime fn that calls eprintln.
notes: Landed in 1cd23a1f alongside so07.7.11. eprintln added to call_builtin + value_builtin recognition. Scoped to println + eprintln to match codegen surface (no print / eprint variants — would ICE).

title: [core] Mark type_short_name + similar helpers @comptime so macros can import vs duplicate
description:
## Problem

derive_walker inlines its own `short_name` helper because the existing `type_short_name` in core/ast.av isn't `@comptime`-callable. Same with the `name_matches` family — duplicated logic across the macro and the typeck.

The comment in derive.av says:
> Helpers live inline (not imported from `core`) because eval can only call `@comptime` fns; copying the few lines we need keeps derive_walker eval-safe without leaking @comptime onto core.

Result: every macro that wants nominal-name handling reimplements its own copy.

## Fix

1. Audit `core/ast.av` for helpers macros need: `type_short_name`, `vtype_enum_name`, name-matching utilities, FieldEntry / Variant projections.
2. Annotate each with `@comptime` so the eval interpreter can call them.
3. Verify nothing leaks (the @comptime annotation should be additive — runtime callers still work).
4. derive_walker imports + calls; deletes its inline copies.

Same treatment likely applies to other future @comptime macros (derive_marshal etc.).

## Acceptance

- `type_short_name` carries `@comptime`.
- derive_walker drops its `short_name` and any other inline copies of core helpers.
- All walker tests still pass.

## Note

Sub-issue of T6 because once nominal identity is handle-based, half these string helpers become single-line id lookups and the @comptime exposure question shrinks.
notes: Landed in 03acb807. type_short_name @comptime via indexing back-scan (also removes the runtime .split allocation). derive_walker imports + uses; inline short_name deleted (-18 LoC).

title: [walker] Replace Binding.unwrap_fn sentinel with proper enum FieldKind variant
description:
## Problem

`derive.av` encodes field roles as `kind: int` (0/1/2/3) + a separate `unwrap_fn: string` that's empty for kinds 0/1/2:

```
type Binding = { binding_name: string, is_child: bool, kind: int, unwrap_fn: string }
```

Reading the code requires the mental table:
- kind 0 = scalar, unwrap_fn = ""
- kind 1 = DirectSelf, unwrap_fn = ""
- kind 2 = ListOfSelf, unwrap_fn = ""
- kind 3 = WrapperListOfSelf, unwrap_fn = name of helper

The empty-string for kinds 0/1/2 is a sentinel; the integer code is opaque. `is_child = kind != 0` is derivable from kind. The struct is a 4-field union pretending to be flat.

## Fix

Proper enum variant:

```
enum FieldKind {
    Scalar,
    DirectSelf,
    ListOfSelf,
    WrapperListOfSelf(unwrap_fn: string)
}

type Binding = { binding_name: string, kind: FieldKind }
```

`is_child` becomes a method or local pattern match. The unwrap_fn lives on the variant where it belongs.

## Acceptance

- Binding shape simplified.
- arm_body / block_expr_for_children match on FieldKind directly instead of comparing `b.kind == N`.
- All walker specs still pass.

## Note

Pre-existing pattern (kind=int) — extended in y9y4.11 with the kind=3 case. The enum form is the right shape once we're touching this.
notes: Landed in 54041843. enum FieldKind { Scalar, DirectSelf, ListOfSelf, WrapperListOfSelf(unwrap_fn: string) }. Required adding is_eval to is_keyword feature (registered eval_expr for IsCheck so @comptime can use k is .Variant). Two-step seed bootstrap: is_eval first, then derive_walker refactor.

title: [walker] DRY: merge is_wrapper_list_of_self + wrapper_list_unwrap_fn into single fn
description:
## Problem

derive_walker has two functions doing the same wrapper-list classification work:

```
fn is_wrapper_list_of_self(vt, parent_name) -> bool { ... }
fn wrapper_list_unwrap_fn(vt, parent_name) -> string { ... }
```

Both call `list_elem_or_unknown(vt)`, `short_name(self_type_name(elem))`, `wrapper_inner_type(wrapper)`, `name_matches(inner, parent_name)`. The bool one returns true/false; the string one returns the unwrap helper name (or "" on miss). They were split for debugging and never re-merged.

## Fix

Single function:
```
fn wrapper_list_unwrap_fn(vt, parent_name) -> string {
    // ... returns helper name on hit, "" on miss
}
```

Callers:
- `classify_field_kind`: `if wrapper_list_unwrap_fn(vt, parent_name) != "" { return 3 }`
- `classify_variant`: `let unwrap = if kind == 3 { wrapper_list_unwrap_fn(f.resolved, parent_name) } else { "" }`

Saves ~10 LoC; single source of truth for the wrapper-list detection logic.

## Acceptance

- One function instead of two.
- All walker tests still pass (block=3, call=3 wrapper-list cases plus all earlier shapes).
notes: Landed in 780becd2.

title: [walker] DRY: collapse unwrap_sstmt_list + unwrap_sexpr_list duplication
description:
## Problem

`core/ast.av` ships two near-identical helpers:

```
export fn unwrap_sstmt_list(xs: List<SStmt>) -> List<Stmt> {
    mut out: List<Stmt> = []
    for x in xs { out.push(x.node) }
    out
}

export fn unwrap_sexpr_list(xs: List<SExpr>) -> List<Expr> {
    mut out: List<Expr> = []
    for x in xs { out.push(x.node) }
    out
}
```

Same loop, same projection, different types. Currently called from derive_walker-generated `Type__children` for `List<SStmt>` / `List<SExpr>` fields.

## Fix options

**A. Generic helper**: `list_unwrap_node<W, T>(xs: List<W>) -> List<T>` if Avra's generics + the dot-projection infer cleanly. May not work today (no way to express "W has a .node field of type T" without traits).

**B. Inline at macro emit**: derive_walker emits the for-loop body directly into Stmt__children instead of calling a helper. Removes the two helpers entirely; each generated walker carries its own unwrap.

**C. Trait-based**: define `trait NodeWrapper { fn node(self) -> Self::Inner }`. Wrappers `impl NodeWrapper`. Helper becomes `fn list_unwrap<W: NodeWrapper>(xs: List<W>) -> List<W::Inner>`. Cleanest but needs assoc types.

(B) is the pragmatic option today; (C) is the right long-term shape once traits + assoc types reach that point in the bootstrap.

## Acceptance

- Zero handwritten unwrap_X_list helpers in core/ast.av.
- derive_walker either inlines the unwrap loop or uses a generic helper.
- Stmt.Block / Expr.Call walker tests still pass (block=3, call=3).
notes: Landed in 87e2e553 alongside W16. unwrap_sstmt_list + unwrap_sexpr_list now thin wrappers over generic unwrap_node_list<W,T>.

title: [parse/foundations] T2: Reserved-word audit + F0017 at binding sites
description:
## Problem

A parameter named `bare` triggers F0001 "expected expression" at the first USE site, with no diagnostic at the binding site. Reproduced in 35bf070b's intermediate iteration: `if bare.contains("::")` parsed cleanly when the param was renamed to `short`. The specific case is filed as 1rzz.

The structural issue is broader: the parser silently rejects identifier uses that shadow contextual keywords, but never tells the user at the BINDING site that the name is reserved. Sites affected: fn params, let/mut/const names, type params, pattern bindings.

This is also why `otherwise` failed in /tmp/derive_walker_valuetype_repro.av earlier this session — turned out to be similarly reserved, again only surfacing as a use-site F3000 with no binding-site signal.

## Fix

1. Audit src/parse/lexer.av + src/parse/mod.av for every contextual/reserved keyword. Build a single source-of-truth `reserved_names()` table.
2. Parser binding sites (param decl, let/mut/const, type param, pattern bind, fn name, type name) check the name against the table. On hit, emit F0017 "reserved keyword `<name>`; rename the binding" at the binding span, not the use span.
3. The `Tk` enum in core/ast.av already enumerates keywords — wire reserved_names() to it so adding a new keyword automatically extends the reject list.

Edge case: some keywords are only reserved in specific positions (e.g. `it` is a pronoun only inside method-call closures). Document those in reserved_names() with a position-set; the binding-site check uses the position-set.

## Acceptance

- `fn f(bare: string) -> bool { bare == "" }` either compiles cleanly OR errors at the param decl `bare: string` with F0017 (not at the use site)
- Test corpus generator: for each reserved word w, synthesize `fn test_${w}(${w}: string) -> int { 0 }` and assert it either parses or errors at the param-decl span with F0017
- Existing passing tests stay green
- 1rzz closes as a child of this work

## Impact

Eliminates a recurring class of confusing diagnostics. Every future contextual-keyword addition extends the table; no silent breakage.
notes: Landed in e0e68fe2. consume_identifier strict at binding sites, consume_field_name lenient for field/method access. 5-spec test covers bare/await/move/unsafe binding rejection + safe-identifier regression guard. Closes 1rzz.

title: [parser] parameter named 'bare' triggers F0001 'expected expression' on first use site
description:
Repro: define a fn with a string parameter named 'bare', then reference 'bare.contains(...)' or 'bare == ""' in the body. The parser reports F0001 'parse error at <line>:<col>: expected expression' pointing at the first use site. Renaming to 'short' / 'name' fixes it.

Concrete repro that triggered the bug in 35bf070b's intermediate iteration (before being renamed):

  fn enum_type_find_by_short(reg: EnumTypeReg, bare: string) -> string {
      if bare == "" { return "" }
      if bare.contains("::") { return "" }   // <-- F0001 here
      ...
  }

Same syntactic pattern works with 'short' / 'name' / 'n'. Suggests 'bare' is shadowed by a contextual keyword or parser rule (possibly related to 'bare ident' splice form in quote_expr — TBD).

Hypothesis: the parser's p_keyword_kind or quote_expr grammar treats 'bare' as a reserved word in certain expression contexts.

Fix paths:
  (A) Add 'bare' to the parser's allowed-ident-after-keyword list if it's genuinely reserved
  (B) Audit src/parse/lexer.av + src/parse/mod.av for 'bare' string literals and either un-reserve or document it as a reserved word
  (C) If reserved on purpose, emit a clearer F-code (F0017 reserved keyword) at the binding site rather than F0001 at the use site

Acceptance: a test file with 'fn f(bare: string) -> bool { bare == "" }' must compile cleanly, OR the binding must produce a clear reserved-keyword diagnostic at the parameter declaration.
notes: Subsumed by so07.2 (e0e68fe2). The structural fix replaces this single-keyword bug with the broader binding-site reserved-word check.

title: [derive_walker] Slice C.fold generic-return inference: typeck rejects string(t.fold(0, sum_leaves))
description:
Slice C.fold (y9y4.13) attempted but blocked on a generic-method-return inference issue. The macro emits the correct shape:

```avra
fn Tree__fold<S>(self: Tree, init: S, f: fn(S, Tree) -> S) -> S {
    mut acc: S = f(init, self)
    for c in self.children() {
        acc = c.fold(acc, f)
    }
    acc
}
```

Caller `string(t.fold(0, sum_leaves))` fails with F1003 'type S cannot be converted to string — string(value) and ${value} interpolation require a fn display(self) -> string method'. The monomorphizer should specialize S=int from the init arg, but the call-site typeck sees the unspecialized S and rejects the string() conversion.

## Repro

Source: /tmp/fold_probe.av (Tree { Leaf(int), Node(Tree, Tree) }, t.fold(0, sum_leaves) call).
Build: env -u AVRA_USE_METADATA -u AVRA_LIB_OBJS bash scripts/diagnose.sh --run /tmp/fold_probe.av
Output: F1003 type S cannot be converted to string

## Likely root causes (investigation pending)

- Method-dispatch inference for generic methods may not propagate type args from explicit init param to the return type.
- The synthesised TypeParamEntry { name: 'S', bounds: '' } might not register S correctly with the resolver/typeck.
- Or codegen needs an explicit GenericCall shape (`t.fold::<int>(0, sum_leaves)`) until inference catches up.

## Acceptance

- Tree { Leaf(int), Node(Tree, Tree) }.fold(0, sum_leaves) returns the int sum.
- Caller doesn't need explicit type arg.
- Spec test walker_fold_test.av covers sum + count.

## Depends on

- Decoder coverage (y9y4.12 + Expr.Assign decoder — both done in this branch)
- Generic method-dispatch inference for explicit-init-arg case

## Workaround

Use visit/any/find for the common cases; fold is only needed for accumulating returns. The blocker is the language's generic-method inference, not the macro itself.
notes:
Two of three layers landed:
- 353e7a28 — check_method_call tc_subst_generic_method_ret (typeck-side return-type substitution).
- 744017db — annotate_expr rewrites obj.method(args) -> Type__method(obj, args) for generic free-fns. Mono then handles via existing free-fn path. annotate_stmt extended to scope ForIn/For loop bindings so deeper rewrites see the right types.

REMAINING: mono-side dedup for self-recursive generic methods. Tree__fold's body has c.fold(acc, f); rewrite turns it into Tree__fold(c, acc, f). Inside the generic body, S=S (the type-param itself), so mono's infer_from_params binds T=S which renders as empty in the mangled name — produces Tree__fold__ duplicate from both the main call (Tree__fold__Int) and the body's recursive call (Tree__fold__ with no concrete S). Fix: mono's collect pass needs to recognize 'call to self generic fn from inside its body with type-param-as-arg' and skip registering a separate inst (the outer specialization's body substitution will create the right call when run).

Existing suite has zero generic-method-dispatch sites so the two landed layers are safe (no-op for non-fold code). 2555/2555 specs pass.
close_reason: monomorphizer now renames self-recursive generic calls inside spec bodies via specialize_fn → rename_self_calls_stmts (post-substitution pass). drop_already_known dedup added to mono_converge. spec test mono_self_recursive_generic_test.av asserts Tree.fold<int> recurses through 3 levels with no duplicate/undefined errors. all 2555 spec tests pass.

title: [derive_walker] Slice C.fold: Type__fold<S>(self, init, f: (S, Self) -> S) -> S
description:
Generic accumulating walker. Emits:

```avra
fn Type__fold<S>(self: Type, init: S, f: (S, Type) -> S) -> S {
    mut acc = f(init, self)
    for c in self.children() {
        acc = c.fold(acc, f)
    }
    acc
}
```

Needed for any pass that needs a result: counting nodes, collecting names, building a depth map, etc.

## Why split from y9y4.3

visit() landed in y9y4.3 as the simplest case (no generics, no return). fold introduces:
- Generic type param `S` — encoder + decoder need to handle TypeParamEntry with bounds and the recursive ValueType.Struct("S", _) shape on the param
- Mutable accumulator binding — Stmt.Mut already roundtrips post-y9y4.12
- Assignment statement (`acc = f(init, self)`) — Expr.Assign decoder doesn't exist yet (would F4006)

## Acceptance

- Tree { Leaf(int), Node(Tree, Tree) }.fold(0, (acc, t) -> match t { .Leaf(v) -> acc + v; _ -> acc }) sums leaves.
- Pattern.fold collects every TypePattern's binding name into a List<string>.

## Depends on

- y9y4.3 (visit) — closes first, easier
- Expr.Assign decoder (likely a follow-up sub-ticket to y9y4.12)
notes: Initial attempt blocked on F1003 — generic-S return type doesn't propagate to string() conversion at call site. See sibling ticket for repro + acceptance. Macro emission is correct; the gap is in monomorphizer/typeck inference for generic-return method dispatch.

title: [resolve/typeck] Re-infer fn return type from match-expression body post-@expand
description:
When @expand emits a Stmt.Function with body `match self { ... }`, the post-expand resolver currently doesn't re-infer the return type from the match arms — leaving callers with `ty=``` empty errors at .length / iteration.

## Current workaround

derive_walker explicitly sets ret_ty = ValueType.List(self_ty) at macro-emit time. Works, but every macro author has to compute the precise type. For most macros (visit returning Void, fold returning T, etc.), this is non-trivial.

## The fix

After @expand, run a focused typeck pass on the emitted fn body: if the body is a match expression and all arms produce the same type T, infer return type T. Same logic the normal type-checker already has — just route emitted fns through it.

## Acceptance

- Macro can leave ret_ty = ValueType.Unknown and the resolver/typeck infers it.
- Spec: macro emits 'fn foo(x: int) { match x { 1 -> "a" 2 -> "b" _ -> "c" } }'; calling foo(2).length works.

## Related

- y9y4.1 (derive_walker Slice A) — current hard-coded ret_ty in build_children_fn.

title: anonymous rc-allocating expressions leak — nested  without binding
description:
Found during xlho regression-test work. Pattern that leaks:

let u = (h with { a: "A" }) with { b: "B" }

The inner (h with { a: "A" }) is anonymous — never bound to a let, so escape analysis can't add it to rc_releasable, and ctx.bind never schedules a Release for it. The new struct allocated by the inner with leaks (1 leak per nested anon with).

Probably affects any rc-allocating expression used in expression position: StructLit / EnumCtor / Tuple / With / ListLit inside fn-call args, binary exprs, etc. Anywhere we get an rc_alloc without a let binding to attach Release to.

Fix: codegen needs an 'anonymous-value-Release' mechanism. Options:
  1. emit() returns rc-allocated values via a sink that auto-schedules Release at current scope exit.
  2. let-binding lift in desugar: rewrite anonymous allocating subexprs as synthetic let bindings before codegen.

Reproducer: write a fn that returns void, body = let u = (h with { a: "A" }) with { b: "B" }; let _ = u.c. Watch avra_rc_live_count before/after — leaks 1 per nested anon with.
